content.title: Can music and choral singing address young people's hopelessness and create meaning?
content.description: How can we give more young people hope and meaning? Perhaps the solutions already exist, in our schools and choirs, if we dare to invest in what we know works. Research and practice show how singing contributes to mental health and social cohesion, strengthening self-esteem, community and hope for the future.
content.extendedDescription:
The seminar highlights one of the most pressing issues of our time: how can we address young people's hopelessness and sense of meaninglessness? Our starting point is that solutions already exist, right in schools and cultural life. Across Sweden's music sector, music teachers and choir leaders see daily how singing and making music strengthen self-esteem, belonging and hope for the future.
Choral singing is more than an artistic activity. It develops listening, responsibility and cooperation, and creates spaces where every voice counts. In a choir, differences become a strength and community grows organically. Young people experience being genuinely needed and seen within collective meaning-making.
The discussion brings research and practice together to show how music contributes to mental health and social cohesion. We want to highlight bold decisions that strengthen what already works, giving more young people hope and meaning.

Breakfast & Future with Malmö Yrkeshögskola MY.SE

Simona Mohamsson presents Liberalerna's key election pledges for schools and offers a preview of her evening speech. And who knows, Simona herself might be scooping your ice cream.

content.title: How can we move towards climate-neutral construction? What improvements can we make now?
content.description: Steel and cement production account for a significant share of Sweden's greenhouse gas emissions. Yet both materials are essential for building houses and infrastructure with long service lives and low life-cycle costs.
content.extendedDescription:
Greenhouse gas emissions from steel and cement production are both complex and global. Where do the emissions come from, and how can we use existing knowledge to reduce construction's climate impact?

Welcome to a seminar focusing on simple, practical measures to reduce the climate impact of construction.
content.subject: Construction

content.title: What responsibility do politicians take for preserving Swedish openness?
content.description: Over recent electoral terms, political decisions have restricted Swedish openness and public access, including through limitations on the principle of public access to official documents and increased secrecy within public authorities. This has reduced scrutiny by the media and the public.
content.extendedDescription: For the second year running, Sweden has fallen one place in Reporters Without Borders' World Press Freedom Index and is now fifth. A conversation with the Minister for Justice about balancing scrutiny, openness and democracy on one side with security, privacy protection and other considerations on the other.
content.subject: Media/journalism

content.title: Social media and snus – the downfall of the young: what do young people do when politics means bans?
content.description: The government is considering banning social media use for people under 15. Within the EU, there are plans to extend France's ban on white snus to all EU countries, including Sweden. Is this the right approach? The issue concerns young people's freedom, health and trust in society.
content.extendedDescription:
Meet representatives of several parliamentary parties' youth wings for a discussion about life online and with white snus. Are these two threats to our younger generation? What policies do the youth wings want on internet and nicotine regulation?
Comments from businessman and entrepreneur Jan Emanuel, among others.
content.subject: Research

content.title: How is freedom of expression stifled in countries with apostasy and blasphemy laws? How does this affect Sweden?
content.description: Eleven countries impose the death penalty for apostasy or blasphemy. In other countries, those who leave or question Islam face imprisonment, forced divorce, loss of inheritance and other penalties.
content.extendedDescription: What is apostasy? What is blasphemy? In which countries is leaving Islam criminalised? What spillover effect is there in Sweden? Why is it important for Sweden to protect the freedom to leave a faith or religion and to defend freedom of expression?
content.subject: Freedom of expression
speakerTitles: Political scientist, Chair of Persiska missionsföreningen Sthlm

content.title: Children in a burning world – why are young people hesitant about having children?
content.description: The climate crisis affects not only the planet but also people's life choices. One in five young women is considering not having children because of the climate.
content.extendedDescription: When anxiety about the future affects decisions about family and children, the issue also becomes a feminist one. What would enable young women to feel secure about the future and dare to believe in the next generation? In this live podcast, S-kvinnor and S-studenter discuss climate, gender equality and the right to hope for the future.
content.subject: Climate/environment

content.title: Governance and responsibility in healthcare
content.description: The inquiry into nationalising healthcare presented its report a year ago – what happens now? Will it become an election issue, or be buried among all the other topics dominating the debate? The question remains whether increased central government control of medicines could become a reality regardless.
content.extendedDescription: We explore whether central government control of medicines could become a reality and how Sweden, the life science sector and patients are affected by the USA's new pricing reform.

content.extendedDescription: Within the EU, this is regulated in a way that hampers European companies' development and ability to generate revenue in this technological field. This panel discussion will address the issue from the perspective of Swedish competitiveness.
content.subject: Business

content.title: Older, but not old
content.description: More than 2 million Swedes have reached what we call retirement age. They have very different lives, motivations and dreams, but are often portrayed stereotypically and depicted as passive members of society. Why is this, and how can we change it?
content.extendedDescription:
Ahead of the party leaders' speeches, photographer Evelina Carborn and pensions economist Staffan Ström from Alecta present the photo exhibition Äldre men inte gammal (Older, but not old). Listen to Evelina's stories from meeting the models and explore why the public image of older people is so stereotypical.

The exhibition can be viewed throughout Almedalsveckan on Donnersgatan, halfway between Almedalsparken and Almedalsbiblioteket.

Future prototypes from the research project ‘The importance of aesthetics for acceptance of agrivoltaic solar parks in agricultural landscapes’, funded by Energimyndigheten, may inspire new ideas.

content.description: Sweden was long a voice for peace and diplomacy. What does that role look like today?

During Olof Palme's time, Sweden played a prominent role in international peace policy and efforts towards dialogue, disarmament and conflict resolution. Today's world looks different, with new security policy challenges and heightened international tensions. What role can Sweden play in future peace efforts?

A podcast conversation discussing these issues will be recorded on site during this session. It focuses on Sweden's opportunities to contribute to peace, diplomacy and conflict resolution in a changing world, and the lessons that can be learned from earlier generations' peace work.

content.description: The Jesus of the Gospels at a time when authoritarian winds are sweeping through society.
content.extendedDescription: Priest Mats Hermansson reflects on the clear political positions in Jesus' life. Jesus sides with the poor, the oppressed and the marginalised, and calls on his followers to do the same. That is why Jesus has always inspired people working for a just and humane society for everyone. Jesus' message is not so much about heaven and the afterlife. His primary concern is how we live with one another and how we organise our society.

content.title: When words refuse to be silent: literature as resistance
content.description: Literature has the power to reveal what those in power want to hide. Through stories depicting oppression, war and injustice, authors can create spaces for truth, empathy and resistance.
content.extendedDescription: Literature becomes essential resistance when injustice and war silence people. Through words, authors can expose abuses of power, give a voice to those lost in violence and preserve experiences that might otherwise be erased. Stories offer the opportunity to understand, feel and question – and thus to create change. Literature defends human dignity, keeps memories alive and shows that another future is possible.

content.title: Everyone is talking about agents, tokens and AI factories – why?
content.description: It can hardly have escaped anyone's notice that today's conversations about AI are dominated by agents, tokens and AI factories. Why is that?
content.extendedDescription:
How have tokens become the AI era's number-one commodity?
Why has the AI industry rallied around the factory as the model for controlled AI?
What strategic considerations should you keep in mind as a leader when it comes to agents?

The conversation offers concrete examples of what to avoid and what to focus on with AI, and addresses strategic challenges such as sovereignty, energy efficiency and profitability. In this Di Talks, we explore why this is happening.

content.title: Gripen for Ukraine – a new era of security and cooperation
content.description: Swedish fighter aircraft for Ukraine will have significant effects on several levels – for Sweden, Ukraine and Europe.
content.extendedDescription:
Politically, ties between the two countries will strengthen further. In terms of capability, Ukraine's air defence will be substantially reinforced. Industrially, this will create new business opportunities for both Swedish and Ukrainian companies.

Followed by a panel discussion with participants including Svitlana Zalishchuk, Ukraine's Ambassador to Sweden.
content.subject: Security/defence

content.title: Available around the clock – can AI build trust in sensitive parts of the customer journey?
content.description: Many companies use AI to streamline customer service. Few use it in situations where the customer's trust is truly at stake.

The exhibition can be viewed throughout Almedalsveckan on Donnersgatan, halfway between Almedalsparken and Almedalsbiblioteket.

content.extendedDescription: Strengthening Stockholm's position as a world city requires courage, space for culture and new ways of working. Director of Culture Maria Jansén opens with a preview of Stockholm's new strategic cultural programme. An expert panel with representatives from the city and the sector then discusses it.
content.subject: Visitor economy

content.title: Higher vocational education or university — which matters most in addressing businesses' skills shortages?
content.description: Unemployment is rising among recent university graduates. More and more prospective university students are choosing to apply to vocationally oriented programmes. Applications to higher vocational education are also increasing, and this sector has a well-developed model for cooperation with businesses seeking new employees.
content.extendedDescription:
Do we need two different forms of education that both strengthen cooperation with business?
Would it not be better to develop each form's distinctive strengths?
content.subject: Education
speakerTitles: Chair of the Parliamentary Committee on Education

content.title: Animal policy after the election
content.description: A parliamentary term of highs and lows is drawing to a close. Chicken scandals, competitiveness and the push for meat, but also the phasing out of mink farming and the end of caged hens. What is at stake for animals in the next parliamentary term? What do today's featured parties, Miljöpartiet and Socialdemokraterna, want to see?
content.extendedDescription: Are you among the 38 per cent of the population who take animal issues into account when going to the polls in September? Stop by Djurens Rätt's large trailer to get answers to your questions and listen to discussions with representatives of today's featured parties, Miljöpartiet and Socialdemokraterna.
content.subject: Animals/nature

content.title: How can municipalities use background checks to combat crime?
content.description: The question of how municipalities can use background checks to combat crime is becoming increasingly important. There is a great need to protect vulnerable groups, particularly in elderly care, where unsuitable recruitment can have serious consequences.
content.extendedDescription: This seminar brings together representatives of the justice system and municipalities to discuss how background checks can improve safety and combat crime in municipalities, with examples from elderly care and other areas.
content.subject: Older people
speakerTitles: Chair of the Municipal Executive Board

content.title: How does generative AI affect universities' core mission?
content.description: AI development raises fundamental questions about knowledge, education and academic responsibility, creating a clear need for higher education institutions to discuss choices, principles and long-term consequences together.
content.extendedDescription: Development in generative AI is driven largely by global technology companies. How can universities, individually and collectively, engage more actively with this development and help shape their future role, rather than merely reacting to external forces?
content.subject: Education
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: What do the parties want for adult education?
content.description: Adult education serves many purposes and is used in many ways. But how do the different parties view adult education, and what are their political strategies?
content.extendedDescription: Adult education has been described as the Swiss army knife of education. But depending on political ambitions and priorities, different blades have been unfolded according to who is in government. In this seminar, representatives of the different parties meet to present and discuss how they believe adult education should be used after the election.
content.subject: Education
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Vulnerable leadership, ideal leadership — how do we lead the welfare society of the future?
content.description: Is vulnerability the key to tomorrow's leadership? What does public-sector leadership need to get the best out of welfare services? Which qualities are decisive? How can we best meet today's and tomorrow's challenges?
content.extendedDescription: An inspiring introduction opens this important discussion before we meet public-sector managers who share their best tips for successful leadership that develops welfare services.
content.subject: Integration/diversity
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Young people in rural areas
content.description: What is it like to grow up and live as a young person in rural municipalities in inland Västerbotten and Norrbotten?
content.extendedDescription: What is it like to grow up and live as a young person in rural municipalities in inland Västerbotten and Norrbotten? In this panel, we meet young people whose voices are rarely heard in the debate about being young in Sweden today. What does growing up and living in rural Sweden mean when school, activities and friends can be hours away? When the bus runs once a day and you need to leave home to attend upper secondary school?
content.subject: Children/young people

content.title: Why human rights should be at the heart of the 2026 election
content.description: Human rights are under challenge globally and in Sweden. International law is under pressure, security arguments are used to justify restrictions on rights, and democratic space is shrinking. Meanwhile, people around the world are mobilising for justice.
content.extendedDescription: How do we build resilience in an increasingly polarised era? In this discussion, Amnesty, Civil Rights Defenders and Human Rights Watch jointly analyse why human rights must be central to politics, particularly in an election year.
content.subject: Human rights

content.title: Water is our most essential food — are municipalities ready for crisis and war?
content.description: A government inquiry to strengthen preparedness in water and wastewater services was presented in December 2024, but since then the issue has stalled in the political system. What is happening? Why is so little happening? And what should politicians prioritise?
content.extendedDescription: Svenskt Vatten presents its top five proposals from the water and wastewater preparedness inquiry. What do municipalities need to move forward? What can and should happen now, and what must the next government take further?
content.subject: Security/defence
speakerTitles: Climate Adaptation and Civil Preparedness Strategist
Chair of the Municipal Executive Board

content.title: Why does it take five years to build a charging site?
content.description: The will to make the transition exists, but bureaucracy is holding it back. Three years to obtain permission to build a charging site. Municipalities demanding building permits even though the law says otherwise. Short-term rules that make investments outdated before they are made.
content.extendedDescription: Circle K and Alfredsson Transport AB, winners of Transportföretagen's sustainability award in 2025 and 2024, describe what regulatory complexity looks like in practice and what is actually needed to break the deadlock in electrification.
content.subject: Climate/environment
content.accessibility: Event captioning, hearing loop

content.title: Operational preparedness: lessons from Ukraine for Sweden's digital defence
content.description: How can Sweden strengthen its preparedness and develop total defence at a time of rapid technological change?
content.extendedDescription: The discussion explores, among other things, what Sweden can learn from Ukraine's experience of rapid innovation and adaptation in wartime, and the conditions needed to scale up capacity and cooperation between defence, the public sector and business within total defence.
content.subject: Security/defence

content.title: It is too expensive to be a retailer — high costs and unfair competition
content.description: High costs, such as employer contributions, and the consequences of unfair competition from third-country platforms. How do we overcome this?
content.extendedDescription: Retail is Sweden's largest sector by number of employees. It generates 11 per cent of GDP and 14 per cent of tax revenue. Yet costs are high, margins are low and international competition is fierce and not entirely fair. How do we overcome this?
content.subject: Business
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: How do driving licences affect young people's job opportunities?
content.description: What does the path from a driving licence to a job look like for young people in Sweden?
content.extendedDescription:
We invite you to a dynamic discussion in which youth politicians provide clear positions and concrete answers to current issues affecting young people's futures.

Youth politicians take the stage and face topical questions. The format is fast, focused and encourages clear answers rather than lengthy arguments.
Topics discussed:
• CSN loans for driving licences
• Better links between education and the labour market
• Raising the status of vocational education
content.subject: Employment/labour market
content.accessibility: Event captioning, hearing loop

content.title: Agentic AI The Next Frontier
content.description: AI is already a familiar concept to most. But what about Agentic AI - and what does it mean for businesses to stay competitive? How can autonomous AI agents transforming business operations, driving efficiency, and unlocking new possibilities for innovation?
content.extendedDescription: The panel will explore how Sweden can turn its current strengths into long‑term leadership, and what we must adapt and accelerate if we want to set the competitive benchmark for the rest of Europe.
content.subject: Digitalisation

content.title: When did culture become a question of left or right?
content.description: Culture shapes our stories, our meeting places and many of the shared frames of reference that hold a society together. Yet culture is increasingly discussed in terms of political positions rather than its value to people and society.
content.extendedDescription:
How can we create a more nuanced discussion about the role of culture in democracy? How can we create the conditions for a vibrant cultural life regardless of who is in power, and prevent culture from being reduced to a weapon in the debate?

The discussion is recorded as part of the podcast series Din Röst.
content.subject: Culture

content.title: Where did the movement go?
content.description: For a long time, many international researchers and politicians came to Sweden to study the country they considered the most advanced in welfare, equality and gender equality. Social democracy was given the credit. Today, no one looks to social democracy. What happened?
content.extendedDescription: Kjell Östberg, Senior Professor at Samtidshistoriska Institutet at Södertörns Högskola, is interviewed by Åsa Mattsson, journalist and editorial secretary of Internationalen, about his newly published book "Mellan makten och rörelsen – maktspel, intriger och historiens dom", published by Ordfront.
content.subject: Democracy

content.title: What does Sweden want? Healthcare and the economy top the election agenda
content.description: This year's election will be decisive for Sweden's healthcare capacity, growth and preparedness. Sweden is at a stage where changes abroad and demographic challenges at home demand that politics deliver.
content.extendedDescription: Ahead of the 2026 election, Lif's election podcast discusses the pharmaceutical industry's hottest political issues in health, innovation and economics with an expert panel. We take stock of the campaign so far and look ahead.
content.subject: Innovation
speakerTitles: Head of Strategy and Public Affairs

content.title: How can we build a safer world? Global health, aid, innovation and Sweden's role in the world
content.description: The security debate often focuses on defence, rearmament and geopolitics. Less often on investments that can help prevent crises from arising in the first place.
content.extendedDescription: Over the course of an afternoon, ONE Campaign brings together researchers, policymakers, journalists, investors and people shaping society to discuss the links between health, development, security and hope for the future.
content.subject: Security/defence
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet
speakerTitles: Associate Director Advocacy and Campaigns Scandinavia

content.title: The patient in focus: Why is it so difficult to lose weight?
content.description: Obesity is one of our most important public health issues, yet it is surrounded by ignorance and stigma. More and more Swedes live with obesity and an increased risk of serious associated conditions. Children are also affected and therefore risk long-term ill health. Decisive action is needed to halt this development.
content.extendedDescription: In the first of three discussions, we focus on the patient – from society's prejudices to treatment by healthcare services and the reality patients now face: paying for treatment themselves. Is that equitable healthcare?
content.subject: Health and social care

content.title: The media – America's megaphone?
content.description: Why does Putin appear on 87% of Expressen's newsstand posters – but never Netanyahu? Why does SVT refer to Palestine as Hamas? Why have we seen no investigations into the DCA agreement? And where does the information about the world that our media serve us actually come from?
content.extendedDescription: Meet three of Parabol's writers: Valley Ghanem, John Lapidus and Kamal El Salim, who have all examined media coverage of the geopolitical issues of our time, in a discussion with Parabol's editor-in-chief Kajsa Ekis Ekman that you must not miss!
content.subject: Communication/information
speakerTitles: Author, public commentator and PhD in economic history

content.title: Stronger protection or conditional rights?
content.description: How do political decisions affect freedom of expression, artistic freedom and academic freedom?
content.extendedDescription:
A new report from Kommittén för demokratins röstbärare discusses how changes in legislation, economic priorities and institutional governance shape conditions for journalists, cultural practitioners and researchers. Three representatives of these professions contribute their analyses of the report and suggest ways forward.

Coffee and breakfast sandwiches will be served.
content.detail:
Uppsala Universitet - Campus Gotland, Cramérgatan 3, Visby
Building B, B51
content.subject: Democracy

content.title: What do young voters want, and what matters to how they vote?
content.description: In this year's parliamentary election, the youngest voters – first-time voters – make up the largest proportion of the electorate since 2010. But what do young voters want, and what distinguishes them from other voters?
content.extendedDescription: There are more young voters in 2026 than there have been for a long time, with particularly large numbers of first-time voters in metropolitan areas. During the seminar, Johan Martinsson, Head of Public Opinion at Demoskop, presents both previous research and a new opinion poll on young voters conducted by Demoskop in collaboration with Svenska Dagbladet. A panel comments on and discusses the results.
content.subject: Children/young people

content.title: How cross-border cooperation strengthens healthcare preparedness for war – what do exercises teach us?
content.description: An increasingly strained international situation places high demands on healthcare's ability to deliver, even when a crisis is prolonged or occurs beyond our immediate region. How can exercises and cooperation across administrative, civilian/military and geographical boundaries strengthen our preparedness?
content.extendedDescription: Drawing on the large-scale healthcare exercise Resilient Care 25, the seminar highlights the insights that exercises provide and how they translate into greater preparedness in the event of war.
content.subject: Health and social care
speakerTitles: Chair of the Regional Executive Board

content.title: How can we defend industrial workers' conditions in an unsettled world?
content.description: Every day, Sweden's industrial workers help build a strong Sweden, something that is of course particularly important when the world around us is unsettled.
content.extendedDescription: For 20 years, IF Metall has used its combined strength and collective power to safeguard fair conditions for industrial workers – the people who keep Sweden running. How can we continue to defend and improve industrial workers' conditions in the years ahead despite an unsettled world?
content.subject: Employment/labour market
content.instructions: The discussion will be broadcast live on Marie Nilsson's Facebook page.
speakerTitles: former President of IF Metall (2006–2012) and Prime Minister of Sweden (2014–2021)

content.title: No investment, no preparedness – why Sweden must invest in farming and forestry now
content.description: Profitable Swedish farming and forestry businesses with the right investment are crucial to Sweden's food preparedness – in peace, crisis and war. How can the green sector create stable businesses that are born, take root and grow, while remaining resilient in an increasingly uncertain world?
content.extendedDescription: We explore the investments, political decisions and business models needed to secure Swedish food production and a resilient society over the long term.
content.subject: Economy
speakerTitles: Chair of the Committee on Industry and Trade
Member of the Committee on Industry and Trade
Head of Agriculture and Forestry Business Area

content.title: Money morning — today's personal finance issues
content.description: What are today's major personal finance issues, and how do they affect us?
content.extendedDescription:
Join us for coffee at SEB and listen to our personal finance economist Américo Fernández discuss the most important personal finance issues with invited guests.

Wednesday's Plånboksmorgon focuses on the housing market and its future development. How will prices develop? How have the new mortgage rules introduced on 1 April affected supply and demand? And how should we approach buying a home given the geopolitical uncertainty around us?
content.subject: Economy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Reuse then and now – what have we learned from past thinking and practices?
content.description: How can we develop future reuse practices by looking back in a more structured way? What do we actually learn from history?
content.extendedDescription: Reuse regularly returns to the debate about managing existing buildings in a resource-efficient way. There is much to learn from heritage conservation's fundamental principle of care: doing as little as possible and only what is necessary when making changes. Benefits and pitfalls will be discussed.
content.subject: Sustainability
speakerTitles: Head of R&D, Associate Professor of Ethnology
Associate Professor of the History of Ideas

content.title: Beyond the horizon: Next-generation air combat in a multi-domain context
content.description: What will future combat in the air domain look like, and how will air power be projected as threats change faster than ever? Manned and unmanned systems work together, and new technology creates entirely new operational possibilities.
content.extendedDescription:
Followed by a panel discussion with participants including Jonas Wikman, Chief of the Air Force, and Justin Bronks, RUSI.

Gripen becomes part of a larger intelligent ecosystem. The focus is on future capabilities, technological choices and how tomorrow's combat aircraft systems deliver effects in cooperation with other military forces.
content.subject: Security/defence
speakerTitles: Head of Advanced Programs Business Unit

content.title: Partnerships and the ability to deliver – the key to more homes
content.description: Capital is available. Land is available. But how can we create more housing projects and entire neighbourhoods that actually become reality?
content.extendedDescription: Join us for breakfast and a discussion on Bonava's morning sofa about partnerships that make a difference. Drawing on our collaborations in places including Sigtuna Stadsängar and Stora Ursvik, we share experiences of joint ventures between developers, investors and municipal actors. Welcome to a discussion about how we can truly achieve more – together.
content.subject: Construction
speakerTitles: CEO of Sigtuna Stadsängar / Head of Investment at Bonava
Head of Urban and Property Development

content.title: An age limit on social media – will young media users be excluded from news and knowledge?
content.description: A new age limit for social media is now being proposed in Sweden. What could it mean in practice, both for the media industry and for children and young people?
content.extendedDescription: Social media are now an important route to knowledge, news and social interaction for children and young people. Do we risk shutting them out of important public information if we introduce an age limit? How will the media market be affected? Will we see entirely new media habits in the future?
content.subject: Media/journalism
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: How can background checks stop crime in business?
content.description: The question of how businesses can protect themselves against infiltration and organised crime is becoming increasingly central. As threats increase, so does the need for effective tools to identify risks early.
content.extendedDescription:
This seminar brings together representatives of business and the justice system to discuss how background checks can counter infiltration and strengthen companies' resilience to crime.

The discussion opens with a keynote speaker (TBA) and is moderated by Cassandra Lundgren. Panel members will be announced ahead of the seminar.
content.subject: Business
speakerTitles: Expert on crime and public safety policy

content.title: How can the technology sector strengthen Europe's competitiveness?
content.description: What opportunities and challenges do companies see in Europe's technological development? And how can policy help create the right conditions for innovation and investment?
content.extendedDescription:
Europe faces several crucial choices on technology and innovation – from implementing the AI Act to growing competition with the US and China.

This discussion brings together companies, policymakers and experts to explore how cooperation can strengthen Europe's competitiveness while protecting democratic values.
content.subject: Innovation

content.title: Sweden's AI potential – how can we enable innovation and scale up competitiveness?
content.description: AI is changing the playing field – and the pace is accelerating rapidly. How can Sweden speed up?
content.extendedDescription: Sweden's new AI strategy aims to make Sweden one of the world's top 10 AI countries and the Nordic region a global AI hub. But getting there requires more than visions – it requires infrastructure, skills and clear regulation. How can we turn ambition into action? And how can we unlock Sweden's full AI potential?
content.subject: Digitalisation
speakerTitles: VP Head of AI Innovation & Incubation & Head of Silicon Valley Site

content.title: How can journalists get the best answers from politicians during election campaigns?
content.description: Domestic political journalism develops and faces challenges during election campaigns. When politicians deliver rehearsed talking points, journalists need even more thorough research and interview techniques. But how does a journalist conduct a really good interview that holds someone to account? What different methods are available?
content.extendedDescription: What does it take for domestic political journalism to feel engaging and important to the entire population? A discussion between political journalists who all interview and hold politicians to account, in different ways and for different audiences.
content.subject: Media/journalism
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Sustainable mobility throughout the country – why is progress so slow?
content.description: Municipalities and regions have policy documents calling for a larger share of sustainable mobility. Rådslaget and ShiftSweden have clearly identified that an expanded role for public transport and new structures are necessary to increase sustainable mobility across Sweden. But very little is happening. Why?
content.extendedDescription: A panel of experts and policymakers will discuss why the transition is not moving faster and what needs to be done.
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport
speakerTitles: Chair of the Regional Development Committee, Member of Kommunalförbundet Norrbottens läns kollektivtrafikmyndighet

content.title: AI everywhere – but where is the impact?
content.description: Many organisations are investing in AI, but few can demonstrate clear business results. At the same time, pressure to deliver impact is growing. How do you set the right priorities – and what does it take for AI to actually contribute to organisational results?
content.extendedDescription: Most organisations today have many AI initiatives – but few can demonstrate real business impact. PwC's AI Performance Study 2026 shows that 20% of companies account for 74% of the total business value driven by AI. What are they doing differently – and what does it take to take the next step?
content.subject: Digitalisation
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: The Minister for Infrastructure – how important is shipping?
content.description: Almost everything we produce and consume in this country has at some point been transported by sea. Shipping is therefore important to society, but how much weight do shipping issues carry in the corridors of political power?
content.extendedDescription:
Unfortunately, plans changed for our Minister for Infrastructure and Housing, Andreas Carlson, so we had to rethink.

Can the operation and maintenance of all transport modes be incorporated into the national infrastructure plan to create a transport system that makes the best use of every mode? How can we achieve a thriving shipping industry with political winds in its sails?
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport

content.title: Data sovereignty in practice: how Sweden's public sector secures control of data, AI and the cloud
content.description: Public bodies hold data critical to society. EU regulation is tightening requirements – while organisations want to use cloud services and AI. How can we create genuine data sovereignty without hampering innovation? The panel presents a practical roadmap, with lessons learned, technological insights and clear advice for procurement officers and CIOs.
content.extendedDescription: The panel presents a practical roadmap, with lessons learned, technological insights and clear advice for procurement officers and CIOs.
content.subject: Digitalisation
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Head of Guidance, Innovation and Technology

content.title: Which issues are shaping Europe's future?
content.description: The EU faces important choices on competitiveness, climate, AI and digitalisation. Europe's green and digital transitions are particularly important in the unsettled world we live in. But how should the EU's work develop?
content.extendedDescription:
In this panel discussion, leading experts in climate, energy and digitalisation discuss which issues will be most important for Sweden's next government to pursue in EU cooperation.

The moderators will be Pia Högset and Anton Olsson from Impact Europe.
content.subject: EU
speakerTitles: VP Head of AI Innovation & Incubation & Head of Silicon Valley Site

content.title: Mental health on the timetable – what does it mean in practice?
content.description: Mental health in school teaching under the forthcoming curriculum changes. How can schools address these issues in practice?
content.extendedDescription: During work on Mindmap – new school materials about feelings, thoughts and mental health – young people have described what they need for schools to contribute to their psychological well-being. Knowledge of mental health is highlighted as important, alongside the need for a school environment that as a whole promotes every student's health. The seminar provides an up-to-date overview and highlights the roles different actors can play in strengthening young people's well-being.
content.subject: Children/young people

content.title: Education and preparedness – the role of Swedish media when war comes
content.description: The media play a key role in a crisis. But how prepared is Sweden's media industry? What can viewers, listeners and readers expect?
content.extendedDescription: How well equipped are the media to withstand cyberattacks, for example, and how prepared are journalists to maintain their independence in war? Who is responsible for ensuring that children and young people receive information at the right level, and what demands can Försvarsmakten place on Swedish media? A discussion about the media and independent journalism in Sweden if the worst happens.
content.subject: Media/journalism
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Rear Admiral (lower half) and Communications Director

content.title: The role of the campfire in an unsettled world
content.description: In an age marked by uncertainty, polarisation and growing preparedness requirements, a larger question arises: what holds us together when society comes under pressure?
content.extendedDescription: Culture and shared experiences are often seen as secondary during crises and transitions, but may in fact play a crucial role in social cohesion, meaning and resilience. The seminar takes as its starting point the importance of the campfire in an unsettled world: the need for shared stories, experiences and spaces where people can feel belonging, hope and community.
content.subject: Culture

content.title: Leadership for transition through reuse – who are the role models?
content.description: Reuse is a necessary part of the transition in the built environment today. But the search for the market, for business models and for ways to scale up successful projects continues. What stands in the way of bigger steps for the climate?
content.extendedDescription:
In this seminar, we put the spotlight on leadership issues together with the industry.

This seminar is part of the practice-oriented research school ASSURE, jointly organised by Uppsala universitet Campus Gotland, Lunds universitet, RISE and Malmö universitet.
content.subject: Construction
speakerTitles: Head of R&D, Associate Professor of Ethnology

content.title: When 5G becomes part of defence – industry's response to Europe's growing drone threat
content.description: Drones have rapidly become one of the greatest security threats to military and civilian infrastructure, while new network technology opens up entirely new defence capabilities.
content.extendedDescription: In Almedalen, Ericsson and Nordic Air Defence join Myndigheten för civilt försvar for a panel discussion on how Swedish 5G innovation, sensor technology and industrial cooperation strengthen total defence and Europe's security.
content.detail: Dagens industri's arena - the Talks stage
content.subject: Security/defence
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Head of Cybersecurity and Information Critical to Society

content.title: The local newspaper of the future?
content.description: Sweden has many local newspapers, and digital reader revenue increased by 24 percent in the first quarter of 2026. Digital advertising revenue also rose by 20 percent. In recent years, fewer but stronger local newspaper owners have enabled even small titles to continue publication.
content.extendedDescription: How is journalism affected by developments in the local newspaper market? What happens to local newsrooms? Investigative journalism? Media groups' cooperation on live sports television? What will the local newspaper of the future look like?
content.subject: Media/journalism
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Moderator, editor-in-chief and incoming Media Ombudsman

content.title: From revolution to independent school entrepreneurship, towards the AI society
content.description: The development of schools, the role of business in building society, public debate and the opportunities of AI – how can we strengthen quality, innovation and competitiveness in an age of rapid technological change?
content.extendedDescription: Drawing on his new book Välfärdsoligarkens bekännelser, Bijan Fahimi offers an entrepreneur's perspective on the development of schools, the role of business in building society, public debate and the opportunities of AI. A discussion about the future of education and Sweden's way forward.
content.subject: Education
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Expert on media and opinion formation

content.title: Digitalisation in schools – what do we actually know?
content.description: Discussion of digitalisation in schools is characterised by categorical claims, but what do we actually know?
content.extendedDescription:
The Swedish school debate on digitalisation is often characterised by strong positions and hasty conclusions. But what does the research actually say? What evidence is there about how digital tools and digital learning materials affect students' learning, teaching quality and schools' responsibility to compensate for unequal backgrounds?
In this discussion, Pernilla Nilsson, Secretary General at Vetenskapsrådet, explains what research actually shows about digitalisation in schools, and what it does not show.
The audience will be invited to join the dialogue.
content.subject: Education

content.title: Christian schools – the real picture
content.description: Several parties describe faith-based schools as a problem, but the debate is often shaped more by prejudice than facts. A new report shows that Christian schools achieve better results than municipal schools. Should this not encourage parties to support these schools instead of demanding a ban?
content.extendedDescription: Segregation, poor knowledge, inflated grades and weak shared values are some of the terms critics of independent schools tend to highlight. In this seminar, we discuss arguments and facts based on current debate and Claphaminstitutet's new report "Kristna skolor - den verkliga bilden".
content.subject: Education

content.title: West Sweden's industry as an engine for Swedish defence production
content.description: West Sweden is Sweden's strongest industrial hub. With a high concentration of basic and strategically important industries, it has the potential to strengthen Sweden's defence production – but this requires a clear national mandate and stable long-term rules.
content.extendedDescription: Welcome to a panel discussion focusing on how actors in West Sweden can enable a competitive and innovative business sector and strengthen Sweden's defence capability.
content.subject: Security/defence
speakerTitles: Chair of the Environment and Regional Development Committee
Chief of the Defence Staff / Lieutenant General

content.title: What should knowledge cost?
content.description: Students spend an average of SEK 730 a month on course literature and study materials. In most cases, this does not cover all the literature on their reading lists, and just over 90 percent of students think course literature is too expensive.
content.extendedDescription: Lower prices are by far the most important issue for students. 60 percent say that lower literature costs would make them less likely to download it illegally. According to students themselves, prices need to fall by between 25 and 50 percent. But is that possible? If not, how do we solve the funding issue?
content.subject: Education
speakerTitles: Strategic adviser and public affairs consultant

content.title: From initiatives to accelerated capability – how can the public sector build a lasting AI strategy?
content.description: Sweden now has a national AI strategy and an AI workshop under development. But research shows that the gap between what public-sector strategies promise and what organisations actually deliver is a phenomenon across sectors.
content.extendedDescription: Who actually owns capability development in a government agency or municipality? How do you move from pilots to sustained operations without losing legal certainty and trust? And what does genuine control over your AI mean when the infrastructure depends on external actors?
content.subject: Innovation

content.title: What role does the property industry play in total defence?
content.description: How prepared is the property industry for its role in total defence?
content.extendedDescription: Lunch special: How prepared is the property industry for its role in total defence? Preparedness and resilience are central issues in today's unsettled world. How does the industry/built environment sector view leadership, skills and responsibility for total defence? In this discussion, we explore the state of knowledge, current preparedness and what needs to happen, based on Byggcheferna's report launch.
content.subject: Other
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Head of Security and Defence Policy and Protective Security Officer

content.title: What does it take for offices to remain relevant as customers' needs change?
content.description: The office offering is becoming less about square metres and more about function, flexibility and experience. From the customer's perspective, how are new expectations reshaping the office market?
content.extendedDescription: The office offering is becoming less about square metres and more about function, flexibility and experience. Taking the customer's perspective as a starting point, we discuss how new expectations are reshaping the office market as tenants increasingly compare offices with the service levels and user experiences they encounter in other industries.
content.subject: Other
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: What should climate policy look like after the election?
content.description:
What will they do if they win the election? Sverigedemokraterna and Miljöpartiet discuss the way forward for climate policy after election day.

Which Tidö decisions does MP want to reverse first? What would the next step look like for SD?

Which parts of climate policy can Martin Kinnunen and Katarina Luhr actually agree on?
content.extendedDescription: Politikerfrukost is an interview series in which Altinget editors interview prominent politicians. Grab a coffee and take a seat in our courtyard for questions and answers with some of today's most topical politicians in environmental, education and defence policy.
content.subject: Climate/environment
content.accessibility: Event captioned, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Ukraine's ambassador on the war against journalists
content.description: Russia is waging war not only against Ukraine's armed forces – but also against free speech. Journalists are kidnapped, taken to Russian camps, tortured or killed. Newsrooms are bombed.
content.extendedDescription:
Former television journalist Svitjana Zalisjtjuk is Ukraine's ambassador to Sweden and is interviewed by Thomas Mattsson, who has visited Ukrainian media companies and media organisations during the war. What are working conditions like? Is there censorship? What does the ambassador think Swedish media companies can learn?

But Ukrainian Media Fund, founded in 2022 by organisations including Tidningsutgivarna and Bonnier News, provides financial support.
content.subject: Media/journalism
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Focus on the future – can we reverse the rising weight curve?
content.description: Obesity is one of our most important public health issues, surrounded by ignorance and stigma. More Swedes are living with obesity, with an increased risk of serious associated conditions. Children are also affected and risk long-term ill health. Decisive action is needed to halt this development. How can we reverse the curve?
content.extendedDescription: In the third discussion, we focus on the future for patients with obesity. Questions include: is obesity treatment also moving towards precision treatment? Which preventive measures make a real difference?
content.subject: Health and social care
speakerTitles: Second Vice-Chair of the Primary Care Committee
Specialist in internal medicine and Head of Operations

content.title: How does Islam's system of norms affect women and girls in a secular state governed by the rule of law?
content.description: Systems of norms and Swedish law. If a religious system of norms contains rules for family life, inheritance, divorce or social relationships, how should it relate to Swedish law?
content.extendedDescription:
Islam as a religion or something more? Many Swedes see Islam as a religion much like Christianity. Do you see Islam solely as a religion, or also as a system of norms that influences family life, relationships and everyday life?

The limits of religious freedom: freedom of religion protects people's right to believe and practise religion. Does it also protect religious systems of norms that affect how other people are expected to live?
content.subject: Democracy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Retail concepts that create value
content.description: Retail is constantly changing, but what actually creates value today, and how do retail, property and consumers interact?
content.extendedDescription: A report launch with HUI followed by two panel discussions on why retail is once again an attractive investment, which concepts create value and how close partnerships between property owners and tenants will be crucial for the retail destinations of the future.
content.subject: Business
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation

content.title: How can Sweden get the greatest value from AI responsibly and sustainably?
content.description: AI has the potential to become the biggest force for productivity and innovation since the internet – but value is not created by the technology itself, but by how quickly organisations turn it into real change.
content.extendedDescription:
How can Sweden move from experimentation to real value creation? What does it take for Swedish companies and the public sector to achieve measurable effects in the form of greater competitiveness, higher productivity and new business models? And who risks falling behind?

We discuss how Sweden can get the greatest possible value from AI – in practice.
content.subject: Digitalisation
speakerTitles: Global AI Lead, Sales and Strategy

content.title: Real democracy – the youth movement in an election year
content.description: What opportunities do young people have to organise? Which issues matter most to young people ahead of the election?
content.extendedDescription: The 2026 parliamentary election is approaching, and the question of young people's place in democracy is more urgent than ever. In this panel discussion, LSU brings together leading representatives of party-political youth organisations for a conversation spanning young people's political engagement, conditions for civil society and the resilience of democracy. What draws young people towards – or away from – politics? And what does the youth movement need to operate freely, safely and over the long term? The discussion is moderated by Sigge Eriksson, Chair of LSU – Sveriges barn- och ungdomsorganisationer.
content.subject: Children/young people

content.title: Choices facing adult and community education
content.description: What will happen to adult and community education after the September 2026 election? The Tidö parties have proposed removing all support for study associations during the next parliamentary term. Opposition parties have presented shadow budgets restoring state funding, though at different speeds.
content.extendedDescription: The seminar addresses the following questions: What choices will adult and community education face after this year's election? Will there be study associations in Sweden in 2030? What role can study associations play in society's future development? What values do we want adult and community education to embody? A substantial panel discusses these choices.
content.subject: Democracy

content.title: Benefits cut under new reform – how will children be affected?
content.description: Families with children living on the margins will be affected by reduced or withdrawn benefits under the new benefit reform. New rules risk negative effects on physical and mental health, inclusion, schooling and opportunities for meaningful leisure activities.
content.extendedDescription: The benefit reform particularly affects large families, single parents and older people without support networks. What are politicians thinking? Panel discussion.
content.subject: Children/young people
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Corps Officer / Head of Operations, moderator
Member of the Riksdag and Chair of the Committee on Social Insurance
Social policy spokesperson, Member of Parliament

content.title: Housing development with a human focus
content.description: Homes with aesthetic qualities always meet demand. When housing also encourages encounters between neighbours, both security and shared responsibility are strengthened.
content.extendedDescription: Homes with aesthetic qualities always meet demand. Another dimension that enhances housing quality is when it encourages contact with neighbours and others nearby. This fosters security and shared responsibility for the surroundings. Here, housing developers describe their strategies for creating comfort and security for customers.
content.subject: Other
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Municipal Commissioner and Chair of the Environment and Urban Planning Committee
Director of the Urban Planning Department

content.title: Developing Västerbotten by leading the transition: change happens together
content.description: “Together in change” means placing even greater emphasis on collaboration, bringing together north, south, urban and rural areas, and involving more people in this major transformation. Because we are not just transforming technology – we are transforming society.
content.extendedDescription: Västerbotten is a leader in the transition. For almost a decade, northern Sweden has been a European centre for a societal transformation in which we move beyond fossil-fuel thinking to build a more sustainable, resilient and balanced society. This transformation is a major and complex challenge that we can only address together. By bringing together businesses, associations, organisations, public bodies and individuals, we can solve problems and seize all the opportunities available.
content.subject: Regional issues
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: The media and power: public service broadcasting in the firing line
content.description: The debate about public service broadcasting has intensified as media habits change and competition for audiences' attention increases.
content.extendedDescription:
Its remit, funding and role are also being debated at a time when global platforms and commercial media compete for the same audiences. What role should public service broadcasting play in the media landscape of the future? How can demands for independent journalism be balanced against criticism concerning competition, impartiality and reach? A discussion about changing audience behaviour, competition for advertising revenue and the struggle for attention.
In a series of interviews, Dagens Media and Resumé question leading figures in media, advertising, PR and communications.
content.subject: Media/journalism
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: How do aviation and space strengthen the security, accessibility and competitiveness of Sweden and Europe?
content.description: The aerospace industry is crucial to the competitiveness and security of Sweden and Europe. For Sweden, this means ensuring accessible air transport throughout the country and harnessing the opportunities of space. How do we develop a robust system, drive innovation and learn from international cooperation?
content.extendedDescription: Aerospace Almedalen is the arena for aviation and space. It offers a day filled with seminars, conversations and debate on aviation and space, drawing on current societal issues such as security and total defence, NATO, air defence and protecting our airspace, the growing importance of space for society, the climate transition, competitiveness and conditions for our businesses. You will meet representatives of the government and parliament, Swedish public authorities, space companies, airports and industry organisations.
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: How have hidden money, lobbying and right-wing networks changed Sweden?
content.description: Has Sweden become a banana republic? Why do state-owned companies pay for Svenskt Näringsliv's opinion-forming activities? What do the networks connecting the political and economic elites really look like?
content.extendedDescription:
In a series of reports, Emma Fastesson Lindgren has examined right-wing networks and the money behind them. Johannes Klenell is a journalist and author of the widely discussed book Bananrepubliken Sverige, in which he describes the corruption and lobbying that characterise Sweden today.

Together with Johan Sjölander, head of Tankesmedjan Tiden, they discuss how money flows, lobbying and informal networks influence Swedish politics and democracy.

Participants
- Johannes Klenell, journalist and author
- Emma Fastesson Lindgren, researcher and writer
- Johan Sjölander, head of Tankesmedjan Tiden
content.subject: Democracy

content.title: How can research without animal testing lead to better results for humans?
content.description: Why are animals used in research? Why does animal-free research lead to better results for humans? What methods can replace animal testing? Why should animal testing be replaced? What is an organoid?
content.extendedDescription:
During this open house, you can drop in and meet the people working in our organisation, ask questions and talk to previous grant recipients. Interested researchers can also learn more about opportunities to apply for our research grants.

We also welcome members of the public to stop by and learn more about how to contribute to a future without animal testing. You can find out why animal-free methods can often be better than traditional methods based on animal testing, and what is actually tested on animals in research today.
content.subject: Research

content.title: How to spot the signals in Almedalen that point to our shared future
content.description: Global challenges are substantial and societal development is accelerating. What signals can we see here in Almedalen, and what possible clues to our future can they offer?
content.extendedDescription: Foresight is an approach that gives us the power to help shape the future, rather than simply letting it happen. It is not about predicting the future – nobody can do that! It is about using the signals we see and the knowledge we have today to work with future scenarios. These can help us make better-informed decisions. How can you prepare to notice and interpret the signals Almedalsveckan gives us about the future?
content.subject: Innovation
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: New building regulations – how do they affect renovation and new construction? Opportunity or obstacle?
content.description: The new building regulations are described as regulations of opportunity and have opened the door to new solutions, particularly for indoor climate. How can we approach ventilation and heating?
content.extendedDescription: In Sweden, we have moved from a fairly prescriptive regulatory framework, SBN, towards increasingly open, performance-based rules. The new building regulations, described as regulations of opportunity, set few requirements for how things are done and more requirements for performance. This requires designers to demonstrate how these performance requirements are met, but also creates significant opportunities for new sustainable solutions or for retaining well-functioning solutions in existing buildings. We show the differences in the rules and how to think in new ways.
content.subject: Construction
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
content.detail: Tent by the guest harbour near the Strandgatan — Kaserngatan junction

content.title: What determines whether Swedes donate, sell or throw things away – how do they view second-hand goods?
content.description: Many Swedes want to buy and donate second-hand goods. At the same time, systems and regulations for collecting, sorting and reusing textiles are changing. What determines whether clothes get a new life, and how can regulations help more items be reused?
content.extendedDescription: Second-hand goods and reuse play an important role in the transition to a more circular economy. For textile collection and handling systems to work, the entire value chain must connect – from donation and collection to sorting, reuse and recycling. Giva Sverige presents a survey of Swedes' attitudes and behaviour towards second-hand goods and giving. What determines whether people choose to donate, sell or throw things away? What motivations and barriers are there?
content.subject: Climate/environment

content.title: Markets or politics – what determines whether the transport sector can meet its 2030 goals?
content.description: How is the mobility of the future developing – and what solutions are needed to create a more sustainable and accessible transport system?
content.extendedDescription:
During Almedalsveckan, Mobilitetspodden is recorded live from the arena at Hästgatan 12. Through short conversations with politicians, researchers, businesses and other actors in society, the podcast captures current perspectives on mobility, transport and spatial planning.

The conversations draw on issues discussed during the week and events at the arena. The focus is on how mobility affects societal development, climate targets, urban and rural development and people's everyday journeys.

The public is welcome to listen on site. The recordings will later be published in Mobilitetspodden.
content.subject: Sustainability
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: The surveillance society – safety or control?
content.description: Camera surveillance, data retention and digital tracking are growing rapidly. Where is the line between security and privacy?
content.extendedDescription:
Digital technology makes it possible to collect, store and analyse information about people on a scale previously difficult to imagine. At the same time, surveillance is often justified by the need for safety, crime prevention and national security. Where is the line between necessary security measures and the right to personal privacy?

During this session, a podcast discussion will be recorded on site, exploring these issues from different perspectives. The discussion examines the balance between freedom, privacy and security, and the consequences technological development may have for individuals, democracy and an open society.
content.subject: Freedom of expression

content.title: The awakened left – does it exist in Sweden?
content.description: More and more voters feel politically homeless. Could a new political movement emerge around peace, freedom and social justice?
content.extendedDescription:
Many feel that today's political landscape no longer reflects their values or addresses the challenges facing society. The closing session therefore includes a podcast recording and a discussion of democracy, citizen influence and the possibility of developing new political directions based on participation, social solidarity and hope for the future.
To round off Almedalsveckan, party leader Gustaf Rydelius and deputy party leader Andreas Sidkvist take part in a reflective conversation about current societal issues and the future of democracy. Drawing on ideas and values often associated with Olof Palme's commitment to society, the discussion touches on peace, freedom, democracy and social justice.
content.subject: Democracy

content.title: How the fight for Ojnareskogen became front-page news
content.description: What can we in Sápmi learn from the long struggle to protect Ojnareskogen and Lake Bästeträsk from industrial exploitation, and what can the special “Ojnare spirit” that developed during the process tell us about the power of civil society?
content.extendedDescription: The road towards the first national park on Gotland's main island has been long. Since Nordkalk applied to quarry limestone near Lake Bästeträsk more than 20 years ago, the struggle has involved legal proceedings, protests and strong local commitment. The planned Bästeträsk national park was due to open this summer, but parliament's decision has been delayed. Sofia Bothorp from Urbergsgruppen describes the battle for Ojnareskogen and the work behind the forthcoming national park.
content.subject: Human rights

content.title: What does the government want for adult education?
content.description: The government is announcing the biggest education reforms in many years. But what changes and developments does it envisage for adult education? And what are its plans if it remains in government?
content.extendedDescription: Is adult education also included in the current government's reform plan? An inquiry is currently examining parts of municipal adult education criticised by Skolinspektionen, but does the government merely want to correct minor shortcomings, or does it have a broader, longer-term plan for developing adult education? VIS talks to State Secretary Adam Alfredsson about the government's plans for adult education.
speakerTitles: State Secretary to the Minister for Education
content.subject: Education
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Almedalen's slowest place – where we take things easy
content.description: Sweden is heading into an election at a time of profound change. Quick fixes and short-term initiatives are not enough. Strengthening growth, tackling unemployment and securing welfare funding require reflection, knowledge and the ability to make decisions that are sustainable in the long term.
content.extendedDescription:
Saco's tent in Folkhälsodalen is a meeting place for reflection and calm conversation. We want to make room for thoughtful, respectful discussion and let everyone finish speaking. We call it Slow Politics. Saco advocates a more balanced political conversation and political reforms grounded in facts and knowledge.

Take a seat and join a conversation that offers new perspectives and challenges your thinking. Perhaps you will talk to someone you would not otherwise speak to? We believe in active listening, daring to reconsider and reaching across divides. Welcome!
content.subject: Democracy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
content.detail: Folkhälsodalen, S:t Hans and S:t Per church ruins

content.title: A safe, clean and thriving marine environment – now and for the future
content.description: The security situation has remained uncertain and challenging recently, with a complex range of threats and risks at sea. Constant preparedness is therefore needed to handle disruptions in the world around us that risk affecting society in various ways.
content.extendedDescription:
Kustbevakningen is Sweden's civilian maritime hub. We protect lives and the environment, combat crime and strengthen society's preparedness and total defence.

During Almedalsveckan, one of Kustbevakningen's largest vessels, KBV 002 Triton, will be in Visby harbour. Meet the crew and learn more about Kustbevakningen's unique capabilities and equipment.

If you are interested in working at Kustbevakningen, take the opportunity to speak with our recruitment partners, who will also be there.

Welcome aboard!

content.title: How does exercise build strong communities?
content.description: Everyone agrees that exercise is good for you. But the true extent of its benefit to society is discussed far too rarely.
content.extendedDescription:
On Tuesday, Friskis presents a new report focusing on exercise, societal costs and interpersonal trust. Join us for follow-up discussion and analysis during a morning jog.

We meet at Friskis Pop up, begin with a summary of the Friskis report and then jog or run together for about 20 minutes. Choose a gentler or slightly faster pace. Friskis running coach Andreas Dahlqvist will be there to guide you alongside Freja Andersdotter from Svensk Friidrott. Afterwards, we refuel.
content.subject: Economy

content.title: The household finances meeting – how does the Minister for Financial Markets view the economy and household finances?
content.description: Recent years have been challenging for Swedish households. The parliamentary term began with high inflation and has since been marked by an increasingly unsettled world. The Tidö parties have taken a range of measures to strengthen household finances and purchasing power and try to kick-start Swedish growth.
content.extendedDescription: But are these measures enough? And what awaits households after the election in September? SEB's personal finance economist Américo Fernández talks to Minister for Financial Markets Niklas Wykman about the outlook for the Swedish economy, how government policy during the past parliamentary term has affected households, and what the future holds given developments around the world.
content.subject: Economy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Older but not old
content.description: More than 2 million Swedes have reached what we call retirement age. They are individuals with very different lives, motivations and dreams, yet they are often portrayed stereotypically and as passive members of society. Why?
content.extendedDescription:
In Sweden, more than two million people have reached what we call retirement age. They are often depicted stereotypically and portrayed as passive members of society.

Photographer Evelina Carborn wants to help change that image with the exhibition Äldre men inte gammal. It portrays people with very different lives, motivations and dreams. Many may be older, but they are far from old – and share the view that the general image of “older people” is simplistic and outdated.

The exhibition can be seen throughout Almedalsveckan on Donnersgatan, halfway between Almedalsparken and Almedalsbiblioteket. Guided tours are also offered on Wednesday and Thursday.
content.subject: Older people

content.description: More than 2 million Swedes have reached what we call retirement age. They are individuals with very different lives, motivations and dreams, yet they are often portrayed stereotypically and as passive members of society. Why?
content.extendedDescription:
In Sweden, more than two million people have reached what we call retirement age. They are often depicted stereotypically and portrayed as passive members of society.

Photographer Evelina Carborn wants to help change that image with the exhibition Äldre men inte gammal. It portrays people with very different lives, motivations and dreams. Many may be older, but they are far from old – and share the view that the general image of “older people” is simplistic and outdated.

The exhibition can be seen throughout Almedalsveckan on Donnersgatan, halfway between Almedalsparken and Almedalsbiblioteket. Guided tours are also offered on Wednesday and Thursday.

content.title: One in five households has a boat – time for a Minister for Boating?
content.description: One in five households has a boat, and what people appreciate about boating is experiencing nature, companionship and adventure. Boating should be simple, vibrant and accessible to everyone – but too many ministries and authorities are involved, and one hand does not know what the other is doing. Time for a boating coordinator.
content.extendedDescription:
Båtliv Sverige is an informal and exceptionally strong collaboration between Sweboat, Svenska Båtunionen, Svenska Kryssarklubben, Svenska Seglarförbundet and Riksföreningen Gästhamnar Sverige.
Our vision is for boating to be simple, vibrant and accessible to everyone. Welcome to Båtlivsarenan (223) in Gästhamnen on Tuesday and Wednesday. At 14:00 on Wednesday, we host a panel discussion with members of parliament from most parties. How do our elected decision-makers view boating, and how do they want to make it easier so that more people can get out on the water?
content.subject: Visitor economy

content.title: Mälardalen – one of Europe's most dynamic industrial regions, but what comes next?
content.description: Stockholm-Mälardalen is Sweden's largest labour market, accounts for half the country's GDP and is home to several global multibillion corporations, including some of Sweden's largest companies. But what needs to develop? What will it take for the region to remain an engine of the country's transition?
content.extendedDescription:
Welcome to Mälardalsarenan, where we join business, politics and academia to discuss three critical issues for today and tomorrow that are vital to Sweden's future competitiveness.

14.00 - 14:45
World-class automation and electrification – but what is needed at national level to achieve the targets?

15.00 - 15.45
How can Mälardalen and Sweden win the battle for talent?

16:00 - 16:45
The Stockholm-Mälar region in the national plan – major benefits but implementation challenges
content.subject: Regional issues
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation

content.title: Leadership for working life in times of great uncertainty and rapid change
content.description: Working life is shaped by rapid change, AI, geopolitical shifts and economic pressure. When direction, focus and collaboration falter, organisations lose momentum. The question is how leaders can create clarity, trust and the ability to act without having all the answers.
content.extendedDescription:
The event takes the form of a guided breakfast walk from 08.00-08.50. We meet at Strandvägen 1, Kallis, where Siri Wikander from Beyond Talking welcomes participants, briefly introduces the survey and frames the discussion.

During the walk, we explore two questions: what leadership is needed when uncertainty and the pace of change are high, and how organisations can develop that capability in practice.

The walk ends where we started, with a short summary. The content is based on Beyond Talking's survey “Ledarskapsinsikter inför 2026”.
