content.title: How can we build a green and fair society?
content.description: How can we achieve a fair climate transition, thriving nature and ecosystems, and a free and democratic society?
content.extendedDescription: Miljöpartiet thinks bigger about the future – everything is connected. We are part of the global movement working to enable everyone to live good lives within the planet's limits and in a way that preserves opportunities for future generations. Our green ideology takes a holistic approach rooted in solidarity with all people, other species and ecosystems. It recognises the great value of thinking bigger together, for a future that is fair, free and sustainable.

content.title: Profitability is determined before the first ground is broken
content.description: The decisions with the greatest impact on a property's profitability and long-term value are often made before construction begins. Yet many projects focus on construction costs, while fewer focus on decisions affecting the property's operation, flexibility and development potential.
content.extendedDescription:
Building services and energy affect a property throughout its lifetime. They influence how the building is used, managed, adapted and developed.

At Hamnplan 222, we are displaying EkoNod's demonstration module. It offers a practical insight into how building services and energy can be viewed as a system, and how that perspective can influence a project's development.

Visit the module and discuss how earlier decisions can contribute to more profitable properties, lower project risk, greater flexibility over time and higher long-term property value.
content.subject: Energy

content.description: What has Almedalen 2026 been like? What observations and trends can we identify, and how does the week contribute to societal development in general and to solving the property market's challenges in particular?
content.extendedDescription: Svefa's courtyard at Adelsgatan 25 is a natural meeting place where public and private actors can meet, exchange ideas, share knowledge, discuss property-related issues and build relationships in both informal and formal settings. This year we are collaborating with Fråga Lou and have created Fastighetshubben, offering a packed programme addressing important issues at the intersection of public and private actors in the property market. content.title: The Refugee Convention at 75 – celebrating the world's greatest lifesaver against the odds
content.description: When the Refugee Convention was adopted after the Second World War, the world's countries agreed that people fleeing for their lives have a right to protection. For 75 years, the Convention has saved millions of lives. What does the Refugee Convention mean today – and how do we defend the right to protection in an increasingly uncertain world?
content.extendedDescription:
This year, the world's greatest lifesaver turns 75. It was born in the shadow of the Second World War, when Europe was badly scarred. In a time of darkness and despair, world leaders gathered to answer a crucial question: how do we ensure that people forced to flee for their lives are not left without protection? The answer was the UN Refugee Convention, one of the most central agreements in international law. Since that day, the Refugee Convention has saved millions of lives around the world.
Join us in celebrating the world's best 75-year-old!
content.subject: Human rights

content.title: When shopping moves to China – what happens to Sweden?
content.description: More and more people are buying from global low-price platforms whose prices are pushed far below what Swedish retailers can match. content.extendedDescription:
Questions:
* Can Swedish retailers survive competition from global low-price platforms?
* Should politicians regulate or tax international e-commerce giants more heavily?
* What does this development mean for Swedish jobs, town centres and tax revenues?
* Do consumers have a responsibility, or will price always win?

content.title: The return of the Monroe Doctrine: Latin America's strategic choices?
content.description: Trump's security strategy represents a major return to the Monroe Doctrine, with the US asserting its right to dominate the Western Hemisphere politically, economically and militarily. How can Latin America avoid open confrontation with the US?
content.extendedDescription: Trump's security strategy marks a clear return to the Monroe Doctrine, now in the form of the so-called “Trump Corollary”, with the US asserting its right to dominate the entire Western Hemisphere politically, economically and militarily. The strategy entails increased military presence, control over strategic resources, measures against migration and an ambition to keep the region free of outside powers such as China. This is reinforced by concrete measures such as interventions in the Caribbean, blockades and threats of economic sanctions against countries that do not follow Washington's line. What can Latin America do to avoid open confrontation with the US?
content.subject: International affairs

content.title: From guidelines to reality – how do we ensure that menopause care improves?
content.description: Socialstyrelsen has produced new national guidelines for treating menopausal symptoms. This is an important and welcome step. But guidelines alone do not change healthcare: political will, clear responsibilities and follow-up are needed.
content.extendedDescription:
Today, women receive different care depending on where in the country they live. Knowledge levels vary, structures are lacking, and many patients feel they are not properly assessed or offered evidence-based treatment. The new guidelines clarify what should be done – but how do we ensure that it actually happens? What is required of regional political leaders? How can primary care be given the right conditions?
How are the guidelines followed up, and who is accountable if they are not implemented?
Welcome to a discussion about the next step towards equitable, evidence-based menopause care for women throughout the country.
content.subject: Health and social care

content.title: Election year at last – how is Swedish politics doing?
content.description: How is the Tidö cooperation going, and will Magdalena Andersson manage to assemble any team at all? Which ministerial posts will Åkesson get? Will the election be about the economy and integration, or perhaps Donald Trump?
content.extendedDescription:
Where others mostly skim the headlines, Svenska Dagbladet's podcast “Politiken” pauses to explore in depth. Today's headlines are linked to the longer sweep of history. Svenska Dagbladet's political stars Maggie Strömberg, Torbjörn Nilsson and Henrik Torehammar present a live podcast tackling Almedalsveckan and picking up the latest from the speakers' stage.
We offer a light lunch to the first 75 arrivals.

content.title: The future of the principle of public access to official documents – alive or dead?
content.description: Sweden's principle of public access to official documents is now more than 250 years old. It is unique and laid the foundation for a Scandinavian democratic tradition. Today it is affected not only by Sweden's EU membership but also by special interests that want to restrict it for various reasons.
content.extendedDescription:
The event begins with a brief introduction and a closer examination of the problem: the forces influencing Anders Chyttenius's democratic reform of 1766 in different ways, and how they have manifested themselves from the 1930s onwards. The focus is on how the EU has come to affect citizens' previous rights to information, journalists' rights to obtain information and protections for those who disclose information to the media.

The seminar takes the form of a discussion with representatives of the youth wings of the three largest parties: MUF, SSU and Ungsvenskarna.
content.subject: Democracy

content.title: Can a CEO vibe-code a business management system?
content.description: Agentic coding enables more people to build more, faster. But it does not automatically make solutions secure, maintainable or legal. The cost of code is falling. The cost of responsibility is not.
content.extendedDescription:
We explain how we moved from experimentation to verified resilience – and why the answer to almost every AI question in the public sector starts with sovereignty, information management and control over one's own data.

Digitalist has worked on AI deliveries for Socialstyrelsen, Adda, Linköpings kommun and Digg. In parallel, we have tested the limits internally: our CEO has vibe-coded an application that is actually in production. This forced us to build processes for reviewing AI-generated code, subagents that review other agents, hardened containers with SBOMs, and an evidence trail that stands up to audit.
content.subject: Digitalisation

content.title: Socioeconomic benefits of dynamic architecture?
content.description: How can more flexible buildings create greater public benefit when needs change faster than the built environment?
content.extendedDescription: How can more flexible buildings create greater public benefit when needs change faster than the built environment? Demographics, activities and the functions of places shift over time, while traditional construction often ties up both capital and land for long periods. In this discussion, we explore whether more adaptable buildings/dynamic architecture can become a tool for better resource use and lower risk, and what socioeconomic benefits can arise when premises can be adapted and relocated over time.
content.subject: Other

content.title: Accelerate preparedness efforts – with secure data communications and a reliable electricity supply
content.description: How do we create a real plan B for data communications and electricity supply? Municipalities, authorities and businesses depend on digital infrastructure. How can preparedness be strengthened through continuity planning, backup power and the right skills?
content.extendedDescription: How do we create a real plan B for data communications and electricity supply? Municipalities, authorities and businesses are now entirely dependent on digital infrastructure, making vulnerability to outages, attacks and power shortages a critical issue. It is time to step up preparedness efforts – from continuity planning to backup power and the skills needed to secure robust infrastructure.

content.title: Why a Swedish language model is needed
content.description: Global tech giants create business models and language models based on content produced by Swedish journalists, authors and playwrights. This scraping undermines the ability of newspapers, magazines, book publishers and others to fund their content and compensate creators.
content.extendedDescription: Project SE.LLMA brings together Tidningsutgivarna, Sveriges Tidskrifter, Svenska Förläggareföreningen and Sveriges Författarförbund, among others. Its purpose is to contribute to a Swedish language model and develop a licensing model that respects copyright holders' rights.

content.description: There are only three months until the election, and the news media are also busy covering energy crises, the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East and, of course, the football World Cup. How are journalists fulfilling their remit? And how have the media influenced Almedalsveckan this year?

Which media stages looked best, and where were the best media networking events? Here, media executives sum up the political week.

content.title: How does Uppdrag Granskning work behind the scenes?
content.description: Investigative journalism – uncovering what would otherwise remain hidden – is essential to a well-functioning democracy. But persuading authorities, businesses, organisations and individuals to agree to an interview is becoming increasingly difficult. What methods does the editorial team use?
content.extendedDescription: What can a spokesperson do when Uppdrag Granskning knocks on the door? How does Uppdrag Granskning work behind the scenes? For 25 years, Uppdrag Granskning has exposed wrongdoing and abuses of power – and demanded accountability. Many of its reports over the years have had major consequences for society and led to changes in procedures and laws.

content.title: Everyone wants to build communities; fewer talk about who will keep them alive
content.description: What makes a community work? Why do some networks become powerful while others are just meetings?
content.extendedDescription:
Some communities create real value. Others never become more than a meeting.
But project results can become living resources. That does not happen by itself.

Welcome to a fireside conversation about trust, shared resources and the often invisible art of keeping people contributing. Many good partnerships and effective collaborations die when a project ends. What can we do about that? How do we build something that lives on?

We will discuss what it takes to build communities, shared knowledge and innovation environments that actually endure.
content.subject: Innovation

content.title: One Cosmic, nine experiences – what influenced outcomes in the Sussa regions?
content.description: The Sussa regions have introduced the same patient record system, but experiences of the results vary. Why is that?
content.extendedDescription:
In this seminar, we discuss the factors that determine outcomes – from leadership, staff involvement and implementation to working practices and local conditions. Regional representatives share experiences, obstacles and success factors, focusing on lessons for future digitalisation initiatives.

With a focus on lessons for future joint initiatives, the panel shares practical insights into what has worked well, the obstacles encountered and the compromises needed between shared and regional approaches. How is value created through collaboration between nine regions? Which common principles need to endure over time – and where should there be room for regional adaptation?
content.subject: Digitalisation

content.title: New production methods and value chains for using unconventional timber in construction
content.description: Today, hardwood accounts for 20 % of our timber production. Almost all of it goes into paper production. New craft-based production methods allow more unusual wood species to be used in construction.
content.extendedDescription:
We are building more and more with wood, with major climate benefits. To support biodiversity in our forests and make use of more wood species, we need new production technologies that are more craft-based. We also need new certification of hardwood as structural timber.
We demonstrate methods that make it possible to maintain mixed forests and use all the wood species available for purposes other than paper production.
content.subject: Construction

content.title: What is a garden city – and why is it returning to urban planning?
content.description: The garden city is presented as a model for small-scale development, greenery and urban qualities. At the same time, it raises questions about density, costs, climate and segregation.
content.extendedDescription:
The seminar discusses what a garden city actually is, the historical ideas that shaped this urban model and how it is used in planning today. The discussion includes Swedish examples such as Gamla Enskede, Landala and new projects such as Tullingeträdgårdsstad and Tyresö strandtorg.
Can the garden city combine urban density with the qualities of nature? Is it a model for sustainable urban development in the future – an alternative to the consistently high investment and operating costs of detached housing areas?
speakerTitles: CEO and PhD in Urban Planning

content.title: What is quantum, really – and why is everyone talking about it?
content.description: Quantum physics describes how the universe's smallest building blocks work. Ordinary physical laws are not enough there, and probabilities govern. But what does that mean in practice – and how does it differ from classical physics?
content.extendedDescription:
Join a journey into a world where reality behaves differently from what we are used to, and where the technology of the future is taking shape.

In this conversation, we explore what quantum is and how it is applied today. We also discuss how we know quantum works, why quantum technology could be crucial to the future, and whether you can really be in two places at once.

Welcome to a conversation with quantum professor Peter Samuelsson, who works in Lunds universitet's Nobel Prize-winning research environment.

content.title: My voice counts – what issues matter most to young people before the election?
content.description: Young people's voices, stories and perspectives are heavily underrepresented in public debate. People under 25 are mentioned in only 11 % of all news stories and account for just 6 % of everyone given a voice in them, even though they make up around 30 % of Sweden's population.
content.extendedDescription: Welcome to a creative and inclusive meeting between young people, politicians and civil society, following Fanzingo's “Reversed Townhall - powered by young peoples stories” model. Young people and their stories and perspectives take centre stage, and we aim to give them 80 % of the speaking time. In the remaining time, representatives of politics and civil society reflect on what the young people have shared and how they can use these insights and perspectives in their everyday work.

content.title: Parkinson's disease – the right treatment at the right time and the importance of physical activity
content.description: Parkinson's disease affects increasing numbers of people. In addition to medication, staying physically active is important. It is a central part of treatment for maintaining functions and training balance and reaction skills.
content.extendedDescription: We will provide information about Parkinson's disease and the importance of receiving the right treatment at the right time, with the right support over time. Together with the Arvsfonden-funded Pingis Parkinson project and Parkinson Gotland, we will offer politicians and the public information about how physical activity should be regarded as part of treatment. You can also try playing table tennis with us. We will present several proposals that can contribute to better public health, better care and treatment, greater knowledge in elderly care, and the application of sickness insurance, rules for sickness compensation and opportunities to participate in associations despite having a chronic illness.

content.title: How can AI and technological innovation stop organised crime?
content.description: Organised crime is infiltrating more and more sectors of society. At the same time, Sweden is a world leader in technological innovation, and AI is creating new opportunities to tackle welfare fraud, scams and financial crime. How can AI and technological development help reduce crime?
content.extendedDescription: What political action is needed, and how can different sectors work together to stop organised crime?

content.title: China, Norrbotten and Europe

Norrbotten, for example, has substantial deposits of the rare earth elements that the EU currently imports from China.
content.extendedDescription:
Welcome to a conversation about China, Sweden, the EU and Norrbotten!

Can we learn anything from China in our ongoing industrial transition, or should we focus solely on EU independence?

content.title: Crash or consensus? The Solna of the future as a hub in the capital region
content.description: Between Stockholm and Arlanda lies Solna, one of Sweden's most strategically important urban development areas. What could it look like if we planned around the region's full potential?
content.extendedDescription:
During Almedalsveckan, a shared vision for Solna's future will be presented for the first time, showing how it can develop with new urban environments, stronger connections and improved access to Arlanda and the capital region.

Moderator Mats Rönnbo, Head of Strategic Business Development and Partnerships, Skanska.

content.title: Market rents: whose security is at stake?
content.description: Ahead of the election, market rents are more topical than they have been for a long time. The issue affects people's everyday lives and living conditions.
content.extendedDescription:
In a political debate, the parliamentary parties meet to discuss how market rents would affect tenants and society. The discussion starts from Hyresgästföreningen's report on market rents.

Follow-up discussion:

Marie Linder comments on the debate and puts the issue in a broader perspective: what is at stake for Sweden's tenants? Drawing on Hyresgästföreningen's market rent report and the political debate we have heard.
content.subject: Construction

content.title: Four years to a binding climate target – how do the parties plan to cut emissions in time?
content.description: By 2030, Sweden's emissions need to fall sharply to meet climate targets at both national and EU level. Despite this, emissions have risen during the current parliamentary term. All parties support the targets, but achieving them will require a much faster pace of climate policy during the next term.
content.extendedDescription: All Swedish parliamentary parties support the climate targets, but what policies do they propose to achieve them? Naturskyddsföreningen invites you to take a closer look at the parties' proposals through a questioning session with all parties.
content.subject: Climate/environment
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Education in uncertain times
content.description: Education is a fundamental right – even when a crisis strikes. How do we ensure every student's right to learning in uncertain times, and what lessons can we draw already today?
content.extendedDescription: Sveriges Elevkårer brings together students, decision-makers and experts to discuss what happens to schools when circumstances suddenly change. Drawing on past experiences in Sweden and internationally, we explore how Sweden can safeguard students' right to education in a changed security environment and what genuine educational preparedness requires.
content.subject: Education
speakerTitles: Timbro Fellow and Former CEO of Viktor Rydberg skolor
Chair of the Parliamentary Committee on Education

content.title: What is happening with the Defence Commission's funding?
content.description: The Defence Commission is to decide how the 300 billion for defence will be allocated – how is it going? And should the Defence Commission even exist?
content.extendedDescription: This autumn, the Defence Commission is due to agree on how the 300 billion for defence will be allocated – how are negotiations progressing? What does the panel think of the first interim report, with its new security policy analysis? And should the parties argue more openly about defence policy?
content.subject: Security/defence

content.title: A long-term approach as the key to urban development
content.description: An attractive city offers a varied range of services, shops and culture. Safety and sustainability are increasingly sought-after qualities. Success requires a long-term perspective on urban development.
content.extendedDescription: An attractive city offers a varied range of services, shops and culture. Safety and sustainability are other increasingly sought-after qualities. Getting the whole picture right requires a long-term approach to the urban development process. In this conversation, we discuss how to develop cities with long-term responsibility.
content.subject: Construction

content.title: A visionary cultural policy for a new era
content.description:
Sweden adopted its first comprehensive cultural policy in 1974. It was shaped in a different era, with different social challenges and opportunities.
Now a new cultural policy is needed – as a central part of building society, rather than a special interest.
content.extendedDescription: A conversation about how Sweden can become a nation of culture: a society in which culture permeates the entire country and all policy areas, and art and culture are a natural part of everyday life, democracy and building the future. In Kulturriket Sverige, creativity, learning and stories strengthen people's ability to understand themselves and the world.
content.subject: Culture

content.title: From cost savings to more healthy years – vaccination as a long-term investment in society
content.description: The issue of a national vaccination programme for older people has received increasing attention as more people highlight the need for stronger preventive efforts in an ageing society.
content.extendedDescription: Following two earlier seminars focusing on loneliness and health economics, the conversation about a national vaccination programme for older people continues in Almedalen – now with little time left before the 2026 election.
content.subject: Health and social care
speakerTitles: Minister for Older People and Social Security
Chair of the Regional Executive Board in Region Östergötland and Vice Chair of SKR's Healthcare Delegation

content.title: What economic future awaits today's young people after this autumn's parliamentary election?
content.description: More first-time voters will go to the polls in this autumn's parliamentary election than in the previous election. At the same time, one in three voters is expected to be over 65, and older people's votes carry increasing demographic weight. How do we ensure young people's voices are heard? And what are their most important issues ahead of the election?
content.extendedDescription: Welcome to a discussion with the political youth organisations in SEB's garden about their views on the September election, the most important political and economic issues for young people today, and their proposals for meeting young people's needs.
content.subject: Economy

content.title: More babies wanted – but how?
content.description: Birth rates in Sweden, Europe and elsewhere have fallen dramatically. The government has produced an inquiry on childbearing and families. But research shows that more factors may be decisive.
content.extendedDescription: The world appears to be heading towards a possible population crisis, and Sweden is expected soon to enter natural population decline as those born in the 1940s pass 80 and the number of births keeps falling. Are the analysis and proposals in the government's inquiry sufficient, or are further measures and a change in outlook across society needed to reverse this trend, including in Europe and Sweden?
content.subject: Children/young people
speakerTitles: Family and gender equality policy spokesperson

content.title: How do we prepare the electricity supply for war?
content.description: A secure electricity supply is essential to the functioning of society and therefore plays an important role in Sweden's crisis preparedness and total defence.
content.extendedDescription:
How far have we come in this work, what is in place, and what remains to ensure the entire electricity supply can withstand the pressures of war?
Svenska kraftnät invites societal stakeholders and electricity supply representatives to discuss the preparedness challenges facing the electricity supply and initiatives to make it more robust and better prepared.
content.subject: Energy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: How do we meet growing rail travel demand? Infrastructure and urban development for Sweden's growth
content.description: Rail travel continues to increase, placing new demands on both the country's infrastructure and our cities. As more people choose rail, a holistic approach is needed in which railway capacity and modern urban development go hand in hand to secure Swedish growth.
content.extendedDescription: Jernhusen invites you to a conversation about how we can jointly create long-term solutions and urban development near stations that meet future needs. How do we find new, innovative ways forward that benefit both people and the economy while avoiding new bottlenecks?
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Are small independent schools endangered – or is there a political way back?
content.description: Small independent schools and preschools are finding it increasingly difficult to manage growing administrative, financial and regulatory requirements, risking an increasingly consolidated education sector.
content.extendedDescription: Many smaller organisations are run by entrepreneurs, nonprofit initiatives and committed school leaders with strong roots in their local communities. What do stricter requirements mean for freedom of choice, diversity and local engagement if smaller providers find it harder to operate?
content.subject: Education
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Between headlines and reality – what research on young women's mental health shows
content.description: How should we understand young women's mental ill health, and what needs to happen to strengthen their living conditions and equal rights? What do we know about their situation that can help us help them?
content.extendedDescription: Political representatives and experts discuss how young women's mental ill health should be understood and what needs to happen to strengthen their living conditions and equal rights. We also present a new research review from Mind and the two research networks WOMHER and UPIC.

speakerTitles: Member of Parliament, social policy spokesperson and vice chair of the Parliamentary Committee on Health and Welfare

content.title: Stopping unscrupulous operators in public procurement
content.description: Public procurement is an important strategic policy tool that affects working conditions, competition and climate impact. Procurement improves when trade unions are involved early in the process.
content.extendedDescription:
The seminar discusses how trade union influence can strengthen requirements and monitoring to ensure fair conditions, stop unscrupulous operators and contribute to climate responsibility and sustainable development in public services.

An updated version of the trade union handbook “Bättre offentlig upphandling” is presented. New sections include climate and labour-related crime.
content.subject: Business
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: When AI takes over commerce – does consumer protection need strengthening?
content.description: AI and advanced data collection allow companies to predict what we want to buy, sometimes before we know it ourselves. At the same time, questions about privacy, manipulation and control over consumer behaviour are growing. Is the future of commerce smart service or sophisticated influence?
content.extendedDescription:
Questions:
How much data about our shopping habits is it reasonable for companies to collect? Does AI risk manipulating consumers rather than helping them? Should policymakers set clearer limits on personalised commerce? Who really controls consumption: the consumer or the tech giants?
content.subject: Digitalisation
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Should patients have to go blind on a waiting list?
content.description: The average waiting time for specialist eye care in Sweden is 106 days, even though patients should receive care within 90 days under the healthcare guarantee. In some regions, patients have lost their sight because they had to wait so long for care.
content.extendedDescription:
Should keeping your sight have to be a lottery depending on where you live?

Synskadades Riksförbund raises this issue at a seminar where we also present a new report on the state of the country's vision rehabilitation centres. Once you have lost your sight, why is it so hard to get the rehabilitation you are entitled to? And should access to assistive devices depend on money?
content.detail: Hjärtat i Almedalen – A meeting place by FOKUS Patient
content.subject: Health and social care

content.title: The future of knowledge-based healthcare management – from paperwork to real patient benefit
content.description: How does knowledge-based healthcare management move from documents to real patient benefit?
content.extendedDescription: The seminar discusses how Swedish knowledge-based healthcare management can move from administrative documents to tangible patient benefit. Drawing on interviews with key healthcare figures and regional politicians, it highlights implementation barriers, the need for clearer priorities and political ownership, and ways forward: simpler guidelines close to patient records, open comparisons and transparent collaboration between professionals, patients and Life Science.
content.subject: Health and social care
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Second Vice-Chair of the Primary Care Committee
Head of Health and Social Care

content.title: Take the train from Tranås to Tokyo – securing southern Sweden's international competitiveness
content.description: When access to international markets is inadequate, regions lose competitiveness. Southern Sweden's development is held back by an insufficient transport system. How do we create better, connected links to key hubs such as Copenhagen, with fast, reliable journeys?
content.extendedDescription:
What investments in infrastructure, interoperability and collaboration are needed to make the whole journey work better? Jönköping is highlighted as a concrete example of the value unlocked when connections work.

The seminar is organised in collaboration with Greater Copenhagen.
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Regional Councillor, Chair of the Transport, Infrastructure and Environment Committee

content.title: How do we get construction moving?
content.description: The housing shortage affects everyone. Many people today struggle to find a home of their own at a reasonable rent. Too little has been built for a long time. For many young people, the situation is particularly acute, with almost 200,000 still living at home because they lack affordable alternatives. How can this trend be reversed?
content.extendedDescription:
Hyresgästföreningen brings together stakeholders from business, construction and trade unions to discuss solutions and how to get construction moving.

Follow-up discussion: Who will solve the housing crisis?

In a commentary discussion, tomorrow's leaders discuss the needs, challenges and solutions they see for young people to get a home of their own and start their lives.
content.subject: Construction
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Crisis as a driving force
content.description: We face several parallel crises, both for our planet and for those of us who live on it.
content.extendedDescription:
War, economic crisis, a changing climate and biodiversity loss – and, on a smaller scale, crises of a more technical construction nature that may seem small compared with war and the climate crisis, but which we nevertheless need to manage alongside the larger crises. Crises force us to do things in new ways, making crisis a driving force for innovation and development.

In this panel discussion, we discuss how the crises we face are driving timber construction forward, with society as the winner.
content.subject: Construction

content.title: Swedes have spoken: culture matters
content.description: How do Swedes view culture today – and what does that mean for the cultural policy of the future?
content.extendedDescription: How do Swedes view culture today – and what does that mean for the cultural policy of the future? Drawing on Kulturbarometern 2026, we discuss the importance of culture for democracy, wellbeing and social cohesion. The seminar highlights Swedes' strong support for public cultural funding, children and young people's access to culture, and culture as part of preventive wellbeing. What is needed to enable more people to participate in cultural life across the country?
content.subject: Culture
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Author, Culture Editor at Liberal Debatt and Political Reporter at Smedjan

content.title: AI is no longer a technology issue – it is a leadership issue: is Sweden Inc. ready?
content.description: AI is changing the balance of power between companies, sectors and nations. The organisations – and countries – that succeed best are not those with the most pilot projects, but those with clear leadership, the courage to prioritise and the ability to scale.
content.extendedDescription:
In this panel, we move the AI discussion from IT departments to boardrooms and public agency leadership. What transformation is required of leaders in business and the public sector as AI moves from experiment to business-critical infrastructure that underpins society?

Who takes responsibility for pace, skills and implementation – and what happens if no one does?
content.subject: Digitalisation

content.title: Gotland leads the way – securing water for the future
content.description: In summer 2025, groundwater levels on Gotland were so low that Visby risked being unable to maintain its water supply. In spring 2026, the alarm was raised about the risk of water shortages throughout southern Sweden – Skåne, Blekinge, Öland, Småland and Gotland. How do we join forces to secure access to tap water in the future?
content.extendedDescription: What is needed for Gotland and other counties facing water shortages to maintain their water supply in the long term? What can the region do, and what requires political decisions at a higher level? And what role do municipal housing companies play, as they now make the investment decisions that will determine water use for decades to come?
content.subject: Climate/environment
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Chair of the environment and building committee
Climate Adaptation and Civil Preparedness Strategist

content.title: What will it take to break the gang economy?
content.description: Organised crime is estimated to generate hundreds of billions of kronor in turnover each year. This involves drugs and weapons, but also welfare crime in which gangs profit from society's shared resources.
content.extendedDescription: The challenges are considerable, and greater collaboration between society's different stakeholders is needed to reverse the trend. What role can Sweden's municipalities play in crime prevention? What challenges does business face, and how do we make it as difficult as possible for gangs to continue their activities that threaten society?
content.subject: Justice/crime
speakerTitles: Chair of the Municipal Executive Board
Expert on crime and public safety policy
Head of the Law Enforcement Department

content.title: From Vision Zero to full innovation – how do we create procurement that saves lives?
content.description: Safety innovations in mobility show promising results but do not always scale up. How can procurement and governance evolve to better reward impact, road safety and long-term value – and enable widespread implementation?
content.extendedDescription: The conversation brings together key stakeholders from the public sector, business and research to discuss how procurement, governance and collaboration can evolve to enable innovation in practice. The focus is on concrete experience, systemic barriers and ways forward to improve road safety and create long-term value.
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation

content.title: Is the built environment sector ready for change?
content.description: The built environment sector needs to attract and retain skills. This makes workplace culture, leadership and norms decisive factors in working conditions, safety and the industry's future development, rather than soft side issues.
content.extendedDescription: How does macho culture affect leadership, working conditions and skills supply in the built environment sector? As the industry needs to attract more people and retain skills, norms, jargon and attitudes towards responsibility become increasingly important. Byggcheferna releases this year's Machoindex, and we discuss what the results say about the industry's development – and what it takes to move from insight to change.
content.subject: Other
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Evictions affecting children are increasing – what can we do?
content.description: Despite the zero vision, evictions of families with children are increasing. Between January and June 2025, 422 children were affected by evictions, an increase of almost 60 per cent in three years. Why is it so hard to stop evictions affecting children?
content.extendedDescription: At the seminar, Frälsningsarmén highlights the conflict between the Convention on the Rights of the Child and tenancy law, geographical differences and the groups most affected. At least 5,900 children today live in homelessness with a parent, often a woman who has fled violence. Frälsningsarmén has therefore launched the Housing First project Hedvig, aimed at women and children exposed to violence. But what are politicians doing? Panel discussion.
content.subject: Children/young people
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Deputy Head of the Social Services Division
Senior Lecturer at the Department of Social Work

content.title: Everyone calls for more primary care – why is nothing happening?
content.description: How can we have the world's best healthcare when you cannot get an appointment at your primary care centre? Sweden lags far behind other countries in primary care, despite every inquiry pointing out that a regular doctor providing continuity would solve many healthcare problems. Why is progress so slow?
content.extendedDescription: A panel discussion about why everyone agrees yet change fails to happen. Is it politicians, healthcare management – or the profession itself – that must take greater responsibility?

content.title: Is Gotland Sweden's most protected place – or its most vulnerable?
content.description:
Robust Ö – are islands systemic risks in Swedish preparedness?
Sweden talks about total defence – but planning is in practice centred on the mainland.
content.extendedDescription:
Welcome to an in-depth conversation about preparedness and security, with a particular focus on Gotland's importance for Sweden's and Europe's collective resilience, together with key stakeholders in total defence.
The discussion will explore how we strengthen civil and military preparedness, how responsibilities and roles evolve in practice, and what is required of cooperation between the state, regions and municipalities at a time of growing security tensions.

content.title: From skills to climate: how Europe strengthens Västerbotten
content.description: What policy shift is needed for Västerbotten to meet its skills needs? And what policy improvements are needed for climate adaptation in coastal regions?
content.extendedDescription:
Region Västerbotten is an active participant in various Interreg Europe projects that strengthen our region.
A seminar about two Interreg Europe projects addressing what policy shift is needed for Västerbotten to meet its skills needs, and what policy improvements are needed for climate adaptation in coastal regions.
content.subject: Regional issues
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Head of External Relations and Strategic Place Development

content.title: Vision Zero 2.0 – air is free! But who is responsible for making it healthy?
content.description: Every year, around 1,400 people in Sweden die prematurely because of unhealthy air. Today, no minister, ministry or public agency has responsibility for making outdoor air less harmful. This must be resolved. Clear responsibility and an updated Vision Zero are two important building blocks.
content.extendedDescription: The seminar consists of a short introduction clarifying the problem and the needs. This is followed by a panel of relevant politicians and public agencies discussing and answering how we can ensure that no one dies prematurely because of unhealthy air caused by traffic in Sweden.
content.subject: Climate/environment
speakerTitles: Member of the Committee on Transport and Communications

content.title: How well should we eat, and what should it cost?
content.description: We already know that household finances will be an important issue in the 2026 election, but which issues can win elections and make a difference in the longer term?
content.extendedDescription:
Lidl Sverige invites you to an election debate with representatives of the parliamentary parties' youth organisations. The debate will address how or why we can and should reduce food prices, whether halving food VAT is a good thing, the role of grocery retail in strengthening Swedish preparedness, whether consumers should pay for the green transition, and much more.

Do not miss a Lidl-style election debate with tomorrow's political leaders!
content.subject: Business

content.title: From vision to action – patient focus in national strategies
content.description: For patients, national plans only have value if they make a difference in everyday life. For someone living with heart disease, cancer or a rare condition, the issue is getting the right diagnosis, timely care and the same chance of life and health regardless of where in the country they live.
content.extendedDescription: Vård och omsorgsanalys shares a situation overview from the report “en plats runt bordet”, followed by patient and service-user organisations discussing how national strategies for cancer, rare conditions, heart health, and asthma and allergy can be put into practice for patients' benefit. Patient representatives have the floor in the morning panel.
content.subject: Health and social care
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: When money talks – whose voices disappear?
content.description: How can we build a democracy in which everyone is heard and decisions are based on our shared collective will rather than well-resourced special interests?
content.extendedDescription:
A functioning democracy depends on all voices having an equal opportunity to be heard. Yet we know this is not the reality: instead, those with the strongest financial resources are usually heard most, often at the expense of the planet, our health, facts and our rights.

We invite you to a conversation about how we can build a democracy in which everyone is heard and decisions are based on our shared collective will rather than well-resourced special interests.
content.subject: Democracy

content.title: How do we systematically strengthen total defence's capacity for innovation?
content.description: Sweden faces growing security and societal challenges amid considerable uncertainty. For total defence, this means civilian and military stakeholders need to strengthen their innovation capacity together, nationally, regionally and locally.
content.extendedDescription: Sweden's security and societal challenges require stronger interaction around innovation in total defence. This seminar brings together stakeholders from the total defence and innovation systems to explore how professionalisation and standards in innovation management can strengthen innovation capacity. We discuss needs, opportunities and how frameworks can support development.
content.subject: Innovation
speakerTitles: Head of Information Technology and Command and Control Systems

content.title: Media and power: algorithms' power over young voters
content.description: The media have great power to shape our thoughts, but who has real power over the media? Senior executives, politicians, individual journalists, or communications professionals and lobbyists?
content.extendedDescription:
More and more young people encounter politics for the first time through social media. Today, algorithms determine which clips and messages appear in their feeds and thus which perspectives are most visible. Which algorithms shape democracy and young people's political worldview? How does this affect their view of society, identity and democracy? A conversation about how algorithms influence the political messages young people encounter and how tomorrow's voters are shaped in a digital media landscape.
In a series of questioning sessions, Dagens Media and Resumé put leading figures in media, advertising, PR and communications in the spotlight.
content.subject: Media/journalism
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: A harsher tone of debate – what responsibility do the media take?
content.description: What responsibility do the media have for this development, and for helping audiences understand the issues rather than the political game? Where is the line between reflecting conflict and amplifying it?
content.extendedDescription: The tone of political debate has become harsher over several election campaigns. This is noticeable in debate studios, on social media and in voters' experiences. In a survey commissioned by Ekot, seven in ten voters say politicians do not speak respectfully to one another, and eight in ten say discussions focus more on tactics than substance.
content.subject: Media/journalism
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Founder and Editor-in-Chief, The Local, and Chair of Sveriges Tidskrifter

content.title: From words to action – how AI and law unlock the public sector's potential
content.description: The technology is already here, but transformation in the public sector is moving too slowly. AI, automation and smart use of the law offer enormous opportunities to free up resources, shorten processing times and strengthen public welfare services today.
content.extendedDescription: By focusing on enabling rather than obstacles, we can show what is possible. How does the public sector move from planning to operation? Which legal doors are already open but unused? And how do we build trust as the technology is put to use?
content.subject: Digitalisation
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Legal Adviser, Digital Transformation, Risk and Compliance

content.title: Between myth and reality – who is right about welfare services?
content.description: What is true – and what is myth – about companies in education, healthcare and social care? The welfare debate contains many claims about profits, quality, working conditions and transparency. But what is the reality for those who run and develop these services every day?
content.extendedDescription:
Almega invites you to a seminar where entrepreneurs from education, healthcare and social care share their perspectives and address the most common myths about the sector. This is followed by a political debate in which representatives of both government and opposition comment on and discuss the issues raised.

A warm welcome!
content.subject: Education
speakerTitles: Minister for Older People and Social Security
Education Policy Spokesperson and Member of Parliament

content.title: History that shapes the future – what conclusions do young people draw about lessons, responsibility and action?
content.description: How can history help us understand the times we live in – and the society we want to shape for the future? What lessons can we learn from the Holocaust, and how can they strengthen our ability to take responsibility, stand up for democratic values and influence the future?
content.extendedDescription: Young experts from different parts of Sweden, with different backgrounds and experiences, discuss how knowledge of history can encourage reflection, responsibility and the ability to act. The conversation is part of a collaboration between Forum för levande historia and Fryshuset exploring which stories we pass on, why they matter and how they can reach the next generation.
content.subject: Children/young people

content.title: Free market, high price – the consequences of alcohol and nicotine advertising
content.description: How does the free market affect sales, addiction, public health and harm to individuals and society? Who is responsible for the consequences and costs that dependence on these products causes, including costs to society?
content.extendedDescription:
Studies and research will be presented on how advertising affects individuals' use of these products. The respective industries spend large sums on advertising, often targeting young people. How is advertising regulated, and what happens next?
The downsides of addiction are often costly and harmful to both individuals and society.
content.subject: Children/young people

content.title: Total defence is being built now – what must business deliver?
content.description: What happens if the water supply is disrupted and the power goes down? The government has been clear: business plays a crucial role in building Sweden's civil defence. But what is required of companies to strengthen preparedness?
content.extendedDescription: Here, the industries the government has identified as central to total defence come together to discuss how we strengthen society's preparedness for a digital attack. Can we still supply electricity, distribute food, secure the water supply and build what is needed?
content.subject: Construction
speakerTitles: Lead for Societal Security and Civil Defence
Head of the Supply Preparedness Department

content.title: Leading 150 years of technological shifts – Swedish engineering from the telegraph to AI
content.description: Sweden has long been a leading technology nation, from the telegraph to today's AI development. At a time of rapid technological shifts, the question is how Sweden can stay at the forefront and create the conditions for innovation, competitiveness and societal benefit.
content.extendedDescription: Drawing on Gunnar Wetterberg's book “Uppkopplad: Ingenjörskonst i generationer”, the conversation will focus on how Ericsson and Sweden as a technology nation have developed over the past 150 years, and what is required for Ericsson and other Swedish companies to remain globally competitive over the next 150 years.
content.subject: Digitalisation
speakerTitles: CEO of Politea and Senior Researcher

content.title: 1.3 billion Muslims lack freedom of religion – why is that? Is there hope for change?
content.description: Everyone has the right to freedom of thought, conscience and religion. This right includes freedom to change religion or belief, under Article 18 of the UN Universal Declaration of Human Rights. This right is violated in several OIC (Organisation of Islamic Cooperation) countries.
content.extendedDescription: The right to change belief in OIC countries is violated through the application of apostasy or blasphemy laws in both criminal and civil law. We highlight examples of positive change at both local and international level. The hour will offer a mix of speeches, conversation and questions.
content.subject: Human rights
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Political scientist, Chair of Persiska missionsföreningen Sthlm

content.title: How should allergy be prioritised in 2026–2030?
content.description: Allergy is a widespread condition with significant societal costs. Working while ill alone, for example, costs billions annually. People with allergies easily fall through the cracks. A new national strategy, action plan and guideline for allergy have now been developed. How will they be implemented?
content.extendedDescription:
What will the next parliamentary term mean for one of Sweden's most common patient groups? Will the state send allergy funding to the regions? And how will regional politicians act?

Welcome to an evening of learning about allergy, with three themes, from 17–19 in our garden.

Hot food and drinks will be available during the evening, along with opportunities to mingle.
content.subject: Health and social care
speakerTitles: Chair of the Regional Executive Board

content.title: Women, peace and security facing headwinds
content.description: Conflicts are spreading globally while gender equality is being pushed back. More women and girls than in decades live close to armed violence, while their influence over the decisions shaping their lives is diminishing. How can we strengthen women's influence in peace processes?
content.extendedDescription:
A panel discussion on women, peace and security focusing on how we can increase women's influence in peace processes and conflict resolution.

Operation 1325 advocates, informs, educates and creates platforms for debate and dialogue to influence decision-makers, civil society and the public, with the aim of implementing UN Security Council Resolution 1325 on women, peace and security.
content.subject: International affairs

content.title: Living conditions for people facing vulnerability and mental ill health – what is the situation and what are the needs?
content.description: What are living conditions like for people in vulnerable circumstances? What opportunities do we have to improve their circumstances? What do people in vulnerable situations themselves say?
content.extendedDescription: Political representatives discuss living conditions for people in vulnerable circumstances and highlight opportunities to improve them. Mind also presents its report on living conditions among people seeking support, including through Självmordslinjen, and others in similar situations, with more than 1,600 respondents.
content.subject: Human rights
speakerTitles: Chair of the Primary Care and Elderly Care Committee, SKR
Moderator, Lawyer, Investigator and Chair of Mind

content.title: Who will lead tomorrow's healthcare? Young doctors want flexibility, and healthcare needs doctors as managers
content.description: Swedish healthcare cannot take its future medical leadership for granted. What is needed for more young doctors to want, dare and be able to lead healthcare – and why is this a crucial question for the future of the entire healthcare system?
content.extendedDescription: Sveriges läkarförbund Student and Sveriges läkarförbunds chefsförening invite you to a joint panel discussion on how tomorrow's healthcare should be led and what conditions young doctors need to take on management roles early in their careers.
content.subject: Health and social care
speakerTitles: Director of Health and Medical Care
Chief Medical Officer responsible for Preparedness
Chair of Parliament's Committee on Health and Welfare

content.title: Research in focus – what does science say?
content.description: Obesity is one of our most important public health issues, yet it is surrounded by ignorance and stigma. More and more Swedes live with obesity and an increased risk of serious secondary conditions. Children are also affected and therefore risk long-term ill health. Decisive action must be taken to stop this trend.
content.extendedDescription: In this second of three conversations, focusing on research, we highlight the current state of obesity research. What is genetic and what is self-inflicted? Are there different types of fat, and what does addiction research say? And how do we spread the new knowledge?
content.subject: Health and social care

content.title: What do politicians from M and V want to happen in healthcare?
content.description: How should tomorrow's healthcare be designed?
content.extendedDescription:
Here we reverse the perspective and let politicians question a panel of experts about the issues closest to their hearts. From Tuesday to Thursday, you can listen to “Heta panelen”, today featuring representatives of Moderaterna and Vänsterpartiet. The politicians put questions to experts from organisational research, the professions and patient organisations, who answer from their respective roles. Breakfast is served from 07.30 to 08.00.

The seminar is part of Arena Tillsammans – the meeting place for healthcare's major systemic issues during Almedalsveckan.
content.detail: Arena Tillsammans: the arena for healthcare's major systemic issues
content.subject: Health and social care

content.title: From power capacity shortages to leadership
content.description:
Today's model for electricity prices and capacity now faces a new global reality.
How can energy become a competitive advantage for the whole country?
content.extendedDescription:
Today's model for electricity prices and capacity now faces a new global reality. Do we dare respond with rapid and powerful change, focusing more on users' and industry's need for predictability? When will Sweden reconsider old assumptions that fail to deliver?
Representatives of companies across Sweden will share their view of the challenges and opportunities and challenge policymakers with their perspectives.
content.subject: Energy
speakerTitles: Chair of the Committee on Industry and Trade
Moderator and Head of Business Policy, moderator

content.title: Out-of-home care for children and young people at a crossroads
content.description: Compulsory care of children, especially children with disabilities, has received serious criticism from UN committees. Sweden now faces important choices: how can we break the pattern and create good, safe conditions for children who need society's support?
content.extendedDescription: How do we guarantee that Sweden is a country where human rights are safeguarded? A state governed by the rule of law, where democracy is strong and vibrant, no one faces discrimination and people stand up for everyone's equal worth.
content.detail: Torget för Mänskliga Rättigheter och Demokrati
content.subject: Human rights
content.accessibility: The event is captioned, Hearing loop, Sign language interpretation, Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: A zero vision for men's violence – what are the results?
content.description: In December, the government finally announced a zero vision for men's lethal violence and the crisis council that the women's shelter movement had long demanded. Six months have now passed: what is the result? Has Sweden become safer for women and children? What election pledges do the parties have for women and children exposed to violence?
content.extendedDescription: According to both current and previous governments, men's violence against women should have the same priority as other serious crime. Yet women and children continue to face violence, often in their homes, where they should feel safest of all. What do the parties want to do for women and children exposed to violence? Unizon takes the parties' temperature.
content.subject: Justice/crime
speakerTitles: Member of Parliament, Parliamentary Group Leader

content.title: From risk to progress: cybersecurity as a catalyst for innovation
content.description: Agile cybersecurity work creates bolder and more secure organisations. In other words, cybersecurity can lay the foundation for innovation and competitiveness today and in the long term. But what does this mean in everyday practice for innovation-driven companies and organisations?
content.extendedDescription: This seminar brings together leading business stakeholders to highlight how cybersecurity can be integrated into fast-moving organisations without becoming a brake. It focuses on how security work is organised to support innovation, how decision-making processes adapt to rapid change and how responsibility is allocated in complex environments.
content.subject: Security/defence
speakerTitles: Head of the National Cyber Security Centre

content.title: Sustainability that lasts – from climate targets to viable business
content.description: Climate requirements for construction are tightening, while more homes are needed and there is talk of a crisis in the industry. How do we reconcile climate targets with financial viability and projects that can be built?
content.extendedDescription: Welcome to breakfast and a conversation about how sustainability can work in practice. Drawing on the housing projects Årsta Park – sustainable rental homes in Uppsala – and Villa Verde in Järfälla, Bonava's most sustainable single-family homes, we discuss what is needed to reduce climate impact without stopping much-needed housing construction. An in-depth conversation about concrete lessons, new solutions and next steps, covering collaboration, materials, ambitions and processes.
content.subject: Construction
speakerTitles: Head of Transactions and Business Development

content.title: The pace of innovation during war – how do we turn Ukraine's lessons into Swedish capability?
content.description: In wartime, the playing field changes in real time. For Ukraine, the pace of innovation has been crucial to defence capability. For Sweden and NATO, the question is equally relevant: how can we adapt when it really matters? How can Sweden turn civilian technology into direct defence capability more quickly?
content.extendedDescription: With a representative of Ukraine's army corps, we gain unique first-hand perspectives from a reality where innovation takes place under extreme pressure. How can we accelerate collaboration between civilian stakeholders, startups and defence? What barriers exist in today's system, and how can they be overcome?
content.subject: Innovation
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Bureaucracy and the rule of law – pillars of liberal democracy
content.description: Bureaucracy and the rule of law have proved more important as a foundation for democracy than one might think. Yet both are now challenged by AI and autocrats. Many people do not even know what bureaucracy is, seeing it mainly as red tape that should preferably be removed.
content.extendedDescription: Media scholar Anne Kaun discusses bureaucracy's AI challenges, joined by filmmaker Karin Wegsjö, who has made a film about the rule of law, and former State Secretary Maja Fjaestad. The discussion is led by Jenny Björkman of Riksbankens Jubileumsfond, editor of Byråkrati, a box set of six essays written by researchers.
content.subject: Democracy
speakerTitles: Professor of Media and Communication Studies
Associate Professor, Director of External Engagement

content.title: Healthcare according to need or ability to pay?
content.description: How should healthcare resources be prioritised when the principle of need conflicts with goals such as access, freedom of choice and efficiency?
content.extendedDescription:
The panel discussion starts from the ethical platform for priority-setting and explores how the principle of care according to need relates to greater access and freedom of choice. Particular attention is given to the role of private health insurance in Swedish healthcare and its impact on priorities and resource allocation.

The conversation also addresses how patient choice schemes, funding to reduce waiting lists, online doctors and other measures to improve access affect healthcare priorities, and the potential consequences for patients and the healthcare system.
content.subject: Health and social care
speakerTitles: Author, public commentator and PhD in economic history

content.title: Media at a turning point – who controls the story of Sweden?
content.description: Power over public debate has shifted. From newsrooms to platforms. From accountable editors to feeds driven by speed and reach. Meanwhile, trust is under pressure. Whoever evokes the strongest emotions has the greatest impact. So who is really in control?
content.extendedDescription: Who takes responsibility in the media when boundaries become unclear? Journalism is challenged by new business models. Platforms set the rules. Politics tries to establish frameworks in a rapidly changing landscape. What happens to fact-based debate when attention becomes currency? And can trust be created in a system driven by speed and impact?
content.subject: Media/journalism
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Head of External Relations and Strategic Place Development

content.title: Can tax policy help increase mobility in the housing market?
content.description: New housing construction and moving home involve several taxes and charges. Can changes to taxes influence mobility in the housing market so that we make optimal use of the existing housing stock?
content.extendedDescription:
One proposal raised by KD in the political debate ahead of the next parliamentary term is to differentiate capital gains tax, giving those who have lived in a home for a long time a lower capital gains tax when selling, as an incentive. Another proposal is to review the different levels of stamp duty.
What other proposals do our parliamentary parties have for the next term?
Join an engaging debate and discussion!
content.subject: Construction
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: How do we create robust communities for our own sake? Local economies in theory and practice
content.description: The risk of war has highlighted how to build robust communities, from small communities to parts of larger cities. How can we organise ourselves? How do we bring about change? How do we truly become a collective?
content.extendedDescription: Here you will meet doers: local stakeholders who build robust and resilient communities together. This seminar highlights concrete examples where a focus on local economies encompasses everything from access to capital and organisation to care for the environment and climate and stronger community ties. Half the seminar consists of short presentations, and the other half of conversations.
content.subject: Economy
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: How do we create cultural welfare?
content.description: Cultural funding has been eroded over a long period, and differences between parts of the country are growing. Today, postcodes largely determine people's access to libraries, museums, municipal arts schools and rehearsal spaces. How does this development square with the constitution's requirement for cultural welfare?
content.extendedDescription: DIK therefore brings together leading cultural policy representatives for a debate to ask the crucial questions: how do we secure equal access to culture across the country? What cultural policy differences divide the parties? And what can we expect after the election?
content.subject: Culture
speakerTitles: Chair of the Committee on Cultural Affairs
Vice Chair of the Committee on Cultural Affairs
Group Leader and Municipal Council Member

content.title: Taking back sovereignty without changing everything – is it possible?
content.description: The need for digital sovereignty is growing, but few organisations can or want to isolate themselves. Are there ways other than complete isolation to guarantee that no external actor can threaten an organisation and its systems?
content.extendedDescription: Red Hat, Cambio and Atea have experience from different perspectives of building sovereign and secure AI services for both the public and private sectors. We know the challenge is simultaneously easier and harder to solve than most people think. This session's discussion will give you new perspectives and probably some food for thought. Solutions exist, but some of the costs lie in areas other than those you might first imagine.
content.subject: Digitalisation
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Clinical research – a luxury or a necessity in healthcare?
content.description: Sweden has long been a strong medical research nation. But as care needs grow and services face pressure, fewer practising doctors have the time and opportunity to conduct research. Is clinical research a luxury in a strained healthcare system – or a prerequisite for better treatments?
content.extendedDescription: Panel discussion on the conditions for clinical research and its importance in healthcare.
content.subject: Health and social care
speakerTitles: Moderator, Chair of SLS's Delegation for Medical Research
Senior Consultant in Neurology, former Head of the University Healthcare Department Neuro-, huvud- och halscentrum
Head of the Research and Health Department

content.title: Can you trust what you see on screen?
content.description: AI advances in the media industry every day. This opens up new ways to create and reach audiences, but also raises a crucial question: what happens to trust when it becomes increasingly difficult to know what is authentic?
content.extendedDescription: For the media, the challenge is twofold. It involves both using AI in ways that strengthen content without undermining credibility and continuing to build the skills the industry needs to keep pace with developments. At the seminar, media stakeholders meet to discuss how AI is already changing the industry, the choices ahead and what is needed for audiences to continue trusting what they see, hear and read.
content.subject: Media/journalism

content.title: What have 60 years of development aid taught us?
content.description:
The world is marked by crises. Meanwhile, development aid is increasingly used to promote Swedish exports and reduce migration.
For 60 years, we have worked to ensure that aid strengthens democracy and human rights. What have we learned, and how can political work in Sweden contribute to global development?
content.extendedDescription:
To mark our 60th anniversary, we bring together voices and experiences for a conversation about the past and future of development aid, solidarity and people's right to shape their own lives. We discuss how we have linked our political work in Sweden to our work elsewhere in the world.
There will be personal stories, guests and perspectives on the future, followed by anniversary mingling with ice cream and party games. Welcome!
content.subject: International affairs
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: A global economy in turmoil – what does it mean for Sweden?
content.description: The global economy in 2026 is marked by war, greater protectionism and geopolitical uncertainty – how does this affect Sweden? What are the biggest threats to the Swedish economy, and how much do Sweden's leading chief economists differ in their assessments of the economic situation?
content.extendedDescription: Hear the experts present their forecasts in a sharp macroeconomic duel: for the fourth consecutive year, Länsförsäkringar invites you to a macroeconomic battle featuring Sweden's leading chief economists. Over 45 minutes, we discuss inflation, growth, risks and choices, focusing on fiscal policy and geopolitics. Welcome to a probing macroeconomic conversation with some of the country's most influential economists.
content.subject: Economy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.description: How should tomorrow's healthcare be designed?
content.extendedDescription:
Here we reverse the perspective and let politicians question a panel of experts about the issues closest to their hearts. The politicians put questions to experts from organisational research, the professions and patient organisations, who answer from their respective roles. Breakfast is served from 07.30 to 08.00.

The seminar is part of Arena Tillsammans – the meeting place for healthcare's major systemic issues during Almedalsveckan.
