content.title: Who owns trust in an AI-driven economy?
content.description: Who bears responsibility as AI makes more and more decisions in customer service, recruitment and customer relations? And as AI expansion meets growing scepticism, how do we strengthen employees', customers' and capital markets' confidence in the technology's continued potential?
content.extendedDescription: AI is high on the agenda as organisations move from strategy to reality. How can organisations create value, build trust and take responsibility in an AI-driven economy? How do you bring employees along in a change that affects both ways of working and responsibilities? What is actually hardest – the technology or the organisation? And when the measurable effects of AI
content.subject: Business
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: The importance of pharmacies and retail for reducing exclusion and creating safe neighbourhoods
content.description: How do we ensure access to pharmacies and retail throughout the country, including in socially excluded areas?
content.extendedDescription:
Pharmacies serve an important public function by providing nearby access to medicines and advice, thereby supporting public health. Together with other retail and services, pharmacies contribute to vibrant urban environments, jobs and safe neighbourhoods.

With the right conditions, retail can help turn things around and create hope for the future, health and safety in our disadvantaged areas.

Welcome to an engaging discussion about both challenges and opportunities!
content.subject: Business

content.title: Fighting ageism – how do we increase age representation in the labour market?
content.description: The retirement age is rising, and the importance of lifelong learning in the labour market is increasingly emphasised. Yet many older jobseekers continue to face resistance. What is needed to make better use of experience and skills in a labour market undergoing major and rapid change?
content.extendedDescription: The seminar concludes with the presentation and celebration of the Senior Talent Award 2026 winners. The Senior Talent Award recognises stakeholders who highlight the value of senior expertise and actively combat ageism at work. The award is presented in three categories: individual, organisation and company.
content.subject: Employment/labour market
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Minister for Older People and Social Security

content.title: Hope is not a strategy – critical minerals and Europe's future
content.description: Europe cannot build its industrial future on the hope of stable supplies of critical minerals from the other side of the world. If we are serious about transition, competitiveness and security, we must start using the resources we have here – and Europe's greatest opportunities are in Sweden.
content.extendedDescription: LKAB invites you to a roundtable on the opportunities Sweden's mineral resources offer the country and Europe, and the risks if we fail to use them. The discussion features specially invited guests and is open to anyone who wants to listen.
content.subject: Business
speakerTitles: Director of Public Affairs and External Relations
Head of NATO Cyber & Hybrid Policy Section

content.description: How should tomorrow's healthcare be designed?
content.extendedDescription:
What do politicians from KD, L and SD want to happen in healthcare?

Here we reverse the perspective and let politicians question a panel of experts about the issues closest to their hearts. The politicians put questions to experts from organisational research, the professions and patient organisations, who answer from their respective roles. Breakfast is served from 07.30 to 08.00.

Member of the Parliamentary Committee on Health and Welfare

content.title: Aviation of the future for Sweden's and Arlanda's competitiveness
content.description: Sweden's competitiveness depends on good connectivity throughout the country. In a long, export-dependent country, aviation is central. At the same time, it needs to transition in a way that both reduces its climate impact and secures the connectivity on which business and the public sector depend.
content.extendedDescription:
Welcome to a seminar bringing together perspectives from politics, business and the public sector to discuss:
• Aviation's role in Sweden's connectivity and competitiveness.
• How travel policies and procurement of sustainable aviation fuel can help reduce emissions without restricting necessary travel.
• The importance of effective infrastructure to and from Arlanda.
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Director of Public Affairs and External Relations

content.title: Does the protection of human rights, democracy and the rule of law need strengthening in Sweden?
content.description: The rule of law and human rights face headwinds around the world. But what is the situation in Sweden? Are we immune, or does protection need strengthening here too?
content.extendedDescription: A conversation between Erik Ottoson, Member of Parliament (m) and Chair of Parliament's Committee on EU Affairs; Göran Sundström, Professor of Political Science at Stockholms universitet; Britta Lejon, President of Statsanställdas förbund; Anders Hagsgård, President of Hovrätten Västra Götaland; and Fredrik Malmberg, Director of Institutet för mänskliga rättigheter. The conversation is moderated by Anna Rosenmüller Nordlander, Lawyer at Institutet för mänskliga rättigheter.
content.detail: Torget för mänskliga rättigheter och demokrati
content.subject: Human rights
content.accessibility: The event is captioned, Hearing loop, Sign language interpretation, Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Chair of the Committee on EU Affairs
President of the Court of Appeal

content.title: Politics on ragebait platforms' terms
content.description: What happens to democracy when politics becomes content and emotional outbursts have more impact than substantive issues? What happens when the trivialisation of politics, ragebait, media logic and online feeds set the agenda?
content.extendedDescription: Tuesday ends with a conversation – also a live podcast! – between three of the Swedish left's best-loved voices: Johannes Klenell, Karina Cubilla and Daniel Swedin of the podcast Kommentariatet. Together, they dissect the political situation, unpack statements, rhetoric and realities, and help us understand what is really happening in Swedish politics right now. A perfect end to the day for anyone who wants to spot political trends before they become retrospective analysis.
content.subject: Media/journalism

content.title: Is there a solution to crime other than tougher measures?
content.description: When the prison service doubles up rooms with bunk beds and money goes to new prisons instead of rehabilitation programmes, what happens to the prison environment? What happens to inmates? And to crime in Sweden?
content.extendedDescription: Sweden used to be a role model for other countries in rehabilitating offenders. But the political line now is that it does not work, and decisions are instead being made to introduce longer sentences and tougher measures, despite protests from prosecutors, judges, criminologists and prison officers. In this seminar, we discuss whether tougher measures really are the best way to reduce crime, and what other alternatives actually exist.
content.subject: Justice/crime
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Should all of Sweden grow – or merely function?
content.description: Sweden has great potential to grow outside its major cities, but creating vibrant towns and rural areas requires conditions for entrepreneurship, financing and opportunities for children, adults and older people to participate and develop. Who is responsible for ensuring that all of Sweden grows?
content.extendedDescription:
A young family wants to start a business and buy a house in a small town. The school's future is uncertain. The bank hesitates. Public transport is being reduced. Broadband works – sometimes.

This seminar brings together representatives of rural communities, politics and business for a conversation about what is needed to create viable communities where people, businesses and the economy have the conditions to grow.
content.subject: Economy

content.title: The railway industry joins forces – is today's policy enough for tomorrow's railway?
content.description: Railways are decisive for the climate, growth and preparedness. The industry is working together to accelerate progress, strengthen delivery and take greater responsibility for the whole system. But without clear policy, long-term rules and sustainable funding, development stalls.
content.extendedDescription:
Session 1: From deadlock to solutions – the unique power of railway industry collaboration through Vision 2050 and the Roadmap

Session 2: Trains need to keep running while the railway needs upgrading – what is required?

Session 3: For a competitive Sweden – how do we ensure a railway that strengthens growth and business?
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport

content.title: More seafood on the menu – but how do we guide consumers well?
content.description: We should eat more fish – a couple of times a week, according to Livsmedelsverket. So how can we make it easier for consumers to find their way around the fish counter? How do we help retailers with clear, factual information? How do we provide clear guidance and strengthen trust in seafood?
content.extendedDescription: Where does the fish come from? How was it caught or farmed? These are questions the fish industry often encounters and must be able to answer. How do we create clearer communication and greater confidence in the seafood on our plates? And how can retailers, public agencies and the industry work together to make it easier for consumers to choose well?
content.detail:
Dagens industri's arena – Future Food Forum on
Samhällsscenen
content.subject: Food
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: RUT – work, family and parenthood on (un)equal terms?
content.description: What do RUT household services mean for balancing everyday life?
content.extendedDescription:
For whom does buying household services free up time? How does RUT affect the distribution of work, responsibility and time within families? What significance does RUT have for relationships, parenthood and decisions about having children? Are there effects linked to working life, income and gender equality? Who benefits most from the reform, and how should RUT be understood in relation to state subsidies and economic priorities?

New research addresses these questions and shows clear links between family life and the use of RUT.
content.subject: Research
content.accessibility: Event captioned, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Postdoctoral Researcher in Sociology at Lunds universitet
Associate Professor and Deputy Director, SOM-institutet

content.title: Circular textile jobs – does Sweden have the right skills for the transition?
content.description: The circular transition in the textile and fashion industry creates new skills needs throughout the value chain, from materials knowledge and production to repair, remanufacturing, sorting and quality assurance.
content.extendedDescription:
At the same time, companies report skills shortages, and many skilled workers lack formal validation of their knowledge.
How can education, the labour market and industry work together to ensure the right skills for tomorrow's circular textile value chains? What new professional roles are emerging, and how can education, validation and lifelong learning become more accessible to both individuals and companies? This is central to both Swedish competitiveness and society's resilience.
content.subject: Sustainability
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Chair of the Municipal Executive Board

content.title: Why should we listen to public agencies? Election year and rumblings of war: agency reputations in 2026
content.description: People's trust acts as society's gold reserve, and public agencies' reputations are a measure of its value. How quickly do disinformation and influence campaigns erode it during elections and crises?
content.extendedDescription: Drawing on Verian's Anseendeindex Myndigheter 2026, we invite some of our most topical public agencies to explain how they strengthen their reputations and counter destabilising forces. What has the greatest impact on perceptions of them? How is Valmyndigheten working preventively ahead of the autumn election? How are Livsmedelsverket and Läkemedelsverket preparing for an unforeseen societal crisis in which whether the population listens is absolutely crucial?
content.subject: Democracy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: The security paradox: more defence, less security?
content.description: How is global security affected by increasing conflict, new weapons technologies, human rights violations and threats to health security?
content.extendedDescription: A panel discussion organised by ONE Campaign and Human Rights Watch highlighting how global security is challenged by rapid military development, new weapons technologies and increasing human rights violations, as well as growing threats to health security. The conversation explores whether diplomacy, development and health can keep pace with these changes, and highlights the need for a broader concept of security in which investments in diplomacy, development and health work together for long-term, sustainable security.
content.subject: Human rights
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Associate Director Advocacy and Campaigns Scandinavia
Dag Hammarsköld Professor of Peace and Conflict Research

content.title: Stop the loss of valuable nature
content.description: Although Sweden and the world's countries agreed in 2022 to halt and reverse biodiversity loss by 2030, policy in Sweden is moving in the opposite direction. Budget cuts, opposition to important environmental laws and the dismantling of Sweden's nature conservation work threaten our shared natural environment.
content.extendedDescription:
Welcome to Världsnaturfonden WWF's Almedalen gathering 2026 – an open breakfast networking event for anyone interested in climate and environmental policy.
Over breakfast, WWF will highlight important biodiversity issues with concrete proposals for politicians ahead of the next parliamentary term, followed by a political debate.

Breakfast is provided while supplies last.
content.detail: Hållbarhetsarenan, M/S Teaterskeppet's large dining room
content.subject: Animals/nature

content.title: How can we use urban development in preventive safety work?
content.description: How can urban planning contribute to safer environments that prevent crime? Safety requires collaboration between more stakeholders. This discussion explores how the built environment can reduce crime and insecurity, from early planning to management.
content.extendedDescription: How can urban planning be used to create environments that prevent crime and provide good conditions for safety and wellbeing? Safety is an increasingly important issue, and more stakeholders need to work together to address crime and insecurity. In this conversation, we discuss how the built environment can reduce crime and insecurity, and what needs to be considered at different stages of the urban development process to achieve this.
content.subject: Other
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Is defence innovation the key to a safer world?
content.description: A more complex security environment and rapid technological development place new demands on the defence sector. How do we meet the future and successfully make use of new technology? Is defence innovation the key? And what is Sweden's role?
content.extendedDescription: This seminar highlights current examples of Sweden's work on defence innovation and discusses how to strengthen the conditions for it. We ask what role research and innovation play in developing tomorrow's defence, and how we can strengthen collaboration between public agencies, business, academia and international partners. The challenges are many, as are the opportunities.
content.subject: Security/defence
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Sustainable shipping on hold – where are we and what is the next step?
content.description: Shipping's climate transition is often described as ongoing, but the truth is that progress is too slow. The technology exists, the ambitions have been there for years, yet decisive breakthroughs remain elusive. What is really holding things back?
content.extendedDescription: This seminar brings together shipping companies, business, politics and ports for an honest reality check: what progress has actually been made, what barriers are slowing development and who bears responsibility? And what does shipping's transition mean for business competitiveness? Looking five years ahead, the discussion also explores what is needed to move from vision to reality, and whether Sweden will lead the transition or risk falling behind.
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Balancing workplaces and a vibrant city – how can it be done?
content.description: In Stockholm's harbour districts, life between buildings and the historic harbour environments are crucial assets in urban development. How do property owners create public spaces alongside office workplaces?
content.extendedDescription: When new districts with office workplaces are developed, factors such as tenant mix, phasing, mobility and technical infrastructure are considered. In Stockholm's harbour districts, life between buildings and the historic harbour environments are crucial assets in urban development. The idea is to make room for people strolling and children playing. How do property owners create public spaces alongside office workplaces?
content.subject: Construction
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Time for an electricity producers' revolt? The energy transition risks stalling
content.description: During the year, electricity producers have encountered resistance in trying to obtain judicial review of grid charge issues through regulatory supervision.
content.extendedDescription: Last year's panel organised by Svensk Vindkraft discussed the unequal situation for feed-in customers (electricity producers) in Sweden compared with the rest of the EU. A particular question was whether the then-new grid tariff rules were EU-compatible. These regulations from Energimarknadsinspektionen (EIFS 2022:1) are now to be repealed by 30 June 2026 at the latest. What comes next is unclear and is something we will discuss.
content.detail:
Hållbarhetsarenan, M/S Teaterskeppet
Small dining room
content.subject: Energy

content.title: From the lab to life – how cancer research becomes innovation
content.description: Swedish cancer research is world-class, but many research findings never reach patients or deliver societal benefit. How can we strengthen the conditions for researchers to commercialise their findings?
content.extendedDescription: The seminar brings together researchers, civil society, business and decision-makers to discuss barriers, opportunities and concrete solutions to strengthen the commercialisation of Swedish cancer research and Sweden's competitiveness in life science.
content.subject: Research
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
speakerTitles: Professor, Biomedical Radiation Sciences, Uppsala universitet, and CEO and Co-Founder, Akiram Therapeutics
Head of the Research and Health Department

content.title: A resilient society in troubled times – how do we build Sweden's civil and military defence?
content.description: Sweden's security situation has changed fundamentally. Strong defence is not just about military capability, but about the resilience of society as a whole and its capacity to produce, deliver and maintain critical functions.
content.extendedDescription:
Industry plays a central role, from raw materials and advanced technology to transport and energy supply. At the same time, a robust society requires functioning value chains in which companies, public agencies and politics work together.

Against this backdrop, a crucial question arises:
Does Sweden today have the structures, incentives and partnerships needed to build strong civil and military defence? Or do they need fundamental development?
content.subject: Business

content.title: Access and security in healthcare and social care
content.description: Can Sweden guarantee healthcare within 48 hours? Do we receive better and faster care depending on who provides it? What does separating provision from funding mean? Why is a fresh start needed in social care?
content.extendedDescription: The panel takes the form of an open conversation led by a moderator. The audience will also have opportunities to ask questions and comment. The aim is to seek understanding of one of the state's most important core responsibilities: healthcare and social care. Does spending more money help, and if so, where should it go? Are regions right to close down private alternatives? Are there examples in neighbouring countries we should follow? What happens to social care as demographics change?
content.subject: Health and social care
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: One step ahead of type 1 diabetes: from experience to action
content.description: Early detection of type 1 diabetes changes care. How do we move from research advances to everyday clinical practice?
content.extendedDescription: Knowledge about early detection of type 1 diabetes has developed rapidly, opening up new opportunities in healthcare. But how do we put research findings into practice? In this seminar, we discuss how experience from research and pilot initiatives can become an integral part of everyday clinical work. Region Skåne is highlighted as an example, with a focus on how approaches can be implemented widely, what structures are needed and how healthcare services, decision-makers and patient organisations can contribute. The aim is to show how early detection can become a natural part of tomorrow's healthcare.
content.subject: Health and social care
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Build your digital immune system – vaccinate yourself against cyber threats
content.description: Rapid digitalisation creates new vulnerabilities affecting both individuals and societal functions. By raising the baseline level of cybersecurity, we can strengthen our collective resilience and reduce the effects of cyberattacks.
content.extendedDescription: CYVAC, Cybervaccination, is an interactive introductory cybersecurity training programme designed to strengthen basic knowledge and resilience against current cyber threats. It covers key areas such as password management, phishing and everyday digital security. During the event, you will first see a demonstration of CYVAC and then have the opportunity to try the exercises yourself. Bring your own computer if you would like to try it.
content.subject: Education

content.title: The Swedish egg boom – preparedness and confidence in the future
content.description: Sweden's food preparedness and nutritional supply are crucial in uncertain times. Eggs are a nutritious source of protein and an important part of everyday life. The industry is growing through investment, increased production and export opportunities. How can we make the most of the Swedish egg boom?
content.extendedDescription: The breakfast event opens with Svenska Ägg, followed by industry representatives and invited guests discussing the egg industry and its importance for Sweden's food preparedness. The conversation highlights eggs as a nutritious everyday protein source, investment in increased production, opportunities for future growth and exports, and reflections on how Sweden can make the most of the Swedish egg boom.
content.subject: Food

content.title: The events sector's contribution to the economy
content.description: How large is the events industry? How do its activities contribute to the economy?
content.extendedDescription: In 2021, Svensk Scenkonst, Svensk Live, Riksidrottsförbundet and Visita came together with BFUF (Besöksnäringens forsknings- och utvecklingsfond) around the project “Evenemang i siffror”, aiming to produce relevant and reliable national statistics. The partners saw the need to strengthen knowledge about the industry and how it can develop, not least as a basis for priorities and political decisions. The conversation will explore questions such as: how large is the events industry? How do its activities contribute to related industries such as hospitality and tourism?
content.subject: Visitor economy
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Defending the whole of society – what role should civil society play in crisis and war?
content.description: Sweden is strengthening its total defence. But strong civil defence is not built by public agencies, municipalities and regions alone. It also rests on people's engagement, volunteering, local networks, nonprofit organisations and faith communities. So what role should civil society actually play in civil defence?
content.extendedDescription: What does the Defence Commission say about volunteering, public involvement and staffing? How can civil society contribute to stronger civil defence, and what is needed to realise its potential? How should funding be designed to make civil society a real part of preparedness, rather than merely a resource we hope will be there when crisis strikes?
content.subject: Security/defence
content.accessibility: The event is captioned, Hearing loop, Wheelchair-accessible toilet, Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: How do we strengthen Sweden's payment infrastructure?
content.description: As geopolitical tensions have increased and transatlantic relations have weakened, Europe's and Sweden's independence and strategic autonomy have come into focus. One widely debated issue is our heavy dependence on American suppliers and technology, particularly for payment systems.
content.extendedDescription: What risks does this dependence entail? How do we strengthen Sweden's payment preparedness and build more resilient financial infrastructure? What solutions should we consider? What aspects need consideration from a supervisory perspective? And what risks, such as fraud and financial crime, should be taken into account?
content.subject: Economy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Moderator and Head of Strategic Ownerships & Partnerships

content.title: Innovation or stagnation: Sweden's choices for patients in 2035
content.description: Sweden's investments in research, prevention and the introduction of new treatments determine the care patients will have access to in 2035.
content.extendedDescription: This seminar highlights two alternative futures: a Sweden that invests in innovation and gives patients faster, more equitable access, and a Sweden where stagnant systems, slow adoption and growing global price pressures constrain progress. We discuss what is needed to secure medical breakthroughs, prevent disease and maintain our competitiveness, starting from patient benefit. The conversation opens with Eva Nordmark in the hot seat, followed by a panel discussion.
content.subject: Health and social care

content.title: Electric cars for everyone – democratising the electric car
content.description: Electrification is underway, and the opportunity to open it up to more people is greater than ever. What can actually get the market to take its next leap? We know that when the conditions are right, things happen.
content.extendedDescription:
Access to charging could effectively double the electric car market. And once people have switched, they do not choose to go back. That is a strong signal: the potential is already here.
Now the task is to make taking the step easier, more accessible and more affordable for more people. When we solve charging, we also unlock demand. Here is a concrete opportunity both to accelerate electrification and make it more inclusive.
content.subject: Energy
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Lead for Behaviour and Mobility Issues

content.title: AI in central government – how do we take the leap without stumbling?
content.description: According to the government's AI strategy, Sweden aims to become the world leader in AI in public administration. So how can public agencies use AI to develop their operations without compromising legal certainty, quality and public trust?
content.extendedDescription:
In this seminar, directors-general and central government leaders discuss operational uses of AI, how to accelerate adoption, and how to ensure accountability, control and transparency. The discussion also addresses what is needed to build trust internally and externally, and how to avoid every agency reinventing the wheel. Participants share experiences and look ahead.

Coffee and breakfast sandwiches will be served.
content.subject: Digitalisation

content.title: When the silent majority awakens – changing norms, from collective insights to new behaviours
content.description: How can the silent majority – those unseen in media clips and party leaders' debates – awaken and lead Sweden towards a shift in norms?
content.extendedDescription: Public debate can sometimes make interest in sustainability and circularity sound low. Yet political scientists describe relatively strong interest in sustainability among many people, even if it is not voters' top priority. Across the country, many people are reacting to rising emissions and shortcomings in measures for circularity and sustainability. Together, we explore how the silent majority – those unseen in media clips and party leaders' debates – awakens and leads Sweden towards a shift in norms. Welcome to contribute your perspectives!
content.subject: Sustainability

content.title: Where camping stoves meet societal collapse – in the same grab bag
content.description: Outdoor recreation benefits society in many ways, but in these uncertain times it is greatly underestimated as a preparedness resource.
content.extendedDescription: We invite you to a lively, entertaining and important live podcast about why outdoor recreation and the outdoor movement are among Sweden's most underestimated preparedness resources. We explore how everyday outdoor habits, such as packing a backpack, cooking on a camping stove or keeping warm outdoors, are actually preparedness. We show how people who already enjoy outdoor activities often have a complete emergency kit without knowing it, and how outdoor recreation genuinely strengthens our civil preparedness.
content.subject: Security/defence
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: What is around the corner for business – which trends are shaping the future?
content.description: AI partners and the diminishing role of screens. A longing for physical products, a vintage boom and microgeneration as more people prepare for emergencies in uncertain times: which emerging trends are shaping the future and could significantly affect business?
content.extendedDescription: Welcome to a session spotting emerging signals with Dagens industri, identifying trends now taking shape at the margins of society. We look for signals in niche groups, research labs and obscure platforms: phenomena that have yet to reach the mainstream but could become decisive for companies and organisations in the coming years. What new opportunities, risks and needs are emerging? And how can you become an accomplished trend spotter yourself?
content.subject: Business
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Norrbotten's industrial transition, Sweden and the future
content.description: Norrbotten's industry is in the midst of a historic transition. What is happening, how is it going, and is anything else needed?
content.extendedDescription:
Welcome to a breakfast seminar on the industrial transition in Norrbotten!

Norrbotten holds many of the strategic assets and raw materials that strengthen Sweden's competitiveness and enable EU independence. What is actually happening in transitions and new establishments, and is anything missing for them to succeed?

We discuss this using a new report released by Region Norrbotten at this seminar: an updated version of the widely noted report launched at Norra Scen two years ago.
content.subject: Regional issues
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Chair of the Regional Executive Board
Member of Parliament on the Committee on Industry and Trade

content.title: The Capital of Scandinavia – reality or branding dream: can Stockholm beat Copenhagen and Oslo?
content.description: Stockholm has long positioned itself as Scandinavia's leading growth engine, with strong innovative capacity and appeal to capital and talent.
content.extendedDescription:
Meanwhile, competition is growing from Copenhagen and Oslo, which are investing aggressively in urban development, infrastructure and the business climate to attract tomorrow's companies.

As capital becomes more selective and talent more mobile, demands increase for attractive environments, functioning ecosystems and rapid delivery. The question is whether Stockholm already holds, or risks losing, its position, and what role urban development plays in strengthening the region's long-term competitiveness.
content.subject: Innovation

content.title: How crucial is Stockholm's identity to competing as a global city?
content.description: How does the city's identity affect competitiveness in practice, and what is needed for Stockholm to remain relevant and leading among tomorrow's global cities?
content.extendedDescription: Stockholm's identity, shaped by trust, innovation, wellbeing, openness and collaboration, has been crucial to our position as one of Europe's leading innovation environments. Global competition for talent, capital, companies and ideas is intensifying. In an era of AI and global uncertainty, competitiveness depends on a city's collective ability to deliver innovation, stability and quality of life. A conversation about important issues for a global city. What will determine Stockholm's future performance? What are tomorrow's priorities?
content.subject: Visitor economy

content.title: From paralysis to action – closing the cybersecurity gap
content.description: Sweden is no longer heading into a cyber threat landscape: we are in the middle of it. According to Svenskt Säkerhetsindex 2026, 7 out of 10 decision-makers see the threats as serious, but many still lack a clear direction for action. The result is a gap between awareness and action.
content.extendedDescription: This seminar brings together leading stakeholders from business, the public sector and research to unpack what works, what is missing and what must be done now. The focus is on concrete choices about how organisations can structure their security work, mobilise the right expertise and create preparedness that works in practice, not just on paper.
content.subject: Security/defence

content.title: What is happening in Israel and Palestine? What do we do with our knowledge of events? What is our responsibility?
content.description: Sharing news about the situation in Israel and Palestine is as difficult to grasp as it is harrowing. We need the ability to tell what we know without shying away from the difficult and complex. How do we strike that balance? Can we bear to take in what is happening, or is truth being sacrificed? What do we know, and what never even gets out?
content.extendedDescription: What moral responsibility do we have to stand up for what we hear and read? What can each of us contribute? What is justice in these issues, and how do we speak truthfully about what is happening? What is Sweden's legal responsibility?
content.subject: International affairs
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Journalist, Middle East Analyst, Associate Senior Fellow
Member of Parliament, Vice Chair of the Committee on Foreign Affairs
Director, Swedish Christian Study Center Jerusalem

content.title: What do youth politicians want from development aid?
content.description: In many countries, Generation Z is driving democratic development, but what does global engagement look like among Sweden's youth politicians?
content.extendedDescription:
In this seminar, representatives of political youth organisations must take a stand on key questions:
- How large should Sweden's development aid be?
- Which countries and issues should aid focus on, and is it right to use aid as a tool for Swedish interests?
- And perhaps most importantly, what role can young people play in the struggle for a safer, more democratic world?

Expect an international outlook, quick answers and, hopefully, clear visions for the future. All participants have completed IM's aid compass.
content.subject: Democracy

content.title: What do we really know about the media?
content.description: Threats and hatred against journalists. Disputed trust figures. Polarisation and the power of algorithms. Debate about the media's role is ever-present, but what does research actually say?
content.extendedDescription:
Three of Sweden's leading media researchers meet in a fact-based conversation about what we actually know about today's media landscape. Which assumptions about the media are true, and which are not? What does trust in journalism look like? How are Swedish media affected by politics and audience behaviour? And what crucial knowledge gaps remain?

A conversation about the research behind the headlines and what we need to understand better to discuss the future of the media.
content.subject: Media/journalism
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Professor of Media and Communication Studies

content.title: The megatrends shaping the built environment – AI, sustainability and a new world order
content.description: Geopolitical uncertainty, accelerating climate requirements and AI breakthroughs are changing the playing field for the entire built environment sector. Meanwhile, an uncertain macroeconomic outlook, with higher interest rates, squeezed investment and weaker growth, creates new challenges for the industry.
content.extendedDescription:
What happens to investment, urban development and business models when conditions shift in real time? And how is the industry preparing for a future in which digital intelligence, resource scarcity and new regulations set the agenda?

In this forward-looking conversation, leading stakeholders from property, business and politics dissect the forces currently driving the transition, and what is needed to stay ahead.
content.subject: Construction
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: The threat to democracy: young people, war and a changing world order
content.description: How is young people's trust in democracy affected when leaders depart from shared agreements and political decisions contribute to conflict, global instability and growing migration and security threats?
content.extendedDescription:
Young people's trust in democratic institutions is declining while the world is marked by war, growing security threats and increasing migration challenges.
Historically, conflicts have led to increases in terrorism, migration flows and economic instability. At the same time, we see a global trend towards increasingly criminalising migrants and closing borders.
What consequences does this have for democracy and young people's confidence in the future?
content.subject: Democracy

content.title: The downside of patient choice – who pays the price for today's access?
content.description: Patient choice has improved access for many patients. Resources, expertise and training responsibilities are distributed between providers with a focus on rapid access, risking weaker long-term skills provision and quality in healthcare.
content.extendedDescription:
A seminar on the consequences of patient choice for the entire healthcare system, from today's patient encounters to tomorrow's specialists.
In today's patient choice system, it is very unclear how training responsibilities should follow patients when they are no longer treated in public healthcare. How will tomorrow's specialists gain practical experience of care provided by private providers?
content.subject: Health and social care
speakerTitles: Head of the Health and Social Care Department
Regional Commissioner for Health and Medical Care

content.title: Abortion rights, sex education and youth clinics – what do politicians want?
content.description: We need to talk about sex in politics. When will all young people have a youth clinic in their home municipality? How can all students receive equally good education on sexuality, consent and relationships? And should home abortions be possible without a required hospital visit?
content.extendedDescription: RFSU President Lina Fridén puts the parties on the spot in Almedalen's most burning debate on issues that easily get overlooked, despite affecting us all. What concrete proposals are our politicians advancing to strengthen sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR)?
content.subject: Human rights
speakerTitles: Member of Parliament and Spokesperson on LGBTQI Rights and Children's Rights
Member of Parliament and Healthcare Policy Spokesperson
Member of Parliament and Group Leader

content.title: From Swedish phenomenon to global hype – how can more brands succeed abroad?
content.description: Swedish brands, from sweets to beauty products, are taking the world by storm. Trends, e-commerce and social media have opened new markets and created new routes to consumers. How does this change the rules of international trade? What barriers do companies face when they want to export digitally?
content.extendedDescription: Several Swedish brands have gone from local favourites to global phenomena, helping create more jobs, drive innovation and strengthen the image of Sweden and Swedish companies abroad. What do these successes tell us about building a global following? How do global marketplaces change the rules for reaching customers far beyond Sweden?
content.subject: Business
speakerTitles: Head of public policy, Nordics and CEE

content.title: AI, jobs and society – what will the consequences be, and how well prepared are we?
content.description: With AI development, Sweden is undergoing a technological shift that will change society and how we work. What will the consequences be, and how well prepared are Swedish society and Swedish companies? How do we seize the opportunities AI brings?
content.extendedDescription:
A warm welcome to Superkraft Sverige, the podcast about Sweden's strengths and how we seize our opportunities. If we could remake Sweden today, what would we keep and what would we leave behind? And do we need a new story about Sweden?

In this episode, produced in collaboration with PwC, we focus on AI. What effects is AI expected to have, and how do we make sure we seize its opportunities?
content.subject: Economy

content.title: The labour market policy that disappeared – concrete action is now needed
content.description: At a time when unemployment goes hand in hand with skills shortages, better labour market policy is needed. What support do unemployed people actually want, and what investments are needed to make matching work? Does Arbetsförmedlingen's role need to change?
content.extendedDescription: Drawing on a new survey by Fackförbundet ST, we discuss what measures are needed to genuinely turn around Sweden's unemployment figures: we have asked both unemployed people and Arbetsförmedlingen staff. For example, we ask whether it is time to scrap digital meetings and reopen employment service offices instead.
content.subject: Employment/labour market
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Head of the Labour Market Section

content.title: AI and edge computing – key technologies for modern defence capability
content.description: Traditional AI relies on centralised infrastructure. But future conflicts take place in disrupted and dynamic environments. How do distributed AI and robust edge infrastructure create real-time operational impact?
content.extendedDescription:
Is Sweden prepared to build AI capability for peacetime's connected environment, or for the disrupted reality of war?

Who takes responsibility for Sweden developing distributed, resilient AI capability, and how quickly must it happen?

How must Swedish defence procurement change to enable AI that actually works on the front line?
content.subject: Security/defence
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Senior Consultant, former Head of Air and Space Materiel at FMV Rote, Member of Krigsvetenskapsakademin

content.title: From social sustainability to measurable business value
content.description: What is social sustainability actually worth? How do investments in Gottsunda Centrum affect jobs, safety and the local economy, and how can social initiatives create both socioeconomic and commercial value?
content.extendedDescription: Safer places, more people in work and stronger local entrepreneurship are often described as social sustainability. But what are they actually worth? Together with RISE, Hemmaplan has analysed how investments in Gottsunda Centrum affect employment, the local economy, safety and the area's long-term attractiveness. Three years of research show how social effects can be translated into socioeconomic and commercial value. A conversation about why tomorrow's property owners need to understand more than square metres.
content.subject: Other
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Chair of the Municipal Executive Board

content.title: Hydrogen, e-fuels and energy preparedness – a key to stronger security of supply
content.description: How robust are Sweden's energy and raw material supplies in an uncertain world?
content.extendedDescription:
Please note that the entire hydrogen arena is broadcast via the link above.

This seminar focuses on the role of hydrogen and e-fuels in strengthening security of supply and preparedness.
The conversation starts from the need to reduce vulnerabilities linked to import dependence and highlights how domestic production of energy carriers and inputs can strengthen resilience in the energy system and industrial value chains. We discuss hydrogen's role both as an energy carrier and as an input for e-fuels and, for example, fertiliser production, as well as what is needed to enable robust, sustainable long-term systems in Sweden.
content.subject: Energy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Sustainable food production – from global responsibility to Swedish policy
content.description: How does our food system affect the climate, biodiversity and animal welfare? What are the conditions, and how can Swedish policy influence them?
content.extendedDescription: An introduction with presentations of Axfood Mat2030, setting out the measures different stakeholders, including political decision-makers, need to take from a sustainability perspective to achieve sustainable food production and consumption. Naturskyddsföreningen's view of sustainable agriculture. Politicians are questioned about the effects of food production and consumption on the climate, biodiversity and animal welfare. All parliamentary parties participate, mainly through the Committee on Environment and Agriculture. The question session is led by Vi Konsumenter and World Animal Protection.
content.subject: Food

content.title: A lifelong cultural promise – for a society that thrives
content.description: Culture improves our wellbeing, reduces stress and boosts public health. But a coordinated approach is missing. How do we guarantee every child a dose of cultural medicine, stressed workers theatre through their wellness allowance, and music for older and ill people who cannot get to a concert themselves?
content.extendedDescription: Engaging with culture improves our wellbeing, reduces stress and boosts public health. Study after study demonstrates this. Yet a coordinated approach is still missing. The seminar aims to discuss structural change through cultural guarantees for children and young people throughout their school years and for older people in residential care, as well as wellness allowances for everyone in work.
content.subject: Culture
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
speakerTitles: Chair of Region Skåne's Primary Care Committee
Chair of the Municipal Executive Board

content.title: Enough is enough – new steps towards greater safety
content.description: Sweden faces a serious societal challenge, with too many children drawn into gang-related violence, crime and destructive environments, often before society's support reaches them. Recruitment is rapid and systematic, with consequences affecting all of society. How do we act together?
content.extendedDescription: For a long time, society's response to young people in gang crime has mainly been reactive and focused on law enforcement. Yet developments clearly show that this is not enough. How do we move from reaction to prevention before children are drawn into violence? It is time to move from words to action and seriously develop the close collaboration between a range of societal stakeholders needed to create real change.
content.subject: Justice/crime
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: AI in public procurement – better deals, or not?
content.description: When technology can review procurement documents in seconds, new questions arise: can AI contribute to better decisions, higher quality and stronger competition? Do we risk major changes to the value-creating purchasing process by relying too heavily on an AI assistant?
content.extendedDescription:
In this conversation, we explore how AI can change the playing field for public procurement, how collaboration between the public sector and companies is affected, and which perspectives will be crucial going forward.

The panel brings together public sector stakeholders, suppliers and AI experts to highlight opportunities, risks and concrete experience of how AI is already used in procurement today.
content.subject: Digitalisation
speakerTitles: Head of Finance and Operational Support

content.title: Funding adult and community education – whose responsibility?
content.description: Adult and community education reaches hundreds of thousands of people each year, but how is it funded? The state, municipalities and regions share responsibility, but the picture is uneven.
content.extendedDescription: In a new report, Folkbildningsrådet commissioned Governo to map structures, challenges and opportunities in support for adult and community education. A conversation about the report “Folkbildningens flernivåfinansiering” and what its findings mean in practice: for local associations, municipal or regional politicians allocating resources, and the national level setting the framework. How can the state, regions and municipalities collaborate better for stable, long-term funding? And what adult and community education can we afford in the future?
content.detail: Room D22 – floor 2 – Betty Petterssons hus
content.subject: Democracy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Robustness starts in everyday life, not in systems
content.description: Society's robustness depends not only on plans, stockpiles and systems, but on what people can actually do when something happens. We have built efficient structures while losing practical everyday skills. What role do local knowledge, relationships and skills play when systems are no longer enough?
content.extendedDescription: Preparedness is often described in terms of organisation, responsibility and resources. But a crucial part of society's resilience lies closer to home, with people themselves. The ability to mend, grow, repair and cooperate locally has gradually weakened. When disruptions occur, the question becomes concrete: if systems fail, what can we do ourselves?
content.subject: Security/defence
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Head of Innovation and Attractiveness Section (moderator)
Regional Councillor, Chair of the Labour Market, Business and Attractiveness Committee

content.title: Relationships and collaboration boost the local economy
content.description: New solutions are needed to shape robust and resilient communities. This involves both organisation and funding for sustainable local solutions through interaction between the public, private and nonprofit sectors.
content.extendedDescription: This is the third of our four seminars on “Lokal ekonomi - sätt ekonomin på plats?”. In this seminar, we explain how local solutions to societal challenges can be scaled up through collaboration between local capital, public stakeholders and innovative financial players. We also present proposals for how policy can achieve greater leverage from public funds and unlock the innovative capacity of the local and social economy. A short introduction followed by conversation.
content.subject: Economy
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Can a neighbourhood for young people become an engine for Sweden's innovation?
content.description: How many ideas, innovations and future entrepreneurs does Sweden miss out on when young people lack equal opportunities? When too few perspectives are represented, we risk losing talent, development and future competitiveness, even though diversity strengthens growth.
content.extendedDescription: How do we create more safe and inspiring settings where young people's ideas, entrepreneurship and innovative capacity can grow, regardless of background and circumstances? Kvarteret Fryshuset is a historic initiative that will become the world's largest holistic meeting place for young people. Using it as a starting point, we explore how meeting places for young people can contribute to both social sustainability and Sweden's future capacity for innovation.
content.subject: Children/young people
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Media and power: from crisis to comeback, rebuilding after trust collapses
content.description: The media have great power to shape our thoughts, but who has real power over the media? Senior executives, politicians, individual journalists, or communications professionals and lobbyists?
content.extendedDescription:
Companies and organisations today operate in a landscape where crises quickly become public and communications are scrutinised in real time. Trust is one of a brand's most important assets, but it can also collapse quickly. How should companies and stakeholders act when criticism grows and trust falters? What strategies are needed to handle criticism, public opinion and uncertainty in the public eye? How do you rebuild trust once it has been damaged?
A conversation about crisis management, accountability and rebuilding trust.

In a series of questioning sessions, Dagens Media and Resumé put leading figures in media, advertising, PR and communications in the spotlight.
content.subject: Media/journalism
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: The taxi industry – from deadlock to solutions
content.description: Urban travel patterns are becoming increasingly dynamic, with a seamless mix of sustainable, digital and shared transport modes. The transport sector explicitly focuses on accessibility, reliability and efficiency to meet future challenges.
content.extendedDescription:
By contrast, the taxi industry is marked by conflict and outdated regulations. This creates ambiguity for decision-makers and uncertainty for those working in the industry. What is needed to move from deadlock to solutions?

To mark the launch of Sweco's updated report “Taxibranschen i Sverige”, we bring together decision-makers and industry stakeholders to discuss how regulations can be modernised, clearer rules created and taxis' full potential realised in future mobility systems.
content.subject: Climate/environment
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Who supports young people who are struggling?
content.description:
Mental ill health among young people is increasing and is one of Sweden's biggest public health challenges; suicide is the most common cause of death among young people. Long waiting times make the problems worse.
- How do we get more adults to act in time when healthcare is not enough?
- Who does what: the state/society, parents and civil society?
content.extendedDescription:
Johanniterhjälpen highlights MHFA – Mental Health First Aid – as a concrete, evidence-based method for strengthening adults' ability to act. It provides tools to spot early signs, dare to ask questions and guide people towards appropriate support.

The seminar is a discussion between different stakeholders, including politicians, schools, civil society and leisure services, about how we can jointly shorten the path from initial concern to intervention.
content.subject: Children/young people

content.title: Do we need more or less Swedish moderation in the AI era?
content.description: The government's ambition is for Sweden to rank among the world's ten leading countries in AI. But the question is how we get there and why it matters, and whether AI is the answer to all our questions or the last thing we need.
content.extendedDescription:
What values should characterise Sweden as an AI nation, and how do we become the best at sustainable, responsible and reliable AI? Is there a common thread in Sweden's history of trust, safety, sustainability, equality and collaboration that can guide us in the AI era? Is Sweden's AI strategy what we need to build a Swedish AI miracle, and is the Swedish labour market model a secret superpower as the labour market is reshaped?

Welcome to an unusually reasonable conversation about carving out a Swedish path through the AI transformation.
content.subject: Employment/labour market
speakerTitles: Expert on AI, Transition and Lifelong Learning

content.title: How do we build value chains, business models and demand that secure hydrogen's future?
content.description: Despite technically mature projects, major industrial ambitions and various EU regulations and directives, demand for hydrogen remains limited. Value chains and their associated business models are often insufficiently developed to enable investment decisions.
content.extendedDescription:
Please note that the entire hydrogen arena is broadcast via the link above.

In this seminar, we highlight how industry and policymakers need to jointly show the way forward so that hydrogen can contribute to a robust, strong and competitive Sweden across industry, transport and energy. What obstacles stand in the way of progress, and how do we overcome them together?
content.subject: Energy

content.title: A crossroads for Swedish polar research
content.description: If we can break ice, we can also break new ground in polar research.
content.extendedDescription:
There is broad support for Sweden investing in a new research icebreaker to succeed Oden. This is an important investment for maintaining our strong Arctic research and enabling major infrastructure projects such as Polar Connect. But what other opportunities and added value could such an investment create for research and international cooperation?

Polar Connect is a northern European initiative to enable a fibre connection between Europe and Asia via the Arctic, thereby contributing to more secure global communications.
content.subject: Research

content.title: Norrbotten – Sweden's Klondike?
content.description: Is Sweden's northernmost county good for anything beyond supplying the rest of the country with natural resources?
content.extendedDescription:
Welcome to a breakfast seminar on cultural policy!

Iron ore, forests and hydropower have made, and continue to make, Sweden a wealthy country. But what is a society without culture, and what happens when the market proves unable to provide what gives our lives meaning?

We ask how continued and renewed demand for the raw materials extracted in Norrbotten affects those who live and work there. How is this portrayed in art, film, literature and music, and what makes a community attractive? The discussion opens with a conversation about the book Mjuk makt with author and journalist Martin Gelin.

content.title: Patients have a right to their own data – and to the experiences of others
content.description: Sweden has a long tradition of collecting data through patient records, biobanks, clinical trials and health data registers. New legislation and rapid AI development open up new opportunities, but also challenges concerning privacy and security in collecting and using health data.
content.extendedDescription:
The seminar discusses experience from establishing a data lake in Region Skåne, the industry's perspective, and how to maximise the benefits of health data while safeguarding patient safety.

This event is part of Life Science Day, an initiative of the Medicon Village research park.
content.subject: Health and social care
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: AI, stablecoins and tokenisation – what will the financial system of the future look like?
content.description: Technological development is accelerating, from research, development and innovation to new products and services. Two areas are expected to have a particularly strong impact on finance: AI and blockchain technology, where tokenisation and stablecoins could become central to future financial systems.
content.extendedDescription: What exactly are blockchains, tokenisation and stablecoins? How will these new technologies and products shape future financial systems? What value could this create for customers, business and society as a whole? Welcome to a conversation about the financial system of the future and the technology that will shape it.
content.subject: Digitalisation
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Moderator and Head of SEB's Newsroom

content.title: Sexual harassment and discrimination go unrecognised – those affected are left to cope alone
content.description: Stable figures mean nothing is changing. Are we seeing the normalisation and neutralisation of sexual harassment and discrimination in the Swedish labour market? The current system fails to identify the problems, and signs of changing attitudes are now emerging.
content.extendedDescription: For the fifth time, the working population's exposure to sexual harassment and discrimination at work is being measured. Together with experts and social partners, we draw on this year's report to pinpoint what needs to change in Swedish workplaces. With Kommunal and Akademikerförbundet SSR, we discuss how Trakasseribarometern's insights can be used to work towards change.
content.subject: Gender equality
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

Deputy Chief Executive of the Association

content.title: When crisis strikes – securing access to essential goods and services
content.description: Sweden's preparedness agencies are to prevent vulnerabilities and maintain operations during heightened preparedness. But what preparations must our companies make to help in crisis and war?
content.extendedDescription: Supply preparedness concerns everyone and has come increasingly into focus. Sweden's preparedness agencies have a special responsibility to draw up supply plans securing access to essential goods and services. Meanwhile, the role and responsibility of business are widely debated. This seminar highlights supply preparedness challenges and invites representatives of key stakeholders to chart the way forward.
content.detail: Main hall, entrance from Korsgatan opposite Villa Gutebagge

speakerTitles: Head of Food and Drinking Water Supply Department
Head of Information Technology and Command and Control Systems

content.title: How do the parliamentary parties want to promote inclusion?
content.description: How can everyone enter the labour market, participate actively in society and improve their living conditions? What proposals are the parliamentary parties advancing, and what integration policies are they campaigning on?
content.extendedDescription: Belong works to enable everyone to enter the labour market, participate actively in society and improve their living conditions. But what proposals are the parliamentary parties advancing? Belong presents its election survey Integrationsvalet 2026, showing the integration policies on which the parties are campaigning. Immediately afterwards, panellists debate their proposals for a more inclusive Sweden. Labour market policy experts then comment on the panel discussion and analyse how we can promote labour market integration.
content.subject: Integration/diversity

content.title: Welcome in – making the Swedish music industry a place for more young people
content.description: How can the music industry help open more doors and create long-term career paths? What role do culture and music play in society for young people, and what responsibility do record labels, music publishers and live event organisers have for integration in the industry? And what political decisions can make a real difference?
content.extendedDescription: Drawing on the joint industry initiative You+ Music, representatives of the music industry, civil society and politics discuss how more young people with different backgrounds and experiences can enter the industry, and why it matters. A conversation about talent, structures and how music and culture can become a real engine for integration.
content.subject: Integration/diversity
speakerTitles: Inclusion Strategist and Cultural Producer, Moderator

content.title: The role of adult education in regional development
content.description: Skills supply is a key issue in regional development, and adult education is a key player in skills supply. How do you develop adult education to play that role most effectively?
content.extendedDescription: Everyone agrees that adult education plays a crucial role in regional skills supply. But not everyone agrees on how that role should be played, or on the most effective division of responsibilities between adult education, regional employers and political governance. The seminar presents expectations, opportunities and practical examples from various representatives working on regional development.
content.subject: Education
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Head of Business and Skills Supply Unit

content.title: Supply preparedness for housing: when the chain breaks, who takes responsibility?
content.description: The housing sector is an essential societal function, responsible for heat, water, electricity, sanitation and the building components needed for operation and restoration.
content.extendedDescription:
In Almedalen, we have talked about collaboration for years. But we talk less often about what happens when collaboration is not enough, because that is when it becomes real.

To put it in a concrete situation:
It is -15 degrees. District heating fails in an area with 3,000 apartments.
The emergency service is operating. Contractors are available. Contracts are in place.
But there is nothing to deliver.

Response time is meaningless when resources are missing.

As a housing company, we are the last link in the chain, but the first to receive the call.
content.subject: Construction

content.title: How do we protect general elections together?
content.description: Sweden holds general elections on 13 September. In a deteriorating security environment and amid rapid technological development, democratic elections need protection against threats such as disinformation and influence campaigns. What do the threats look like, and how do the responsible agencies work to secure elections?
content.extendedDescription: The security situation, rapid technological development and experience from other European elections show that democratic elections must be protected against various threats, particularly disinformation and influence campaigns. What do these threats look like, and what are the responsible agencies doing individually and together to protect the conduct of elections and maintain trust in the democratic process?
content.subject: Democracy
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: How do we remove digital barriers in society?
content.description: Differences in digital skills can reinforce existing inequalities in society. Digital services are often designed without considering people whose needs fall outside the norm. When technical perspectives dominate, important societal values such as accessibility, participation and democracy risk being lost.
content.extendedDescription:
The mapping identifies everyday situations in which digital barriers arise and concrete measures to improve digital inclusion. The report was produced by Terese Raymond of Digidelnätverket on behalf of Region Gotland.
It is highly relevant to other regions and stakeholders and has already been widely circulated. A panel of participants from Region Gotland describes the initiatives they have undertaken and what they hope to see in the future.
content.subject: Digitalisation

content.title: Politics' new view of the media – who sets the rules?
content.description: Politicians no longer need traditional media to reach people. Through their own channels, messages can go directly to audiences without journalists acting as intermediaries. Meanwhile, media reporting and credibility are increasingly questioned, both by politicians and in public debate.
content.extendedDescription:
What happens to journalism's role when power over the narrative changes? How is political debate affected when parties and those in power can set the agenda on their own terms? And who scrutinises those who choose to bypass traditional media?

The seminar brings together politicians, media representatives and researchers to discuss the changing balance of power between politics and journalism, and what it means for democracy, trust and the future media landscape.
content.subject: Media/journalism
speakerTitles: Professor of Media and Communication Studies

content.title: Putting the economy in its place – how can local economies drive sustainable community development?
content.description: Economics and business administration are disciplines that leave place out of the picture. We challenge these academic disciplines. We argue that local economics offers a third way of understanding an economy in a particular place, and can therefore also drive sustainable social change.
content.extendedDescription:
Drawing on a new book with the same title as the seminar, we discuss the theoretical foundations of local economics as a better tool than traditional disciplines for understanding the local context and engaging people, businesses and municipalities. There will be a 20-minute presentation followed by an open conversation. The presentation starts at 08.30, preceded by breakfast networking from 08.00.

Part 1 of 3

content.title: Joining forces for gender equality

TCO President Therese Svanström and Susannah Sjöberg, Chair of Sveriges kvinnoorganisationer, welcome you. We will also be joined by Emma Holten, author and feminist commentator.

We offer snacks, drinks and a wonderful feminist atmosphere!

A warm welcome!

When one stakeholder's by-product becomes another's raw material, both business and climate benefits can arise. This affects companies' calculations, the municipality's attractiveness and how we should think about future industrial areas.
In this conversation, we discuss how industrial symbiosis can contribute to sustainable growth, smarter business establishments and places the next generation wants to work in, invest in and be part of.

Supply chain transparency, climate requirements for materials and industry's ability to transition are crucial if the entire construction chain is to meet climate targets.
content.extendedDescription: This seminar focuses on industry's role in the climate transition. How can manufacturers reduce their products' climate footprint? What change – regulation, incentives or technology – would have the greatest effect right now? The seminar consists of short presentations by industry stakeholders followed by a moderated panel discussion with audience questions.

content.title: What must policymakers do to secure water supplies and save the Baltic Sea?
content.description: We face several simultaneous crises that risk worsening the situation unless policymakers address them in a coordinated way. Climate change and biodiversity loss affect the condition of our seas and undermine water quality and supplies internationally, nationally and locally.
content.extendedDescription: Protecting our seas, saving the Baltic Sea from dying and ensuring access to clean water require both cooperation and sufficient financial resources. Representatives of Miljöpartiet in the European Parliament, national politics and local politics on Gotland will attend the seminar to share their views of the challenges and solutions.

The question is how Sweden can contribute to greater energy security using the resources available.

Europe's reduced domestic production and heavy import dependence make the issue increasingly tangible for Sweden too. Capacity and expertise here can contribute to a more stable system, but the conditions are changing.

content.description: The construction and property sector accounts for substantial emissions, but its transition is too slow. content.extendedDescription:
Schoolchildren need more food during the school day: how can this be achieved? In a constructive and bold conversation, we create a concrete picture of school meals' importance for individuals, society and preparedness. The audience will also have opportunities to ask questions. The discussion is aimed at decision-makers, procurement managers, nutrition professionals and members of the public interested in children's health and learning, and effects on society and preparedness.

content.title: How can aviation contribute to connectivity across Sweden?
content.description: Aviation provides important connectivity in our long country. Smart combinations of transport modes can enable residents throughout Sweden to make day trips to larger cities. The government should set an ambitious connectivity target. How can policy ensure this in practice?
content.extendedDescription:
How can Sweden achieve domestic connectivity as good as Norway's, where flights serve around 50 smaller domestic destinations? We have many well-distributed airfields, but fewer and fewer routes. Many regions now have poorer connections to Stockholm and abroad: how can we change this? Do we need a nationwide route network so the whole country can be reached, ideally on day trips?

The panel includes representatives of the government, airlines and business.

content.title: Beyond the server hall: how data centres build communities
content.description: Data centres play an increasingly important role in Sweden's digitalisation, competitiveness and green transition. But what does establishing one mean for local development? This conversation discusses effects on jobs, investment and local development, as well as the sector's importance for Sweden's competitiveness, digitalisation and green transition. Business and political representatives meet for an open conversation about opportunities, challenges and future establishments.

content.title: The future of abortion – what do tomorrow's leaders want?

Swedish civil society took shape during much of the twentieth century under Social Democratic rule. But is there a conservative idea of civil society, and if so, what does it look like?

Professor Magnus Karlsson opens the seminar and presents his research during the first 15 minutes.

content.description: Sweden's forest industry supplies the world with important everyday products, creates 140,000 jobs across the country and is essential to the green transition. But declining and unpredictable raw material flows risk holding it back.

What rules need to be established for Sweden to remain a leading industrial nation with a growing bioeconomy? Welcome to a seminar where trade unions, employers and political representatives discuss one of the most crucial issues for our shared future.

content.title: Are parents the problem? Vocational programmes and tomorrow's upper secondary schools
content.description: To meet society's skills needs, between 40% and 50% of each age cohort would need to choose a vocational programme at upper secondary school. While young people's interest is growing, a new study suggests their guardians remain resistant.

Meanwhile, a new study suggests guardians still prefer their children to choose programmes preparing them for higher education. What should tomorrow's upper secondary schools look like to remain relevant to young people, guardians and society?
