content.title: Sweden in the AI era – from ambition to results
content.description: Sweden ranks 19th globally in AI, with a target of the top ten. The strategy is clear and investments have been allocated. But an implementation gap is opening between strategy and results.

The challenge is similar in the public and private sectors, as are the solutions. How can they learn from each other and scale together? content.title: Leadership in crisis – the role of companies in a robust society

content.title: Strengthening Sweden's competitiveness through commercialising research
content.description: The government wants Sweden to compete with the best in the world in technological development. A focus on excellence, internationalisation and innovation is therefore crucial.
content.extendedDescription: It is clear that research investment needs to be matched by putting findings to use and commercialising them. It is positive that the government is emphasising even more strongly that research should lead to more innovation, create more jobs and secure our welfare through concrete results and stronger competitiveness. Representatives of academia and business discuss further steps to move research towards commercialisation.
content.subject: Research
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: How does political manoeuvring affect actual policy?
content.description: How does political manoeuvring affect actual policy? Is Swedish politics in 2026 about ideologically driven visions, or hard compromises, tactical concessions and smart voter segmentation? Is reality either-or, or both?
content.extendedDescription:
At a time when the question of who will govern is more open than it has been for a long time, we delve deeper:
What will it take to win government after the election, and what is really at stake?

Experience Sveriges Radio's biggest political podcast, Det politiska spelet, live on stage. Presenter Parisa Höglund is joined by political commentators Fredrik Furtenbach and Helena Gissén, who, together with colleagues from P4 Gotland, offer a sharp, entertaining and informative show filled with analysis, surprises and audience-focused conversation.
content.subject: Media/journalism
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: How do we build the next global tech success? What will determine Sweden's next 20 years as a technology powerhouse
content.description: Over recent decades, Sweden has established itself as one of the world's most successful startup environments, with several global technology companies emerging from a small ecosystem. At the same time, international competition for capital, skills and innovation is intensifying.
content.extendedDescription: What political and structural conditions are needed for the next generation of global companies to be built in Sweden? The conversation focuses on growth regulations, access to capital and research funding, attracting international talent and the importance of competitive employee stock option programmes. How can decision-makers and business jointly strengthen Sweden's position as a leading technology nation over the next 20 years?
content.subject: Business
speakerTitles: Head of the EU Single Market Unit

content.title: Sudan – the world's largest humanitarian catastrophe?
content.description: How can cooperation between governments, the UN, civil society and business strengthen the response in Sudan, where one of the world's largest humanitarian catastrophes has left over 30 million people needing support, more than half of them children whose homes, schools and families have been torn apart by conflict?
content.extendedDescription:
The crisis in Sudan is marked by massive internal displacement, lack of protection and collapsed public services. Despite this, the crisis is severely underfunded and receives limited international attention.

Sweden is an important humanitarian donor, channelling support through the UN and civil society organisations, including UNHCR and Rädda Barnen.

This conversation brings together some of the stakeholders with experience of navigating the Sudan crisis.
content.subject: International affairs

content.title: Is there a future for Sweden's airports?
content.description: Sweden's airports are at a crossroads. With declining domestic aviation, financial pressure and changing total defence needs, the entire airport network faces major questions about ownership, funding, function and societal benefit. What does the future hold for Sweden's airports?
content.extendedDescription:
What role should the state play in Sweden's airports, and how do we secure long-term connectivity, preparedness and regional development across the country?
At this seminar, we meet Anders Flanking, the government's special inquiry chair on the state's role as airport owner and operator, including Bromma, along with airport and airline representatives and a political panel, to discuss Sweden's future airport system.
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport
content.accessibility: Event captioning, hearing loop

content.title: Norwegian public procurement boosts competitiveness and climate action – can Sweden copy and paste?
content.description: A thousand billion kronor, or one trillion kronor: that is the annual value of public procurement in Sweden. Used well, parts of this procurement could provide powerful leverage to accelerate the climate transition and strengthen Sweden's competitiveness.
content.extendedDescription: Norway is already taking action. Since 2024, clear requirements for climate-smart solutions in public procurement are intended not only to reduce emissions but also to create development and business opportunities for Norwegian companies. How has it gone so far? What can Sweden learn from the Norwegian model? And what changes are needed to unlock procurement's full potential?
content.subject: Business
speakerTitles: Department Director responsible for Sustainable Procurement

content.title: Transformative change – when social sustainability, partnerships and ESG drive business value
content.description: How do companies identify where social sustainability actually creates business value? And what is needed to move from ambition to results?
content.extendedDescription:
How do companies identify where social sustainability actually creates business value? And what is needed to move from ambition to results? This seminar focuses on companies that integrate societal benefit into their core business and make it a competitive advantage.
Using concrete examples and sharp perspectives, we discuss how investment in social sustainability, strategic partnerships and collective impact can strengthen both profitability and relevance as demands for responsibility and transparency increase.
content.subject: Sustainability
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Everyone says they want nonprofit independent schools – why do politicians propose so many setbacks?
content.description: Sweden's independent school sector comprises many different types of providers. Alongside larger school groups are foundations, cooperatives and mission-driven organisations that do not operate to distribute profits.
content.extendedDescription:
There is broad political agreement that mission-driven schools are a valuable part of Swedish education. Meanwhile, extensive re-regulation of the school sector is underway, and many proposals under discussion risk affecting schools without a profit motive too.

The seminar's central question is therefore:
In its pursuit of problems linked to for-profit schools, is politics prepared to sacrifice schools run without a requirement to distribute profits?
content.subject: Education
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Head of Education/CEO and Convener of Rådet för Ideella friskolor

content.title: Recession, global uncertainty and climate transition – what challenges face the property market?
content.description: How does the uncertain market situation affect public and private property stakeholders, and how should they respond? What consequences do these developments have for municipalities and property owners? What are the actual challenges?
content.extendedDescription: Svefa's courtyard at Adelsgatan 25 is the natural meeting place for public and private stakeholders to exchange ideas, share knowledge, discuss property issues and build relationships both informally and formally. This year, we are collaborating with Fråga Lou and have created Fastighetshubben, offering a packed programme addressing important issues at the interface between private and public property market stakeholders. Breakfast conversations between market participants. A warm welcome!
content.subject: Economy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Leading when it matters – are central government employers ready for heightened preparedness?
content.description: In an uncertain world, government agencies need to adapt quickly, make decisions under pressure and get their entire organisations acting in coordination. This places demands on how central government employers organise work, staff operations and prepare managers and employees.
content.extendedDescription:
The seminar opens with a concrete example of how a government agency adapts when circumstances change. We discuss the employer issues that arise, how to secure skills and staffing, and how agencies build organisational capacity to act, preparedness and endurance in their own operations.

After the seminar, you are welcome to stay for Arbetsgivarverket's networking event in Länsstyrelsens trädgård until 19. Light food and drinks will be served.
content.subject: Employment/labour market

content.title: Can transforming major industries be profitable?
content.description: The climate transition is often criticised as expensive and dependent on subsidies, yet major industrial initiatives driven by real demand are underway. How can major industries reduce emissions while strengthening competitiveness and profitability? What rules are needed to enable this?
content.extendedDescription: The seminar starts from the fact that the transition is already underway in parts of Swedish industry, with investments motivated by customer requirements, market developments and long-term business decisions. Meanwhile, uncertainty about electricity prices, permitting, infrastructure and policy instruments affects which projects proceed, how they are financed and how quickly they can grow.
content.subject: Economy
speakerTitles: Erik Pedersen, Head of Governmental Relations Sweden

content.title: Psychological defence in a troubled world
content.description: We live in an uncertain and unpredictable world that requires strong psychological defence to safeguard an open, democratic society, free formation of opinion, and Sweden's freedom and independence. How can we jointly strengthen society's resilience and willingness to defend the country?
content.extendedDescription: Försvarsmakten, Myndigheten för civilt försvar and Myndigheten för psykologiskt försvar have an important task in protecting Sweden and strengthening its ability to resist cognitive threats from foreign powers and other threat actors. At the seminar, the agencies will discuss the importance of strong resilience and willingness to defend the country, the new national psychological defence strategy, and its implications for their joint work going forward.
content.subject: Democracy
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Head of the Capability Development Unit, Moderator

content.title: The role of biofuels in the maritime transition
content.description: The shipping industry must reduce emissions rapidly to meet the International Maritime Organization’s climate targets. Biogenic fuels are part of the solution, but transitioning to large-scale use requires long-term regulatory frameworks, a competitive market and broad collaboration.
content.extendedDescription:
In this seminar, Gotlandsbolaget brings together stakeholders from across the entire value chain. With perspectives ranging from biogas production facilities, through regulatory frameworks and all the way to vessels, we shift the discussion from long-term goals to opportunities available today. 

The seminar provides an in-depth look at how fuel markets, partnerships and regulatory measures can accelerate the shipping sector’s adoption of biofuels.
content.subject: Sustainability
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation

content.title: Extreme weather – a personal financial risk or society's responsibility?
content.description: Climate change brings heavier rainfall and resulting floods. What responsibility do housing developers and homeowners have, and what broader measures are needed across society? How are insurance premiums, access to mortgages and property prices in high-risk areas affected?
content.extendedDescription:
Climate change brings heavier rainfall and resulting floods. Rising seas and higher river flows increase the risks. Meanwhile, housing areas are being built and planned near shorelines and former quays and harbours.

What responsibility do housing developers and homeowners have, and what broader measures are needed across society? How are insurance premiums, access to mortgages and property prices in high-risk areas affected?
content.subject: Climate/environment
speakerTitles: Vice Mayor for Environment and Climate

content.title: Future-proofing social infrastructure properties – starting at the design stage
content.description: How do we future-proof social infrastructure properties as demands for sustainability, safety and resilience increase? The focus is on how design and construction can account for fire risks, physical protection, evacuation and robust technical systems.
content.extendedDescription: How do we secure essential properties and operations as demands for sustainability, safety and resilience increase? Properties and operations need to function day to day in a changing world marked by crises and evolving threats. Safety is a broad concept. This conversation discusses how design and construction need to account for fire risk, physical protection, sheltering in place and evacuation, robust technical systems and organisational challenges, including where current rules do not provide the full answer.
content.subject: Other
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: What does failure at school cost?
content.description: Every year, tens of thousands of pupils are failed by the Swedish school system. This costs both individuals and society dearly. What does educational failure cost, and what needs to be done so more pupils succeed at school?
content.extendedDescription: Pupils failing at school has major consequences for individuals and society as a whole. In collaboration with economist Ingvar Nilsson and behavioural scientist Eva Nilsson, Sveriges Lärare has made new calculations of the cost of educational failure. A clue: considerably more than preventing it would have cost. Welcome to a seminar where we present the figures and discuss what needs to be done.

content.description: What consequences will national implementation of the EU directive on the energy performance of buildings have for safeguarding cultural heritage values in the built environment? content.extendedDescription: During Almedalsveckan, we open Kulturmiljöarena Burmeisterska huset for discussions and conversations where issues of the historic environment, cultural heritage values and preservation meet today's and tomorrow's challenges in sustainability, climate and planning. As part of the European research project INHERIT, this seminar will discuss energy efficiency and preserving cultural heritage values from a policy perspective.

content.title: How do we reinvigorate investment in the climate transition?
content.description: According to a member survey by the Swedish branch of the world's largest corporate sustainability initiative, half the responding companies have reduced their investment in the sustainability transition over the past three years.
content.extendedDescription: What explains this development? What are its consequences for the pace of Sweden's transition, and how could it affect competitiveness and growth? What is needed to stimulate investment, and how can policymakers, business and the financial sector contribute? SEB and UNGC Sverige welcome you to a seminar on these questions in SEB's garden at Kinbergs Plats 5.

Head of Sustainability Strategy and Policy

content.description: Six in ten Swedes were exposed to criminal advertisements last year. At least 315,000 Swedes were defrauded of money, and the most common tools used were Meta-owned Facebook and Instagram. According to the Reuters news agency, Meta earns around 136 billion kronor a year from these advertising deals.
content.extendedDescription: What can media companies and organisations do to stop advertising fraud? And why do reputable companies continue buying advertising from Meta despite knowing that Facebook, for example, is used as a tool for crime? Have reputable publishers really done enough to offer advertisers competitive, legal alternatives? This discussion explores both the problem and possible solutions.

content.title: The importance of technological innovation for tomorrow's defence

content.extendedDescription: Civilian innovation is becoming increasingly important for our defence capability. Small and medium-sized companies, as well as startups, therefore play an important role in contributing solutions that strengthen supply capability, robustness and redundancy, for example. Welcome to a seminar highlighting technological innovation opportunities for future defence and discussing the policy and funding conditions needed to fully strengthen total defence's innovative capacity.

content.title: Supply and demand – who gets access to learning and culture?

content.extendedDescription: Libraries and adult and community education play a crucial role in cultural infrastructure across the country. Through presentations and conversations, we examine figures from the SOM survey and conclusions from the report “Vid Vägs ände”: the effects are particularly significant in rural and sparsely populated areas. Should culture and learning be accessible throughout the country? Following the presentations, a panel discusses the findings.

content.extendedDescription:
According to trade union DIK's cultural report, Umeå, Malmö and Västra Götalandsregionen invest the most in culture. Why do some municipalities and regions prioritise culture while the state reduces its investment? Is culture a luxury in difficult times, or an investment in democracy, public health and social cohesion?
This conversation brings together politicians from three of Sweden's highest-investing municipalities and regions in culture to discuss what actually happens to a community when culture is strengthened, and what is at stake when it is deprioritised.

content.title: From tithes to a billionaire tax – taxation according to ability to pay, then, now and in the future
content.description: For most of history, tax has been about morality, justice and building society rather than marginal effects and incentives. Who should contribute, how much, and to what?
content.extendedDescription:
From tithes paid to the church to today's discussions of a billionaire tax, attitudes to taxation have reflected society's ideas about justice, responsibility and community.
Drawing on history, the think tank Arena Idé hosts a conversation about why tax is needed, then, now and in the future. We hear perspectives on the church's historical view of taxation, how tax revenue is used today and what it does not cover. Arena Idé's tax review offers insight into what a future tax system could look like and how it could improve society.

content.title: The consequences of closing schools run as limited companies
content.description: The debate about a profit ban in schools is loud. Several parties have said their goal is for schools not to be run as limited companies. This would affect hundreds of thousands of pupils. Evaluations also show that for-profit schools generally perform best.
content.extendedDescription: Implementing such a policy would be a far-reaching reform, requiring an impact assessment. Svenskt Näringsliv commissioned Lars Henriksson, Professor of Law, to study the legal aspects of banning schools run as limited companies. Consultancy Azets has examined the financial consequences for the state and analysed what such a reform would mean in municipalities. The results will be presented at this seminar.

content.title: From crisis to opportunity – how do we build a stronger society?
content.description: Climate change, geopolitical uncertainty and rapid technological development challenge our social structures, but also open doors to new thinking. How do we build the capacity to act in troubled times? And how do we strengthen it for future changes?
content.extendedDescription: We live in a time of global uncertainty and rapid shifts, where our ability to adapt and transition determines our resilience. But what does it actually take to enable major transitions? Can we even harness the power of change to make society stronger, smarter and more capable of action? In this panel discussion, we explore how crises can become opportunities and what role local capacity to act plays in our collective preparedness when the next crisis arrives.

content.title: How do we improve integration? Schools as an engine for social mobility
content.description: Integration is a hot topic in political debate. Many believe it should improve, but how is this achieved in practice? All pupils must have the same chance to meet learning goals. Yet every year, 20% leave compulsory school without eligibility for further study. How do we change this?
content.extendedDescription:
Some schools have cracked the code for enabling pupils facing the toughest circumstances to reach the highest goals.

Drawing on concrete examples from Kunskapsskolan and Internationella engelska skolan, both of which have schools with high proportions of pupils from foreign backgrounds, we discuss what actually works for successful inclusion. We invite decision-makers to discuss how to make more happen and spread good examples.
content.subject: Integration/diversity

content.title: 100 per cent electrification of heavy transport – is the planned charging infrastructure enough?
content.description: Heavy transport accounts for a large share of transport sector emissions. Electrifying it could therefore deliver substantial climate benefits. But what is needed to enable the electrification of heavy transport?
content.extendedDescription:
In this webinar, using Gävleregionen as an example, we take an in-depth look at what is needed to enable the electrification of heavy transport.

We have analysed how well planned charging infrastructure meets actual transport needs. Combining planned charging stations with detailed traffic data and simulations of thousands of journeys provides an unusually concrete picture of the future system. Here we share five key insights from the study.

content.title: Aviation is more than charter flights – connectivity, preparedness and competitiveness
content.description: The aviation debate often centres on holiday travel and emissions. But aviation also plays a crucial role in medical transport, business, emergency services, total defence and keeping a geographically large country connected.
content.extendedDescription:
Swedish domestic aviation is at a crucial stage. How should aviation infrastructure be funded? What does the path towards fossil-free aviation look like? And what happens to Sweden's connectivity if airports and routes disappear before the transition is in place?

The seminar brings together representatives of politics, business and transport to discuss aviation's role in tomorrow's Sweden, where climate, competitiveness, preparedness and regional development intersect.

Our starting point is four innovation and research projects specifically addressing traffic transformation in villages. Which investments, reforms and priorities will be decisive in the coming years? And how do we ensure AI becomes an engine for productivity, innovation and competitiveness rather than a missed opportunity?

content.title: Does Sweden's energy transition risk stalling?
content.description: During the year, electricity producers have encountered resistance in trying to obtain judicial review of grid charge issues through regulatory supervision.

Last year's panel organised by Svensk Vindkraft discussed the unequal situation for feed-in customers (electricity producers) in Sweden compared with the rest of the EU. These regulations from Energimarknadsinspektionen (EIFS 2022:1) are now to be repealed by 30 June 2026 at the latest. What comes next is unclear.

The question Svensk Vindkraft wants to highlight this year is whether it is almost time for an electricity producers' revolt. Does Sweden's energy transition risk stalling if producers' costs become significantly higher than elsewhere in the EU?

IKEM invites you to a discussion of industrial economics, risk, competitiveness and the reforms that actually attract investment. The conversation is moderated by Kristian Åström.

content.title: Lebanon – is peace possible?
content.description: The relationship between Israel and Lebanon is an important part of the peace negotiations. Is there a path to genuine peace between Jerusalem and Beirut despite Hezbollah's and Iran's strong position?
content.extendedDescription:
Sweden's relationship with Israel and the Palestinians has shaped our foreign policy for over seven decades and is one of our most debated issues. But what happened behind closed doors from 1948 to 2026 has never been told. Until now.
In “Från Stockholm till Jerusalem: Den okända historien om Sveriges Mellanösternpolitik”, fifteen Swedish, Israeli and Palestinian prime ministers and foreign ministers, along with around eighty ambassadors and senior politicians, share their experiences and reveal what actually happened behind the scenes.
The book draws on 15 years of research, previously classified archival material and over a hundred in-depth interviews.
content.subject: International affairs

content.title: What are happiness, wellbeing and a rich life?
content.description: What is a rich life, really? Happiness and wellbeing have many dimensions. What can we learn from current research and insights?
content.extendedDescription:
Drawing on psychology, behavioural science and Nordic happiness research, we discuss:
• What creates lasting happiness over time?
• How do relationships, meaning and belonging affect wellbeing?
• Why are achievement and material success not always enough to feel rich in life?
• How can work, recovery and community contribute to greater quality of life?
• What can we learn from Nordic perspectives on balance, trust and societal wellbeing?
In a conversation with happiness professor Micael Dahlen, we weave together research, contemporary life and personal reflections on creating more meaning, presence and joy, both as individuals and as a society.
content.subject: Economy
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Professor of well-being, welfare and happiness
Chair of Skandia's Foundation Idéer För Livet

content.title: The parties' views on stronger protection for the rule of law and democracy: who safeguards the rule of law?
content.description: The rule of law is a foundation of democracy, but its protection is weakened by pressure on civil society, rushed legislation and inadequate legal safeguards. Ahead of the 2026 election, what choices are needed to strengthen it in the long term?
content.extendedDescription:
Ahead of the 2026 parliamentary election, Civil Rights Defenders has developed concrete reform proposals to strengthen the rule of law and democracy's fundamental principles in Sweden. These concern constitutional protection, legal certainty, criminal justice policy, the conditions for civil society and protection of fundamental rights and freedoms.

What are the parties' priorities and differences? Which reforms are they prepared to implement to strengthen the rule of law over the long term? Where is the resistance, and what risks do the parties see in failing to act?
content.subject: Human rights

content.title: As defence grows, what happens to healthcare?
content.description: When defence grows while healthcare is under pressure, total defence's local capability is tested. What happens to preparedness, working conditions and skills supply when defence investment and healthcare resources do not develop in step?
content.extendedDescription: A panel discussion about what happens when the state expands defence capability while regional healthcare is under severe pressure or being cut back. As defence expansion accelerates in several locations, questions arise about total defence's endurance and local communities' preparedness. The conversation explores how changes in healthcare affect staff, residents and the defence sector's ability to grow sustainably. The focus is on working conditions, skills supply and the division of responsibilities between the state, regions and municipalities when essential societal functions must work together.
content.subject: Security/defence
speakerTitles: State Secretary to the Minister for Health Care

content.title: The importance of electricity bidding zones for Sweden's competitiveness
content.description: The division into electricity bidding zones affects how electricity prices are set across the country. A single bidding zone for all of Sweden could, however, reduce opportunities to attract new industrial transition investments.
content.extendedDescription: The division into electricity bidding zones affects how prices are set in different parts of the country according to supply and demand in each zone. Low prices in SE1 and SE2 have been important in attracting electricity-intensive companies to Sweden. Quickly creating a single bidding zone for the whole country could potentially reduce opportunities to attract new industrial transition investments. Ultimately, bidding zones are not just about technical adjustments or consumer fairness, but about Swedish industry's future competitiveness.
content.subject: Energy

content.title: Who saves lives in war? The interplay between military and civilian healthcare
content.description: The deteriorating security situation places new demands on Sweden's preparedness. A central question is how cooperation between Försvarsmakten, military healthcare and civilian healthcare can develop. How do we secure life-saving equipment and resources for healthcare in crisis and war?
content.extendedDescription: Försvarsmakten's assessment from November 2025 states that medical capacity is crucial to successful military operations, but that military healthcare capability is currently limited. Effective cooperation with civilian healthcare is therefore a fundamental prerequisite for total defence capability.
content.subject: Security/defence

content.title: What is a better railway worth to Sweden Inc.?
content.description: Railways are crucial to Sweden's competitiveness and growth. They connect labour markets, strengthen companies' access to skills and enable industrial transport to ports and export markets. However, capacity shortages in parts of the network and the maintenance backlog make the system vulnerable.
content.extendedDescription: What would a better railway mean for Sweden Inc.? How would it affect companies' access to skills, the emergence of innovation, the attractiveness of our growth regions and businesses' ability to invest and grow? In a new report, Omtag Svensk Järnväg has analysed the link between Sweden's conditions for growth and shortcomings on its most important railway routes. Welcome to a conversation about the socioeconomic value that greater capacity and reliability in the transport system could create.
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport

content.title: How does prejudice affect entry to the labour market, and what can we do about it?
content.description: While many remain outside the labour market, companies and the public sector struggle to find the right skills. Preconceptions and narrow recruitment practices sometimes create barriers that affect growth and welfare. How can we jointly broaden routes into work so more people can find jobs?
content.extendedDescription: This panel discussion starts from a new report by Järvaveckan Research and PwC Sverige. It shows that many companies recruit through personal networks, limiting opportunities for people without established contacts to enter the labour market. Meanwhile, more business leaders than before say cultural and religious expressions negatively affect their view of a candidate during recruitment.
content.subject: Gender equality

content.title: Working life in 2026 – stress, AI and the struggle over time
content.description: How do Swedes view the labour market's biggest challenges, and what solutions do they want? Should working hours be reduced? How strong is support for the right to strike? Should AI be regulated or given free rein, what role do unemployment insurance and Arbetsförmedlingen play, and how do Swedes view the future of green industry?
content.extendedDescription:
Drawing on a new Novus survey commissioned by Arbetsvärlden, Lisa Pelling of Arena Idé and Albin Zettervall of Timbro meet to discuss democracy, working conditions, relations between social partners and the future of work.

What worries Swedes most about democracy? How can stress at work be reduced? Whom do we trust most: trade unions or employers?

A conversation about the labour market as it is today and as it might be tomorrow.
content.subject: Economy

content.title: Swedish cultural life and broader funding

Welcome to the hit comedy “Mecenatens återkomst - en snabbproducerad komedi utan statligt stöd”.
This highly topical play about Swedish cultural policy is spiced with homemade bombs, Russian gangsters and quick cash. Experience private funding at its most brutal, to the sounds of popular ballads, Tchaikovsky and spiritual classics.

Mecenatens återkomst is a dark comedy, divinely inspired by Roland Utbult's (KD) speech in the parliamentary debate on the cultural budget held on 4 December 2024. Come and take the chance to laugh at the misery!

Mecenatens återkomst is written and directed by Gertrud Larsson.

content.extendedDescription: How big a problem is ageism in Sweden today? And how do working conditions affect the pension we eventually receive? The conversation connects individual realities with political decisions. With Minister for Older People and Social Security Anna Tenje, we discuss the entire chain, from attitudes and working life to pension developments, focusing particularly on the Pensions Group's work during the parliamentary term. What has actually been delivered, and what remains for more people to be able and willing to work longer and receive a pension they can live on?

content.title: Extremism in transition: how do violent extremism and gang crime overlap?
content.description: Recently, links between organised crime and violent extremism have become increasingly prominent. What does research say about these connections? What does the threat to Sweden look like, and what happens when violence is not primarily driven by ideology?
content.extendedDescription: In this panel discussion, researchers and practitioners meet to discuss changing extremism. The conversation focuses on new drivers of violence, international dimensions and a reality in which organised crime and violent extremism are increasingly converging.

content.title: MS is more than relapses – how do we take responsibility for the whole disease journey?
content.description: MS is more than relapses. How do we ensure equitable care throughout the disease journey?
content.extendedDescription: MS is a complex disease affecting far more than acute relapses, but healthcare is not always organised to address the whole disease journey. There are also significant differences in access to care, follow-up and support across the country. This seminar discusses how care can become more equitable and better adapted to patients' long-term needs. The focus is on continuity, follow-up and how healthcare structures can develop amid everyday pressures. We also highlight the political priorities needed to give MS a clearer place on the agenda. How do we ensure all patients receive the right care, wherever they live?

What is required for the different parts of vocational education to fully fulfil their missions?
content.extendedDescription: Prioritising vocational education for adults is crucial to skills supply. Municipal adult education, adult vocational education and higher vocational education all receive substantial public funding to ensure the skills employers need. But there are other challenges, including student recruitment, work placements and work-integrated learning placements, and access to qualified vocational teachers. What shared experience do municipal adult education and higher vocational education providers have of these challenges, and how can they be resolved?

content.title: Are you worthless when you are unemployed?
content.description: If you have done everything required to get a job but still cannot find one, what do you do? What support does society provide? What happens to someone who is unemployed? And how are work and human worth connected?
content.extendedDescription: Come and listen to a conversation about the people behind the statistics. 350,000 people are registered as unemployed with Arbetsförmedlingen, and over 40 per cent are long-term unemployed. Debate often focuses on rules, money and fraud. But what is it like for unemployed people? What does long-term unemployment do to their confidence in the future, self-esteem and motivation? What are society's and individuals' responsibilities, and how should support, requirements and trust be balanced? How much of a person's worth lies in their job?

content.extendedDescription:
This seminar gets straight to the point: how do we move from pitch to deal to scalable business? We focus on what actually makes a difference:

• Creating engagement that leads to business.
• Building a process, not just a pitch.
• What successful startups do differently.
Welcome to a conversation about truly turning innovation into business.

content.title: From cancer research to patient benefit – how do we encourage more researchers to take the next step?
content.description: Between research findings and real patient benefit lies a gap where ideas need testing, validation and further development. Researchers need support and funding from various stakeholders to take the next step.
content.extendedDescription:
At the seminar, researchers, funders, innovation offices and decision-makers discuss how to strengthen incentives, support structures and partnerships so that more research findings benefit patients and society. How can we jointly encourage researchers to take their work further?

Welcome to a conversation about shortening the time between research and patient benefit, and why this is crucial both for people's lives and Sweden's future innovative capacity.

content.description: Children and young people in rural and suburban areas express growing distrust of politics. Limited influence, unequal conditions growing up and difficulties affecting decisions about daily life contribute to declining trust and greater democratic exclusion.
content.extendedDescription: The seminar starts from young people's own experiences of democracy, trust and influence. They explain why trust in politics is declining and how limited participation shapes their view of society. Accessible schooling, student influence and the option to remain in or leave their area are considered in relation to young people's views of politics, responsibility and participation. content.title: AI, productivity and growth – how Sweden can step up to compete and realise the potential
content.description: AI could become a decisive driver of productivity and growth. But realising its potential requires more than technology. How do we create the conditions for AI to have an impact throughout the economy?
content.extendedDescription:
AI could become a decisive driver of productivity, growth and competitiveness. But realising its potential requires more than technology. Sweden has strong companies and favourable conditions, but faces a crucial need to move from isolated initiatives to a concerted effort. How do we scale up AI use throughout the economy, from established businesses to new fast-growing companies?

Do we need a new agreement between politics and business? And which priorities will be decisive in translating AI into increased productivity and long-term growth?

content.title: Has social development gone too far? Should everyone resign?

The Katalys team is recording a live podcast!

Feeling lost among Almedalen's thousands of events? Fear not. Katalys is ready to guide you through the crowds.

AVGÅ ALLA is the only news and politics podcast you need. And now it is also the only Almedalen podcast you need. Start your morning with the Katalys team and the funniest guests Visby has to offer. content.title: Six hours a day – is it time to question how we work?
content.description: Research shows shorter working days can increase productivity and reduce sick leave, yet the eight-hour day remains the norm. Would a six-hour day make Sweden poorer or stronger? Is it time to question how we work?
content.extendedDescription:
Shorter working hours are not just an HR issue: they affect society, gender equality, public health and democratic participation. Companies such as GoClimate have chosen a different path and show that shorter hours mean working smarter, not less.
This panel brings together stress research, entrepreneurial experience and business perspectives to explore what is really holding change back, and whether there is another way forward.

content.title: From words to action – collaboration as a competitive advantage in Swedish life science
content.description: What is Sweden's real strength in life science, and how do we move from ambition to action?
content.extendedDescription:
Sweden has world-leading research, a top-ranked healthcare system and innovative businesses. Yet its potential is far from fully realised. What is Sweden's real strength in global life science competition, and what is needed for collaboration between academia, healthcare, business and the public sector to move from ambition to genuine action?

This seminar highlights concrete examples where collaboration has delivered results and discusses what they have in common. We also conclude by summarising the week's most important impressions from Almedalen: what do we take with us from words to action?

content.title: What policies are needed for more industrial jobs?
content.description: Industrial jobs are crucial to Sweden's competitiveness, regional development and welfare. They create employment across the country and enable the climate transition, stronger defence and a society built on shared values. But industrial jobs do not stay of their own accord.
content.extendedDescription:
Global competition for future investment is fierce. If Sweden does not offer reliable, long-term conditions, industry will grow elsewhere instead.

Industry's growth in Sweden requires active industrial policy. Functioning infrastructure, fossil-free electricity at competitive prices and industrial municipalities where people can live well are crucial. When the state collects industry's tax revenues, it must also take responsibility for the community investments needed locally.

So what policies are needed to create more industrial jobs?

content.title: Is the Swedish language dying out?
content.description: English-language course literature has become commonplace in higher education, despite research showing we learn less effectively when we do not read in our mother tongue. What are the consequences?
content.extendedDescription:
The dominance of English-language course literature leads students to fall behind in their reading. Studies from Chalmers show that English course literature is increasingly common even in courses taught entirely in Swedish, and in some programmes it is the norm rather than the exception.

What consequences does this have for students' learning and Swedish's status as an academic language? We know people learn better in their first language, so why do we continue to let English take over?

Welcome to a panel discussion on the importance of language for learning, education and academic discourse.

content.title: From 130 to 100 litres per person per day – achieving it together
content.description: Water-saving measures in homes are gaining ground. But new technology is not the whole answer. Reducing consumption requires changing our habits and sustaining those changes. How much can be asked of residents? And how do we encourage more tenants to voluntarily reduce their consumption?
content.extendedDescription:
In one year, Gotlandshem's tenants have reduced consumption from 130 to 115 litres per person per day. This is close to Region Gotland's interim target of 112 litres, but still some distance from the long-term target of 100 litres.

What are the limits of what a property owner can achieve alone? How can behaviour be influenced without assigning blame? What is reasonable to ask of a tenant, and what is not?

Dramaten and Stockholms universitet jointly highlight the crucial role of academic, artistic and editorial freedom in democracy.
Internationally, we see free art and independent research being restricted, with serious consequences for democratic society. In Sweden too, the arm's-length principle is challenged. Universities and cultural institutions face increased political control, researchers warn of threats to independent research, and culture is squeezed by historically low funding and new financing models.
Meanwhile, public debate is weakened by polarisation, disinformation and online hate. Journalists, researchers and artists are threatened into silence, and silence itself is a threat to democracy.

content.title: Young people and financial security: from first job to retirement
content.description: Young people today often face a tough financial start: difficulties entering the housing market, an uncertain labour market and growing debt. How can young people build long-term security and reduce risks, and what reforms could strengthen their financial health?
content.extendedDescription: Sweden's pension system rests on a contract between generations. The idea is simple: you work, pay into the system and can then rely on a reasonable pension when you grow older. But much has changed, and responsibility for pensions rests more heavily on individuals than before. Today's young people study longer, enter the labour market later and often start their working lives in insecure jobs. Meanwhile, each generation lives longer, increasing the need to work longer.

How should companies in these sectors be financed, what role can bank capital play, what other financing solutions are available, and how can capital markets and government agencies collaborate to make investments both effective and long term?
content.subject: Economy
speakerTitles: Vice Admiral, Chief of Joint Operations

content.title: Visby's water shortage – what are we doing now, and how do we solve it in the long term?
content.description: Visby's water supply has long faced capacity shortages and, in recent years, quality deviations too. Several measures are now being implemented at existing facilities to strengthen supplies over the coming years. In the longer term, Visby's water supply needs further reinforcement.
content.extendedDescription:
Meeting the challenges while laying the foundations for a sustainable future water supply requires both short- and long-term measures:
1. Short-term measures: renovating and strengthening pipelines, waterworks and reservoirs, and connecting to Södra Gotlands avsaltningsverk.
2. Long-term measures: five possible new raw water sources have been assessed using multi-criteria analysis. Drinking water production must meet the needs of Visby and surrounding areas until 2100.
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport

content.title: 100 years of occupational pensions – from collective security to individual responsibility
content.description: Over 100 years, occupational pensions have gone from a voluntary benefit to a crucial part of Swedes' pensions as the public pension has declined in importance. They are expected to become even more important as a flexible, long-term tool for security in a longer and more changeable working life.
content.extendedDescription: What does this development mean for society, companies and individuals? And what responsibility do different stakeholders have for making it easy for tomorrow's pensioners to take responsibility for their future income? Welcome to a seminar where the panel discusses occupational pensions' growing importance. The seminar is led by Américo Fernández, SEB's Personal Finance Economist.
content.subject: Economy

content.extendedDescription:
In a time of crises, preparedness, rapid global change and growing demands for decisive action, the Swedish administrative model is being tested. Are today's processes sufficient, or do they risk becoming a brake when society needs to act?

Akavia invites you to a seminar addressing a crucial question: can speed and legal certainty be reconciled, or must something give?

Does the policy preparation system need sharpening to meet both acute crises and long-term societal challenges? What would such a system look like? In this conversation, we challenge established structures and seek answers about how future decision-making processes should work.
content.subject: Democracy

content.title: Leadership in turbulent times
content.description: One model of society is dying, and another, more sustainable one needs to emerge. How do we exercise leadership capable of building both trust and the capacity to act?
content.extendedDescription:
In turbulent times, leadership becomes central. Our success in achieving organisational and societal goals and responding meaningfully to an uncertain future depends on renewing and clarifying our leadership.

Welcome to a conversation about insights and experiences from research and practice, and why leadership matters more than ever:
- What characterises successful leaders in turbulent times?
- What leadership skills are required?
- Can the future be predicted in turbulent times?
- What does leadership for an ecosystem mean?
- How do you lead with culture as a key tool?
content.subject: Sustainability
speakerTitles: Moderator and Director Global Industry Innovation

content.title: Truth under pressure – who shapes our view of reality?

Information influence, social media and AI are changing how we think, feel and make decisions. Meanwhile, trust in public agencies and the media is being challenged. content.title: Challenging the Norm: Business as a Catalyst for Societal Shifts
content.description: How are societal norms created, challenged, and changed? Alcohol has long been central to social life, yet growing demands for inclusion and wellbeing are reshaping expectations. Can businesses play a role in driving positive cultural change while remaining commercially successful?
content.extendedDescription:
While most companies respond to societal shifts, a select few have the courage to drive them.

Drawing on more than two decades of experience as a family therapist, Moa Gürbüzer founded Oddbird to challenge one of society’s most deeply rooted norms: alcohol’s central role in social life. In this conversation, she shares insights into how norms are created, how businesses can influence cultural change, and why purpose-driven brands that promote inclusion, wellbeing, and positive behavior may define the next generation of market leaders.

content.title: How Stockholm can strengthen its position as one of Europe's leading financial capitals
content.description: Ahead of Brexit, discussion focused on which city would replace London as Europe's leading financial centre: Frankfurt, Paris or Amsterdam. But Stockholm, described by The Economist as Europe's new capital of capital because of the country's deep and strong capital markets, was barely mentioned.
content.extendedDescription: Sweden and Stockholm are increasingly cited as a model for Europe as the region seeks to strengthen its capital markets, sharpen competitiveness and find funding for growing challenges. How have Stockholm and Sweden created such a strong financial centre? How can we further strengthen the position as one of Europe's leading financial cities? And how can Sweden inspire the rest of Europe?
content.subject: Economy

content.title: How do we ensure enough doctors throughout Sweden?
content.description: Sweden faces a growing shortage of specialist doctors, and time to act is short. Training a specialist takes at least 11.5 years, meaning today's decisions determine healthcare's skills supply well into the 2030s.
content.extendedDescription:
Yet there is no national body responsible for collecting, analysing and providing comprehensive statistics on doctors in training. Without this information, planning how many specialists Sweden actually needs is impossible.

More and more proposals suggest the state must take responsibility for determining the number of training posts, but nothing has happened yet.

Welcome to a seminar focusing on the most urgent questions:

How do we move from awareness to action? And what is required to ensure all of Sweden has access to specialist doctors in time?
content.subject: Health and social care

content.description: According to Folkhälsomyndigheten and Livsmedelsverket, the food environment in which children and young people live does not promote healthy eating habits. content.extendedDescription: As three stakeholders with shared interests and different perspectives in the sector and society, Arla, Sodexo and Cancerfonden jointly highlight young people's food environments. What do we actually know about their current eating habits? What role do social media and the supply of empty calories play, and how well do school meals guarantee more equal nutritional intake? Without investment, both staff working conditions and the quality of services for citizens are at risk. Many welfare workers also risk leaving the sector entirely.
Politicians in parliament, government, regions and municipalities set the framework for workplace conditions through resources, governance and requirements. This conversation brings together responsible politicians to examine the investments we can expect depending on which parties win the autumn parliamentary, regional and municipal elections.

Meanwhile, several voices call for removing the qualifying deduction from sick pay, which would significantly increase employers' short-term sickness absence costs and require finding replacements at short notice. At the seminar, you will hear different perspectives on the practical consequences of shorter working hours and removing the deduction. Which tasks risk going undone if we work less?

Economic signals, political choices and market developments affect the investment climate and bring valuations, growth strategies and deal activity into focus for the coming six months.

This seminar brings together DNB Carnegie's leading experts for a forward-looking panel discussion on questions including: the economic outlook for Swedish companies; prospects for corporate transactions and IPOs in H2 2026; and the parliamentary election's implications for investors and entrepreneurs.

content.description: Fossil fuels drive the climate crisis yet remain central to Europe's energy system. Debate often focuses on emissions when fuels are used, but substantial emissions already occur during extraction and refining, particularly methane, a very powerful greenhouse gas.
content.extendedDescription:
Dependence on fossil fuels is also about security and economics. Europe's fossil fuel imports can help finance authoritarian states and create economic vulnerability, as recent months have shown.
The seminar highlights Sweden's responsibility, possible policy instruments such as the EU Methane Regulation, and ways to reduce fossil fuel dependence.

Programme:
Ebba Malmqvist, Lunds Universitet/AirClim – Oil extraction in the Amazon.
Per Östborn, IVL/Gröna Mobilister – Traceability of fossil fuels.
Contributions from stakeholders including Drivkraft Sverige.
Followed by a panel with politicians.

content.description: Electrification is essential to Sweden's future. But to avoid an overly expensive transition, electricity system expansion must keep pace with demand. Everyone talks about coordination, but less about how to achieve it.

Investments in electricity generation, grids and industrial projects occur under different conditions and at different speeds. This is a major problem when the electricity system must expand substantially to meet society's needs at the right time, place and cost. Its expansion must therefore keep pace with Sweden's development. The seminar discusses how to make that happen in practice.

content.extendedDescription:
Report presentation
CommToAct and Differ's insights from the Novus and PUSH reports: two reports examining how Swedish consumers perceive companies' sustainability communication in a changing world and how brands can drive change.

Panel discussion
Greenwash, greenhush or something else? What happens when fear of saying the wrong thing leads us to say nothing? How do communications and marketing departments balance credibility and courage?
content.subject: Sustainability
speakerTitles: Partner and Head of Sustainability Services
Head of Innovation and Concept Development

content.title: How long is an arm?
content.description: Both politicians and visitors attempt to influence cultural content. Politicians' attempts breach the arm's-length principle and create an environment where visitors consider it acceptable to do the same. How does this affect culture?
content.extendedDescription:
The arm's-length principle between culture and politics is well established in Sweden. Yet three in ten public library directors believe elected politicians show insufficient respect for it (Biblioteksbladet no. 1, 2026). Politicians also attempt to influence library programmes, which art receives funding and what is staged across Sweden.

In this conversation, we discuss what the arm's-length principle means and what happens to culture and its workers when it is not upheld. And what is the role of politics when the principle is challenged?
content.subject: Culture

content.title: Indigenous peoples in the Arctic – the right to shape their own future
content.description: Indigenous peoples in the Arctic, including Sámi, Inuit, Chukchi and many others, actively fight for the right to shape their own future in a region undergoing drastic change. Their self-determination includes rights to traditional lands, waters and natural resources, and to their culture.
content.extendedDescription:
Challenges and future issues:
- Climate change: the Arctic is warming rapidly, threatening the ecological balance and thus food security, health and cultural identity for its inhabitants.
- Increased exploitation: more accessible natural resources increase external pressure on Indigenous territories.
- Cooperation: Arctic Indigenous peoples are strengthening cooperation, including through initiatives such as the Arctic People's Conference, to stand united on welfare and environmental issues.
content.subject: Culture
speakerTitles: Newly Elected Member of Denmark's Folketing for Greenland's Naleraq

content.title: Migration: can Sweden be both generous and sustainable?
content.description: Swedish migration policy has changed significantly over the past decade. Today's focus is on control, return and integration. How can international responsibility be reconciled with long-term sustainability and social cohesion?
content.extendedDescription:
For two decades, (G) som i Gud has focused on a clear task: bringing the Christian perspective into public debate.
(G) som i Gud has become a regular, appreciated part of Almedalsveckan, where politicians, opinion leaders, church figures and civil society stakeholders discuss the place of God and the church in politics.

(G) som i Gud is organised in collaboration with the newspaper Dagen, Frälsningsarmén, EFK and Pingst. Welcome to follow the seminars online or in person in Visby.

The conversation addresses which principles should guide future migration policy.
content.subject: Religion
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
speakerTitles: Member of Parliament and Labour Market Policy Spokesperson

content.title: What makes neighbourhood collaboration work, and what does it mean in practice?
content.description: How can areas develop through neighbourhood collaboration?
content.extendedDescription:
Bergsjön in Gothenburg is one of Sweden's particularly vulnerable areas. Yet reported crime has fallen by 27 per cent and the share of residents feeling safe has risen from 60 to 88 per cent. In the report Bergsjön i rörelse, Bergsjön 2031 analyses the district's development between 2015 and 2025.

Since 2011, Bergsjön 2031 has brought residents, property owners, the municipality, police and civil society together around shared development work. The seminar starts from the results and focuses on fifteen years of neighbourhood collaboration and long-term district development.

What makes long-term collaboration work? What has succeeded, what has been difficult, and what experiences might be relevant elsewhere?

We discuss these questions with representatives who have authority and expertise in the issues.
content.subject: Democracy

content.title: From research to defence: how do we build the skills?
content.description: How is Sweden preparing for a more uncertain future? What knowledge and skills does society need for total defence to meet tomorrow's challenges?
content.extendedDescription:
Swedish total defence faces a historic expansion while society becomes increasingly complex, from security threats and disinformation to climate-related crises and technological vulnerabilities. Meeting tomorrow's challenges requires knowledge, skills and capability throughout society.

But whose responsibility is it to build these skills? How should roles and responsibilities be divided between the state, agencies, regions, higher education institutions, business and private stakeholders? What role do research, education and lifelong learning play in modern total defence?

Welcome to a panel discussion on skills supply in total defence. Moderator: Lollo Pierce
content.subject: Research
content.accessibility: Event captioned, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: When no one has the full picture – cooperation for northern Sweden's development
content.description: Northern Sweden is undergoing rapid and extensive change. Major industrial investments, new establishments and growing flows of people, goods and energy affect how our communities develop, simultaneously and in close interaction.
content.extendedDescription:
To better understand what is coming, analysis company Polar Associates has mapped development at system level: which investments are planned, where they are happening, who is driving them and how they connect in time and space. A clear picture emerges: many elements are developing in parallel, and their interdependencies are strengthening.

Against this backdrop, we invite you to a conversation bringing together several perspectives. Together with and more voices, we explore what these developments mean here and now.

This is a conversation in which no one has the whole picture, but together we can get closer to it.
content.subject: Economy

content.title: How waiting lists in Swedish eye care can be shortened
content.description: Swedish eye care is under severe pressure. Needs are growing faster than capacity due to an ageing population, long waiting times and major regional differences. Today, one in three patients does not receive specialist care within the healthcare guarantee.
content.extendedDescription:
These developments risk deepening inequality and worsening eye health across large parts of the country.

The seminar discusses organising eye care more efficiently to meet future needs. Could a national strategy, more efficient care processes and greater cooperation with private optometrists shorten waiting lists? What lessons can be learned from dentistry's development? The conversation focuses on how earlier detection, structured follow-up and better use of optometrists' expertise can relieve specialist services, improve access and secure more equitable eye care throughout the country.

content.subject: Health and social care

content.title: Who should receive obesity medication, and who pays?
content.description: Obesity medicines have become more effective and accessible, but should the state and healthcare system pay, or should individuals pay themselves?
content.extendedDescription:
The debate about obesity medicines concerns both health and economics. Supporters believe the medicines should be offered to everyone with obesity, particularly those who also have conditions such as diabetes or hypertension. Treatment can improve quality of life and reduce future healthcare costs by preventing serious disease.

Others consider the medicines too expensive and point to limited healthcare resources. They argue society cannot afford treatment for everyone who wants to lose weight and believe the focus should be on better eating habits and exercise.

Should the state and healthcare system pay, or should individuals pay themselves? Both sides meet on Läkartidningen's stage for a discussion.
content.subject: Health and social care
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Different needs, different messages – how pension information is changing
content.description: All pension savers are different, so why does the information look the same? We are now taking the next step towards more tailored pension information. What does that mean?
content.extendedDescription:
In June, minPension launches its first adaptation for younger pension savers. Others will also notice changes in how information is presented and what is highlighted.

But what does tailoring information to target groups mean in practice? What information matters at different life stages, and how do the needs of someone just starting work differ from those of someone about to draw their pension? The seminar discusses which questions savers actually want answered, what creates understanding rather than confusion, and the trade-offs required to make complex information more targeted and useful.
content.subject: Economy
speakerTitles: Professor of well-being, welfare and happiness
Head of Public and Regulatory Affairs/Pensions Economist

content.title: Have we misunderstood the problems of the school market?
content.description: The government promises a complete overhaul of the independent school system. The opposition wants to go even further if possible. But do politicians understand what has gone wrong in the school market? Or are the proposed solutions shaping the definition of the problem, rather than the other way around?
content.extendedDescription:
Näringslivets skolforum is an initiative by Svenskt Näringsliv to strengthen Sweden's skills supply and improve educational outcomes in Swedish schools. Its aim is to provide an arena for greater understanding of problems, open-minded dialogue, international perspectives and the exchange of experience.

In Almedalen, we hold school forums at lunchtime every day from Tuesday to Friday. Wraps and other light refreshments are available to buy; new knowledge and engaging conversations are on us.

Skolforum@Almedalen opens at 11.30; panel discussions start around 12 and finish by 12.50.

Welcome!

content.title: The great inheritance shift in the single-family housing market – a national change with local consequences
content.description: The great inheritance shift could redraw the single-family housing market. What happens when 300,000 houses change hands – to housing chains, prices, planning and housing policy?
content.extendedDescription: Over the next 20 years, more than 300,000 single-family homes are expected to change hands through inheritance and, in many cases, come onto the market instead of staying in the family. That is more homes than have been built in Sweden in just over three decades. As large numbers of single-family homes gradually reach the market, this could change the conditions for housing chains, price formation and housing provision in many municipalities. Our stock of single-family homes, currently largely occupied by older people, is likely to gain younger residents. What does this great inheritance shift mean for the single-family housing market, local planning and housing policy as a whole?
content.subject: Construction
speakerTitles: Head of Analysis and Communications / moderator

content.title: Leadership in a hard-to-read world
content.description: Today, being able to read a market is not enough. Companies and leaders who want to succeed must also be able to read society. As geopolitical tensions, AI shifts and political polarisation reshape the landscape, the ability to interpret it becomes increasingly crucial.
content.extendedDescription:
What business has long regarded as soft skills – judgement, cultural understanding and the ability to understand people – is becoming critical to business success.
In this seminar, leaders, entrepreneurs and thinkers come together to share perspectives on what is needed when the world becomes harder to read. Which capabilities will matter most? How do we build judgement, direction and trust in more unstable times? And how do we create competitiveness when understanding the market alone is no longer enough?
content.subject: Business
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation

content.title: Greenwashing or greenhushing – do the new rules threaten companies' sustainability communications?
content.description: How do we ensure that new rules against misleading sustainability claims strengthen consumer protection without companies falling silent about their sustainability work?
content.extendedDescription:
As the EU directive on empowering consumers for the green transition is implemented in Swedish law, requirements for how companies may communicate about sustainability are being tightened. The aim is clear: to stop greenwashing and give consumers better information. But do we risk creating a new problem at the same time?

As uncertainty over what may be said increases, companies may end up saying less, not more, about their sustainability work, and may also choose not to invest in it. Are we moving from greenwashing to greenhushing? What does this mean for consumers' access to information, companies' capacity for innovation and the green transition as a whole?
content.subject: Communication/information

content.title: Is the right to learning materials secured?
content.description: Teachers can now buy learning materials to a greater extent than before, yet inequalities are still not decreasing. What is needed in learning materials going forward, and what can we expect after the election?
content.extendedDescription: It is two years since pupils' right to learning materials was written into the Education Act, and schools have been able to apply for government grants to buy learning materials for the past three years. Yet inequalities between subjects, schools and municipalities are still not decreasing. Why? 1 in 6 schools has shortcomings in pupils' access to learning materials, according to a review by Skolinspektionen covering 30 schools in total. The findings form an interim report on an assignment given to the agency by the government, with the final review to be presented this autumn. What results can we expect? And how should we think about the future of learning materials after the election?
content.subject: Education
speakerTitles: State Secretary to Minister for Education and Integration Simona Mohamsson

content.title: The consequences of discriminatory ethnic profiling
content.description: What consequences can experiences of discriminatory ethnic profiling have for individuals and for trust in law enforcement agencies – and how can it be prevented?
content.extendedDescription:
It is established that ethnic profiling occurs and is used within law enforcement agencies. This also brings a risk of discriminatory ethnic profiling. Developments in society and initiatives taken in recent years to counter organised crime give considerable reason to believe that these risks have increased.

DO's seminar takes place at Torget för mänskliga rättigheter och demokrati, organised in cooperation with Forum för levande historia and Institutet för mänskliga rättigheter.

content.title: Weight-loss medicines are changing purchasing behaviour – what does this mean for retail and growth?
content.description: How is the sector affected when population growth slows, competition for customers intensifies and new lifestyle trends – such as weight-loss medicines – change how and how much we consume?
content.extendedDescription:
The use of weight-loss medicines is growing rapidly in Sweden, with documented positive health effects. At the same time, a new study by Svensk Handel shows that these medicines also change purchasing behaviour, particularly when it comes to food.
A panel discussion follows the study's findings: how quickly could this development have a broad impact? What does a smaller and different food basket mean for retailers and food companies? And how should policymakers respond when medical innovations have clear effects beyond public health and healthcare?

content.title: Linguistic exclusion among deaf and hard-of-hearing children – what are the consequences?
content.description: Everyone talks about children's rights, but in practice those rights do not reach all children in Sweden. Sign language can counter loneliness and ill health, yet for the majority of the country's approximately 8,900 deaf and hard-of-hearing children, it is not a given part of life.
content.extendedDescription:
The report Dinner Table Syndrome and Existential Health – Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing Children's Experiences of Linguistic Exclusion, produced by Barn- och ungdomsjour på teckenspråk, deepens our understanding of what happens when children are not given the right to sign language and a language guarantee from day one.
The combination of research and in-depth interviews with support workers known as ‘syssnare’, who staff the world's only sign-language helpline for deaf and hard-of-hearing children and young people, clearly shows that this group needs support and empowerment to reduce its vulnerability and exposure to harm.
content.subject: Human rights

content.title: When competitiveness becomes resilience – how do we build the total defence of the future?
content.description: The deteriorating global situation, cyber threats and vulnerable supply chains show that cities, energy systems and infrastructure are part of total defence. How do we build robust communities that can handle both crises and growth – without compromising democracy and openness?
content.extendedDescription: The deteriorating global situation, cyber threats and vulnerable supply chains have made it clear that the built environment – cities, energy systems and infrastructure – is a central part of total defence. How do we design communities that can handle both growth and crises? How do we build everyday resilience without compromising democratic values and an open society? And how can architects, engineers, business and the public sector jointly contribute to a modern total defence?
content.subject: Construction
