content.title: Digital vulnerability – are Swedish media naive?
content.description: The Swedish media industry is structurally dependent on major American tech platforms. This is efficient and, in many cases, technically necessary. But it also creates a vulnerability that could threaten the industry's independence.
content.extendedDescription:
Developments in the USA's global relations raise legitimate questions about trust in American services and have prompted growing calls in Brussels for greater investment in European digital solutions, known as digital sovereignty.

How can Swedish media deliver news without interference from government agencies, political leaders or commercial actors? Should Swedish media do more to build preparedness that works across multiple systems and cloud providers? Are we naive, or can we safely stay the course?

We will discuss this with a number of media industry experts and representatives of technology solutions.
content.subject: Media/journalism
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: How do we strengthen Sweden's space industry in a new commercial and security policy reality?
content.description: Access to space is a prerequisite for modern society and crucial to our security. Sweden has leading space capabilities and a unique spaceport. How do we use and develop these to strengthen our resilience and competitiveness? And what can we learn from others?
content.extendedDescription: Space is now deeply integrated into our everyday lives and crucial to critical societal functions. The global space market is growing at record speed and is a strategic resource for security, communications and economic growth. Sweden has strong space capabilities, ranging from components and subsystems for rockets and satellites to complete small satellites, launches, and the reception and analysis of space data. Welcome to a discussion about how we strengthen society through leading space capabilities and international cooperation.
content.subject: Security/defence
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Head of the Aviation and Space Business Area
Head of Cybersecurity and Critical Communications
Global Head of Business Development and Strategy

content.title: Sovereignty and alliances in the AI era – how does Sweden secure its freedom of action in a new geopolitical landscape?
content.description: AI is reshaping the global balance of power and bringing questions of dependence and control into focus. For Sweden, this means balancing national capacity with international cooperation. How do we secure freedom of action in a new geopolitical reality?
content.extendedDescription:
AI is rapidly reshaping the global balance of power. Questions of sovereignty, dependence and strategic alliances are moving up the political agenda.
How do we build national capacity in critical areas such as data, infrastructure and skills while remaining part of global ecosystems? And which partnerships are necessary, and which are risky?

At a time of increasing geopolitical tensions, fundamental questions arise: which critical capabilities does Sweden need to control itself, and where is cooperation essential? What choices and investments will shape Sweden's freedom of action in the coming years?
content.subject: Innovation
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: The internal threat – to face an external threat, the internal threat must be addressed, understood and resolved
content.description: Increased domestic production counters external threats. Sweden has technology, capital and willingness, but systemic flaws created by laws, regulations and administrative machinery obstruct development. Without changes to the system, nothing will happen.
content.extendedDescription:
It is very clear that politicians expect us business owners to take responsibility for building a strong Sweden. We are happy to do so. But to do the job, we need the factors that put us in this situation to be addressed.

In a panel debate, we will discuss investments that never happened, relocation and long lead times – as well as resistance within the system, such as interpretations, policy intentions and sniping. We also discuss the political paradox: what politicians want and what businesses can actually do – and the way forward.

The internal threat can be turned into Sweden's greatest strength.
content.subject: Business

content.title: Can Sweden and the US build nuclear faster for Europe?
content.description: Europe needs more dispatchable clean energy. Advanced nuclear reactors could be part of the answer, but getting there requires capital, regulation and cross-border collaboration. What structures do we need to actually bring new nuclear to market in time?
content.extendedDescription:
Blykalla and Oklo use different technologies – liquid lead and sodium respectively – but share the same conviction: that the transatlantic relationship is the fastest route to commercial nuclear power. They are part-competitors, part-partners, and have chosen to invest in each other.

In this fireside chat, Blykalla CEO Jacob Stedman and Oklo CEO Jacob DeWitte get candid about what it actually takes to build a new kind of nuclear company: the capital, the regulation, the timelines – and why co-opetition turned out to be the smartest move. What does it mean for Sweden, for US-European energy ties, and for the pace of the energy transition?
content.detail: Loops arena för impact, industri och energi
content.subject: Energy

content.title: A housing shortage or a responsibility shortage – what is housing policy's real problem?
content.description: If the problem is not primarily a lack of housing but a system with inadequate responsibilities and incentives, how should housing policy be understood? And who actually bears responsibility for housing policy objectives?
content.extendedDescription:
Parliament's objectives require a well-functioning housing market where supply meets need, but in today's hybrid arrangement of central government, municipalities, the market and stakeholder interests, it is unclear who is expected to deliver what. New research suggests that the insider–outsider structure, weak incentives and unclear institutional roles make it harder to achieve the objectives.
We discuss how responsibility should be allocated in a housing policy that does more than dutifully repeat that we must ‘build our way out of the housing shortage’. What lessons can be drawn from other countries' governance models?

A warm welcome!

content.title: The return of sustainability – when the green transition becomes security
content.description: Geopolitical uncertainty makes energy a central security issue. Europe's dependence on imports creates vulnerability while the transition requires enormous investments. What role can pension capital play in building fossil-free energy and strengthening resilience – and what rules are needed?
content.extendedDescription:
At a time of geopolitical uncertainty, energy has become a central security issue. Europe's dependence on imported energy has proved to create economic and political vulnerabilities, while the energy transition requires investment on a historic scale.
The seminar discusses the role long-term pension capital can play in financing the expansion of fossil-free energy, electricity grids and other strategic infrastructure, thereby strengthening Sweden's and Europe's resilience, and the political and regulatory conditions needed to mobilise capital.
content.subject: International affairs
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Member of Parliament and Spokesperson for Biodiversity and Animal Rights

content.title: How electricity market design can contribute to Sweden's competitiveness
content.description: Electrification is crucial to climate targets and competitiveness. The electricity system is being planned to enable consumption of 300 TWh per year. To realise this, the electricity market needs to be designed to enable investment and efficient resource use.
content.extendedDescription:
- Are the current design and functioning of the electricity market fit for enabling electrification?
- Can the electricity market create conditions for investment and efficient resource use?
- How can the market develop to meet different actors' needs and create conditions for an economically efficient electricity system?
- How can risks be managed, and how can the financial electricity market develop to meet future needs for stability?
- What is Svenska kraftnät's role in creating appropriate conditions for the electricity market and its participants?
content.subject: Energy

content.title: The fragile goal – when building society requires both trust and control
content.description: During the spring, Sweden's church leaders met parliamentary party leaders to discuss trust and its breakdown. What happens to the goal when fear becomes the driving force rather than the vision? What does it say about society when the church's work becomes a political statement? What can politics and the church learn from each other?
content.extendedDescription: Archbishop Martin Modéus and church leader Karin Wiborn took part in the spring's discussions with party leaders, which covered migration, development aid, children's vulnerability and the new democracy requirements. Here, they meet Professor of Political Science Marie Demker and Aftonbladet editorial writer Susanna Kierkegaard in a panel discussion about trust and control, distrust and shifting values – concepts that recurred in the reflections after every party leader discussion. Do the churches have something to teach politics, and how can we help each other build a society in which we actually dare to trust one another?
content.subject: Democracy
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Societal transformation in the north – what becomes reality and what stays on the drawing board?
content.description: Northern Sweden is at the heart of the green industrial transition and some of Europe's largest investments. Meanwhile, a new security situation and economic uncertainty are changing the conditions. What has become reality? How are municipalities, businesses and community development in the north affected?
content.extendedDescription: Svefa's courtyard, Fastighetshubben, at Adelsgatan 25 is the meeting place in Almedalen where the public and private sectors can meet, exchange experiences, talk and discuss property-related issues, focusing on urban development, the built environment and a sustainable society. On stage, we will organise seminars, panel debates and networking receptions focusing on strategic urban development, the property market and sustainability. Here you can meet property specialists from every part of the sector. Find our full Almedalen programme at www.svefa.se
content.subject: Economy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Head of Planning and Land Development

content.title: Between caring for sick children and harvesting grass – is that when we are supposed to build Sweden's preparedness?
content.description: Sweden's food supply depends on young people being able to take over, start and develop businesses in the green industries. Young people want to, but face high barriers: expensive start-up costs, difficult succession, complicated rules and everyday pressures on finances, mental health and family life.
content.extendedDescription:
Sweden's future food production and preparedness depend on the next generation of food producers. But young farmers today struggle to make both their businesses and everyday lives work.

The Bondepitchen concept returns to Almedalen. This year, LRF Ungdomen invites the parliamentary parties' youth organisations to the most important debate on food and preparedness ahead of the 2026 election, to discuss how Sweden can create better conditions for the next generation of food producers and preparedness builders.
content.subject: Security/defence
speakerTitles: Spokesperson for Environment, Defence and Foreign Policy
National Board Member with Special Responsibility for Defence and Security Policy

content.title: Get ready for the election
content.description: AI hoaxes, hidden senders and coordinated campaigns. During the 2026 election year, we face a fast-moving social media flow in which journalists must be equally quick to distinguish real from fake and uncover those deliberately misleading us. How can we collaborate better?
content.extendedDescription: ‘Get ready for the election – fact-checking hangout with Valkollen 2026’ is a meeting place for journalists at Almedalen who want to learn more about scrutinising digital dirty tricks and investigating them further. Come to Valkollen-scenen for coffee and an update! We open at 12 with refreshments, cake and a lounge. Bring your lunch, work on your story, recharge and relax in the courtyard. At 14, the Valkollen 2026 project team will share what we have seen so far – from fake election posters to Vietnamese clickbait factories. End the day from 17 with an after-work election fact-checking gathering featuring some of Sweden's sharpest fact-checkers and researchers in the field. Join Valkollen 2026!
content.subject: Media/journalism
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation

content.title: The Baltic Sea and the 2026 election – what do the political parties want?
content.description: Parliamentary elections take place this autumn. Which issues relating to the Baltic Sea and water matter to the parties, and what concrete policy proposals do they have? Do they want to implement and fund Parliament's agreed direction for marine and aquatic environmental policy, and where do their views differ?
content.extendedDescription:
In the closing seminar of Östersjödagarna, we bring together issues linked to political decisions and discuss with representatives of the parliamentary parties how the next steps in marine environmental policy should be shaped. The marine environment bill contains good statements of intent, such as broad implementation of the ecosystem approach in marine management and reduced eutrophication and overfishing, but concrete measures are still lacking.

Ahead of the 2026 election, all parties have the opportunity to propose and pursue their own marine policies. In this seminar, we hear which issues they consider important and how they want to address them going forward.
content.subject: Climate/environment
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Prevention, precision and partnership for the cancer care of the future
content.description:
How do we move from political ambitions to real change in cancer care?
Cancer is a global societal challenge. To address it, we must create better conditions for implementing new knowledge, methods and interventions. We need fresh thinking and a holistic approach to health.
content.extendedDescription: Cancer Mission Day brings together leading actors from healthcare, research, government agencies, industry and civil society to explore how prevention, precision medicine, health data and new ways of working can strengthen both patient benefits and Sweden's competitiveness. Through cross-sector discussions and concrete examples, the day shows how the cancer strategy can be put into action – from early detection and data-driven innovation to equitable follow-up and quality of life. The day concludes with the launch of SweCan, Sweden's Cancer Mission Hub, where unexpected encounters drive the next steps in systemic change.
content.subject: Health and social care
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Why must we stop wasting taxpayers' money?
content.description: Is wasting taxpayers' money just about municipalities buying pink unicorns or a swimming pool running over budget – or is it a systemic failure? Where do the wasted billions go? What happens to a society that fails to manage its finances responsibly? Would stopping waste give us better welfare services?
content.extendedDescription: The panel takes the form of an open, moderated discussion. The audience will also have opportunities to ask questions and comment. The aim is to discuss the consequences of systemic failures that cause municipalities, regions and central government to lose billions every year. The primary purpose is not to debate which policies we should have, but to highlight what happens when shared resources disappear. What are the biggest examples of waste? What can be changed to address the problem? What kind of society could we have simply by taking better care of our hard-earned tax money?
content.subject: Economy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: AI on drugs – how do we get AI to stop being so predictable?
content.description: Do you also think tech has become rather boring? How can we influence the way AI thinks to make the technology more creative, surprising and useful?
content.extendedDescription:
AI can write, summarise, code and improve efficiency. But how do we stop it being a bland, less-than-smart assistant? And can we make it think less like a well-behaved assistant and more like a creative colleague with unexpected ideas by taking code-based substances that open up the digital brain, just as humanity has done for thousands of years? André Frisk, Head of Tech at Geelmuyden Kiese, takes us through how to make technology think differently – and more entertainingly.

An occasionally comprehensible introduction to why AI often becomes predictable, how to steer it towards more original ideas, and what that means for creativity, innovation and working life. At the end, there is room for your most unpredictable question about AI!
content.subject: Digitalisation

content.title: Sky-high trust in the deposit return system – have we succeeded?
content.description: Sweden's deposit return system efficiently collects drinks containers and enjoys high public trust. Meanwhile, society's needs and expectations are changing, requiring systems to develop and improve continuously.
content.extendedDescription:
We will be there with our Pantobil to explain more about how Sweden's deposit return system works. Drop by and talk to us about returning containers, recycling and how we can continue developing effective collection solutions and circular material flows together.

Ask questions, discuss future deposit return systems and learn from our experience of collecting billions of deposit containers every year. Welcome to network and talk about deposit returns with us!

content.title: From investment to real operational benefits
content.description: How do you ensure that an initiative or investment actually delivers benefits in an organisation's operations?
content.extendedDescription:
The seminar explores how to build a business case that holds up over time, how qualitative and financial benefits can be meaningfully monitored, and above all how to create the conditions for those benefits to materialise in practice.

Drawing on the implementation of Production and Capacity Management (PKS), the panel shares concrete experiences, from unexpected lessons to misjudgements along the way.

Participants will gain practical perspectives and tools to strengthen benefits realisation in their own organisations: how to build stronger business cases, link follow-up to actual operational change and challenge unclear assumptions about impact, responsibility and monitoring.
content.subject: Economy
speakerTitles: Researcher in Benefits Realisation and Digitalisation

content.title: How can a cardiovascular disease action plan help me?
content.description: Every year, thousands of people in Sweden experience events related to cardiovascular disease. The costs to society are considerable, and modern innovations are available.
content.extendedDescription:
Welcome to a seminar focusing on Socialstyrelsen's ongoing work to develop a new national action plan for preventing and treating cardiovascular disease. The seminar brings together representatives from healthcare, a patient organisation and a government agency to contribute perspectives, experiences and concrete input to the continuing work.

The seminar aims to promote collaboration and contribute to a well-grounded, effective action plan that strengthens efforts against cardiovascular disease in Sweden.
content.subject: Health and social care
speakerTitles: Professor of Cardiology, President-Elect of the European Society of Cardiology

content.title: What value are we getting from healthcare policy – why are reforms not delivering results?
content.description: Why do politically driven healthcare reforms fail to have their intended impact? Despite major initiatives, challenges remain. What is holding back development – and how must governance and policymaking change amid demographic and technological transformation?
content.extendedDescription:
LHC has followed politically driven reforms, initiatives and governance models for almost 20 years. What can we learn from the outcomes of all the attempts to improve healthcare? Examples include the waiting-list funding initiative, patient choice, care close to home, and targeted grants to drive development, collaboration and more. Reforms to operating models, ownership and responsibility. How have they gone, and what has prevented them from going all the way? How must policymaking change to have an impact when both demographics and technology are changing the conditions?

The seminar is part of Arena Tillsammans, the meeting place for healthcare's major systemic issues during Almedalsveckan.
content.detail: Arena Tillsammans: the arena for healthcare's major systemic issues
content.subject: Health and social care

content.title: From Greenland to Hormuz – a year of tests for NATO
content.description: NATO's July summit will test the alliance's strength and how to secure long-term support for Ukraine. Will there be tension around the table, or a meeting among friends?
content.extendedDescription:
Over the past year, NATO has faced a series of political tests, not least Donald Trump's statements about Greenland and his criticism of NATO allies for insufficient engagement in the Strait of Hormuz. The USA is also reducing its troop presence on European soil, but Europeans have accepted the challenge of taking greater responsibility for their continent's security, not least in the war in Ukraine.

Welcome to Utrikespolitiska institutet's morning in Almedalen. We discuss today's major foreign policy issues and offer perspectives on dramatic developments around the world. There will also be opportunities to mingle, talk to our experts and make connections.

Utrikespolitiska institutet combines research, analysis and public education on international affairs.
content.subject: International affairs

content.title: The municipality and capital
content.description: It takes a municipality to build a factory. But what do businesses and municipalities need from national policymakers to get the factory built?
content.extendedDescription:
Industry's profitability and ability to deliver the products society needs are crucial to resilience in turbulent times. Municipalities and industries always operate in local symbiosis. But both are held back by rules and requirements that do not reflect the times we live in.

With tougher international competition for industrial establishments and resources, central government's responsibilities, from environmental permits and electricity access to skills provision, need to be handled more effectively. Done correctly, this strengthens industry and municipalities together. IKEM and Svenska Industrikommuner therefore highlight the mutual dependence between municipalities and industry and how we can support each other. Is it time for central government to take responsibility for ensuring the right conditions for both municipalities and industry to grow?
content.subject: Economy
speakerTitles: Chair of the Municipal Executive Board
Chair of the Municipal Executive Board
Member of the Committee on Industry and Trade
Member of the Committee on Industry and Trade
Member of the Committee on Industry and Trade

content.title: What value are we getting from healthcare workforce provision – why are there not enough staff?
content.description: How do we secure the skills needed in health and social care as demand increases? Despite initiatives, challenges remain. What are the right skills in different contexts – and how must skills be used and developed to meet future demands?
content.extendedDescription:
Will there be enough staff? Securing skills is one of the major challenges for future health and social care. Investment in training places, working conditions and staffing benchmarks are among current governance initiatives. But how can we ensure that different skills are used in the best way to meet patients' needs? What are the ‘right’ skills in different contexts, and what new skills are needed to work efficiently and safely as healthcare conditions change?

The seminar is part of Arena Tillsammans, the meeting place for healthcare's major systemic issues during Almedalsveckan.
content.detail: Arena Tillsammans: the arena for healthcare's major systemic issues
content.subject: Health and social care

content.title: A higher age limit and AI in breast cancer screening – the path to equitable care
content.description: How do we save more lives from breast cancer, from mammography to the right treatment in time? Through modernised screening with a higher age limit and AI support for image assessment and triage. How can equitable access to precision medicine and person-centred care become reality nationwide?
content.extendedDescription: Drawing on the new national cancer strategy, we bring together patients, professionals and policymakers to identify concrete next steps. The government has tasked Socialstyrelsen with reviewing national screening programmes, with a final report in 2028. How can we ensure early detection and equitable care using today's knowledge and systems, and help a review of the national breast cancer screening programme take another step towards better, more precise breast cancer care?
content.subject: Health and social care
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Regional Councillor, Chair of the Health and Medical Care Committee
Regional Councillor and Chair, Strategic Health and Medical Care Committee
Regional Commissioner responsible for Health and Medical Care

content.title: 89% want stronger climate policy – what could the measures look like?
content.description: A majority of the world's population (89%) wants stronger climate action. Yet creative ideas and smart measures are conspicuously absent. Klimatklubben wants to change that!
content.extendedDescription:
According to a global study, a majority of the world's population wants stronger climate action.

Wanting strong climate policy is more common than watching Mello or being an adult with a driving licence in Sweden. Yet both climate issues and measures are conspicuously absent from the debate.
The non-profit organisation Klimatklubben wants to change that.

In a talk show hosted by Klimatklubben co-founders Maria Soxbo and Emma Sundh, a succession of guests will brainstorm creative, smart measures that reduce emissions and/or support biodiversity. In short: make a real difference.
The goal? A bank of ideas for political parties to draw on and a wealth of measures for citizens to demand.
content.subject: Climate/environment

content.title: Artistic freedom in turbulent times – from Katrineholm to Brussels
content.description: Freedom of expression, a fundamental part of democracy, has declined dramatically worldwide. How does this affect artistic freedom and policy for artists?
content.extendedDescription: Researchers at V-Dem-institutet at Göteborgs universitet conclude in a recently published report that freedom of expression, a fundamental part of democracy, has declined dramatically worldwide. We discuss with politicians, government agency representatives and opinion leaders how this affects artistic freedom, part of the freedom of expression protected by our constitution, at supranational, national and local levels. Among other issues, we address the European Commission's focus on protecting artistic freedom in the strategic framework ‘Culture Compass for Europe’ and discuss whether Swedish law also needs stronger protection for artistic freedom, taking the Museums Act as a starting point.
content.subject: Democracy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Chair of the Committee on Cultural Affairs
