content.title: As AI accelerates – how do we safeguard trust?
content.description: AI is fundamentally changing operations faster than organisations can adapt their security structures. The technology drives efficiency and innovation but also introduces risks such as vulnerable decision-making processes, unclear responsibilities and systems not built to withstand attacks.
content.extendedDescription:
This seminar brings together experts from business and the public sector to identify what is needed to use AI without compromising security or trust. It focuses on integrating AI into operations in ways that stand the test of time, clarifying responsibilities and managing risks before they materialise.

How do we protect systems and data in an environment where threats evolve as quickly as technology? How do we equip organisations and employees to make decisions in an AI-driven reality? And how do we ensure trust endures as complexity increases?
content.subject: Security/defence

content.title: World-class AI skills: how do we make Sweden's public sector the best in the world?
content.description: Sweden aims to become the world leader in public-sector AI to increase efficiency and free up time for human interaction. The technology already exists, but the challenge now is to develop the skills and capacity to use AI across the entire public sector at scale.
content.extendedDescription:
In the initiative A Shared Digital Assistant for the Public Sector (Svea), more than 100 organisations collaborate to develop and share an AI assistant. But Svea is more than a tool – it is a way to train the public sector to use AI while building digital sovereignty and shared capacity.

How do we build skills, and what must Sweden do to achieve its ambition?
Do public-sector leaders have what it takes to put AI into practice? And how do we build genuine sovereignty, not just in strategy but in capability?
content.subject: Innovation
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Senior Researcher CSDI – Center for Security Design and Innovation

content.title: A new generation of politicians takes over – but does it matter?
content.description: How do today's young politicians view the future of municipal finances? Is there the courage to make decisions that may not affect the next budget but build sustainable municipalities over time?
content.extendedDescription: Four young local politicians discuss responsibility, legacy and the future. What mistakes do they want to avoid passing on, and how do they want their own political generation to be remembered? In a time of strained finances, growing welfare needs and rising expectations, difficult questions come to the fore: what have previous generations of politicians left behind in debts, structures and systems? And what mistakes risk being repeated if nothing changes? How do today's young politicians view the future of municipal finances? Is there the courage to make decisions that may not affect the next budget but build sustainable municipalities over time? And how do they view cooperation across party lines, between municipalities and with business?
content.subject: Economy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Chair of the Municipal Executive Board
Chair of the Municipal Executive Board

content.title: Save Sweden's deposit return system!
content.description: Sweden has one of the world's most effective deposit return systems, with high collection rates and clear climate benefits. Yet the EU's new Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) risks changing the landscape, even in countries where systems already work well.
content.extendedDescription:
Several Nordic countries have already acted and requested exemptions from EU requirements that effectively mean returning to glass bottles in red and blue plastic crates, citing increased costs, more complex logistics and, in some cases, a risk of higher emissions. Sweden's path remains unclear.

In this panel discussion, we explore what overimplementation of the PPWR would mean in practice. What would the consequences be for Swedish breweries and retailers? Is there a risk of undermining a well-functioning system? And how have other countries, such as Norway, approached their choices?

We also raise the fundamental question: if Sweden is already a leader, what problem are we actually trying to solve?
content.subject: Business

content.title: How we challenge ageism through action and become the change we want to see
content.description:
Why do ‘old’ and ‘senior’ have negative connotations while ‘young’ is a compliment?
Are we older people a major part of the problem through our pursuit of youth?
We believe the path to change is accepting and celebrating ageing rather than showing how youthful, strong, slim and clever we are.
content.extendedDescription:
Join us for an interactive presentation and fashion show challenging society's prevailing beauty ideals and demonstrating the beauty of ageing. Through action, we show a side of society that is joyful, attractive and inspiring for old and young alike.

Words without action are dead; many talk about ageism, but very few act.
We need more role models who clearly demonstrate that ageing is not something to fear but something to look forward to. Every age has its charm, and you will experience the knowledge and beauty our older role models represent.
content.subject: Integration/diversity

content.title: Can Sweden build robust infrastructure fast enough?
content.description: Sweden faces a new security reality in which demands to strengthen total defence and protect critical infrastructure are increasing rapidly. Transport, energy, water, digital systems and public-service properties are essential to society's functioning in everyday life, crisis and war.
content.extendedDescription:
At the same time, more built-environment projects are subject to security classification and special protective security rules. This changes how projects are planned, procured and delivered. Many experience greater complexity, more uncertain processes and longer lead times.

How do we develop working methods that meet high security requirements while enabling efficient, predictable and feasible projects?

A warm welcome to a seminar on how collaboration, processes and working methods can evolve as security requirements rise and projects become more complex.
content.subject: Construction
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Successes and failures: what we have really learned from municipal collaboration on construction and circularity
content.description: With demanding climate targets and a need for rapid action, municipalities must learn from each other to succeed. In recent decades, several initiatives have been launched to build cooperation, collaboration and shared learning. But how have they actually gone?
content.extendedDescription:
The seminar highlights experiences from recent municipal collaborations on construction and circularity. What lessons can we draw? Why have some succeeded while others failed? How do we handle differences that remain despite very similar mandates?

The seminar is primarily aimed at municipal officials and politicians, as well as anyone who organises, leads or is curious about municipal collaboration.
content.subject: Climate/environment
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Head of Research and Industrial Transformation
Head of Strategy for Sustainable Construction
Innovation Leader and Coordinator in Klimat 2030

content.title: The USA and China are pulling ahead – what should Europe do?
content.description: Sweden ranks among the EU's most innovative countries, while Europe as a whole lags behind the USA and China. Europe must step up in the competition for talent, business establishments and investment in the coming years.
content.extendedDescription:
The seminar discusses how to unlock the strength of regional environments and what role cross-border regions such as Öresundsregionen can play from Swedish and European perspectives. This includes creating powerful industrial and economic clusters to meet competition from the USA and China, and the reforms needed to strengthen Sweden's position in a turbulent world.

This event is part of Skånes Innovationsarena, an initiative by leading innovation actors in Skåne on Thursday 25 June.
content.subject: Innovation
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: President of Research Education, Development and Innovation
Head of Host States Relations and coordinator High Level Industrial Forum European Spallation Source ERIC

content.title: What is the government doing to save snus in the EU?
content.description: Several EU countries are moving towards banning or restricting snus. The government says it is fighting for snus, which is manufactured in Sweden and used by many Swedes. The opposition, by contrast, believes the government has not done enough.
content.extendedDescription:
Snus has become a hot political issue. France has introduced a total ban making snus use punishable by substantial fines. Other countries are preparing similar rules against snus. At EU level, proposals also include major restrictions and tax increases.
For Swedes who use snus, this can create major problems when travelling, while also reducing export opportunities and jobs in Sweden.
The Swedish government says it is fighting for snus in the EU. The opposition says the government has not done nearly enough. To find out what Sweden is doing – or should do – to save snus, we are organising an open political debate on the subject!
content.subject: EU
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: The housing market – a brake on growth or an opportunity?
content.description: Many young people say they cannot afford to leave home and believe high housing costs could obstruct work and study, and even prevent them from starting a family. Why is building and housing so expensive? What needs to change in the rules?
content.extendedDescription: Housing construction costs have soared, driven by regulation, bureaucracy, long processing times and ever higher connection charges. The result is low housing construction, high property prices, expensive rents and long queues, risking both growth and individuals' opportunities. Many young people say they cannot afford to leave home and believe high housing costs could obstruct work and study and even prevent them from starting a family. Why is building and housing so expensive? What needs to change in the rules? What effects do changes to mortgage repayment requirements and loan caps have?
content.subject: Construction
speakerTitles: Deputy Chair of Stockholm's City Planning Committee

content.title: Older people with complex needs – how do we create capacity where pressure on care is greatest?
content.description: Older, frail patients with multiple conditions account for a large share of care needs but often become stuck in overloaded acute hospitals and unclear transitions between services. The question is how to organise care so that the right care is delivered in time, at the right level and with better continuity for the patient.
content.extendedDescription:
The seminar focuses on healthcare capacity for older, frail patients with multiple conditions, a group often needing both healthcare and eldercare. Drawing on experiences from geriatrics, advanced home healthcare, specialist palliative care and inpatient rehabilitation, we discuss how care pathways can be organised to reduce readmissions, make discharge safer and relieve acute hospitals.

The discussion explores the structural choices needed as the proportion of older patients grows rapidly. The event is a moderated discussion, opening with an address by the Minister for the Elderly.
content.subject: Health and social care
speakerTitles: Minister for Older People and Social Security

content.title: Securing critical construction materials in crisis and war
content.description: Reliable access to construction materials is a cornerstone of Sweden's preparedness. One example is cement production in Slite, which is of national interest. Hear leading industry and government agency representatives discuss how a stable supply of construction materials safeguards critical societal functions.
content.extendedDescription: Reliable access to construction materials is a central cornerstone of Sweden's preparedness. For example, both Myndigheten för civilt försvar and Tillväxtverket classify cement production in Slite as being of national interest because it is strategically critical to total defence. In this seminar, leading representatives from the construction materials industry, Boverket and Försvarsdepartementet / Myndigheten för civilt försvar (TBD) discuss how industry can best prepare to ensure the stable supply of construction materials needed for a range of critical societal functions.
content.subject: Security/defence
speakerTitles: Special Inquiry Chair on Establishing a New Environmental Permitting Agency

content.title: Building secure, adaptive and resilient digital capabilities for Modern defense and security
content.description: Security and defense are no longer defined by stability—they are shaped by constant disruption, hybrid threats, and rapidly shifting risk landscapes. In this environment, siloed systems and slow decision-making are no longer sustainable.
content.extendedDescription:
To stay ahead, organizations must be able to act on data in real time, collaborate across domains, and adopt new, faster ways of working.
This session explores how defense and public sector actors can move from fragmented structures to integrated, data-driven operations, drawing on lessons from NATO and national security environments.
We will highlight practical lessons learned and discuss how to build secure, adaptive and resilient digital capabilities—leveraging modern cloud technologies while meeting the highest security requirements.
content.subject: Communication/information
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Assistant Chief Officer - Director of Resources & Enabling Services

content.title: From ambition to the road: what is needed now for electric trucks in the haulage transition?
content.description: New data takes the pulse of the haulage transition: how many operators plan electric vehicles within 24 months, what prevents investment and which decisions make a difference?
content.extendedDescription:
We present a new study of haulage operators' actual transition intentions: the proportion planning electric trucks within 24 months, how plans differ by size, region and type of operation, and the most significant barriers – purchase costs, technology, charging infrastructure, residual value, customer requirements and rules.

The panel brings together different industry stakeholders to examine and discuss what is needed to accelerate the transition to electrified road transport, starting from haulage operators' perspectives. The audience will take away priority policy and market measures and concrete recommendations for industry actors – from insight to action.
content.subject: Energy
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Price tag or investment – when is a pill more than an expense?
content.description: Could a pill be society's best investment? Do we dare invest in innovation even when budgets are tight?
content.extendedDescription: The price of new medicines is often debated, but what happens if we look beyond the numbers? The seminar brings together an experienced panel with perspectives from decision-makers, government agencies, patients and healthcare for an open discussion about balancing innovation, cost-effectiveness and societal benefit. We discuss concrete challenges: how do we assess the value and societal benefits of different care interventions, and how do we prioritise when resources are limited? What risks and opportunities arise if we invest – or refrain? We are in an exciting period in which future views on medicines are being shaped, with both investments and tough cost decisions playing a role. Together, we seek new perspectives and solutions that can help people live healthier lives, transform Swedish healthcare and strengthen Sweden as a country.
content.subject: Health and social care

content.title: Data centres are crucial to Sweden's competitiveness
content.description: Data centres underpin AI, digitalisation and future growth. How do we ensure Sweden remains competitive in the global race for investment, innovation and digital infrastructure?
content.extendedDescription:
Data centres are increasingly highlighted as a key factor in Sweden's competitiveness, with major potential for investment, employment and innovation. At the same time, rapid technological change linked to AI and digitalisation is driving development, placing new demands on energy systems, infrastructure and permitting processes.

In this panel, actors from different parts of the value chain discuss:

- how Sweden can seize this growth opportunity,
- barriers relating to electricity supply, skills and regulation,
- how data centres can be integrated into the energy system in ways that strengthen both competitiveness and societal benefit.
content.subject: Digitalisation
speakerTitles: Head of External Relations and Sustainability

content.title: The EU's Culture Compass – a step towards a European policy for artists?
content.description: Ahead of its next long-term budget, the European Commission has developed a cultural strategy for Europe that includes a charter on artists' working conditions. What will the charter mean for Swedish policy for artists?
content.extendedDescription: Ahead of the next long-term budget, the European Commission has developed a cultural strategy entitled ‘A Culture Compass for Europe’, with proposals representing steps towards a coherent European policy for artists. The Commission wants to intensify efforts to improve artists' working conditions and will propose an EU charter for artists to establish basic principles, guidance and commitments for fair working conditions, and increase compliance and accountability, especially among recipients of EU cultural funding. In this discussion, we explore with politicians and government agency representatives what the charter could mean for Swedish policy for artists.
content.subject: EU
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Swedish Middle East policy 1948–2026
content.description: Israel and the Middle East are constantly in focus in Swedish politics. But how has Swedish policy developed and changed since Israel was established in 1948? Where do the political parties stand today?
content.extendedDescription:
Sweden's relations with Israel and the Palestinians have shaped our foreign policy for over seven decades and remain among our most debated issues. But what happened behind closed doors from 1948 to 2026 has never been told. Until now.

In the book ‘From Stockholm to Jerusalem: The Untold History of Sweden's Middle East Policy’ by Daniel Schatz, PhD, fifteen Swedish, Israeli and Palestinian heads of government and foreign ministers, along with around eighty ambassadors and senior politicians, share their experiences and reveal what actually happened behind the scenes.

This is followed by a panel with political party representatives. It will be a very engaging seminar and discussion! Based on 15 years of research, previously classified archive material and over a hundred in-depth interviews.
content.subject: International affairs

content.title: A new innovation strategy at the intersection of the built environment and mobility – crucial to the transition
content.description: The built environment and mobility are two systems that create many fundamental benefits for individuals, organisations and society as a whole, but also significantly affect the climate and resource consumption. How can we create conditions for sustainable innovation where the built environment and mobility meet?
content.extendedDescription:
Despite the strong connection between the built environment and mobility, these two systems have often developed along separate tracks rooted in different sectors. Integrating them creates conditions for more coherent, sustainable societal development, with added value benefiting both those alive today and future generations.

Here, ShiftSweden launches its strategy for the challenge of moving from separate sectors to integrated working methods and solutions at the intersection of the built environment and mobility. What is the strategy about? What is needed to achieve it?

Participating speakers will be updated.
content.subject: Innovation
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: The event is captioned, Wheelchair-accessible toilet, Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: The bank as coach or custodian? How to win Gen Z's trust in the financial market of the future
content.description: The financial sector faces a generational shift that challenges traditional customer relationship models. How are the economy and financial loyalty affected when tomorrow's most important customer group no longer trusts the established system?
content.extendedDescription:
In this seminar, we present insights from SKI and discuss the paradox that Gen Z demands more guidance than any other generation while trusting themselves more than their bank. Data from SKI's report ‘Young Customers' Expectations of the Financial Sector’ shows that the industry faces a major transition. Fully 48% of Gen Z want proactive contact at important life events, compared with just 16% of Gen X. The younger generation sees the bank as a partner in realising dreams rather than merely somewhere to keep money.
Yet one in four young customers would choose a different bank today if given the chance.
content.subject: Economy

content.title: Economic developments and monetary policy – what are the consequences for municipalities and regions?
content.description: Municipalities and regions with large loans can be affected by rising interest costs. We want to highlight this, explain the current situation and explore what today's economic conditions mean for Riksbanken's monetary policy considerations.
content.extendedDescription:
In a turbulent world, interest rates may need to rise quickly, potentially causing sharply higher interest costs for municipalities and regions with large loans and short fixed-rate periods. What is the situation now, and what do current economic conditions mean for Riksbanken's monetary policy considerations? How often should we expect Riksbanken to change interest rates going forward?

In this seminar, we hear from Deputy Governor Aino Bunge, who provides an up-to-date picture of the economic situation and its implications for lending to households, businesses, municipalities and regions.

Immediately after the address, we offer light refreshments, drinks and opportunities to network until 18.45.
content.subject: Economy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: On the front line against lethal violence: how do we prepare police and emergency services for ongoing lethal violence, PDV?
content.description: Ongoing lethal violence (PDV) places major demands on police. How should we prepare Swedish police for an increasingly complex society and ensure readiness when serious violent incidents occur?
content.extendedDescription:
Ongoing lethal violence requires rapid decisions, coordination and knowledge of both policing and tactical emergency medicine. Meanwhile, the threat landscape is changing as society becomes more complex. How do we equip police and other emergency services for this reality?

The discussion begins with a short introduction to how Swedish police are trained for PDV. A panel then discusses training, collaboration and research in tactical emergency medicine, as well as the conditions policymakers need to provide. The focus is on what Swedish police and emergency services need to be ready when the worst happens.
content.subject: Justice/crime
speakerTitles: Moderator and Head of the Academy of Police Work
Deputy Director of Segerstedtinstitutet and Senior Lecturer in Police Work at Akademin för polisiärt arbete

content.title: The right to asylum and Swedish asylum policy – are they compatible?
content.description: Sweden has adopted many national asylum laws in recent years while the EU's new Pact on Migration and Asylum is being implemented. But how well do the new laws respect international law, particularly the right to asylum?
content.extendedDescription:
In just a few years, Swedish asylum policy has been reformed in line with a political desire to sharply reduce immigration to Sweden. Some effects have received more attention than others, such as the deportation of teenagers, babies and very elderly people living alone. Is this policy compatible with the right to asylum? Meanwhile, the EU's Pact on Migration and Asylum has recently entered into force: what does it mean for the right to asylum in Sweden and Europe?
Starting with concrete questions, we discuss current asylum policy from a rights perspective.
content.subject: Human rights
speakerTitles: Lawyer specialising in Asylum and Migration Law

content.title: Why does a women's lifestyle magazine focus on algorithms that pressure young girls to be thin?
content.description: An investigation into algorithms on TikTok that pressure young girls to be thin recently attracted considerable attention. Who is responsible when social media harms young people's wellbeing?
content.extendedDescription:
Sweden's largest women's lifestyle magazine has won awards in recent years for a series of appeals and campaigns on current social issues. Femina has repeatedly confirmed that readers of a women's magazine want in-depth journalism on society. Femina's Editor-in-Chief Malin Roos explains why this is exactly what a ‘magazine for older women’ should do. After previously highlighting waiting lists for child and adolescent psychiatry and sexism in sport, a recent investigation into TikTok algorithms that pressure young girls to be thin attracted considerable attention. Who is responsible when social media harms young people's wellbeing?
A panel discussion brings together Nordic TikTok head Lukasz Lindell and Nikita Zeiloth, Chair of Frisk & Fri, Riksföreningen mot ätstörningar.
content.subject: Media/journalism
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: A new election, new opportunities – what is the future of new main railway lines?
content.description: New main railway lines affect Sweden's growth, skills provision and climate transition. The project is paused, but the 2026 election could change that. How do we bring the issue into the election campaign and onto the next government's agenda?
content.extendedDescription:
New main railway lines are crucial to increasing railway capacity, shortening journey times and connecting larger labour market regions across Sweden. For Jönköping, strategically located in the centre of southern Sweden, better connections are essential to strengthen business, facilitate commuting and contribute to national growth.

The seminar brings together representatives from politics, think tanks, business and the rail sector to discuss growth, commuting and the future of railways throughout Sweden. How can the new main lines project be revived ahead of the 2026 election and become one of the next government's priorities? Audience contributions are welcome towards the end of the seminar.
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport

content.title: Ports in the transition – stay the course
content.description: Swedish ports are now essential not only for exporting and importing goods but also as energy hubs for fuel bunkering and the future handling of new energy carriers.
content.extendedDescription:
Ports face major challenges in planning long-term investments in a rapidly changing world. Unlike investments in other sectors, maritime time horizons are often long, sometimes over 50 years. The importance of shipping and Swedish ports therefore needs highlighting, not only for daily imports and exports but also for ports' role in preparedness for essential transport and the importance of policies providing long-term stability.

Some port stakeholders will highlight this complexity, followed by a concluding panel discussion that explores the subject further with questions and contributions from the engaged audience.

Welcome!
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Head of Customer Relations and Marketing

content.title: The superstate – what is happening to European politics?
content.description: Recent turbulence in global politics is testing Europe. In an increasingly uncertain world, the EU is under pressure to step forward as the foremost defender of peace, freedom and democracy. Can the superstate meet the challenge?
content.extendedDescription:
Recent turbulence in global politics is testing Europe. In an increasingly uncertain world, the EU is under pressure to step forward as the foremost defender of peace, freedom and democracy. Can the superstate meet the challenge? What is happening to European politics in the shadow of Sweden's election campaign?

The EU is an unusual, voluntary collaboration between countries. In a new book, Susanna Kierkegaard describes a union where ‘bureaucrats are powerful, elected representatives unruly and officials love to party’. The seminar focuses on the future direction of the European superstate and the EU's unique potential to lead the world in addressing the defining challenges of our time.
content.subject: EU
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Donald Trump's friends and foes – the USA's new role in Asia
content.description: Donald Trump has not only stirred emotions in Europe but also challenged partners and allies in Asia. What are the sensitive issues, and how have America's friends in Asia responded to Trump's assertive foreign policy?
content.extendedDescription:
The USA has long declared that the future lies in Asia, but what has happened in practice? Washington's resources and attention have recently focused on the Middle East, despite a new security strategy that prioritises Asia as the USA's most important security region alongside the Western Hemisphere. Meanwhile, US–China relations appear to have entered a less confrontational phase.

Welcome to Utrikespolitiska institutet's morning in Almedalen. We discuss today's major foreign policy issues and offer perspectives on dramatic developments around the world. There will also be opportunities to mingle, talk to our experts and make connections.

Utrikespolitiska institutet combines research, analysis and public education on international affairs.
content.subject: International affairs

content.title: EHDS and national digital infrastructure – what long-term value is created and what are government agencies doing?
content.description: For decades, healthcare has struggled with fragmented systems where information gets trapped in silos and patients have to tell their stories repeatedly. That is now changing.
content.extendedDescription:
Sweden is in the midst of one of the most ambitious digital transformation projects in the sector's history. The European Health Data Space (EHDS) requires us as a nation to move from vision to implementation of major changes. A national digital infrastructure (NDI) is taking shape, and it needs to happen quickly.

This seminar gives you a clear picture of what is underway, the benefits of sharing health data and what happens next. You will leave understanding what national digital infrastructure means in practice, the long-term value it creates and why decisions and action are needed now, not later.
content.subject: Digitalisation
speakerTitles: President of Research Education, Development and Innovation
Specialist Physician and Country Manager, Sweden

content.title: Waiting lists, capacity and collaboration: how do we get healthcare to deliver on time?
content.description: Healthcare waiting lists are long despite historically high resources. Meanwhile, spare capacity is not fully used. The question is how to organise, coordinate and govern healthcare so patients receive timely care sooner, regardless of region or provider.
content.extendedDescription:
This seminar focuses on healthcare waiting lists as a systemic and capacity problem rather than solely a resource issue. Drawing on research, policy analysis and ongoing national reforms, it discusses how collaboration between providers, regions and patients can better match needs with available care.

The discussion addresses how governance, organisation and information sharing affect actual delivery, and which tools exist or could be developed to shorten waiting lists, increase mobility within the system and use healthcare's combined capacity more efficiently.

The seminar concludes with a panel discussion featuring relevant politicians.
content.subject: Health and social care

content.title: How can Mälardalen and Sweden win the competition for skills?
content.description: Swedish employers lack around 61,000 people with the right skills. Three in four say recruitment is difficult, and one in four recruitment attempts fails. Meanwhile, many highly educated people are unemployed or work below their skill level. These are not coincidences – they are a systemic failure.
content.extendedDescription:
Sweden attracts international talent, but lengthy establishment processes and inadequate integration mean we lose it again. Swedish higher education institutions attract international students, but only one in four remains in the Swedish labour market after graduation, although three in four want to.

Stockholm-Mälardalen has Sweden's largest labour market and its strongest concentration of industry, energy systems, logistics and technology-intensive companies. Skills shortages have immediate consequences here: investments are delayed, expansion fails to materialise and the transition slows.
content.subject: Employment/labour market
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Politics and meaning after liberalism?
content.description: The era of liberalism is over and winds of change are blowing, but what comes next? What is the meaning of life, democracy's crisis and political renewal, and how do we include perspectives from different voices?
content.extendedDescription:
It was said that history had ended, liberal democracy had triumphed and the future promised continual improvement. That did not happen. Instead, we live amid intertwined economic, political and existential crises. How did we get here? And what can we do about it?

The panellists discuss the meaning of life, human nature and democracy's decline. How deep is our societal crisis, and how could politics have gone astray? What are the roles of the labour movement and LO? What would returning to its roots mean for social democracy? How does the centre-right view the weakening of liberalism?

Welcome to a discussion of political ideas based on Payam Moula's book Det goda, with panellists bringing different perspectives.
content.subject: Democracy
speakerTitles: Doctor of Theology in Ethics, Author, Cultural Commentator

content.title: Military communications security – knowledge that has yet to reach civilian society
content.description: For decades, the military has protected communications and command systems against interception, interference and electromagnetic pulses. This knowledge is proven. But as the same threats now reach civilian agencies and critical infrastructure, both expertise and tools are lacking. The gap is growing.
content.extendedDescription:
The boundary between military communications security and civilian preparedness is no longer clear. Hostile actors use the same methods against civilian targets that were previously directed only at military ones: jammers, IMSI catchers, electromagnetic pulses and remote control of devices that should be offline.
The discussion connects military experience to civilian application: what works in the field, what can be transferred and where civilian society's responsibility begins.
An open, question-led discussion. Held outside BLCKR's Signalskugga, a signal-blocking tent in Visby harbour where all communication is cut off. Coffee is served.
content.subject: Security/defence
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: How can policy secure a local energy transition that strengthens industry and preparedness?
content.description: Initiatives in Jönköpings län aim to secure energy supply and accelerate electrification through regional collaboration. Investments cover energy planning, island operation, flexibility, energy storage and energy efficiency. With the right political conditions, each initiative can have greater impact.
content.extendedDescription:
Amid geopolitical turmoil and accelerating climate change, the energy transition is not only crucial to Sweden's competitiveness, industrial development and preparedness – it is also an enabler. How do we use the energy transition to create jobs, growth and security?
What decisions and conditions are needed from national and local policymakers to move forward, scale up and ultimately maintain the competitiveness of industry and Sweden as a whole? How can regional energy transitions strengthen Sweden?
content.subject: Energy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Deputy CEO and Head of Offering and Digitalisation
Head of Energy and Community Development Section
Regional Councillor, Chair of the Transport, Infrastructure and Environment Committee

content.title: The regional airport of the future – what opportunities and challenges?
content.description: What role will regional airports play in the future? New technology and renewable fuels offer opportunities, but challenges are numerous. Where are we today, and what does the journey ahead look like?
content.extendedDescription:
Regional airports are essential to accessibility and preparedness across much of Sweden. Yet they face challenges in operations, profitability and the transition to fossil-free aviation in the air, in the tank and on the ground. Solutions exist, but progress is slow. What is needed to accelerate?

Sveriges Regionala Flygplatser and Grön Flygplats bring together representatives from aircraft manufacturing, fuels and regional airport operations to discuss concrete solutions already within reach: new aviation technology, Swedish-produced renewable fuel and transformed airport operations. We conclude by identifying what would make the greatest difference in reaching the goal efficiently.
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Political advertising in transition – how are democracy's rules affected?
content.description: New transparency and technology requirements are emerging for political advertising. How do we ensure open, safe and inclusive democratic debate amid rapid change and under the EU's new political advertising regulation?
content.extendedDescription:
Ahead of the 2026 election year, Sweden faces a perfect storm: the EU's new regulation on transparency in political advertising (TTPA), tech platforms' decisions to stop or restrict political ads, growing threats of foreign interference and increasing debate about AI-generated content.

What does it mean for democracy when opportunities to communicate messages are restricted, smaller parties struggle for visibility or troll factories operate beyond the rules' reach?
This seminar brings stakeholders together to discuss how to ensure open, safe and inclusive democratic debate amid rapid change.
content.subject: Communication/information
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: The broken world order – can we patch it up?
content.description: Donald Trump has challenged the world order, international law and international cooperation. What are the greatest challenges and possible future scenarios? And what difference can Europe make?
content.extendedDescription:
Today's world is marked by great uncertainty and intense competition between the major powers, the USA and China. Meanwhile, democracies are declining in number and authoritarian states are gaining ground. The institutions created after the Second World War to regulate and stabilise relations between states are also severely weakened. And for Europe, the relationship with the USA is no longer what it was.

Welcome to Utrikespolitiska institutet's morning in Almedalen. We discuss today's major foreign policy issues and offer perspectives on dramatic global developments. There are also opportunities to mingle, talk to our experts and make connections.

Utrikespolitiska institutet combines research, analysis and public education on international affairs.
content.subject: International affairs

content.title: Nuclear weapons in space: physics, politics and the future
content.description: The 1967 Outer Space Treaty prohibits nuclear weapons in space, but major powers appear to have renewed interest in deploying weapons systems and countermeasures there. Combined with the growing role of private actors in space, this could have far-reaching consequences for humanity.
content.extendedDescription:
Welcome to an interdisciplinary panel discussion with nuclear weapons experts from nuclear physics, peace and conflict research, and civil society. The seminar will discuss:

• What is the greatest danger of nuclear weapons in space – how could they affect life on Earth?
• How would a nuclear explosion in space affect satellites and spacecraft?
• How can nuclear weapons in space be detected; can we verify that states do not have them there?
• How is the Outer Space Treaty observed, and what is its future?
• What diplomatic initiatives can Sweden, as a space nation, take to promote compliance with the Outer Space Treaty?
content.subject: International affairs
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Faster, more efficient environmental permits – a prerequisite for industrial development in Sweden
content.description: Unpredictable environmental permitting processes obstruct industrial development in Sweden. Could the proposals presented so far by the ongoing inquiry be part of the solution? And what do politicians think?
content.extendedDescription:
Industrirådet, comprising industry's five trade unions and eleven employer and industry organisations, is organising an Almedalen seminar on one of industry's major challenges today: permitting processes.

The seminar starts from the ongoing environmental permitting inquiry and the proposals presented so far, and examines what further measures are needed to achieve faster, more efficient assessment processes. This is crucial to a favourable industrial climate in Sweden, enabling investment and allowing Swedish industry to contribute to greater competitiveness, employment and long-term environmental sustainability.
content.subject: Climate/environment
speakerTitles: Member of Parliament, Chair of the Committee on Environment and Agriculture

content.title: How much should a beer be allowed to cost?
content.description: Alcohol tax is an important public health tool, but also depends on legitimacy among consumers and businesses. Where is the threshold beyond which further increases risk having the opposite effect through changing purchasing habits, cross-border shopping or reduced acceptance of the system?
content.extendedDescription:
The price of a beer is determined not just by what is in the bottle but above all by political decisions throughout the value chain. In recent years, Swedish households have seen costs rise sharply. Meanwhile, breweries face rising prices for raw materials, energy, transport and packaging.

Reasonable excise duties on beer matter. Excessively high prices risk not only harming businesses and jobs but also changing consumer behaviour, increasing cross-border shopping and illegal imports, and ultimately challenging trust in Sweden's entire alcohol model.

This seminar starts with a simple but crucial question: how much should a beer cost, and what happens when the bill becomes too high?
content.subject: Business
speakerTitles: PhD in Economics or Business Administration

content.title: Young people's future choices and tomorrow's skills supply – where are we falling short today?
content.description: How do we help young people make well-informed choices about their futures amid uncertainty, wrong turns and skills shortages?
content.extendedDescription:
Young people's choices about the future are often described as an individual responsibility, but the consequences of inadequate guidance, unclear information and weak links to working life are very much a societal issue. If young people lack relevant, understandable pictures of education, occupations and possible paths ahead, the risk of wrong choices, dropouts and poor matching increases, while many sectors struggle to secure the skills they need.

In this presentation, we discuss where things fall short today at the intersection of schools, study and career guidance, communications and working life. Can we, together with politicians, organisations and other societal actors, identify solutions, partnerships and new ways to strengthen young people's future choices?
content.subject: Children/young people

content.title: The city of the future is already built – why is it half-empty?
content.description: Empty offices, unused industrial premises, buildings in limbo – middle-aged buildings are the city's neglected assets and untapped potential. Transforming existing buildings can revitalise an area and an entire city. It saves time, money and climate emissions, but currently faces obstacles.
content.extendedDescription:
In this seminar, we present the opportunities. We highlight the project, commercial and financial challenges that property stakeholders and planners encounter in practice. We discuss municipalities' role and show concrete examples from Gothenburg where transformation is already bringing new life to old neighbourhoods.

But obstacles often lie in regulations and business models not designed for transformation. What national reforms are needed? What can municipalities do today? And what will enable more middle-aged buildings to find new life?
content.subject: Construction
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Project Manager, Sustainable and Circular Construction
Housing Policy Spokesperson, Member of Parliament
Group Leader and Municipal Councillor, Gothenburg

content.title: From ferry to destination – a seamless journey on Gotland without your own car
content.description: Trips to destinations generally involve travelling in your own car, which can be expensive, bad for the climate and almost impossible if you do not have one. This is especially true for destinations on Gotland. How can a door-to-door journey be put together without your own car?
content.extendedDescription: This seminar focuses on combining a door-to-door journey from home to Gotland without your own car, and the additional opportunities autonomous technology could offer in future. Partnerships and digital solutions can integrate booking and improve journey coordination, creating greater flexibility and faster, cheaper travel. Autonomous transport can increase accessibility where transport options are currently limited. During the seminar, we learn from different projects about opportunities and challenges associated with autonomous and integrated multimodal transport solutions.
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Asthma, allergies, eczema – new knowledge of type 2 inflammation changes our understanding of atopic diseases
content.description: Asthma, allergies, eczema and nasal polyps – one diagnosis rarely comes alone. If you have one of these conditions, the likelihood of also having at least one more is up to 70%. How can we break down silos and create more multidisciplinary, holistic care for people living with several atopic diseases?
content.extendedDescription:
Live podcast and panel discussion with Manne Forssberg – light lunch provided!

During this seminar, experts guide us through new knowledge about the connections between these diseases and explain how their impact on life can intensify when several occur together. We highlight patient perspectives, reveal often hidden suffering and discuss how healthcare structures can develop. How are atopic diseases connected, and what role does the underlying type 2 inflammation, driven by an overactive immune system, play?
content.subject: Health and social care
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: PhD in Medicine, Specialist in Allergology

content.title: Customers, capital, skills or rules – what kills growth?
content.description: Sweden produces world-class startups. Yet surprisingly few make it all the way from promising idea to global growth company. Too many stall or die in the critical phase between product and profitability, often called the ‘Valley of Death’. What is actually stopping them?
content.extendedDescription:
Is it a lack of capital during the riskiest phases? A share-option system that makes competing for talent globally difficult? Or rules and structures effectively designed for large companies rather than agile startups? Meanwhile, requirements are tightening in areas such as AI, data and cybersecurity. Necessary, but at what cost? Has Sweden become too complex, too expensive or too cautious to build the next generation of tech companies?

Without the right conditions in the ‘Valley of Death’, the quality of the ideas does not matter. What is holding Swedish startups back, and what must change?
content.subject: Innovation

content.title: Decolonizing Ukrainian narratives: countering Russian propaganda and strengthening Ukraine's voice in Europe
content.description: Russia's information war runs alongside its military war. Russian propaganda shapes opinion in Europe and undermines support for Ukraine. How do we decolonise Ukrainian narratives and ensure Ukraine's voice is heard on its own terms?
content.extendedDescription: For decades, Ukraine has fought Russian attempts to redefine its history, culture and identity. Since the full-scale invasion in 2022, this information struggle has intensified. Russian disinformation spreads through European media, social networks and political discussions, risking erosion of public and political support for Ukraine. The panel brings together researchers and practitioners working on narratives, human rights and security policy to discuss how Europe can strengthen resilience against disinformation and give Ukrainian perspectives space on their own terms, rather than filtering them through Russian or Western interpretive frameworks.
content.subject: International affairs
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: PhD, Director of WarDS Lab and USI – Ukrainian Studies Interhub

content.title: How to get time, cost and quality on your side throughout your construction project
content.description: How can developers and municipalities design and build using fewer natural resources, create less climate impact and still make projects financially viable? How could these options actually be better in today's global context?
content.extendedDescription:
The panel highlights alternative construction concepts and techniques that challenge traditional ways of building and developing built-environment projects. The discussion focuses on how today's construction methods affect finances, climate and resource management.

The panel discusses alternative methods and technical solutions currently available and their potential effects on construction time, climate footprint, finances and quality.
It also addresses what is needed for new, more sustainable building concepts to gain a larger market share, including innovation, regulation, procurement, willingness to invest and how the sector can create better conditions for development and change.
content.subject: Construction

content.title: Construction's hidden waste – can digitalisation cut materials, transport and emissions?
content.description: Construction accounts for a large share of Sweden's resource consumption. Much waste originates early: incorrect quantities, duplicate orders and unnecessary transport. How can digitalisation reduce waste and emissions, and what do smaller actors need to make the transition?
content.extendedDescription:
The discussion starts with a concrete question: how much material is wasted in construction, and where in the chain does this happen? Much waste and unnecessary transport between wholesalers and construction sites originates during quantity estimation and ordering, long before anything is built.
We discuss how digitalisation and AI can reduce material waste and transport, what wholesalers, installers and contractors need to change, and how the green transition can progress without raising costs for smaller actors.
The focus is on structural societal issues, not individual products or solutions.
content.subject: Sustainability

content.title: Should we shut down district heating, or does it have a future?
content.description: In recent years, many municipalities and their public housing companies have seen sharply rising district heating costs for public-service premises and homes.
content.extendedDescription:
Four municipalities in inland Västerbotten have joined a project to highlight rising district heating costs. None operates its own district heating; external operators own and run the systems. The municipalities now face a difficult situation as homeowners switch to other energy sources and municipalities themselves choose alternatives for new public-service properties. What happens when a town's district heating network is no longer considered profitable enough and the external operator withdraws? Small municipalities with declining populations lack investment funds to convert, and doing so would also destroy capital when a fully functioning district heating network already exists.

The seminar examines the current situation for district heating and discusses its possible future.
content.subject: Energy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Chair of the Municipal Executive Board

content.title: Honour the fallen – and what does Sweden promise those who live?
content.description: How can Swedish civil society build long-term structures for cooperation with Ukraine, and why is there still no national platform doing so systematically?
content.extendedDescription:
On 22 June, SPSU opens Almedalsveckan with a ceremony holding two things at once: a moment of silence and honour for those who have fallen defending Ukraine, and an uncomfortable political assertion that Sweden has yet to build the partnership with Ukrainian civil society that the situation demands.

The ceremony includes a minute's silence in memory of Ukraine's fallen. The discussion then opens: what is needed for genuine, long-term, structured civilian cooperation between Sweden and Ukraine, and who will take responsibility for making it happen?

The ceremony marks the start of five days of discussion, debate and meetings in SPSU's tent on Cramérgatan, an initiative by KlinteVolontär giving Ukrainian civil society a voice in Swedish democratic debate.
content.subject: International affairs
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: European control and global technological capability – how do we find the cloud balance?
content.description: As cloud services, AI and data become critical infrastructure for society and business, Sweden and Europe face decisive strategic choices. The question is not whether to choose digital sovereignty or global innovation capacity, but how to combine them.
content.extendedDescription: The panel discusses how Sweden must accelerate substantially and can learn from its Nordic neighbours. We explore how businesses and the public sector can pursue strategic control without technological isolation, and combine European values and regulations with global scalability and innovation. What does digital sovereignty mean in practice? How can Sweden reduce risky dependencies without slowing innovation and progress? The question is not whether to choose digital sovereignty or global innovation capacity, but how to combine them to strengthen both competitiveness and security while ensuring a high degree of autonomy when required.
content.subject: Employment/labour market
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: The value of culture – in an age that has lost its judgement
content.description: What place should art and culture have in a society where economic utility has become the dominant measure of value? How do we understand culture's role in education, democracy and human existential needs?
content.extendedDescription: What is at stake for democracy, education and governance when cultural values are marginalised and measurable utility becomes the dominant measure of meaning? Drawing on the intellectual heritage of popular education and the interaction between universities, civil society and cultural institutions, we examine culture's role today – not as decoration or a product, but as a fundamental dimension of democratic society. How can cultural values be articulated anew and given real significance in societal development?
content.subject: Culture

Vice-Rector for Education, Lifelong Learning and Culture
Chair of Rörelsefolkhögskolornas intresseorganisation RIO and Biskops Arnö Nordens Folkhögskola, former Minister for Education
Vice-Rector for Culture and Educational Development

content.title: How do we increase voter turnout in socioeconomically disadvantaged neighbourhoods?
content.description: Differences in voter turnout between neighbourhoods are a growing democratic challenge in Sweden. Low participation in socioeconomically disadvantaged areas risks reinforcing inequality and reducing political equality. What measures can strengthen democratic participation?
content.extendedDescription:
Differences in voter turnout between neighbourhoods have increased over time and risk deepening existing socioeconomic divides. When people in some areas participate less, political equality and democratic representation suffer.

The discussion draws on a new knowledge review from Delmi, written by Karl-Oskar Lindgren, Professor of Political Science. The publication systematically reviews Swedish and international research on the causes of differences in democratic participation and measures shown to increase voter turnout in disadvantaged areas.
content.detail: Migration och bistånd - två frågor i ett tält
content.subject: Research

content.title: How do we make wise choices when innovation becomes infrastructure?
content.description: New technology is fundamentally changing property management, from reactive to predictive. Electric vehicle charging and drone-based inspections are two examples of moving from firefighting to planning ahead. But how do you invest wisely when technology becomes part of a property's infrastructure?
content.extendedDescription:
New technology is changing what it means to own and manage property. What were once individual optional additions are increasingly part of long-term property infrastructure, creating opportunities for proactive, data-driven management.
We illustrate this through two areas: charging infrastructure's evolution from individual stations into complex systems of hardware, payment services, power management and operations; and how drone inspections of roofs and façades transform maintenance from isolated interventions into a continuous data source for property management.
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Can healthcare focus more on doing things right than simply avoiding mistakes?
content.description: Healthcare culture is largely built on control and regulation. As employees leave healthcare, is it time to review that culture? After years of New Public Management, guideline-based governance and unwieldy medical records systems, can fear of mistakes be complemented by a desire to do things right?
content.extendedDescription: Socialstyrelsen tasked Region Halland with testing the Safety II model to explore potential improvements in staff retention, working conditions and patient safety. Besides focusing more on strengthening good behaviours, Safety II takes greater account of the surrounding system. At the seminar, we hear more about Halland's results and discuss implications for renewed governance aimed at better working conditions, communication and regulatory support, complementing control and compliance.
content.detail: Arena Tillsammans: the arena for healthcare's major systemic issues.
content.subject: Health and social care
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation

content.title: Security and climate preparedness in Swedish and EU ports
content.description: In March 2026, the European Commission adopted two strategies to promote competitiveness, sustainability, security and resilience in the EU's waterborne sector. They focus mainly on ports, shipping and shipbuilding, sectors crucial to EU trade, economic growth, security and defence.
content.extendedDescription:
Swedish ports play an important role in national transport, the economy and preparedness. Port regions need to increase their understanding of how climate change may affect them and strengthen their ability to consider new societal changes and geopolitical threats.

Ports now face several new and complex risks linked to the climate crisis, societal changes and geopolitical challenges. With these new strategies in place, EU member states, including Sweden, will be obliged to adopt strategic, feasible plans addressing and managing climate resilience.
content.subject: Sustainability
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Senior Research Fellow and Team Lead Water Coasts & Ocean

content.title: Early interventions to prevent crime among children and young people
content.description: When young people are drawn into crime, it affects not only their futures but society as a whole. How can police, social services, business and civil society collaborate to prevent crime and create better opportunities for children and young people?
content.extendedDescription:
Rätt Kurva is a crime prevention programme in which police and social services collaborate with business and civil society through Beredskapslyftet to identify and support children and families at risk. After 2.5 years, the programme operates in 11 municipalities, and experience shows the importance of early, coordinated interventions.

The seminar discusses:
• How collaboration between societal actors can strengthen crime prevention
• Experiences and results from Rätt Kurva's work in municipalities across the country
• Challenges and opportunities in reaching children and families at risk
• How more municipalities can access and implement the model
content.subject: Children/young people
speakerTitles: Deputy Head of Local Police Area

content.title: Sweden's action against falsely flagged vessels and the so-called shadow fleet
content.description: How do we act against falsely flagged vessels and the so-called shadow fleet operating in our waters? What have we learned from this spring's boardings, and how do we proceed?
content.extendedDescription:
Since Russia began its war against Ukraine, the number of so-called shadow vessels has increased markedly in the Baltic Sea and along Sweden's coast. Recently, we have seen a new trend: more vessels sailing under false flags and with inadequate documentation. Vessels that disregard national and international law and choose to violate international agreements pose a high risk to shipping in Swedish waters, our shipping lanes and ports, and particularly the environment.

Kustbevakningen, working closely with other agencies, has therefore decided to intervene by boarding several vessels, after which their masters were remanded in custody and the vessels prohibited from use.

Welcome to a highly topical seminar on the strategy behind Sweden's actions.
content.subject: Security/defence
content.accessibility: The event is captioned

content.title: Can shops fine thieves?
content.description: High-volume crime and shop theft are serious societal problems. Police have long struggled to prioritise these offences, and most cases are closed when reported. Could fines following the Dutch model be a way to address the issue?
content.extendedDescription:
Watch the broadcast at
https://www.youtube.com/@livsmedelshandlarna1826

It is important to look at countries facing situations similar to Sweden's to learn and find innovative ways to address retail crime.

The Netherlands stands out as a country that has found new ways to handle retail crime more effectively while relieving pressure on police. By delegating much of the police work to shop owners, making offenders bear part of the costs and coordinating the handling of shop access bans, it has developed new ways to reduce shop theft and shoplifting.

In connection with the seminar, Livsmedelshandlarna will release a report describing the issue.
content.subject: Justice/crime
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

Police Officer and Member of Parliament

content.title: From fossil fuel dependence to e-fuel producer – how do we get there?
content.description: Europe has awakened to a new security situation, but our energy system remains dependent on imported fossil fuels.
content.extendedDescription:
With abundant fossil-free electricity, a strong industrial base and leading innovators, Sweden has a concrete opportunity not only to reduce dependence but to become a leading European e-fuel producer.

Can this development be accelerated?

Hydrogen and e-fuel value chains are taking shape, connecting electricity, industry and transport in new ways. But obstacles remain: an uncertain investment climate, slow permitting processes and a lack of long-term rules hold back a transition Sweden should be leading.

This seminar starts from Sweden's strengths and discusses what is needed to turn potential into reality. What obstacles must be removed? And who needs to act?
content.subject: Energy
speakerTitles: Member of Parliament and Deputy Chair

content.title: Life in displacement – what is everyday life like for those forced to leave everything behind?
content.description: What are everyday life and reality like for the people behind refugee statistics?
content.extendedDescription: In one of the refugee tents we use around the world, we explain our work and offer a concrete insight into everyday life for displaced people. The tent is built to withstand extreme heat, cold, heavy rain and strong winds. But it is more than shelter from the weather. For many families, it becomes a first step towards safety and hope for the future. UNHCR's work also goes beyond providing emergency shelter and relief. In all the more than 130 countries where we operate, we support people forced to flee war, conflict and persecution in many ways. This can mean helping families reunite, offering legal assistance and creating safety and hope so displaced people can rebuild their lives. A warm welcome to our refugee tent for an encounter with the reality behind refugee statistics.
content.subject: International affairs

content.title: From AI pilots to business – how tomorrow's companies are changing
content.description: The AI transition is not just a business and ethics issue. It is one of the most profound societal changes of our time, and its outcome depends on what leaders of established organisations actually do next.
content.extendedDescription:
But much of the debate remains caught in hype: models, billions and visions. Leaders of established organisations face a different question: what do we actually do now, as AI begins changing the business model itself?

This discussion brings together a small group of leaders for an honest conversation about the gap between AI pilot projects and real transformation, and what is needed to bridge it.

We open the roundtable with a provocation: if an AI-native company launched in your industry today, how would it beat yours – and how many months would you have?
content.subject: Digitalisation
speakerTitles: VP Engineering and Head of Bosch Research in Lund

content.title: 19,700 children a year – who catches them when school adjustments disappear?
content.description: Every year, almost 20,000 pupils leave compulsory school without eligibility for upper secondary education. The biggest school reform in 30 years is now being implemented. Does it meet the needs of children who are struggling and failing at school, or abandon them?
content.extendedDescription:
One in six pupils leaves compulsory school without eligibility for upper secondary education, a figure unchanged for decades. Behind it are children with growing mental ill health, increasing absence and paths often leading to exclusion. Many have neurodevelopmental conditions or other support needs that today's schools do not meet.
From 2028, new curricula will follow children's cognitive development. At the same time, additional adjustments and the guarantee of early support are being abolished. Signs often appear in the early primary years. The question is what failing to identify them in time costs.
Does the reform meet the needs of children who are struggling and failing at school, or abandon them?
A discussion about mental ill health, exclusion and what is needed in practice.
content.subject: Education
speakerTitles: Education Policy Spokesperson and Member of Parliament

content.title: When pupils leave school without eligibility – what does it do to their mental health?
content.description: School should prepare young people for the future. But for too many pupils, it has also become the place where anxiety about that future grows. The links between school failure, exclusion and mental ill health are clear. How should society prevent this development and let young people's own voices shape solutions?
content.extendedDescription: Every year, around 35,000 pupils enter adulthood without a complete upper secondary qualification, largely because of incomplete compulsory school grades and introductory programmes that trap pupils in past educational failures. They enter adult life uncertain about the future and at risk of exclusion from both further education and work. Behind these figures are young people who may have carried a fear of failure and a sense of inadequacy throughout their schooling. This is a systemic failure we must address.
content.detail: Folkets park by Tim Bergling Foundation
content.subject: Children/young people

content.title: Can Sweden build more in wood while reducing clear-cutting?
content.description: Wood is central to construction's climate transition. Meanwhile, criticism of forestry's clear-cutting is growing because of its impacts on climate and biodiversity. Can Sweden increase timber construction without increasing pressure on forests – and if so, how?
content.extendedDescription: Today, almost all Swedish construction timber comes from clear-cut forestry followed by replanting a single species, mainly spruce or pine. Meanwhile, new models are emerging in which timber from close-to-nature and continuous-cover forestry can supply construction projects with ambitious climate and biodiversity targets, often at limited additional cost. Can different timber types coexist in the market, with some projects using timber offering extra environmental performance? Can demand from construction help scale up new forestry methods? The seminar discusses how construction can help develop a more sustainable timber market and reconcile timber construction's climate potential with forests' ecological values.
content.detail: Tent by the guest harbour near the Strandgatan — Kaserngatan junction
content.subject: Construction
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Where does Sweden stand in the global AI race – and what is needed to keep up?
content.description: What drives AI adoption in leading countries, and what conditions are missing in Sweden?
content.extendedDescription:
Sweden ranks 33rd out of 44 countries in the WIN World AI Index. Countries such as the USA, Canada, France and Norway rank ahead of us, while the fastest-growing AI nations are at the top. Meanwhile, the survey shows that the proportion of Swedes using AI has increased by 20 percentage points in a year – eight in ten now report using AI in some form.

What explains the differences between the leading countries and Sweden? What roles do trust, skills and workplace conditions play in a country's ability to adopt and benefit from AI?

Karin Nelsson, CEO of Demoskop, presents the global results and what they reveal about conditions for AI adoption in Sweden. A panel of representatives from business, politics and AI research then comments on and discusses the findings.
content.subject: Digitalisation
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: What happens to the electronics tax after the election?
content.description: The electronics tax is added directly to the price when you buy electronics and household appliances. Swedish households pay around SEK 2.7 billion annually, going straight into the public treasury. The tax was supposed to provide environmental benefits but has not done so. Why does it remain?
content.extendedDescription:
A discussion of the electronics tax, sometimes called the chemicals tax: an additional tax on household appliances and consumer electronics found only in Sweden which, despite its ambition, has delivered no environmental benefit. It is added to the product price and based on product weight. The electronics tax can increase the price of a television, computer or household appliance by up to SEK 690. VAT is then charged on the tax. Consumers therefore pay not only the tax but also tax on the tax, making games consoles more expensive in Sweden than in other markets.

What do prospective MPs actually think of the tax, how could it be abolished, and what consequences has it had for Swedish businesses?

content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation

content.title: Medical research and innovation under pressure – can the next government meet voters' expectations?
content.description: A new geopolitical situation, increased preparedness efforts and growing threats to science make it harder to conduct critical activities such as life science research and development and quality-driven healthcare. How can the next government ensure Sweden does not fall behind?
content.extendedDescription:
Forska!Sverige and Uppsala universitet welcome you to a questioning session with Minister for Upper Secondary Education, Higher Education and Research Lotta Edholm and Socialdemokraterna's Education Policy Spokesperson Anders Ygeman.

During the seminar, we present a new survey asking voters about their expectations of an incoming government's ability to strengthen conditions for medical research, business and healthcare in the new global situation. The findings are discussed with Minister Lotta Edholm and Anders Ygeman, who will explain how their parties intend to safeguard and strengthen Swedish research if they form a government after the election.
content.subject: Research

content.title: A national vaccination programme for older people – the next step towards equitable health and preparedness
content.description: Sweden lacks a national vaccination programme for people over 65, leading to unequal access to care. How can a coordinated programme strengthen health, reduce pressure on healthcare and improve preparedness?
content.extendedDescription:
Sweden has a strong childhood vaccination programme, but still lacks systematic, nationally coordinated protection for older people. In Almedalen, we bring together key figures to discuss why a national vaccination programme for older people is a crucial investment in health, quality of life and societal preparedness, and what political decisions are needed to move from words to action.

The seminar presents the new report ‘Prevention, Health & Preparedness – Why a National Vaccination Programme for Older People Is Needed’, produced by PRO, SPF Seniorerna and SKPF Pensionärerna together with industry organisation Lif.
