content.title: Can you build a voter base through housing?
content.description: Detached houses mean right-wing votes and rentals left-wing votes? Hardly. Urban voters reluctant to vote right dominate big-city tenant-owned apartments, and detached-house neighbourhoods are far from ideologically uniform. What role does housing really play in party sympathies and voting patterns in a complex electorate?
content.extendedDescription: Suburban detached housing produces centre-right voters, while renters vote left. Is it really that simple? Housing has become an engine of new political divides cutting across traditional bloc politics. Urban voters reluctant to vote right dominate expensive city apartments, and detached-house neighbourhoods are far from ideologically uniform. For those excluded from home ownership, housing can symbolise political exclusion and a sense of failure, driving sympathies towards populist movements. What role does housing actually play in party sympathies and voting patterns in Sweden's increasingly complex electorate?
content.subject: Construction
speakerTitles: Chair of the Municipal Executive Board, Ekerö
Associate Professor, PI for the Swedish election study

content.title: Cycling's central role in building a sustainable society
content.description: A sustainable society requires sustainable infrastructure, including roads, cycle paths and railways within and beyond our cities. Few transport modes connect society and strengthen public health as cycling can.
content.extendedDescription:
Bring your bicycle and discuss sustainable infrastructure outside the city wall! Everyone with a bicycle is welcome; we adapt the route and pace. Before departure, we gather for 10–15 minutes for an introductory discussion and to wait for everyone. Afterwards, a nourishing breakfast and further conversation await those who wish and are able to stay. Cycle and network!

This is a perfect opportunity to combine exercise with interesting discussions about sustainable solutions and the essential transition from brown to green development. You must bring your own bicycle. We start at Skeppargatan 24 and follow a loop taking about an hour. Breakfast is provided afterwards, and anyone who wishes can stay for further discussion. We recommend exercise clothing or clothes that can withstand wear.
content.subject: Construction

content.title: How can Europe create its own social media platform that serves democracy?
content.description: Social media shape opinion, spread disinformation and store data without democratic scrutiny, but also provide a platform for spreading democracy. Is it time for Europe to create its own social media platform, and what would success require?
content.extendedDescription:
Democracy is being challenged from within by platforms built for engagement rather than truth. Polarisation increases, facts are relativised and citizens' data are controlled by actors without European roots. Meanwhile, opportunities are growing to build alternatives grounded in European values of privacy, transparency and freedom of expression.

How does today's platform logic affect democratic debate? What do regulation, technology and civil society need to reverse the trend? What role can Europe take? Is it time for its own social media platform?

Register for the breakfast seminar using the link below.
content.detail: Loops arena för impact, industri och energi
content.subject: Democracy
speakerTitles: Author, Filmmaker, Public Commentator, former CEO of TV4

content.title: Where are the women? Who gets seen, heard and shapes tomorrow's cities?
content.description: Although women make up most architecture students and a growing share of the profession, men still dominate media visibility, industry awards and public debate. How does this affect the perspectives and role models shaping future cities?
content.extendedDescription:
Architecture still shows an imbalance between those working in the profession and those visible in media, winning awards and setting the public agenda.

Why? How does visibility affect the ability to influence our cities' development? What can the profession, academia and media do to make public discussion more representative?

The event is a public roundtable exploring different perspectives, followed by audience dialogue. Its purpose is to identify structures, challenge entrenched patterns and discuss concrete paths towards greater visibility and representation in the built-environment sector.

No preparation is required.
content.subject: Gender equality

content.title: Energy security when it matters – how do we protect Sweden's energy system from external interference?
content.description: Amid cyber threats, geopolitical uncertainty and growing system complexity, energy security is as much about control and recovery as production and capacity. Can Sweden's energy system really withstand external interference?
content.extendedDescription:
Reports of threats to Nordic energy infrastructure, increasing cyberattacks on Europe's power sector and a stronger total defence focus show that the energy system is a strategic target. Threats to Nordic energy infrastructure are no longer hypothetical. Does Sweden have the control, skills and operational capacity to resist and recover quickly?
Welcome to a topical, forward-looking Rejlers Play discussion on energy security when it matters: how do we protect Sweden's energy system from external interference? In Almedalen, Rejlers brings together agencies, industry and decision-makers to discuss building dependable robustness in an open, interconnected energy system.
content.subject: Energy
speakerTitles: Lieutenant General, Chief of the Defence Staff

content.title: 25 years of crises: what has liberalism been doing?
content.description: A review of liberalism's intellectual development during the first quarter-century of the 2000s. How has the ideology navigated crises, innovations, wars and a pandemic, and perhaps its own fading existence?
content.extendedDescription:
The first quarter-century of the 2000s is said to belong to populists and anti-democrats. There is talk of conservatism's return and the radicalisation of the left. Liberalism, by contrast, is widely regarded as being in crisis.

But is that really true? Liberal thought over the past quarter-century tells another story.
The anthology ‘A Liberal Canon’ collects the 2000s' most important texts for liberalism. It shows how liberalism has shaped, and been shaped by, financial and migration crises, the war on terrorism, right-wing populism's rise, increased prosperity, technological advances and much else.

Liberal kanon was produced by Timbro förlag in collaboration with Liberal Debatt, featuring texts by Anne Applebaum, Karl-Ove Knausgård, Johan Norberg and Boualem Sansal, among others.
content.subject: Democracy
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: From strategy to world leadership – how can the public sector make Sweden a leading AI nation?
content.description: AI is Sweden's next major competitive advantage. But we must stop talking and start delivering. Sweden has world-class research, high digital maturity and a unique energy position. Yet most AI initiatives stall in the pilot phase, never reaching real scale or societal benefit.
content.extendedDescription:
It is time to change that.

This roundtable discusses how the public sector can lead and help Sweden become the world's best at AI, in practice as well as on paper.
We address the tough questions:
How do we accelerate AI use while managing risks and regulation?
How much agility and experimentation can we actually afford?
How do we create new collaboration between the public sector, business and research that delivers results?
content.subject: Digitalisation
speakerTitles: Professor of Scientific Visualisation and Head of Media and Information Technology

content.title: Sweden's new basic industry: building global competitiveness in cultural and creative industries
content.description: In a rapidly growing global market where cultural content has become both geopolitical soft power and a major export commodity, Sweden faces important choices. How do we turn this creative strength into even greater international competitiveness?
content.extendedDescription:
Music, design, games, film, fashion, architecture and gaming: cultural and creative industries are no longer a niche, but among Sweden's most prominent assets. With turnover exceeding SEK 650 billion and 250,000 people employed, the sector is an economic engine strengthening Sweden's reputation as an innovative, creative nation.

Welcome to a discussion of:
• How cultural and creative industries have become a new national basic industry
• How Sweden can scale creative businesses and meet global demand
• The role of culture, design and digital creativity in national brands and soft power
• How a small nation can achieve global influence through culture-driven innovation
content.subject: Economy

content.title: Climate change and cultural heritage values
content.description: Climate change is accelerating risks of damage to cultural heritage. Extreme weather and temperature changes increase risks of moisture damage and physical deterioration. We need knowledge of how buildings with heritage value are affected by rapid climate change.
content.extendedDescription:
Climate change is increasingly evident in heritage environments through mould, rot and more insect attacks. Wall paintings are threatened by condensation damage, and masonry is fractured by more frequent swings between above- and below-freezing temperatures. Sweden still lacks strategic monitoring and thus systematic knowledge of the extent of damage. Norway has developed a method for climate monitoring of culturally significant buildings.

The seminar highlights known damage and discusses how agencies and heritage property managers could jointly build systematic knowledge to reduce and, ideally, prevent damage.
content.subject: Climate/environment

content.title: The growing need for reliable data in an AI-driven world
content.description: How do companies secure reliable, structured data as AI rapidly changes retail and global trade? Why should data be viewed as a strategic resource? Can poor data lead to bad decisions, inefficiency and reduced competitiveness?
content.extendedDescription:
This discussion explores how AI built on structured data can create more efficient, resilient value chains.

The event is aimed at those wanting to understand the connections between structured data, standards and efficient, reliable AI solutions from a retail perspective.

You will gain:
- Concrete examples of AI and standardised data working together in practice.
- Insights into business opportunities and risks when using AI on unstructured data.
- A look ahead: what can and should companies do now to benefit from next-generation AI solutions?
content.detail: Uppsala universitet - Campus Gotland, room D22
content.subject: Digitalisation
speakerTitles: Head of Innovation and Business Development

content.title: Honour-related violence – how did the issue emerge, and where are Sweden and the Nordic countries today?
content.description: Honour-related violence has been discussed as a political issue in Sweden for 30 years. How did debate begin? Which voices and victims came into focus? How have Nordic countries addressed it, and how do we balance recognition against invisibility?
content.extendedDescription:
Several widely reported, brutal murders of young women and a young man in the early 2000s put honour-related violence on Sweden's agenda. Society has since debated and acted against it. Action plans and legislation exist. But how did discussion and work against this violence begin here? How has policy developed in the Nordic countries? Do we know what makes an approach successful? How do we balance recognition against stigmatisation? Is Sweden extreme in its approach?

Meet researchers from three universities discussing past and present work against honour-related violence and oppression in Sweden and the Nordic region.
content.subject: Human rights
speakerTitles: Researcher and Lecturer in Law, Department of Law
Researcher and Lecturer in Social Work
PhD in sociology and researcher at the Department of Government

content.title: Soft power in a hard world – can soft innovation power move Sweden forward?
content.description:
In a world increasingly shaped by global conflicts and hard power, how can soft power serve as a strategic tool for Sweden's impact in the transition towards sustainability and stronger global competitiveness?
The programme and participants will be updated.
content.extendedDescription:
History has shown that soft power – in the form of values, knowledge and culture – can be very powerful. Countries seen as credible, responsible and progressive gain greater influence in international cooperation and global development.
This breakfast seminar explores how society as a whole can be mobilised to achieve Sweden's sustainable transition, both here and now and in the longer term. Starting from the need for broad, coordinated innovation capacity, we discuss how democratically grounded approaches, strong collaborative capabilities, creativity and solutions with export potential can strengthen Sweden's credibility and position as a frontrunner in the EU and globally.
The discussion is led by a moderator.
content.subject: Innovation
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: The event is captioned, Wheelchair-accessible toilet, Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: A regular doctor in primary care – why is it so difficult?
content.description: Providing patients with a regular doctor has long been a central policy goal in Sweden, to strengthen continuity and create safer, more coordinated care. Despite this, progress is slow.
content.extendedDescription:
Today, only around a third of patients have a regular doctor, and Sweden repeatedly ranks near the bottom in international comparisons of continuity in primary care.
Meanwhile, our Nordic neighbours have chosen a different path. In Norway and Denmark, patients have long been registered with a specific doctor, and continuity in that relationship is an integral part of primary care. There, having a regular doctor is standard practice, not a problem. Why is Sweden so different?

In this seminar, researchers from Sweden, Norway and Denmark present possible explanations for developments in Sweden and the differences between the countries. The aim is to offer new perspectives on why Sweden is still struggling with an issue our neighbours resolved long ago, and what is needed to take the next step.
content.subject: Health and social care
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: What do we get for our healthcare spending – why are patients' different needs not being met?
content.description: What does putting the patient first really mean when needs differ greatly? How can healthcare balance person-centred care, efficiency and equity, and do we need more developed organisational triage to meet the needs of different patient groups?
content.extendedDescription:
The patient should be the focus, but who is this patient? Often there are many different individuals with varying needs and preferences, even within the same medical condition. Topics include tailoring care to target groups, person-centred care, general guidelines and the advantages and disadvantages of freedom of choice. How can we meet the needs of expert patients, patients with rare conditions, patients with common, straightforward needs and very ill patients within the same service – and should we really do so everywhere? We are good at medical triage, but can we also develop organisational triage that enables appropriate individualisation while making services more efficient?

The seminar is part of Arena Tillsammans, the meeting place for healthcare's major systemic issues during Almedalsveckan.
content.detail: Arena Tillsammans: the arena for healthcare's major systemic issues
content.subject: Health and social care

content.title: Preparedness and resilience – what can we learn from Swedish companies in Ukraine?
content.description: Swedish companies in Ukraine have to manage the consequences of war in real time, from power outages and cyber threats to disrupted supply chains and staff shortages. What lessons from Swedish companies in Ukraine can strengthen preparedness in Sweden, our resilience and business's role in total defence?
content.extendedDescription: Forever Sustainable presents an ongoing study funded by Myndigheten för civilt försvar on how Swedish companies have adapted their operations in Ukraine. What lessons from Swedish companies in Ukraine can strengthen preparedness in Sweden, our resilience and business's role in total defence? Myndigheten för civilt försvar, Energimyndigheten, Företagarna and Sweco join the report's project manager Sophie Nachemson-Ekwall on stage. We share more about the study of Swedish companies' preparedness in Ukraine and hold a panel discussion with representatives of Myndigheten för civilt försvar, Energimyndigheten, business and academia.
content.subject: Security/defence
speakerTitles: Industry Policy Expert on Preparedness and Total Defence
Head of the Energy Preparedness Department

content.title: How the Nordic region can retain its lead in fusion energy
content.description: With green, safe and inexpensive baseload power, world-leading Nordic fusion technology opens up new opportunities for energy sovereignty, competitiveness, global development and the climate transition.
content.extendedDescription: After a hundred years of research and recent technological and political breakthroughs, fusion energy is approaching industrialisation within the next decade, with the USA and China in the lead and Europe close behind. With major public investment, an explosive increase in private capital and a growing number of private pilot plants, the global fusion race is in full swing, with the Nordic region and Sweden at the forefront. A series of seminars discusses the potential and challenges for Swedish, Nordic and European fusion power. What opportunities for national, regional and global development, prosperity and innovation emerge when energy is no longer a limiting factor?
content.subject: Energy
speakerTitles: Senior Policy Advisor on Energy Technology
Head of Sustainability and Corporate Affairs
Particle Physicist, Fusion Energy Investor and First Nordic Astronaut

content.title: Today's healthcare, tomorrow's solutions – greater national and regional collaboration for innovation
content.description: How do we secure the healthcare of the future when needs are growing faster than resources? Innovation is crucial to saving lives, strengthening the quality of care and creating sustainable societies. Yet today, many solutions get stuck in pilot projects. What is needed nationally for innovation to deliver real benefits for patients?
content.extendedDescription:
Sweden is a world leader in research and innovation, but considerably less successful at implementing new solutions at scale. Innovations get stuck in pilot projects, health data is difficult to use, clinical trials take too long and patients' access to new treatments varies depending on where they live.

The seminar brings together leading representatives of national and regional politics, healthcare, patient organisations and business to discuss how Sweden can create better conditions for innovation in healthcare, and why this is crucial to future patient benefit, quality of care and competitiveness.
content.subject: Health and social care

speakerTitles: Chair of the Regional Executive Board

content.title: How do we accelerate the transition in heavy transport?
content.description: Transport is a cornerstone of our economy, essential for people to live and work and for business and society to function. At the same time, transport – particularly heavy lorries – is one of Sweden's largest sources of emissions.
content.extendedDescription: Making the transport sector emission-free, and above all electrifying heavy transport, is crucial for Sweden to reduce its emissions and meet its climate targets. However, this transition is slow, partly because the necessary infrastructure is being developed slowly and partly because demand for both electric vehicles and green transport has been weak. How do we create the conditions needed for an emission-free transport sector? How do we connect the transport system with the electricity system? How can we best collaborate to make this succeed? What role can the financial sector play? And what is needed from policymakers?
content.subject: Sustainability
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Everyone wants to belong to a group
content.description: What settings make young people feel so involved that they want to give their all? And what can the sports movement, business and the prison and probation service learn from one another about creating environments where young people can have a say, take responsibility and make a difference?
content.extendedDescription:
Community is about more than being part of something. The settings in which people invest their commitment are often characterised by trust, responsibility and the opportunity to influence decisions.
Drawing on experiences from basketball, business and Kriminalvården, we discuss how different stakeholders work to create environments where people want to contribute, develop and take responsibility together. The discussion focuses on how belonging is built in practice, the importance of role models and relationships, and how young people can be given real scope to act.
What can different sectors learn from one another about creating settings that people choose to engage with and stay in?
content.subject: Children/young people

content.title: Culture, creativity and music exports – then, now and in the future
content.description: How have 20 years of streaming and technological development helped make the music industry and creative industries some of Sweden's most important export and future growth sectors? And how is AI affecting how music and culture are created, distributed, discovered and experienced?
content.extendedDescription:
When music streaming took off in the mid-2000s, it ushered in a new era in how music and culture are created, distributed and consumed. Over two decades, technological development has strengthened Sweden's position as a global leader in music, innovation and cultural exports. We now look ahead to what the next major technological shift could mean for music, literature, podcasts and other creative industries.

This discussion brings together different voices to explore how AI and new technology are changing the conditions for creative work, while audiences' ways of discovering and engaging with music and culture evolve. How can Sweden remain a leading player in music, creativity and cultural exports in a time of rapid technological development?
content.subject: Culture

content.title: Luxury or necessity – how should welfare services be funded?
content.description: Have welfare services become a spending trap? How can the finances add up?
content.extendedDescription:
In the TV programme "Lyxfällan", the solution is often to sell assets and cut spending. But what do you do when those "costs" are staff in welfare services?

"Lyxfällan" presenter Magnus Hedberg moderates a discussion with Vision's union president Veronica Magnusson and a panel of politicians and experts, using a budget board that puts welfare services' core mission at the centre.

Have welfare services become a spending trap we can cut our way out of? Or should citizens be able to expect equivalent services wherever they live? Is it efficiency when needs assessors and elderly care managers are forced to ask assistant nurses to shower more people in less time?

When health and social care needs grow faster than the resources provided, Sweden's municipalities and regions face a financial dead end. Major investment in water and wastewater infrastructure is also needed, and the climate issue is more important than ever.

How should welfare services be funded?
content.subject: Economy

content.title: Digital infrastructure takes shape in practice – it is time to get on board!
content.description: In summer 2026, a completely new portal will be launched for connecting to the national digital infrastructure for health, healthcare and social care data. The portal will be the hub where the sector's stakeholders find general information, a timetable and practical guidance.
content.extendedDescription:
E-hälsomyndigheten's portal for connecting to the national digital infrastructure provides both operational and technical support for integration, testing, deployment and management.
In this seminar, you will see the portal's content and functions and how it will facilitate connection across the sector. You will also gain a clear picture of the support needed to meet future requirements and make use of the opportunities created by NDI. You will leave with a practical understanding of how your organisation can begin, or accelerate, its journey towards connecting to the national digital infrastructure.
content.subject: Digitalisation
speakerTitles: Development Lead for Digitalisation, Research, Innovation and Life Science
Vice President Product Management, Marketing and Communication

content.title: Young people's views on sport
content.description: Sport is often highlighted as a positive force in society, but far from all young people feel included. What do they really think about sport and club activities?
content.extendedDescription:
Today, the sports movement is an integral part of many people's lives, contributing to community, health and civic engagement. At the same time, a substantial proportion of young people are wholly or partly outside organised sport. There are many reasons, and the picture is more complex than public debate often suggests.
To better understand young people's views on sport, Svenska Friidrottsförbundet, together with Ungdomsbarometern, has conducted studies examining their attitudes, motivations and perceived barriers. The findings both confirm existing knowledge and offer new perspectives on how the sports movement is perceived today.
During this Almedalsveckan seminar, we present the studies' key conclusions in a lecture, followed by a panel discussion. Together, we discuss how sport and the enjoyment of physical activity can become more relevant, inclusive and appealing to more young people, based entirely on their own motivations and wishes.
content.subject: Children/young people
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Do we have the ability to bring innovative healthcare technology solutions into practice?
content.description: We stand at the intersection of two revolutions: the biomedical revolution, which makes it possible to understand disease at a molecular level, and the technological revolution, in which AI can identify patterns and connections. The question is not whether the technology exists, but how it is used to make a real difference for patients and society.
content.extendedDescription:
The seminar discusses why life-saving development remains slow despite both knowledge and technology being available. Which barriers are real, and which grey areas already offer more scope for action than we currently use?

Drawing on the data-driven collaborative initiative BrainChild, we explore what is needed for stakeholders to dare to lead, collaborate across sectors and stay focused on actual impact.

Join a discussion about courage, collaboration and the systemic change needed to bring health and healthcare technology initiatives such as BrainChild into practice, and make a difference when it really matters.
content.subject: Health and social care

content.title: The consequences of improper influence in welfare services – who will dare to make decisions?
content.description: What happens when decisions about closing a school or individual social services cases risk being influenced by threats and violence? Who will dare to make decisions then? What are the consequences of improper influence, what is needed going forward, and what responsibility do municipalities, regions and the state have?
content.extendedDescription:
Improper influence is a growing problem in municipalities and regions. It affects individual employees, managers and elected representatives, but also risks influencing individual decisions and the democratic mandate. What happens when municipal and regional decisions, such as closing a school or handling individual social services cases, risk being influenced by threats and violence? Who will dare to make decisions, and will they uphold the rule of law?

A discussion about the consequences of improper influence that we see in welfare services today, what is needed going forward, and the responsibility of municipalities, regions and the state.

Wisby Strand Congress
Room: Vall, floor 2.

content.title: The voters who decide the election: who are they and what shapes their choices?
content.description: Behind party preferences lie changes in different voter groups, geographically, demographically and ideologically. Which groups are shifting most ahead of the election, and why? Understanding these shifts is essential to interpreting public opinion and possible election outcomes.
content.extendedDescription:
Public debate often focuses on parties' polling levels. Yet elections are rarely decided by the overall figures alone, but by how different voter groups shift. Small changes among, for example, young voters, city dwellers or voters without a clear party affiliation can have a major impact on the final result.
This seminar examines in greater depth which voters actually decide elections. We look at voter flows over time, which groups are most likely to change their vote, and how patterns differ by gender, age and region. We also explore what will matter to different voter groups ahead of the election. The event takes the form of a discussion in which analyses and insights are presented and debated.
content.subject: Democracy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Your business success depends on your reputation – but do you know what the public thought?
content.description: As sustainability requirements tighten, the gap between reported sustainability and perceived reality becomes increasingly decisive. How are trust, legitimacy and competitiveness affected when communication and reality do not align, and how can organisations future-proof their reputation?
content.extendedDescription: As regulatory requirements such as CSRD tighten, organisations are investing substantial resources in sustainability reporting to meet future demands. But reported sustainability and the reality people experience do not always coincide. When perceptions of sustainability efforts differ from the image communicated, trust, appeal and business results are affected. The seminar examines the gap between reported and perceived sustainability, the strategic risks this creates for Swedish organisations, and how companies can understand the relationship between ESG, reputation and long-term stakeholder support at a time when sustainability has become a decisive competitive factor.
content.detail:
Reputation and Trust Analytics
event tent
content.subject: Sustainability

content.title: Swedish industry in an uncertain world – geopolitics, trade and the path to stronger competitiveness
content.description: Swedish industry has long been hit hard by the challenging geopolitical and trade policy situation. The situation is currently even more difficult because of unrest in the Middle East. These developments have resulted in weak demand and more redundancy notices.
content.extendedDescription:
Global competition has also intensified, particularly from China, where state support is contributing to downward price pressure in the European market.

German industry, which is central to Swedish exports, is also affected by weak demand, changing trade patterns and increased competition, with direct consequences for Swedish industry.

Meanwhile, new EU trade agreements have the potential to strengthen export opportunities over time, although their effects remain uncertain.

The seminar provides an up-to-date overview and discusses dependence on Germany, China's global influence, and whether these developments are temporary or structural. The focus is on strategic choices to strengthen competitiveness.
content.subject: Economy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Growth or staying power – what shapes successful businesses?
content.description: Sweden is one of Europe's best environments for entrepreneurship, characterised by high levels of innovation and technological maturity. But what actually defines a successful business?
content.extendedDescription:
Sweden is one of Europe's best environments for entrepreneurship, characterised by high levels of innovation and technological maturity. But what actually defines a successful business?

Entrepreneurship takes many forms. It encompasses everything from tech companies worth billions to solo entrepreneurs, side projects and creators who generate economic value. Success can therefore mean different things: rapid, scalable growth or long-term stability and quality.

In this seminar, we explore the motivations behind entrepreneurship in all its forms. What connects the hobby entrepreneur with the fast-growing tech company?

Together with entrepreneurs, representatives of Fortnox and moderator Per Schlingmann, we discuss what truly builds success. Join a conversation about the many faces of entrepreneurship.
content.subject: Economy

content.title: The challenges and opportunities of sponsorship
content.description: Sponsorship is an important source of funding for many organisations, but conditions vary. How can long-term partnerships, structured approaches and sustainable relationships be created to strengthen organisations in culture, sport, voluntary associations and events?
content.extendedDescription:
Sponsorship is often essential to creating the financial conditions for associations, cultural activities and events. At the same time, there are major differences in how organisations approach sponsorship and their capacity to develop it.

Many organisations share similar challenges: how can sponsorship work be structured? How can knowledge and relationships be maintained over time? How can administration be reduced so that more attention goes to collaborations that create value?

This meeting place is open for discussion and exchange of experiences about sponsorship's opportunities and challenges. Visitors can discuss current issues, share perspectives from their organisations and contribute to a broader dialogue about the future development of sponsorship.
content.subject: Economy

content.title: AI as a game changer in breast cancer care – from detection to treatment decisions
content.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) could fundamentally change breast cancer care and contribute to equitable care for all breast cancer patients in Sweden. But what is needed to implement AI solutions safely for patients across the country?
content.extendedDescription:
As more people develop breast cancer, precision diagnostics and targeted treatments are opening up entirely new possibilities for care. Today, AI can be used in areas including radiological image interpretation, pathology and individual oncology treatment planning.

During the seminar, doctors show how artificial intelligence can change the breast cancer patient's journey, from screening and early detection to individualised treatment decisions.

Together with decision-makers, we also discuss what is needed for the new methods to benefit all patients and contribute to better, more equitable breast cancer care.
content.detail: The garden at New Republic's arena
content.subject: Health and social care
speakerTitles: Pathologist and Professor of Tumour Pathology

content.title: Are we educating people for the future or for unemployment?
content.description: After a long period of broad agreement that Sweden should compete through knowledge, the value of academic education has begun to be questioned. Graduate unemployment, tougher conditions for new graduates and a long-term erosion of resources for higher education have brought the issue to the fore.
content.extendedDescription:
Which educational programmes best prepare young people for the future? Is it a good thing that almost half pursue higher education? Are students given the right tools to face a rapidly changing labour market?

Unlike previous structural changes, AI is expected to affect skilled professions to a greater extent. Many roles will change, some will disappear and others will emerge. What does this mean for the education that is needed?

Join a discussion that looks beyond the current economic downturn to the long-term value of education and how we can safeguard both specialist expertise and breadth to strengthen Sweden's long-term competitiveness as a knowledge nation.
content.subject: Employment/labour market

content.title: What does it take to succeed with AI?
content.description: AI is often described as the solution. In practice, however, it functions more like a stress test for organisations. If leadership, culture and governance are lacking, AI becomes an amplifier of existing problems rather than a shortcut forward. So what does success require?
content.extendedDescription:
Using practical cases and experiences from the public and private sectors, the seminar addresses one of today's most decisive questions: why some succeed in turning AI into concrete change while others get stuck in pilot projects, fragmented initiatives and a lack of results. We discuss what it takes to build real implementation capacity, what conditions must be in place, what the path from pilot to scale can look like and which pitfalls risk slowing progress.

You will leave with a clearer picture of why those who start first or invest most are not always the ones who succeed with AI.

Breakfast sandwiches will be served to the first 40 guests.
Coffee will be available during the seminar.
content.subject: Innovation
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: From vulnerability to strategic strength – industry's role in Europe's new reality
content.description: How can industry move from vulnerability to strategic strength? How do we ensure that industry becomes a cornerstone of Sweden's and Europe's security and competitiveness? And what political and industrial choices are needed now to strengthen Sweden's long-term ability to act?
content.extendedDescription: An unsettled world has put global value chains and their vulnerabilities in the spotlight. As geopolitical uncertainty increases and the world becomes more regionalised, security of supply, access to raw materials and industrial capacity have become central to both competitiveness and security. Meanwhile, European industry is under pressure from China's aggressive industrial policy and increasingly intense global competition. Over the past year, the steel industry has been at the centre of trade policy shifts, an early indication of steel's role as a strategic resource. What first became evident in the steel sector is now emerging in more and more parts of industry.
content.subject: EU
speakerTitles: Chair of the Municipal Executive Board

content.title: Sustainable business – from risk to opportunity in a turbulent world
content.description: How can companies navigate a time of uncertainty, complex interdependencies and rapid change? By analysing signals in the wider world, organisations can identify risks and opportunities earlier and strengthen their ability to transition towards more resilient and sustainable business models.
content.extendedDescription:
Welcome to the launch of Nätverket för Hållbart Näringsliv's trend report Företagen & Framtiden 2026. A panel discussion presents the report's insights, focusing on five signals and trends affecting business conditions in a time of uncertainty and complex interdependencies. These form the basis for a discussion of practical steps companies can take to work more systematically on strengthening resilience and managing risks and opportunities in the transition.

The seminar consists of an introductory presentation followed by a panel discussion. The event is free and open to everyone.
content.subject: Sustainability

content.title: A meeting place for democracy's defenders
content.description: Swedish democracy remains strong, but faces challenges. Those who refuse to accept this development and instead want to strengthen, protect and deepen democracy therefore need to come together.
content.extendedDescription:
Efficiency drives, rapid decisions, casting suspicion on professionals and an increasingly harsh tone have created a social climate in which many feel growing concern. When threats, hatred and a culture of silence take hold and experts are questioned, democracy's foundations risk being weakened.

As the trade union for those working on behalf of the state, ST has a responsibility to stand up for a strong and open democracy. Together with others, we want to explore, deepen and defend the principles that keep democracy alive – in public authorities, public debate and people's everyday lives.

At this meeting place, we bring together everyone who sees the worrying signs and wants to contribute to a different direction. We listen to insightful perspectives, share experiences and discuss how we can strengthen democracy together where it is actually practised.
content.subject: Democracy
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Author, Filmmaker, Public Commentator, former CEO of TV4

content.title: What is the most uncomfortable truth about Sweden's transition right now?
content.description: A survey of Swedish companies shows that half have reduced investment in the sustainability transition over the past three years. Nine out of ten companies feel that the rules are unstable. What happens when companies doubt the long-term conditions?
content.extendedDescription:
According to a survey conducted by UN Global Compact Sverige among its members, half of the responding companies have reduced their sustainable investments over the past three years. Most cite political uncertainty and unstable rules as the main reasons.

It is easy to point to political uncertainty as the reason the transition has slowed. It is harder to say what is actually needed, and who really bears responsibility.

On the last day in Almedalen, UNGC Sverige invites you to a breakfast seminar where we ask the questions that are hardest to answer without resorting to platitudes.

Coffee/tea and a sandwich are included.

Introduction to the survey (5–10 minutes):
Peter Pierrou, Head of Communications, UNGC Sverige

Followed by a panel discussion (30–35 minutes):
content.subject: Sustainability

content.title: How do we secure the energy of the future?
content.description: What does a green transition mean? Do we save the climate by reducing electricity consumption, or by increasing it? Does building nuclear power plants have to take a long time? Are wind turbines a solution or an environmental hazard?
content.extendedDescription: The panel takes the form of an open discussion led by a moderator. The audience will also have the opportunity to ask questions and comment. The aim is to move beyond party politics and use common sense and scientific truths in physics and economics to find a way forward for Sweden. Why do we need electricity? What happens without growth? How does Denmark manage without nuclear power plants? How long does a wind turbine last? Is a shared EU electricity market a good or a bad thing? Does it make sense for the state to invest in "green" projects? If not, why should the state subsidise nuclear power, or wind power? The aim of the discussion is to encourage participants to deepen their understanding of and interest in energy issues.
content.subject: Energy
speakerTitles: Lawyer, Deputy Chair of MED Sthlm stad

content.title: Security for workers – can we really not afford it?
content.description: Sick pay deductions, dental care, pensions and unemployment insurance are identified as priority issues for members in the 2026 election. But can we afford reforms in areas that matter to workers, or not?
content.extendedDescription:
The past few years have been financially tough for many people. Half of Handels' members identify the economy, household finances and social security systems as the most important areas for politicians to decide on after the next election. Specific issues such as abolishing the qualifying deduction from sick pay, cheaper dental care, better pensions and stronger unemployment insurance are identified as priorities for Handels' members.

At the same time, many politicians say society cannot afford it. Is the era of important political reforms for workers really over, or is it more a question of willingness and priorities?

Taking Handels' election issues as a starting point, political representatives from several parties discuss the financial scope for reforms in each area.
content.subject: Economy
speakerTitles: Member of Parliament, Committee on Finance
Economic Policy Spokesperson, Committee on Finance
Member of the Riksdag, Committee on Social Insurance

content.title: Global gender equality and the rights of women and girls
content.description: Gender equality is a prerequisite for a sustainable and peaceful society. Today, we see setbacks to women's and girls' rights worldwide, alongside reduced funding. This comes at a time when global gender equality is more important than ever.
content.extendedDescription:
Various events will be held in Global Dialogue Garden, discussing international issues including gender equality. You can also meet representatives of UN Women Sverige and PLAN International on site to discuss and ask questions about work for global gender equality and the rights of women and girls, and about the current global situation. Young people aged 18–30 can sign up for UN Women Sverige's platform Generation Equality, a network for young gender equality advocates, and learn more about girls' rights through Plan International's quiz. We can also answer questions about the UN system, UN reforms and global development assistance, and why age-appropriate aid is important to truly reach the world's girls.
Welcome!
content.subject: Gender equality

content.title: From strategy to world leadership: how can Sweden become a leading AI nation?
content.description: AI could become Sweden's next major competitive advantage – but only if we stop talking and start delivering. Sweden has strong research, high digital maturity and a unique energy situation. Yet many AI initiatives remain stuck in pilot mode and never reach production or deliver real benefits to society.
content.extendedDescription:
In fact, AI is an entire industrial stack, from energy and computing power through infrastructure and data to the models and applications where value is created. Only when all these layers work together can AI truly scale.

In this panel, we tackle the crucial question: how do we make Sweden a world leader in AI in practice?
We discuss what is needed for the public sector, business and research to collaborate faster and more intelligently: clearer responsibility and leadership, long-term incentives, usable data, skills that can scale, and the infrastructure and computing capacity that enable us to build, operate and use AI here in Sweden.
content.subject: Digitalisation
speakerTitles: Professor of Scientific Visualisation and Head of Media and Information Technology

content.title: What view of humanity does a society that imprisons 13-year-olds hold?
content.description: What does it say about our view of humanity when children as young as 13 face prison? It exposes a conflict between punishment and care, responsibility and protection. What kind of society do we want to be – one that punishes children or one that invests in their future?
content.extendedDescription:
More and more voices advocate tougher measures against young offenders, including lowering the age of criminal responsibility. But what are the consequences for the individual, the rule of law and society as a whole? Clearly, strong interventions and measures are needed, but prison is hardly the best option.

Through discussions between researchers, professionals, civil society and decision-makers, we examine child development, risk and protective factors, and alternative interventions that can break patterns of crime without making exclusion permanent. Is punishment a solution, or does it risk making the problems worse? We also discuss international experiences and what the Convention on the Rights of the Child means in practice.
content.subject: Justice/crime
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: The power of democracy – how do we turn responsibility into action?
content.description: It is time to mobilise all the strength in society to safeguard democracy. Despite years of global unrest, polarisation and declining trust in institutions, the counterforces of hope and belief in the future have never been extinguished. But hope must be turned into action – what do we need to do together?
content.extendedDescription: In a time of increasing geopolitical instability and major economic fluctuations, there is a growing recognition that democracy's strength ultimately rests on people's engagement and willingness to take responsibility. Democratic power lies in individuals, in movements and initiatives that drive progress, and in the willingness to move from words to action. By mobilising more people and creating room for participation, insight can become agency and help strengthen democracy in practice: in everyday life, at work and across society. Join a seminar about the next step – how we move from hope to collective action to shape the future together.
content.subject: Democracy
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: All-rounder and Former CEO of TV4
Former Minister for Foreign Affairs and UN Deputy Secretary-General
Political Scientist and Former Chair of Botkyrka Youth Council

content.title: What will happen in gambling policy during the next parliamentary term?
content.description: The gambling market has an annual turnover of approximately SEK 28 billion, and just over 70 per cent of Sweden's adult population has gambled at some point in the past year. What do politicians want from Swedish gambling policy?
content.extendedDescription:
Seven in ten adult Swedes gamble at some point each year, yet gambling policy receives very little attention in public debate. For many people, gambling is entertainment and provides a moment of enjoyment or relaxation, but it also has a major negative impact on the lives of a small proportion of the population.

For this gambling policy discussion, we have invited the people responsible for gambling policy from all parliamentary parties to discuss important issues ahead. How should illegal gambling be countered? How can innovation in the gambling market be encouraged? How should responsible gambling be strengthened, and how do politicians view the segmentation of the Swedish gambling market? These are some of the questions addressed.
content.subject: Business
speakerTitles: Member of Parliament, Committee on Civil Affairs
Deputy Chair of the Committee on Cultural Affairs

content.title: Indigenous rights, a mining nation and polarisation – can human rights guide the climate transition?
content.description: As Sweden transitions, conflicts over land, resources and influence are growing. Can human rights and Indigenous rights create clearer rules for mining, energy and the climate transition? How can we bring more nuance to conflicting objectives, and what is the way forward?
content.extendedDescription:
The debate in Sweden about the rights of the Sámi people is polarised. Political statements describe Sámi culture as an obstacle to societal development. At the same time, international criticism and protests continue over the state's handling of Sámi rights to influence and land. Indigenous rights are rendered invisible in many of the decisions that affect Sámi rights the most.

The Sámi are among the first to experience the effects of the climate crisis and have long advocated the urgent need for a transition. How can human rights contribute to clarity and understanding in the decision-making processes surrounding mines, wind power and other land use? Why must the state and companies treat the Sámi people as part of the solution?
content.subject: Human rights

content.title: Integrated home ownership – the housing option missing from our disadvantaged areas
content.description: How do we tackle segregation in disadvantaged areas and make progress on social sustainability? That is the question society is asking.
content.extendedDescription:
In this panel, we discuss how different forms of housing can contribute to social sustainability, safety and long-term urban development, and which models can help break the happiness paradox. The focus is on how a greater element of home ownership can create more variety in the housing market without sacrificing social stability.

Why is this not done more widely? The panel also examines how increased ownership can strengthen individuals' financial opportunities and engagement in their local area, where people with different incomes and life situations can live side by side.
The discussion focuses not only on social values, but also on documented economic effects and how sustainable housing models can create long-term benefits for property owners, municipalities and society as a whole.
content.subject: Integration/diversity
speakerTitles: Former Minister for the Environment, Now an Expert Adviser

content.title: Make gender equality great again?
content.description: Despite many historic advances, progress towards greater gender equality in Sweden has stalled in many areas. Why? And which political reforms are needed to accelerate it?
content.extendedDescription:
Almedalen's major gender equality policy debate! Stress is widespread in female-dominated professions, the gender pay gap remains, the trend towards fathers taking more parental leave has stalled, and women still do more unpaid work at home.

How do we move forward? TCO welcomes you to Almedalen's major gender equality policy debate, with an opening address by author and feminist commentator Emma Holten. This is followed by a political debate between representatives of all parliamentary parties, focusing on two areas crucial to gender equality: parenthood and welfare services. It is when women and men have children that their incomes diverge, and it is primarily women who suffer when welfare services fall short.

The seminar is followed by a gender equality networking reception in TCO-landet.
content.subject: Gender equality
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Discussion Chair, Head of Arena för samverkan

content.title: Education in the AI era – what role does a university actually have now?
content.description: When knowledge is freely available online and AI can answer almost any question, anywhere and at any time, what role do universities have? How are society's expectations of higher education institutions changing in the AI era, and how do universities themselves view their mission?
content.extendedDescription:
Rapid developments in AI are changing how we seek information, learn new things and make decisions. At the same time, the technology raises questions about universities' role in the society of the future. What should students, employers, public authorities and other stakeholders be able to expect from universities in the AI era? If AI can summarise research, write texts and provide sophisticated answers in seconds, what becomes the universities' role?

The discussion examines how universities are affected by AI developments, as well as the responsibility of higher education institutions in a society where the boundary between knowledge, information and automated answers is increasingly blurred. Which human capabilities become important when technology can do more and more?
content.subject: Research

content.title: Diplomacy and the nuclear threat
content.description: The world is entering a new phase of nuclear rearmament. What are the prospects for diplomatic efforts to reduce the nuclear threat after the war in Iran and the expiry of the last bilateral nuclear arms agreement between Russia and the USA? What does the future hold for the Non-Proliferation Treaty?
content.extendedDescription:
Join a panel discussion with experts in nuclear arms control agreements, diplomacy and multilateral negotiations. The panel comments on the current situation and discusses the diplomatic challenges ahead. The seminar will address the following questions:

• What are the prospects for diplomacy after a dramatic spring – the war in Iran, the expired New START Treaty and the conclusion of the Non-Proliferation Treaty Review Conference?
• What makes nuclear disarmament so difficult?
• How does growing great-power rivalry affect ongoing diplomacy in this field?
• How should small and medium-sized states without nuclear weapons act? What can Sweden do?
content.subject: International affairs
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Can Sweden afford to underestimate women's entrepreneurship?
content.description: Sweden faces low growth, increased global competition and a growing need to strengthen innovation and competitiveness. At the same time, major differences between women and men remain in entrepreneurship and access to capital.
content.extendedDescription:
Only three in ten businesses are run by women, and as little as 1–2.5 per cent of venture capital goes to companies founded by women. This risks holding back entrepreneurship, investment and Sweden's long-term competitiveness.

SPP and Almi invite you to a breakfast discussion about entrepreneurship and women's access to capital. This panel discusses capital provision, risk, security and the structures that affect women's opportunities to develop businesses.

What is needed for capital to reach more people? How can financing, advisory services and social protection systems be developed to better support women entrepreneurs? And what role can banks, public bodies and pension capital play in contributing to more gender-equal entrepreneurship and strengthening Sweden's long-term competitiveness?
content.subject: Gender equality
speakerTitles: Minister for Gender Equality and Working Life

content.title: Society under pressure – how do we step up defence capabilities?
content.description: The security situation is more uncertain than it has been for a long time. Wars are ongoing, partnerships are being tested and new risks are emerging. What does Sweden need to act quickly, strengthen preparedness and meet threats in an increasingly unpredictable world?
content.extendedDescription:
We are currently living through an extremely uncertain security situation. Wars are ongoing in different parts of the world, both between and within countries. Institutions and partnerships that have provided guarantees for many years are being tested, including the NATO and UN systems. For Sweden, this means a period of adjustment, both through active preparedness work and through the ability to step up quickly when potential threats risk becoming reality.

In this session, we assess Sweden's ability to adapt, strategically and practically. We will meet a number of top-level leaders who all contribute to a robust society, as well as committed individuals focused on civil preparedness. Come and hear their thoughts, and ask your own questions!
content.subject: Security/defence
speakerTitles: Head of Crisis Management and Preparedness
Deputy Centre Director, Centre for Total Defence and Societal Security

content.title: What world do we want to believe in, and how do we create it together?
content.description: Young people want to make a difference: 86 per cent say helping others is important to living a good life in the future. At the same time, development assistance is being reduced and views of Sweden's global responsibility are changing. Ahead of the 2026 election, this raises questions about Sweden's role in the world and the choices ahead.
content.extendedDescription:
Starting from the campaign En värld att tro på, we move from quick yes-or-no questions to an open discussion about development assistance, human rights and what peace and sustainable development actually require.
This is not a conventional questioning session, but an open conversation between young leaders in civil society and politics about the major choices ahead and the world we want to believe in.

Together, we want to tackle questions such as:
• What future do we actually want to create?
• What role should Sweden play in the world?
• What do development assistance, human rights and peace mean for that direction?
content.subject: International affairs
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Humanitarian Programme Officer and Environment and Climate Adviser, and Moderator

content.title: The Swedish situation – and the way forward
content.description: How did criminal gangs, organised crime and insecurity become established in Sweden? Is Sweden's situation due to chance, bad luck or coincidence? What can be done to reverse the trend, and what role do municipalities and property owners have in this work?
content.extendedDescription: In the wake of recent years' street shootings, record numbers of bomb attacks, lethal violence involving ever younger people and open drug scenes, proposals are pouring in to strengthen domestic security and reverse the trend. Many proposals have a clear ideological starting point, but the analysis itself is often missing. Why are there so many explosions, shootings and criminal gangs? Is Sweden's situation due to chance, bad luck or coincidence, or are there events, decisions or even tipping points that have contributed to this negative development? What can be done to reverse the trend, and what role do municipalities and property owners have in this work?
content.subject: Justice/crime
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Trauma in children and young people: the right support at the right time
content.description: How can society become better at identifying trauma earlier and providing appropriate interventions to reduce the risk of long-term problems and misdirected measures?
content.extendedDescription:
A seminar in collaboration with Ericastiftelsen on how society can better identify and address trauma in children and young people.
Many young people exposed to violence, abuse or other difficult experiences do not receive the right support in time. Inadequate knowledge of trauma risks problems being misinterpreted or interventions coming too late, with potential long-term consequences for mental health, schooling and life chances.
The seminar highlights the need for coordinated, qualified support in which different interventions complement one another, from early psychosocial support to specialised trauma treatment.
It also includes a panel discussion on how collaboration between stakeholders can be strengthened to prevent young people both experiencing and perpetrating violence.
content.subject: Children/young people
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Licensed Psychologist, Licensed Psychotherapist, Project Manager at Våldsmottagningen
Head of Public Opinion and Advocacy, Social Sustainability Expert

content.title: Supporting young leaders who lead with courage, compassion and initiative – for Sweden's future
content.description:
Supporting young leaders who lead with courage, compassion and initiative is more important than ever. Let us celebrate the leadership of the future!

We are experiencing one of the greatest technological shifts in human history, and the world is unstable. That is why we should invest in good leadership.
content.extendedDescription:
Konungens Stiftelse Ungt Ledarskap works to strengthen and promote young, values-based leadership in Sweden. With courage, compassion and initiative as guiding principles, the foundation identifies, recognises and develops young leaders who take responsibility and contribute to positive societal development. Through training, leadership seminars, meeting places and scholarships, it enables young people to develop leadership that inspires confidence in the future and contributes to a better world. For Sweden's future, we say with a royal twinkle.

Konungens Stiftelse Ungt Ledarskap is celebrating 20 years with a cake party! Come, celebrate and mingle with us – together for good leadership!
content.subject: Democracy

content.title: From linear to circular thinking – who takes the risk as the construction sector transitions?
content.description: Sweden aims to reach net-zero emissions by 2045. But business conditions in construction and real estate are already changing rapidly in the run-up to 2030. Does the construction industry risk using the wrong calculations for 2030 and underestimating how quickly climate requirements are becoming business-critical?
content.extendedDescription:
The construction and real estate sector currently accounts for around 20 per cent of Sweden's total greenhouse gas emissions. A large share arises during construction and materials production, in the manufacture of cement, steel and other building materials.

Circular materials and solutions already exist and can substantially reduce climate impact. At the same time, the industry is characterised by complex value chains in which standards, procurement and risk models are still designed around a linear business model.

Does the construction industry risk using the wrong calculations for 2030 and underestimating how quickly climate requirements are becoming business-critical? This panel brings together industry, construction and real estate to discuss how costs, risk and incentives need to be distributed across the value chain to make net zero possible in
content.detail: Loops arena för impact, industri och energi
content.subject: Construction
speakerTitles: Director Market and Segments, BA Buildings

content.title: Personal assistance – a form of life insurance for every citizen
content.description: Anyone can become one of us at any time. No one knows what awaits around the next corner. A wrong step into the street, a serious illness? But Sweden has a unique safety net. No other country offers this kind of assurance that you can continue to live like others despite major disabilities.
content.extendedDescription:
Personal assistance provides security for both families and individuals that you did not know you might need. A single moment can change everything. Yesterday it was me; tomorrow it could be you or someone you love. A wrong step into the street, a misjudged turn on a ski slope, a riding accident, ALS or a stroke in middle age can lead to both physical and intellectual disabilities, where the right to personal assistance enables you to remain in your home and with your family and live a good life.

A vital reform, unique in its kind, for which Sweden is known worldwide. In the JAG tent, you can meet JAG members and learn more about human rights and why personal assistance is a vital service. Welcome!
content.subject: Human rights
