content.title: Renewing conservation
content.description: In the construction sector, conversion is beginning to challenge demolition and new construction as the norm. But both structural and formal barriers remain. Knowledge of the modern building stock's values, both as technical systems and as high-quality cultural environments, needs to be strengthened and shared.
content.extendedDescription: Most of the building stock was constructed after 1945. Re:purpose is a practice-oriented research project that has examined how office buildings from the late 1900s can be adapted and converted for new uses while retaining their cultural heritage value and architectural qualities. Three interdisciplinary teams have worked with three buildings. The project has resulted in proposals for policy changes that emphasise new ways of understanding value, improved environmental certification systems and the need for evidence based on a holistic approach and collaboration. At the seminar, we discuss, among other things, how building conservation needs to change to actively contribute to the careful stewardship of the modern building stock's values.
content.subject: Sustainability

content.title: Safety and security in troubled times
content.description: Sweden faces both internal and external security challenges, from organised crime to a deteriorating global situation with war nearby. How can society strengthen preparedness, prevent threats and increase safety? What measures are needed to build a more resilient society?
content.extendedDescription:
When society is challenged, safety is put to the test. In recent years, both internal and external security challenges have increased the need for discussions about societal security and preparedness.

At SäkerhetsArenan, seven leading stakeholders in safety, security and preparedness organise a meeting place to highlight important issues and contribute to a stronger, safer society today and in the future.

SäkerhetsArenan is organised by SäkerhetsBranschen, Stöldskyddsföreningen, Brandskyddsföreningen, Stiftelsen Tryggare Sverige, Almega Säkerhetsföretagen, Företagsuniversitetet and Säkerhets- och försvarsföretagen (SOFF). Together, we create a shared meeting place with discussions that strengthen Sweden for the future.

You are welcome to attend the opening of the meeting place.
content.subject: Security/defence
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Electrostatehood: What Sweden can teach the world
content.description: How Europe can strengthen its sovereignty in a world where energy, industry and security are increasingly interconnected. Electrification is a key enabler for resilience, competitiveness and the green transition.
content.extendedDescription:
As global uncertainty increases, the links between energy systems, industrial competitiveness and national security are becoming more evident. Electrification plays a central role in enabling a more resilient, sustainable and independent Europe. At the same time, it raises important questions about infrastructure, investments, policy frameworks and cross-sector collaboration.
This seminar will explore how Sweden’s experience of electrification, innovation and public-private cooperation can contribute to addressing these challenges. The discussion will highlight key opportunities and barriers, and what is required to accelerate the transition at scale.
The session will be held as a moderated panel discussion as is co-hosted by Hitachi Energy and Monocle.
content.subject: Energy

content.title: Cybersecurity and resilience – how do we protect society in a digital age?
content.description: Cybersecurity threats against Sweden and critical societal operations are increasing. How do we ensure we can withstand attacks and ransomware from different threat actors and foreign powers? How can society strengthen its resilience when technology creates both opportunities and new vulnerabilities?
content.extendedDescription:
Digitalisation has created major opportunities for society and business, but also new vulnerabilities. Cyberattacks, ransomware and other digital attacks now target companies, public authorities and essential services alike.

In this session, we speak with leading experts in information security, IT and cybersecurity to explore both technological and human needs.

SäkerhetsArenan is organised by SäkerhetsBranschen, Stöldskyddsföreningen, Brandskyddsföreningen, Stiftelsen Tryggare Sverige, Almega Säkerhetsföretagen, Företagsuniversitetet and Säkerhets- och försvarsföretagen (SOFF). Together, we create a shared meeting place with discussions that strengthen Sweden for the future.
content.subject: Security/defence
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: When will the energy grid be flexible enough to avoid new construction – and what will it take to get there?
content.description: Sweden is expanding renewable electricity generation at a record pace. At the same time, pressure is growing from data centres, new industry and electrified transport, all competing for the same renewable kilowatt-hours. How do we make it all work together?
content.extendedDescription:
The technology for flexibility, energy storage and demand management exists, but we are still not making the leap from individual systems to large-scale solutions. The connection queue is growing, regulations were designed for an electricity system that no longer exists, and despite long-standing discussions about a national energy digitalisation plan, no one has taken overall responsibility for digitalising the grid and providing the digital connections that should hold the whole system together.
This panel discusses what is needed for flexible energy management to move from isolated success stories to a broad system-wide solution for Swedish industry: which business models and regulations need to change, how risks should be shared, and who will lead digitalisation.
content.detail: Loops arena för impact, industri och energi
content.subject: Energy
speakerTitles: Business Policy Expert in Energy and Infrastructure

content.title: Commercialising deep tech – from breakthrough to scalable business
content.description: Sweden has the research, but too many deep tech innovations get stuck between the lab and the market. How do we commercialise what the market does not yet know how to buy, and what is needed for Swedish breakthroughs to become scalable global businesses?
content.extendedDescription:
Circle Series is an initiative within Tech Forward, a collaboration between Techarenan and Teknikföretagen, in which 8–16 hand-picked decision-makers, experts and innovators come together to explore an urgent topic related to innovation, growth and the future in depth.

Unlike traditional panel discussions, Circle Series is an active conversation in which all participants contribute. Each circle has a leader and meets 4–6 times over a year, creating continuity, trust and the opportunity to move from insight to actual action.

The circle on commercialising deep tech starts during Almedalsveckan 2026, meets again in the autumn and concludes at Techarenan's major event in February 2027.
content.subject: Research
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: What do we do with children who murder?
content.description: The rise of serious crime involving children in Sweden is alarming. Criminal networks are recruiting ever younger children to commit serious violent offences, murder and drug trafficking. What are the alternatives to imprisoning children, and how do we reverse the trend?
content.extendedDescription:
How did we get here? What can and should society do when prevention has failed and we face the fact that a thirteen-year-old has shot another person dead? And is prison really the best measure to stop this development and change the children's course?

Join a seminar discussing societal developments, children involved in crime, what we can and should do to reach them before it is too late, and what we can and should do when the worst has already happened.

In response to the debate, Akademikerförbundet SSR has produced a memorandum highlighting an alternative to prison: nationally specialised treatment services.
content.detail:
Room: Krumelurum, Fornsalen.
Gotlands museum, entrances via both Strandgatan 14 and Mellangatan 19.
content.subject: Justice/crime

content.title: Can quality become Europe's new competitive advantage?
content.description: How can Sweden take a leading role as the EU introduces higher requirements for transparency, circularity and product data through ESPR and digital product passports? And how can the Swedish furniture industry use digitalisation to turn quality, sustainability and responsibility into competitive advantages?
content.extendedDescription:
Europe is currently reshaping the playing field for industry. With greater emphasis on circularity, transparency and digital product information, the conditions for how value is created, measured and communicated are changing.

For the Swedish furniture industry, this means not only new requirements, but also an opportunity to make existing values visible: enduring craftsmanship, sustainable material choices, high quality and responsible production.

As digital product passports and other EU initiatives emerge, the question is how these values can be translated into data, business benefits and international competitiveness.

The seminar brings together representatives of industry, standardisation, technology and the public sector to discuss how Sweden can strengthen its position in a new European industrial landscape.
content.subject: Digitalisation
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation

content.title: How can Swedish biochar contribute to climate targets and preparedness?
content.description: What role can Swedish biochar and regenerative agriculture play in crisis preparedness, farmers' profitability and achieving national and global climate targets?
content.extendedDescription:
Join an interactive, practical seminar moving from the theory of international emissions credits (ITMOS) to the concrete reality of regenerative practices on Swedish farms.

MAX Burgers is now taking a major step in its climate strategy by investing in local biochar credits for permanent carbon storage, verified for a storage period of at least 1000 years. But how does biochar work in a regenerative cycle, and how can it strengthen Swedish soils against future climate shocks?

Together with a prominent panel of experts, we discuss what is needed for biochar to move from a niche to a widespread national solution, and we want to hear what you in the audience think.

Arrive in good time! Before the seminar, we will serve brand-new burgers and samples of the luxury shake available exclusively during Almedalen.
content.detail: MAX Arena, the restaurant's roof terrace
content.subject: Sustainability

content.title: The home becomes a war zone – the stark, merciless reality of domestic violence
content.description: Domestic violence is one of our most hidden and critical societal issues: violence that often begins in the name of love but gradually wears people down, isolates them and, in the worst cases, threatens their lives.
content.extendedDescription: This event examines one of our most urgent societal issues: domestic violence. We explore how violence develops, becomes normalised and takes hold behind closed doors, from the first subtle signs to full-scale terror that can shatter both body and mind. We also highlight courage, resistance and the paths out of the darkness in which many still live. The programme combines a lecture, an impassioned address and discussion. Participants will hear realistic accounts of how fear grows, boundaries are erased and the perpetrator's control gradually takes over daily life. At the same time, we highlight the forces that can turn things around: insight, support, knowledge and the courage to say no to violence.
content.detail:
Hotell Slottsbacken
Room: Slottsbacken conference room (1 floor down)
content.subject: Gender equality

content.title: Semiconductors and the global race – where does Sweden stand?
content.description: Sweden's future competitiveness in semiconductors depends on our ability to turn research into production. How do we create better coordination, long-term investment and the right skills to strengthen Sweden's position in the international race?
content.extendedDescription:
Sweden has strong research and cutting-edge expertise in semiconductors, but faces crucial challenges in coordination, financing and industrial scale-up. Meanwhile, other countries are making strategic, long-term investments to strengthen their positions.

How can Sweden move from fragmented governance to coordinated efforts? What role do test environments and skills provision play in bringing innovations all the way to market? And how can Sweden position itself in European and global initiatives?

Sweden's future competitiveness, security and exports are closely linked to our ability to act now. What is needed, and what does our shared roadmap look like?

Moderator: Thomas Frostberg, innovation and business journalist
content.subject: Research
content.accessibility: Event captioned, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Who is responsible for funding sport?
content.description: Sport creates great value, but how should it be funded over the long term? Many stakeholders struggle with limited resources. What is needed for more people to want to invest in sport, and how do we build sustainable partnerships between sport, politics and business?
content.extendedDescription:
Swedish sport creates great value for individuals, society and business. It contributes to better public health, community and integration, while engaging millions of people and building strong brands.
Despite this, large parts of the sports sector face financial challenges. Revenues do not always match the value created, and many clubs, leagues and athletes operate with limited resources.

The seminar discusses how sports funding can be developed and strengthened. What is needed for more stakeholders to want to invest in sport? How can sport become better at demonstrating and packaging its value? And how can sport, politics and business together create partnerships that are sustainable in the long term and deliver both business and societal benefits?
content.subject: Economy

content.title: Healthcare supply preparedness – how do we secure access to medical supplies and medicines?
content.description: How far have the regions progressed, and what is the status of some of the many ongoing initiatives to improve preparedness for medical supplies and medicines?
content.extendedDescription:
Legislation now sets out obligations to stockpile healthcare products and for regions and municipalities to help one another when there are capacity shortages affecting the provision of certain care. Supply analyses are being conducted nationally, and guidance is available, with more on the way, on collaborating with business and incorporating preparedness into procurement and contracts.

Questions to be examined include how far we have progressed nationally and regionally in planning supplies and building emergency stockpiles of medical supplies and medicines. Is it enough to build larger stockpiles, and what happens when they run out? Do preparation needs differ between regions with different geography and populations? Should regions and municipalities also enter into supply preparedness agreements?
content.subject: Health and social care
speakerTitles: Director of Health and Medical Care

content.title: The Staybehinds – Secret Resistance, Hidden Networks and the Questions That Returned
content.description: As geopolitical tensions rise, resistance under occupation is once again a relevant question. During the Cold War, Sweden had clear plans for continued resistance. What remains relevant today, and how should a democratic society prepare?
content.extendedDescription: A conversation about Sweden’s secret stay-behind network during the Cold War - the clandestine resistance structure prepared to operate in the event of Soviet occupation. Together with political scientist and researcher Johan Wennström. The discussion explores intelligence, covert planning, civil resistance, neutrality, and the hidden architecture of Swedish security policy beneath the surface of the Cold War. It also examines questions that have once again become highly relevant: how democratic societies prepare for disruption, occupation, sabotage and hybrid warfare  - and what resilience, loyalty and resistance mean in an era of renewed geopolitical confrontation.
content.subject: International affairs

content.title: What LGBTQI policy can we expect after the 2026 election?
content.description: Many LGBTQI people feel increasingly unsafe while rights are being challenged in Sweden and internationally. Which LGBTQI reforms do the parties want to prioritise after the 2026 election?
content.extendedDescription:
RFSL's safety report shows that many LGBTQI people feel increasingly unsafe, have less confidence in the future and trust society's institutions less than the population as a whole. At the same time, negative attitudes towards LGBTQI people are increasing among young people, and LGBTQI rights are being restricted in many countries.

What reforms are needed to respond? How do the parties want to strengthen safety for LGBTQI people in daily life, online, at school and in encounters with the justice system? What responsibility does Sweden have for people fleeing persecution because of sexual orientation or gender identity? And which LGBTQI policy reforms will the parties prioritise during the next parliamentary term?

This discussion brings together representatives of parliamentary parties to give concrete answers about their priorities ahead of the 2026 election and the coming parliamentary term.
content.subject: Human rights

content.title: When trust in the media is tested, what happens to democracy?
content.description: As information influence operations and disinformation increase, trust in verified journalism becomes crucial to democratic stability, public debate and resilience.
content.extendedDescription: In an information landscape characterised by disinformation, polarisation and digital influence operations, credible news media play a central role in sustaining a shared, fact-based public sphere. When public trust in journalism weakens, the consequences affect not only the media sector but also democratic institutions, societal leadership and citizens' ability to make informed decisions. The seminar examines how Swedish citizens view their leading news media, which factors drive or undermine trust, and how this relates to broader international perspectives on public service media and trust in news. By relating Swedish insights to international comparisons, we discuss what is needed to strengthen democratic resilience at a time when the struggle over verified information is a strategic issue for society.

content.title: The green transition in troubled times – how do we secure the electrification of ports and shipping?
content.description:
Electrification is a cornerstone of the green transition and crucial to reducing society's dependence on fossil fuels. The transport sector is transitioning rapidly, including shipping and port operations.
How do we build confidence that the electricity system will work even in a crisis?
content.extendedDescription:
And how do we ensure that critical transport and supplies reach their destinations when they are needed most?
The focus is on ports and shipping, areas where much remains to be done but the potential is substantial. Electrical energy is critical to society, and ports can play an important new role, for example by developing into energy hubs that strengthen both local resilience and national preparedness.
In this discussion, ABB brings together stakeholders from business, the public sector and civil preparedness to explore how electrification, robustness and collaboration can go hand in hand.
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
speakerTitles: Defence Director / Department of Civil Defence and Preparedness

content.title: Genetic engineering and vaccines are security policy – how can Sweden reduce its dependence?
content.description: The fastest-developed vaccines during the pandemic were based on the rational use of genetic engineering and demonstrated how crucial expertise, infrastructure and resources are. How can Sweden strengthen the whole chain, from research and innovation to production and supply, ahead of the next health crisis?
content.extendedDescription:
The Covid-19 pandemic showed how quickly global demand for vaccines can exceed supply and how dependent many countries are on international supply chains. At the same time, biological threats, new viruses and antibiotic resistance have become part of the security and preparedness debate.

What role should Sweden play in the future vaccine and biotechnology landscape? How can research, industry and the public sector collaborate to strengthen national preparedness, from laboratories and clinical studies to production and distribution?

Join us for this important seminar!
content.subject: Security/defence

content.title: From startup to growth company – how do we unlock Sweden's next growth potential?
content.description: Sweden needs more companies that grow, create jobs, attract capital and strengthen our competitiveness. At the same time, there is substantial untapped potential. More and more women are starting businesses, but far too few build companies that scale all the way into strong growth businesses.
content.extendedDescription:
• What is needed for more entrepreneurs to take the next step?
• How do you build companies that attract capital, reach international markets and create long-term value?
• What role do investors, networks, leadership and business models play, and how can we together create better conditions for growth?

Join an inspiring, forward-looking discussion about entrepreneurship, innovation, capital and growth. Some of Sweden's most prominent entrepreneurs, investors and business leaders come together to share their experiences and perspectives on how to unlock the next generation of growth companies.
content.subject: Business

content.title: Falling birth rates – how do we reverse the trend? IVF, greater knowledge and egg freezing
content.description: Historically low birth rates in Sweden and the rest of the world are troubling decision-makers. The government has commissioned an inquiry to understand and reverse the trend. Involuntary childlessness affects 15–20 per cent of all couples of reproductive age. How can more people be given the opportunity to have the children they want?
content.extendedDescription:
Merck invites you to a discussion about the consequences of falling birth rates, including lower GDP and pressure on welfare systems, and how we can move from words to action to make parenthood possible for those who long for children but face involuntary childlessness.
Are political promises of more IVF attempts the solution? The discussion will also explore the role of insufficient knowledge about fertility and how treatment attempts for a sibling and subsidised egg freezing could be important pieces of the puzzle in reversing the trend.
content.subject: Health and social care
speakerTitles: Inquiry Chair for Utredningen för en framtid med barn
Head of Section and Senior Consultant at the Centre for Reproductive Medicine
Entrepreneur Who, Among Other Things, Runs the Podcast

content.title: Sweden's security – everyone's concern
content.description: How can Sweden's security become everyone's concern in a time of uncertainty? It is about engagement, democratic participation and people's willingness to safeguard peace, freedom and societal resilience when peace, safety and democracy are challenged around the world.
content.extendedDescription:
This arena in Almedalen is a meeting place for discussions about Sweden's peace, freedom and democracy. With the vision that Sweden's security is a concern for all of society, we bring together experts, organisations and citizens to discuss, share knowledge and strengthen understanding of our shared security. Experts, member organisations, decision-makers, civil society and engaged citizens meet here to discuss security policy, total defence, democratic resilience and current societal challenges. Through seminars, conversations and meetings, we create a place for exchanging knowledge, gaining new perspectives and having constructive discussions.

You are welcome to join the conversations, meet people working on these issues and learn more about how we can contribute together to a safe, free and democratic Sweden.
content.subject: Security/defence

content.title: What policies are needed to secure Sweden's technological future?
content.description: Sweden is approaching an election at a time of rapid technological development, geopolitical uncertainty and intensifying global competition. Meanwhile, digital technology affects more and more of society. What is needed to secure Sweden's technological future, and which party has the best technology policy?
content.extendedDescription:
In a new technological shift in which AI and digitalisation are reshaping working life, business and the public sector, policymakers face crucial choices. At the same time, demands for competitiveness, digital resilience and security are increasing.

How do we harness technology's opportunities, and how does Sweden position itself in global competition and the emerging AI economy?

This debate brings together representatives of parliamentary parties for a focused discussion about direction, reforms and pace. The focus is on what is actually needed to strengthen Sweden's competitiveness, welfare and security, and secure Sweden's place in global AI development.

The question is simple: who has the best technology policy to take Sweden forward?
content.subject: Digitalisation
speakerTitles: Labour Market Policy Spokesperson and Deputy Chair of the Committee on the Labour Market
Chair of the Committee on Industry and Trade

content.title: How do we invest for the future? Research and innovation as a strategic strength for Sweden
content.description: What do research and innovation mean for Sweden's welfare and economic strength? In a time of uncertainty, technological shifts and global competition, how can government research funding contribute to social sustainability, innovation, competitiveness and long-term growth?
content.extendedDescription: Join a panel discussion starting from the economic conditions that frame investment in research and innovation. Meet the people responsible for all of Sweden's government research funding bodies in a discussion about collaboration and strategies to address today's and tomorrow's challenges. Research and innovation can build new knowledge and generate experience to support well-informed decisions. When global value chains prove unstable and both new and longstanding challenges demand crisis preparedness and resilience, research and innovation can contribute to both adaptation and transformation. This creates new solutions in both the short and long term.
content.subject: Research

content.title: Fair charging – is electrification only for homeowners?
content.description: Apartment buildings face worse charging conditions than houses. Access to charging points is poorer, charging costs are higher and green tax deductions and other support are lacking. A house owner pays a quarter of the charging cost of an apartment household. How long is this difference sustainable?
content.extendedDescription: A large majority of electric car owners live in houses with good access to charging. A private charge point, made more affordable through a green tax deduction, enables charging at low hourly prices at night and on weekends. Meanwhile, residents of apartment buildings often have much poorer access to charging, in terms of physical access to a charging point, the cost of charging and access to government incentives. This means a house owner charges their electric car at a quarter of the cost of a household in an apartment building. Representatives of the automotive industry, property owners and residents discuss what this cost difference means when the entire population is expected to use electric cars.
content.subject: Climate/environment
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Radical innovation for Sweden's needs – how do we meet tomorrow's challenges?
content.description: Many of our societal challenges urgently need solutions, but some require innovation that does not yet exist: something entirely new that changes what is possible. How does that happen? Can Sweden contribute to the next leap, and is there a way to improve the odds?
content.extendedDescription:
09.00-09.45: Seminar
09.45-10.15: Mingling and networking

If we try a new approach, moving from grants to contracts and from funding calls to a challenge, can we develop the solutions of the future? In this seminar, we explore radical innovation as a way to move from needs to action in solving the major societal challenges of our time. Using examples from Swedish-German cooperation on counter-drone technology, we discuss how clear demand, pace and European collaboration can contribute to innovation that makes a real difference and strengthens both security and competitiveness.
content.subject: Innovation
content.accessibility: The event is captioned, Wheelchair-accessible toilet, Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Head of the Department for International Relations, Research and Innovation

content.title: How do we handle hybrid threats in our neighbouring maritime area?
content.description: Threats to underwater infrastructure, substandard ships, environmentally hazardous discharges, drone incidents, GPS interference… In recent years, a range of new threats has emerged against Swedish society and the maritime domain.
content.extendedDescription:
Hybrid threats can take different forms. At sea, we have seen several examples of damaged underwater infrastructure, and we regularly hear reports of navigation interference and drone incidents, information influence operations and cybersecurity threats. At the same time, we see ships in poor condition operated by unqualified crews, with no or limited insurance and under false flags. Extensive oil transport in the Baltic Sea and our neighbouring waters also poses an obvious risk of accidents and serious environmental damage. The difficulty of holding those responsible to account is itself a security risk.

Join a timely seminar about how we are working to strengthen resilience and act proactively against hybrid threats.
content.subject: Security/defence
content.accessibility: The event is captioned
speakerTitles: Head of the Ships and Seaworthiness Unit

content.title: Policy instruments that work in practice – how do we achieve the transition without weakening competitiveness?
content.description: Sweden's climate targets require a rapid transition in the transport sector, while road transport remains essential to trade, industry and supplies. The question is not only which policy instruments are introduced, but how they are designed to work in practice for hauliers and transport buyers.
content.extendedDescription:
In this seminar, we discuss how policy instruments can contribute to both lower emissions and stronger competitiveness. What is needed to create long-term, predictable conditions that enable investment? How do we avoid stop-start policies that slow progress?

We particularly highlight HVO and other biofuels as a necessary option for rapidly reducing emissions from the existing vehicle fleet while electrification and other new technologies are developed.

Join a discussion about how to create policies that deliver climate benefits, security and functioning transport, and enable companies to transition while strengthening competitiveness.
content.subject: Sustainability
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
speakerTitles: Environmental Consultant, Researcher and Climate Policy Analyst

content.title: How Can Sweden become a Global Electrification Leader?
content.description: Can new decentralized EnergyNet systems help Sweden catch up in the climate transition while strengthening competitiveness and regional development?
content.extendedDescription:
The global transition to electrified societies is accelerating rapidly, but many countries are struggling to scale sustainable energy systems fast enough to meet climate goals and remain competitive.
This seminar explores whether decentralized EnergyNet systems — built around smart microgrids, local energy sharing and distributed renewable energy — could become an “expansion vehicle” for the transition to sustainable societies.
Special focus will be given to the emerging Energy Valley initiative around the Scandinavian Bay Area and its potential to position Sweden as a leading international hub for electrification, sustainable infrastructure and next-generation energy innovation.

The discussion explores how collaboration between universities, cities, industry and energy actors could strengthen competitiveness, attract investment and accelerate sustainable regional development.

content.title: From lab to market: why doesn't Sweden buy its own technology?
content.description: After the AI strategy, R&D reform and the EU's new innovation agenda: what is needed for Swedish research to become business deals, procurement contracts and jobs, here and now?
content.extendedDescription:
Sweden spends billions on public procurement every year. Yet we are rarely the first customer for our own technology. Is that a political failure, or a deliberate choice?

At a time when AI, energy, space and medical technology are rapidly becoming increasingly strategic fields, a new question is emerging in both Sweden and the EU: should the state become an active first customer, or remain a passive purchaser?

With new AI targets, forthcoming R&D incentives and a reshaped European procurement policy, Sweden faces a choice.

This panel starts from practical real-world cases and brings together politics, industry and entrepreneurs in a focused discussion about what is actually holding progress back and what must change now.

The question is simple:
Do we want the next wave of technology to be built in Sweden, or exported before it has even reached the market?
content.subject: Innovation

content.title: After the first week – what happens next?
content.description: In a crisis, society's help will first go to those who need it most. Authorities recommend that households manage on their own for at least a week. This requires stable structures, responsibilities and resources, and a civil society that not only wants to contribute but is part of the solution.
content.extendedDescription:
The authorities are now clear: all households should be able to manage on their own for at least a week in a crisis or war, because society's resources will first be directed to the most vulnerable. But what happens after that week? Are society's resources sufficient, and how do we integrate outdoor organisations into Sweden's total defence?

Current analyses show that civil society is crucial to Sweden's ability to manage crises and war. This is evident both in Myndigheten för civilt försvar's civil society forum and in experiences from Ukraine, where voluntary organisations became essential societal actors.

Together with key figures in Sweden's total defence and representatives of the Swedish outdoor movement, we discuss how outdoor organisations can become part of Sweden's preparedness efforts.

content.title: Gotland moves forward – the ideas and people driving development towards something better together
content.description: Gotland faces major challenges, but also a period of renewed energy, new investments and a growing desire to create something better together.
content.extendedDescription:
Gotland faces major challenges, but also a period of renewed energy, new investments and a growing desire to create something better together. Over the past year, discussions have sometimes focused on obstacles: high ferry fares, struggling cultural organisations and questions about water supply. Alongside this, however, a strong positive force is emerging: companies investing, new initiatives and people who see opportunities where others see problems.
We want to bring together some of these stakeholders to discuss confidence in the future, initiative and practical ways forward for Gotland. How can we jointly strengthen the island's appeal, sustainability and vitality? Which initiatives are showing the way? And how can local stakeholders continue to drive development?
Join a seminar focusing on solutions, collaboration and the positive developments already under way.
content.subject: Visitor economy

content.title: Municipal and regional politicians and renewable energy – what is needed to accelerate the energy transition?
content.description: Much of the energy transition happens locally, with municipalities and regions playing a crucial enabling role. Many have ambitious targets for expanding renewable energy but face challenges in putting those targets into practice.
content.extendedDescription:
This seminar brings together representatives of municipalities, regions and the energy industry to discuss what is needed to accelerate the transition. How can municipalities and regions take a more active role? What conditions must be in place to enable more energy projects? And how do we move from ambitious targets to concrete action?

The discussion focuses on solutions, from local benefits and acceptance to more efficient permitting processes and stronger partnerships, to accelerate the energy transition.
content.subject: Energy
speakerTitles: County Governor of Södermanlands län and Former Director-General of Energimyndigheten
Doctoral Researcher in Resilient Energy Systems

content.title: A social contract for young people
content.description: The social contract is broken. Unemployment is among the EU's highest and hits young people particularly hard. At the same time, impunity for high-volume crime is perceived to be increasing. Young people do not receive psychological help in time, and climate policy risks hitting households and businesses hard.
content.extendedDescription:
The social contract is faltering. Sweden now has one of the EU's highest unemployment rates, with young people hit hardest. Meanwhile, many feel that the consequences for high-volume offences such as assault, theft and fraud are too weak. Young people also wait too long for psychological support when they are struggling. Alongside this, concern is growing that climate policy is being designed in ways that harm both household finances and climate effectiveness. Together, this paints a clear picture: today's society is not meeting young people's needs or expectations for the future.

Centerpartiets Ungdomsförbund is therefore launching the report “Samhällskontrakt för unga”, presenting 28 reform proposals on education, mental health, the labour market, safety and the green transition.

🗓 Wednesday 24 June, 17:00
📍 The party tent, Almedalsparken
content.subject: Employment/labour market

content.title: Why do we make building so difficult?
content.description: Up to a million households want to move to a detached or terraced house, but housebuilding is collapsing. At the same time, we also need more apartments in attractive locations, and our existing apartment stock requires extensive renovation.
content.extendedDescription:
Up to a million households want to move to a detached or terraced house, but housebuilding is collapsing. At the same time, we also need more apartments in attractive locations, and our existing apartment stock requires extensive renovation.

In other words, there is plenty of work to do, but unfortunately Sweden is a world champion in regulatory complexity and bureaucracy that obstruct development. Why does a building permit take longer than the construction itself? And how did Sweden become the EU's most expensive country to build in? How do we reduce construction costs and make both new building and renovation easier? Together with politicians, public authorities and business, we discuss how to remove barriers and reduce costs.
content.subject: Construction
speakerTitles: Member of Parliament, Housing Policy Spokesperson, Member of the Committee on Civil Affairs
Head of the Housing Business Area

content.title: From research to the future – accelerating Sweden's new industrialisation!
content.description: What is the secret behind Norrköping's successful approach? How can academia, business and the public sector together take the next step to strengthen Sweden's role as an innovation nation?
content.extendedDescription:
This research is now paving the way for sustained new industrialisation in this historic industrial city. What is the secret behind Norrköping's successful approach?
Sweden's two largest privately funded research programmes, WASP and WISE, are based in Norrköpings Industrilandskap, part of Sveriges Kulturkanon, and Linköpings Universitet. World-leading innovations in visualisation, AI and sustainable materials are taking shape here.

Join an inspiring seminar where key figures share their experiences, thoughts and success factors. Together, we explore what needs to happen to accelerate development: creating more jobs, future solutions and increased competitiveness, both regionally and nationally.

Take the opportunity to be part of Sweden's next wave of innovation!

content.title: Technological sovereignty – how are Sweden and the EU preparing for their own security and defence capability?
content.description: Digital daily life in Sweden and Europe relies on global technology and infrastructure, often from the USA. In a heightened security situation, European technological sovereignty becomes a strategic issue.
content.extendedDescription:
Digital infrastructure is no longer simply a matter of innovation and competitiveness. Cloud services, operating systems, components and communications networks are essential to critical operations, preparedness and military capability. Meanwhile, Europe is heavily dependent on technology and infrastructure controlled by actors outside the EU.
What happens if access to key digital services is restricted? How vulnerable is Europe's digital ecosystem? Which dependencies are most critical from a defence and preparedness perspective? And how can Europe strengthen its technological freedom of action without isolating itself from global innovation?
Tre brings together decision-makers, security policy experts and business representatives to discuss technological sovereignty as a matter of security, defence capability, competitiveness and innovation capacity.
content.subject: Security/defence

content.title: Running builds bridges
content.description: A sustainable life and society require sustainable infrastructure. This includes roads, cycle paths and railways, in and beyond our cities. Your own two feet can connect society and strengthen public health in ways few other forms of transport can.
content.extendedDescription:
Bring your running shoes and discuss sustainable infrastructure outside the city wall! Everyone who can and wants to jog is welcome; we adapt the distance and pace. Before departure, we gather for an introductory discussion and to wait for all participants (10-15 minutes). Afterwards, a nourishing breakfast and further discussion await those who wish and are able to stay. Run and network!

This is a perfect opportunity to combine exercise with interesting discussions about sustainable solutions and the essential transition from brown to green development. We start at Skeppargatan 24 and follow a route taking approximately 45 minutes. Afterwards, breakfast is provided, and anyone who wishes can stay for further discussion.

Missed the start? You are welcome to chat with us on Skeppargatan while waiting for the other participants.
content.subject: Construction

content.title: When crisis strikes – who takes responsibility locally in Sweden?
content.description: More and more Swedes believe the country faces a serious crisis in the next few years. Greater demands are being placed on civil society and the financial sector, while almost half of Swedes have made no preparations for a financial crisis.
content.extendedDescription:
Financial crisis preparedness is about more than digital services: it is about knowledge, financial buffers and functioning local infrastructure. How do we ensure people can pay, shop and access their money even when systems are disrupted?

It is Tuesday morning. Card terminals are flashing red. Swish is down. Cash machines are empty. You cannot refuel your car or buy food. What happens in your municipality in the first 48 hours? Who pays for the fuel? How do older people buy their medicine? How does the shop get paid? And who takes responsibility when digital Sweden shuts down?

This seminar brings together representatives of banks, authorities and civil society to discuss how we can strengthen Sweden's resilience together, across the country.
content.subject: Economy
speakerTitles: State Secretary to the Minister for Civil Defence

content.title: Do Jews need to flee Sweden?
content.description: What are the parliamentary parties doing to counter rampant antisemitism in Sweden? After Hamas's terrorist attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, both Sweden and the rest of the Western world were taken by surprise by the strong antisemitic currents that were suddenly exposed.
content.extendedDescription:
Good values and acceptance of objective truths are important foundations for a safe and prosperous society. It is the free market in the Western world that has created these conditions and built strong, prosperous societies with Western values and culture.

When people reach for simple explanations of societal problems, socialism and collectivism are close at hand, and these are precisely the ideologies now joining forces with antisemitic movements originating primarily in the Middle East. What political initiatives do we need to stop this regression and instead focus on building a safe Sweden that Jews do not have to flee?

Drinks and refreshments will be served after the discussion, with an opportunity to mingle.
content.subject: Democracy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Democracy under threat? Is school fulfilling its societal mission?
content.description: Democracy can no longer be taken for granted, globally or here at home. When Swedish young people question its value and undemocratic forces gain ground, schools' democratic mission becomes more important than ever, particularly in an election year.
content.extendedDescription:
It is clear that we can no longer take democracy for granted, globally or here in Sweden. Challenges are visible not only in undemocratic trends internationally, but also in our immediate surroundings. Meanwhile, more Swedish young people, particularly young men, are questioning whether democracy really is the best form of government.

Schools have a crucial role in strengthening democracy and laying the foundations for the society of the future. But are they fulfilling their democratic mission, not only in classrooms but also in corridors where values are shaped every day? Are schools properly equipped, or do they need support from civil society? What responsibility do politicians have? And how does schools' work on democracy connect to total defence?

These are questions we will discuss during a seminar in Almedalen.
content.subject: Democracy

content.title: Why are we moving less when we need it most?
content.description: In an increasingly digital world, physical activity, fresh air and meeting beyond screens and conference rooms are more important than ever.
content.extendedDescription:
During Almedalsveckan, we invite you to a relaxed morning run along Visby's beautiful shore, a way to start the day with energy, presence and good conversation. Every morning at 08:30, we invite you to a shared 30-minute jog starting and finishing at Sommarnöjen's house beside Kruttornet.

As our days become increasingly sedentary and digital, we want to create a simple opportunity to start the day with movement, fresh air and human connection. Each morning begins with a short discussion about running, wellbeing and the positive effects of regular movement on both the body and mental focus.

The pace is relaxed and sociable, and all levels are welcome. This is about starting the day with energy, inspiration and fresh perspectives together, rather than performance.

Those who do not want to run are invited to discuss the topic in the house at the same time.

content.description: In an increasingly digital world, physical activity, fresh air and meeting beyond screens and conference rooms are more important than ever.
content.extendedDescription:
During Almedalsveckan, we invite you to a relaxed morning run along Visby's beautiful shore, a way to start the day with energy, presence and good conversation. Every morning at 08:30, we invite you to a shared 30-minute jog starting and finishing at Sommarnöjen's house beside Kruttornet.

As our days become increasingly sedentary and digital, we want to create a simple opportunity to start the day with movement, fresh air and human connection. Each morning begins with a short discussion about running, wellbeing and the positive effects of regular movement on both the body and mental focus.

The pace is relaxed and sociable, and all levels are welcome. This is about starting the day with energy, inspiration and fresh perspectives together, rather than performance.

Those who do not want to run are invited to discuss the topic in the house at the same time.
content.subject: Other
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: One disease – two realities for Alzheimer's patients
content.description: Sweden is a world leader in research into Alzheimer's diagnosis and treatment and has every prerequisite for a structured introduction of new medicines. With new EU-approved treatments, there is hope in a field where healthcare has had no options for far too long.
content.extendedDescription:
When patients with early Alzheimer's disease seek treatment, the regions' current approach means doctors meet patients in the midst of life who fulfil all treatment criteria, but must tell them that the medicine is not currently recommended in Swedish public healthcare and refer them to possible treatment abroad.

The number of patients with early Alzheimer's disease is limited and manageable. The SveDem quality registry is in place, enabling detailed follow-up. Experts and doctors advocate a structured introduction at specialist clinics so that those most likely to benefit are offered treatment. What could such a solution look like?
content.subject: Health and social care
speakerTitles: Silvia Doctor, Head of the Cognitive Medicine Service
Opposition Regional Councillor, Member of the Health and Medical Care Committee
Chair of the Primary Care Committee's Public Health and Dental Care Subcommittee

content.title: Always prepared – leadership that holds up in the forest and in a crisis
content.description: At a time when global leadership is failing, worldwide decisions are made at breakneck speed and trust in those in power reaches new lows, today's young people are asking a new question: is this really what leadership should look like?
content.extendedDescription:
In our live podcast, we explore how future leaders are shaped, not in the corridors of power but in the forest, around the fire and through patrol teamwork. Scouterna has long trained the leadership the world is crying out for: calm under pressure, courage to act amid uncertainty, collaboration without ego and the ability to be always prepared.

We discuss why young people value empathy, sustainability, safety and clarity more than ever, and how they are more inspired by experience-based leadership than by today's global displays of power.

The audience will be put to the test in a fast, fun and revealing “Always prepared” exercise, showing how they handle a field problem when the map does not match reality and the situation calls for improvisation.

A live podcast about future leadership, young people's expectations and why the logic of the forest stands the test of time.
content.subject: Democracy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: How free is freedom of school choice really?
content.description: Pupils in adapted schools have a substantial need for appropriate support and adaptations, and the ability to choose a school is often crucial to their development. In practice, however, free choice does not apply: municipalities can circumvent it by offering insurance only in municipal schools or denying school transport despite rights under LSS.
content.extendedDescription:
Freedom of school choice is a statutory right, but for pupils with major and extensive support needs it is too often an illusion. A lack of transparency and widespread ignorance of these pupils' rights severely restrict that freedom. Loopholes exist and are exploited.

We are holding a seminar with a background presentation and overview of the evidence, featuring the headteacher/head of schools and the founder of the adapted school Move & Walk. The introduction highlights areas where pupils with major and extensive support needs are systematically disadvantaged.

This is followed by a political discussion with representatives of Centern and Moderaterna.
content.subject: Education
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Member of Parliament and Education Policy Spokesperson
Founder and Chair of the Board

content.title: Gotland cannot wait – time to take long-term responsibility for the road across the sea
content.description: Gotland is part of Sweden, but access is determined by ferry services, which effectively function as the country's most expensive road. Prices affect residents, businesses and visitors. How can fair conditions and long-term access to and from Gotland be secured?
content.extendedDescription:
For Gotland, the ferry is not a supplement: it is Gotland's road and a prerequisite for equal living conditions. High ferry fares have direct consequences for businesses, residents and the public sector. And when Gotland's strategic importance to Sweden's preparedness and security has never been clearer, the issue goes beyond regional policy. A robust Sweden requires an accessible Gotland.

This seminar focuses on ferry fares to and from the island. They matter to all travellers, to transport and goods, and from a preparedness perspective. Access to Gotland matters to all of Sweden. The seminar is planned as a panel discussion on securing Gotland's accessibility now and in the future.
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Member of the Committee on Transport and Communications
Member of the Committee on Transport and Communications
Chair of the Regional Executive Board

content.title: From housing shortages to building society – how do we modernise housing policy?
content.description: Housing shortages, increasing segregation and major renovation needs characterise today's housing market. At the same time, construction is crucial to jobs, growth and the climate transition. How can modern housing policy meet these challenges?
content.extendedDescription:
Byggnads presents a new housing policy report.
Housing is more than a roof over your head. It affects opportunities to work, study and live safely. Despite this, Sweden currently lacks a long-term strategy for housing construction, and homes have become objects of speculation and major market fluctuations.

Byggnads' new report highlights the need for stable housing construction across economic cycles, extensive renovation of existing homes and investment in safe, pleasant residential areas.

The report also highlights the connection between housing policy, employment and the climate transition.

The seminar starts from the report's proposals and discusses how Sweden can move from short-term solutions to long-term societal development.
content.subject: Construction
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: How can shipping become a first-choice career?
content.description: How can Sweden secure the skills needed in shipping as demand for staff increases? The challenge spans the entire chain, from education and recruitment to opportunities to develop, remain in the sector and build a lifelong maritime career.
content.extendedDescription:
Shipping is a key industry for Sweden's trade, preparedness and climate transition. At the same time, it faces significant challenges in attracting, training and retaining skilled staff. Meeting future needs requires collaboration between business, education providers and political decision-makers.

The seminar discusses how more people can be inspired to choose a maritime career, how the education system can meet industry needs and what measures are needed to create sustainable long-term career paths.

Hear shipping companies and decision-makers share experiences, identify barriers and present solutions to strengthen skills provision and competitiveness in Swedish shipping. Together, we discuss how the maritime industry of the future can secure the right skills at the right time.
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport
speakerTitles: Head of the Ships and Seaworthiness Unit

content.title: Voluntary return migration to Syria: return aspirations among Syrians living in Sweden and the EU
content.description: What do we actually know about return aspirations among Syrians living in Sweden and across the European Union?
content.extendedDescription: The fall of the Assad regime in December 2024 and the end of the Syrian civil war, which lasted more than 13 years, are said to have marked a decisive turning point for Syrians who sought protection in the European Union (EU), with many hoping to return and rebuild their country of origin. In 2025, against the backdrop of the civil war's end, the Swedish government tasked Migrationsverket with assessing the measures needed ahead of a possible increase in returns to Syria. However, Syria remains in a state of deep political uncertainty. Its fragile transition has the potential to shape the country's future and therefore the return aspirations of Syrians living abroad. The event will discuss Delmi's latest policy brief, written by Anna Hammarstedt. The brief aims to improve understanding of current return aspirations among Syrians living in Sweden and the EU.
content.detail: Migration och bistånd-två frågor i ett tält
content.subject: Research
speakerTitles: Head for the Nordic and Baltic Countries

content.title: When the world order has exploded
content.description: We are in a transition towards a new world order, characterised by an unstable and violent interregnum in which economic and military power structures are being renegotiated. What are the dynamics of this systemic change, and what forms could a future world order take?
content.extendedDescription: The world order has exploded into a thousand pieces. The new rule is that there are no rules. Unrestrained protectionism now replaces free trade, and state-subsidised industrial policy replaces free competition. We are at a turning point. The cruel and violent forms this turning point in the world order takes, without a narrative to legitimise them, can be seen as a sign of the twilight of a dominant power. It is the end of a globalisation cycle (40 years) and the US cycle of hegemony (100 years). Every decline of an authority heightens the desperation of those who benefited from it, driving them to try to stop the inevitable through violence. This is “the warlike frivolity of senile empires”.
content.subject: Democracy
speakerTitles: US Expert and Host of the Podcast USA & Co

content.title: When roads and railways become congested, is inland shipping the answer?
content.description: Is it time for a new approach and a boost for Swedish inland shipping? What is actually holding back development, and which reforms are needed to move more freight from road and rail to water?
content.extendedDescription:
Sweden's roads and railways are heavily loaded, and the government is now making historically large investments in maintaining existing infrastructure. Meanwhile, something is rarely discussed in transport policy: spare capacity on our lakes Vänern and Mälaren. Sweden's inland ports could handle a substantially larger share of freight. Moving freight from land to water has long been a political ambition, but without incentives little happens in practice. If we want to reduce congestion, strengthen preparedness and meet climate targets, we cannot keep doing the same things and expect different results.

This seminar presents four proposals for more competitive inland shipping, and a panel of parliamentarians will address how they could be implemented.
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation

content.title: Who takes responsibility for Sweden's largest workplace?
content.description: At 600,000 kilometres, the road network is by far Sweden's largest workplace. But how do we stop human exploitation and safeguard drivers' working conditions when visibility into their working environment is minimal?
content.extendedDescription:
Hundreds of thousands of drivers use the road as their daily workplace, often under conditions that are difficult for authorities to monitor. There are clear indications that drivers are forced to work extremely long shifts and live in inadequate conditions, but the lack of oversight means we know too little about what actually happens behind the wheel.

As roadside checks decline, an uneven market emerges in which unscrupulous operators can exploit drivers' vulnerability without risking penalties. This threatens not only individual drivers but the entire legitimate transport industry.

The seminar discusses how we can increase oversight and strengthen drivers' conditions. What is required of policymakers and authorities to ensure laws and regulations are actually followed throughout Sweden's road network?
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Policy Analyst in the Social Policy Unit

content.title: Innovative food preparedness in practice
content.description: How does the public sector work with food preparedness in practice?
content.extendedDescription:
Södertälje kommun has made substantial progress on food preparedness through innovative procurement and emergency stockpiles, known as the Södertälje model. It shows how robust local food supplies can be secured both in normal conditions and during disruptions. During the seminar, food services director Sara Seing and Tomas Erlandsson, CEO of Nordisk Råvara, describe the work.

The seminar brings together stakeholders highlighting the importance of food preparedness. Participants include Michaela Haga (Region Stockholm), Sanna Palomaa (Region Gotland) and Lina Holmgren (Länsstyrelsen Gotland), who discuss links to national and regional food strategies.

Mikael Furu (Gotland Grönt Centrum and Matbyrån Gotland) discusses small-scale production and heritage crops. Isabella Hernandez, FOI, gives a keynote on municipal and regional responsibilities.

The event begins with a preparedness lunch created by Luqaz Ottoson (Restaurang Rot at Fabriken Furillen), alongside an exhibition area.

See the full programme on MatLust's website: www.matlust.eu.
content.subject: Food

content.title: Joy as medicine? The power of experiences for children and young people with serious illnesses or diagnoses
content.description: Children and young people living with serious illnesses or diagnoses often face daily lives shaped by treatments, worry and limitations. At the same time, experience and accounts from children and healthcare staff show that joy, play and positive experiences can strengthen wellbeing, recovery and hope for the future.
content.extendedDescription:
In this panel discussion, Min Stora Dag raises the question of the importance of joy for children and young people living with serious illnesses or diagnoses. Are experiences merely an added pleasure, or can they also be an important part of recovery, quality of life and mental wellbeing?

Drawing on Min Stora Rapport and a discussion bringing together research, healthcare and children's own perspectives, we explore how experiences can provide strength, hope and better conditions in difficult life circumstances.

The seminar is led by journalist Petra Nordlund McGahan and made possible by Roschier – House of Many Voices.
content.subject: Children/young people
speakerTitles: Member of the Children and Young People's Council
Chair of Sveriges lekterapier, Hospital Play Specialist/Special Education Teacher

content.title: The pocketbook election of 2026 – what do voters want from economic policy?
content.description: Sweden is approaching another election in which the economy and household finances are expected to take centre stage. What do voters really want: measures that improve their own finances here and now, or reforms that strengthen Sweden's economy over the long term?
content.extendedDescription:
Join a discussion about economic policy ahead of the 2026 election: the reforms implemented, how voters have received them and the choices ahead.

The discussion starts from a new survey by Länsförsäkringar and Verian on how Swedish households view some of this parliamentary term's major economic reforms. These include tax cuts on work and pensions, reduced food VAT, lower electricity and fuel costs, tax-free ISK savings and new mortgage rules.

The survey shows how the reforms are assessed generally, for personal finances and for Sweden's economy. This raises a central question for the seminar: is it enough for policies to be felt in household budgets, or must they also be seen as credible for Sweden in the long term?
content.subject: Economy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Are we staying on course? Climate targets, urban development and the economy's new playing field
content.description: Sweden has ambitious climate targets, but the pace of the transition is being questioned. As geopolitics, energy needs and economic uncertainty put pressure on decision-makers, how do we stay on course towards net zero?
content.extendedDescription:
Sweden has ambitious climate targets, but the pace of the transition is being questioned. As geopolitics, energy needs and economic uncertainty put pressure on decision-makers, how do we stay on course towards net zero?
Meanwhile, the built environment – our cities, properties and infrastructure – accounts for a significant share of emissions. Architecture therefore plays a crucial role in the transition, from material choices and design to planning compact, resilient and energy-efficient communities. How can architecture and urban development help reduce climate impact, strengthen quality of life and drive innovation?
What role do the energy system, capital, innovations and civil society play? And how do we ensure the green transition is both competitive and fair, particularly in designing the built environments of the future?
content.subject: Climate/environment

content.title: For democracy, freedom and human dignity: building Folkhemmet 2.0 together
content.description: In a time of distrust and polarisation, we need discussions about peace, freedom and government by the people. Democracy is not a given: it requires open dialogue and shared responsibility. How do we preserve the trust that holds society together?
content.extendedDescription: In a time of growing polarisation and declining trust, Palmedalen becomes an important meeting place for reflection on the values shaping our society. Here, discussions about peace, freedom, public health and democracy take place in the spirit of Olof Palme, reminding us of democracy's vulnerability and the need to nurture shared trust. Bringing together politics, music and art creates a platform where thoughts and feelings meet in new ways. Stina & Solpojkarna contribute music reflecting warmth, solidarity and hope, making culture a central part of the dialogue. At the same time, the vision of Folkhem 2.0 emerges: a renewed society centred on equality, sustainability and participation. This is about developing a new shared “we” that carries democracy into the future, rather than returning to the past.
content.subject: Other

content.title: How do we get housing construction moving – is building more houses the answer?
content.description: Construction is dominated by small apartments in major cities, while many people want to live in houses. Is it time for a new home ownership initiative, or more houses for rent? What political changes are needed to increase housing construction, and who should build?
content.extendedDescription:
How do we accelerate housing construction across the country, and what role can houses play? This panel discusses today's and tomorrow's challenges in getting housing construction moving. Why does production often get stuck on smaller apartments, what barriers block new projects, and how profitable is housebuilding? We discuss financing, land, planning processes and demand, and how a shift in construction could affect mobility, skills provision and the housing issue.

The discussion draws on observations from PwC's Emerging Trends 2026. The questions of which political changes are needed to increase housing construction, whether housebuilding can affect the housing shortage and who should build were highlighted by the panel as among the most important themes for 2026/2027.
content.subject: Construction

content.title: Securing the shelters of the future
content.description: The security situation in Sweden and the wider world has changed. Rebuilding total defence, increased geopolitical uncertainty and new societal disruptions place greater demands on civilian protection. Shelters are a central component, but also a resource that has long been neglected.
content.extendedDescription:
How do we ensure Sweden's shelters meet today's requirements for functionality and accessibility? And how is responsibility translated into actual implementation capacity?

This discussion brings together representatives of public housing, Myndigheten för civilt försvar (MCF) and industry to discuss how shelter renovation, management and development can be accelerated. The focus is on practical initiatives, new forms of collaboration and how public bodies and the market can create scalable, sustainable long-term solutions together.

A discussion for those working in housing provision, preparedness, property management or public governance who want to help strengthen society's resilience in practice.
content.subject: Security/defence

content.title: What are we willing to pay for healthcare preparedness in peacetime?
content.description: In crisis and war, healthcare must be able to scale up rapidly, handle increased demand and keep functioning for a long time without ordinary care collapsing. But if staff cannot manage full-time work in peacetime because conditions are too demanding, how will we cope with a prolonged crisis?
content.extendedDescription:
Swedish healthcare faces major staffing and skills challenges. Access to care and staff is unevenly distributed across the country, the growing administrative burden takes time away from patients, and working conditions often involve heavy workloads, moral distress and repeated demands for savings.
At the same time, healthcare is expected to be central to Sweden's civil preparedness.

This raises crucial questions: how much preparedness should we build in peacetime, and what are politicians willing to pay for it?

Saco Hälso- och sjukvård includes Akademikerförbundet SSR, Fysioterapeuterna, Naturvetarna, SRAT, Sveriges Arbetsterapeuter, Sveriges Farmaceuter, Sveriges läkarförbund, Sveriges Psykologförbund and Sveriges Tandläkarförbund.
content.subject: Health and social care
content.accessibility: The event is captioned, Hearing loop, Wheelchair-accessible toilet, Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: When stress makes employees want to leave – how do we create sustainable workplaces?
content.description: Stress in society continues to increase, and stress-related sickness absence remains high. Meanwhile, an uncertain labour market creates anxiety about job loss, affecting people's security, health and working lives.
content.extendedDescription:
Employers have extensive responsibility for the working environment, but the issue is complex. What can employers and employees do to promote workplace health and create more sustainable working lives?

If's latest Nordic health report shows that many people work while ill and a significant proportion have considered changing jobs or industries because of work-related stress. The report provides deeper insights into public health challenges in the Nordic countries and highlights how stress, sickness absence and loneliness affect individuals and organisations alike.

The seminar discusses what these developments mean for working life and how employers and employees can work preventively to reduce stress, strengthen health and create workplaces where people want and are able to stay.
content.subject: Health and social care

content.title: A cardiovascular plan that lasts across parliamentary terms – how do we build broad political support?
content.description: In Sweden, 2.2 million people live with cardiovascular disease, and around 30,000 Swedes die from these diseases each year. This makes cardiovascular disease both the most common chronic illness and the most common cause of death in Sweden.
content.extendedDescription: At the new policy forum Hjärtdagen 2025, a majority of parliamentary parties expressed support for a national cardiovascular plan, although not all fully agreed on its need and direction. Now that the government has tasked Socialstyrelsen with developing a national action plan to prevent and treat cardiovascular diseases, broad political consensus is crucial. It is a prerequisite for the plan to make a real difference for people living with cardiovascular disease. As part of Hjärtdagen 2026, Riksförbundet HjärtLung, in collaboration with Hjärt-Lungfonden and ten pharmaceutical and medical technology companies, is organising an Almedalen panel discussion aimed at building broad political agreement on the direction and need for the national cardiovascular plan.
content.detail: The garden at New Republic's Almedalen arena
content.subject: Health and social care
speakerTitles: Head of Strategy and Public Affairs

content.title: As the world rearms – how do we build lasting peace and security?
content.description: How can diplomacy, peacebuilding and military capability together contribute to long-term security? And what role does Sweden play in preventing conflicts and strengthening peace in an increasingly uncertain world? What does security mean today in 2026, and what matters most for Sweden?
content.extendedDescription:
Europe is undergoing its largest military build-up since the Cold War. The war in Ukraine, conflicts in the Middle East and growing geopolitical tensions have shifted the focus towards defence capability, deterrence and preparedness.

At the same time, we know that military strength alone rarely creates long-term peace. Sustainable security also requires functioning institutions, diplomacy, conflict prevention and support for people affected by war and violence.

How can diplomacy, peacebuilding and military capability work together in an increasingly uncertain world? Do defence investments risk crowding out investments in peace? Or are they mutually dependent?

And what role can Sweden play in strengthening its own security while contributing to peace and stability internationally?
content.subject: Security/defence
speakerTitles: Chief of Defence and Supreme Commander

content.title: How is AI-driven commerce changing consumption and retail?
content.description: At the beginning of the year, a new standard for AI-driven commerce called UCP was launched. This enables AI assistants to handle the entire customer journey, from discovery to direct purchase. Meanwhile, businesses without UCP support risk becoming invisible. How will this affect the way we shop and the entire industry?
content.extendedDescription:
As AI agents move from simple assistants to autonomous decision-makers, retail and society face a fundamental shift in power. One of the most pressing questions concerns personal autonomy: what happens to people's ability to make active choices when algorithms can curate and complete purchases for us? And what happens to businesses that are absent from the playing field when AI assistants scan the market?
There is also tension between efficiency and control: while agents can drive a resource-efficient, sustainable circular economy, they risk creating an opaque market in which people take a back seat. The question is how retailers and consumers should act to guide this development in the right direction.
content.subject: Economy
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
