content.title: Integration works both ways – is Sweden ready for its own?
content.description: Ukrainian and Swedish values meet in Sweden – but do they really connect? Understanding one another is not automatic. This is about more than integration. It is about how a country that has lived in peace understands a people who have never been able to take peace for granted.
content.extendedDescription:
This is not a seminar. It is an open invitation.

The founders and guests in SPSU's tent answer one question at a time, asked by anyone in the room. No agenda. No prepared answers. If you have always wondered what Ukrainians really think about Sweden, the war, the future or you, this is your opportunity.

Behind the conversation lies a serious question: Ukrainian and Swedish values have been shaped by very different histories. Sweden has not experienced occupation, attempted annihilation or war at home for 200 years. Ukraine has never had that luxury. How does this affect how we understand one another, and what happens when these world views are forced to coexist?

The unsettling thought: perhaps Ukrainians are not the only ones who need to integrate. Perhaps Sweden needs to integrate into a reality in which the safety we have taken for granted is no longer guaranteed.
content.subject: Integration/diversity
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: What is needed for sport to be a positive force in society?
content.description: Young people risk exclusion and involvement in crime, particularly in socioeconomically disadvantaged areas, with major consequences for individuals and society. How can we ensure sport is a safe place that helps create community and hope for the future?
content.extendedDescription:
Initiatives such as Svenska Fotbollförbundet's En bättre väg and Riksidrottsförbundet's Idrottsklivet strengthen sport's presence where needs are greatest. More children and young people gain access to meaningful leisure activities, safe environments and adult role models. These initiatives create more opportunities to enter sport, build relationships and belong, and thereby choose a different path in life.

The seminar discusses how sport, politics, business and the justice system can together create lasting change. What concrete difference does sport make today, what barriers prevent it reaching more people, and how can efforts be strengthened further?
content.subject: Integration/diversity

content.title: Jobs that did not exist three years ago – how do we solve industry's skills shortage?
content.description: Sweden has one of Europe's strongest technology industries and innovation capabilities, but also one of its most serious skills shortages. Industry is crying out for engineers while AI and automation change the skills actually needed. How do we solve industry's skills shortage?
content.extendedDescription:
Six in ten industrial companies say finding the right skills has become harder. Demand is greatest for roles such as industrial electricians, toolmakers and automation technicians, but Swedish industry needs to recruit more than 230,000 people in total within three years. The education system cannot keep up, the pace of transition is uneven and international recruitment is politically sensitive but commercially unavoidable.

Companies that fail to secure skills lose ground. Yet some initiatives work: reskilling programmes, academia–industry collaborations and new routes into technical professions.
Who takes responsibility: companies, the state or academia? Which models can scale? And how do we ensure the transition does not leave parts of the workforce behind?
content.detail: Loops arena för impact, industri och energi
content.subject: Business
speakerTitles: Head of the skills supply unit

content.title: Child poverty is increasing – how do we reverse the trend?
content.description: Many children in Sweden live in financial vulnerability. One in eight is affected, and many families experience serious financial anxiety. This can lead to financial risk-taking and debt. Meanwhile, the government's benefits reform risks increasing pressure on already vulnerable households. How can the trend be reversed?
content.extendedDescription:
How poverty is measured affects the picture, but the inequalities are clear. According to SCB, the number of people experiencing material and social poverty has doubled in five years, from 350,000 (2021) to more than 700,000 (2025). Single mothers are particularly vulnerable, with a sharp increase in the proportion affected. Meanwhile, most families with children live at what is classified as a high economic standard, illustrating growing disparities. Parents' financial stress affects children's security, health and future opportunities.
The seminar examines children's situation from a child rights perspective. Which political reforms can make the greatest difference, and who is responsible? How can civil society help reduce children's economic exclusion and create better conditions for growing up?
content.subject: Children/young people
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Corps Leader and Children's Rights Lawyer

content.title: Only when needed – how do we stop antibiotic resistance together?
content.description: Antibiotic resistance is one of the greatest health threats and sustainability challenges of our time. How can we use antibiotics more responsibly?
content.extendedDescription:
Antibiotic resistance is one of the greatest health threats and sustainability challenges of our time. Meanwhile, antibiotic use is increasing globally, and resistance is growing here in Sweden too. Without action, the consequences will affect not only modern healthcare but also food supplies, animal husbandry and agriculture.

Businesses, authorities, the technology sector and civil society all play crucial roles in tackling resistant bacteria. How can we use antibiotics more responsibly while encouraging innovation? And what roles can public and private stakeholders and the next generation of decision-makers play in combating antibiotic resistance?

This discussion brings together representatives from across society, using a One Health perspective that connects human, animal and environmental health, to discuss practical solutions to one of today's greatest global health challenges.
content.subject: Health and social care
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Sweden and Ukraine's shared future: what do the Swedish parties say?
content.description: Sweden has supported Ukraine financially and militarily since 2022. But what is Sweden's long-term policy, and what do the parties actually say about a shared future beyond the end of the war?
content.extendedDescription:
Sweden has provided military, humanitarian and financial support to Ukraine. But what does a long-term commitment mean, and are Swedish parties prepared to discuss it openly?
This is an open-table discussion without a stage or prepared speeches. Politicians, Ukrainians, volunteers and the public sit around the same table. Everyone is welcome regardless of political views, nationality or background. Questions come from everyone in the room, not just a moderator.

The event takes place twice: Tuesday 23 June at 13:00 and Thursday 25 June at 13:00, at the same location.

The discussion is organised as part of Samarbetsplattformen: Sverige & Ukraina (SPSU), a KlinteVolontär project giving Ukrainian civil society its own voice in Swedish democratic debate and bringing together Swedish and Ukrainian organisations to strengthen long-term cooperation between the countries.
content.subject: International affairs
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Member of Parliament, Chair of the Committee on Foreign Affairs

content.title: Do not ban fishing for household consumption – our oldest form of fishing carries culture into the future
content.description: Coastal communities have fished for their own households for thousands of years. This fishing is sustainable and has never threatened fish stocks. Yet the proposed new fisheries law would ban all net fishing for household consumption in Swedish waters, a proposal we hope never becomes reality.
content.extendedDescription:
Gotlands Husbehovsfiskeförening and Kullens Fiskareförening invite you to a discussion about our oldest and gentlest form of fishing: fishing for household consumption. It has existed as long as people have lived by the sea, threatens no stocks and destroys neither seas nor seabeds. It is sustainable, contributes to thriving fishing villages and carries valuable cultural heritage into the future. It is also an important resource for strong food preparedness.
Come and hear the arguments against a ban, learn more about small-scale fishing, ask questions and meet some of its strongest advocates.
Welcome to our meeting place: fishing for household consumption – an important carrier of culture and essential to food supplies in a crisis.
content.subject: Culture

content.title: Lifelong learning and skills shortages – how do we make them fit together?
content.description: Matching problems in Sweden's labour market are substantial, while the need for lifelong learning is growing. For more people to retrain, pursue further education and enter employment, better support is needed to understand occupations, education and labour market needs.
content.extendedDescription: More educational opportunities alone are not enough to make lifelong learning work in practice. People also need better support to understand emerging occupations, the skills in demand and which routes actually lead to work. This discussion brings together perspectives on skills provision from the labour market, education, civil society and young people. We discuss how to strengthen connections between individual development, educational provision and employers' needs. Where are today's gaps, and what is needed to make career transitions, further education and entry into employment possible for more people? The aim is to highlight a growing societal challenge and open a discussion about building better bridges between people, education and jobs.
content.subject: Employment/labour market

content.title: From climate to security – how do we secure both growth and a stable electricity system, and who takes responsibility?
content.description: Sweden's energy system has shifted from a climate issue to a security issue. How robust is Europe's energy supply? What happens to inflation, investment and competitiveness if electricity is insufficient or too expensive? And who takes responsibility when energy security becomes a total defence issue?
content.extendedDescription:
Sweden's energy system has shifted from a climate issue to a security issue. Industrial electrification, a strained electricity system and a more uncertain world place new demands on politics, markets and capital.

How robust is Sweden's/Europe's energy supply? What happens to inflation, investment and competitiveness if electricity is insufficient or too expensive? And who takes responsibility when energy security becomes a total defence issue?

This panel brings together perspectives from politics, business, macroeconomics and investment for a focused discussion of risks, choices and priorities through 2030.
content.subject: Energy
speakerTitles: Head of Swedish Fixed Income Management

content.title: The economic outlook in 2026: recovery with risks – what lies ahead for Sweden and the world?
content.description: What does the economic outlook look like in 2026? How do geopolitical conflicts, inflation, interest rates and the labour market affect economic development, and what does this mean for businesses, households and decision-makers?
content.extendedDescription: Dagens industri and +Pro invite you to a trend overview with Anna Ekelund, News Editor at Dagens industri. After several years of recession, signs of recovery are emerging in Sweden and globally, but progress is fragile and risks are numerous. The conflict in the Middle East and rising energy prices have dampened growth and increased inflationary pressure, while Sweden's economy benefits from strong public finances and competitive businesses. Household consumption drives the recovery, but unemployment remains high and differences between groups are growing. GDP growth forecasts range from 2 to 3 per cent, but uncertainty is substantial and the future depends on geopolitics, energy prices and global trade. We discuss the key trends, risks and opportunities.
content.subject: Economy
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: War and blockade – what is at stake in the Middle East?
content.description: Negotiations between the USA and Iran are ongoing, but can the Strait of Hormuz become a safe shipping passage again? Points of conflict between the USA and Iran have only increased since the war began in February. The war in Lebanon further complicates the situation. How will the conflict with Iran affect the balance of power in the Middle East?
content.extendedDescription:
Once again, oil is at the centre of a Middle Eastern conflict. Inflation and dramatically higher energy prices loom, while the desired regime change in Iran has not materialised and difficulties preventing the country from developing nuclear weapons remain. A fragile ceasefire is in place after the USA and Israel began war in Iran, but the conflict has already changed the regional balance of power.

Welcome to Utrikespolitiska institutet's morning in Almedalen. We discuss today's major foreign policy issues and offer perspectives on dramatic global developments. There is also an opportunity to mingle, talk to our experts and make contacts.

Utrikespolitiska institutet combines research, analysis and public education on international affairs.

Coffee and sandwiches are available from 07:45!
content.subject: International affairs

content.title: Energy security as a competitive advantage – how can AI and geothermal energy strengthen Sweden's resilience?
content.description: Energy supply has become a strategic security issue. What role can geothermal energy play in Sweden's security and competitiveness, and what is needed to meet future electricity demand? How can digital technology accelerate progress?
content.extendedDescription:
Jordkraft Energy's pilot project with Naftogaz in Ukraine explores how geothermal electricity generation can strengthen resilience in a country whose critical infrastructure is under severe pressure. Meanwhile, global geothermal investment is increasing as AI, data centres and electrification drive rapidly growing demand for stable, fossil-free baseload power. Data, AI and digitalisation are crucial to scaling new energy sources by reducing risks, improving exploration efficiency and providing better evidence for investment decisions.

This seminar brings together representatives of energy, technology and investment to discuss geothermal energy's potential role in Sweden's security and competitiveness, what is needed to meet future electricity demand and how digital technology can accelerate progress.
content.subject: Energy
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation

content.title: Thoughts for the day with the Minister for Justice: a freer and safer Sweden
content.description: Freedom and safety are two sides of the same coin. Parents should feel able to let children cycle home alone from football practice, and women should not have to look over their shoulders on the way home. Dangerous criminals should be inside so you feel safe outside.
content.extendedDescription:
This is Moderaterna's safety pledge for the next parliamentary term.

Sweden is on the right path, but has not arrived. Lethal gang violence has more than halved. So have personal robberies against boys under 18 and profits from fraud against older people. Police numbers have increased substantially, more serious crimes are solved and we are regaining control of more residential areas.

At the same time, the work against gangs must be completed. This concerns violence, the criminal economy and recruitment of children. We must also focus on other serious crime, such as men's violence against women, sexual offences and honour-based oppression.

Join breakfast with Gunnar Strömmer to hear his thoughts on safety and freedom in Sweden over the next four years. Above all, this will be an open discussion with plenty of room for your questions.
content.subject: Other
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: What role does coastal fishing play in the future of Swedish commercial fishing?
content.description: Swedish coastal fishing is at a turning point. Declining stocks, ecosystem imbalances and economic challenges threaten the sector, even though small-scale, selective coastal fishing has considerable potential to benefit the marine environment, local food production and sustainable management that creates value.
content.extendedDescription: Small-scale coastal fishing is often overlooked in discussions of Swedish commercial fishing. Yet it has a key role in the Baltic Sea's future, with today's clear imbalances from eutrophication and altered food chains favouring sticklebacks and carp-family fish in coastal ecosystems. Local roots and knowledge make coastal fishers central to more ecosystem-based management. Selective gear can target problem species or gently harvest coastal stocks with limited bycatch. Small-scale fishing can create jobs, provide sustainable food and strengthen coastal communities, becoming a cornerstone of efforts for a thriving, sustainable sea. Unlocking this potential, however, requires adaptations to regulations, management and other areas.
content.subject: Climate/environment
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Sweden faces major public health challenges as more people are insufficiently active
content.description: How can we highlight that the joy of movement, inclusion and access to sport for all are central to a sustainable and equal society?
content.extendedDescription:
Physical inactivity affects both people's health and society's long-term wellbeing. During Almedalsveckan, we want to turn words into action through Almedalsloppet and the adjoining sports taster area, a demonstration and opportunity for everyone to move. Public health, inclusion and accessibility are central. Run the race and show what or whom you run for: your club, workplace and so on. In the taster area, you can try different sports.

By participating, you show that enjoyment of movement and equal access to sport are important societal issues.
Read more about the race: https://raceid.com/sv/races/14869/about

Start at Kruttornet on Thursday 25 June at 07.30.
The children's race starts at 09.00.
Organisers: Svenska Friidrottsförbundet, Svaide Roma SOK and RBU Gotland.
In collaboration with: Röda Korset, Gotlands Stadsmission and FRO Gotland.
Come as you are and show the way towards a more active and inclusive Sweden.
content.subject: Sustainability
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: How school meals save the world – and how Sweden can contribute
content.description: Amid major humanitarian crises and challenges for the development sector, there is also good news: school meal programmes continue to expand and develop.
content.extendedDescription:
In a global development context with many large-scale challenges, school meals really are a superhero! Good school meal programmes improve education and pupils' concentration, promote health, strengthen children's nutrition and support local economies and food systems. School meals also matter for preparedness in humanitarian crises and have life-changing effects, especially for girls. In short, school meal programmes can save the world!

WFP's goal is bold but clear: every child should have access to a nutritious school meal by 2030! Although 466 million children worldwide are covered by school meal programmes, more than 100 million children and young people still go without. Why, and how can the international community, including humanitarian and development actors, expand these programmes widely?
How does WFP work with school meals in the forgotten crisis in Sudan? And what role can Sweden play in global school meal efforts?
content.subject: International affairs

content.title: Stable growth on three pillars – what is sustainable urban development in 2026?
content.description: Growing cities bring both opportunities and challenges. How can growth, social sustainability and the climate transition be combined in practice?
content.extendedDescription:
Norrköping and Malmö are developing at a rapid pace. Populations are growing, neighbourhoods are being transformed and demands for climate-smart, socially sustainable development are increasing. But how do we create stable growth that lasts economically, socially and environmentally?

Major urban transformation is under way in Norrköping, while Malmö focuses on social sustainability and climate-smart urban development. Exclusion, safety and future urban environments are high on both cities' agendas.

Meanwhile, energy systems, coordinated planning and business investment are crucial to a just transition. How can partnerships between municipalities, business and academia contribute to attractive, inclusive cities?

Join a discussion bringing together political leaders, business and experts to explore what sustainable urban development means in practice and how we can build stable growth on three pillars together.
content.subject: Sustainability
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Chair of the Municipal Executive Board

content.title: Lowering food prices without compromising quality
content.description: How do we lower food prices without compromising quality? Despite reduced food VAT, global conditions risk continuing to drive up food supply chain costs.
content.extendedDescription:
How do we lower food prices without compromising quality, sustainability ambitions or Sweden's food preparedness? The government's food VAT reduction has brought welcome price cuts, but in an unsettled world with rising costs for inputs, transport and energy, efforts to reduce prices must continue. Coop has therefore developed proposals to simplify rules and remove administrative requirements, reducing costs without compromising quality or sustainability.

Together with politicians and food supply chain stakeholders, we open a constructive, solution-oriented discussion of these proposals and other measures for lower food prices, aiming to preserve consumer protection, food safety and sustainability initiatives. Alongside the seminar, Coop launches a report proposing how to move from words to action on simpler rules.
content.subject: Food
speakerTitles: Member of the Committee on Industry and Trade

content.title: Preparing for tomorrow – Swedish defence investment in a new geopolitical context
content.description: Europe's security landscape has fundamentally changed. Several scenarios point to European NATO countries doubling defence investment in the near future. What regulatory measures are required? And how do we build for the long term in a sector expanding so dramatically in so little time?
content.extendedDescription:
Against this backdrop, we invite you to a breakfast seminar in Almedalen, bringing together leading global affairs analysts, investors and lawyers to examine developments from several perspectives.

The morning starts with an overview of global security and its implications for Europe and Sweden, followed by a closer look at how private equity views defence-sector opportunities: what drives investment interest and which factors are crucial to building attractive, sustainable long-term investment cases. The panel also addresses regulatory complexity, from investment to industrial transition, and offers practical insights into navigating a rapidly changing landscape.
content.subject: Security/defence
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation

content.title: With woollen socks and burkinis – how do we engage young people born abroad in societal issues and politics?
content.description: Young people's trust in politics is declining and voter turnout is falling, particularly among those with foreign backgrounds. What is needed when young people feel decision-makers neither listen nor care and that their voices do not matter? And do politicians understand?
content.extendedDescription:
Join a discussion about adapting settings, meeting formats and communication so that politics and democracy become interesting and relevant to young people born abroad, and why we all need to step outside our own frames of reference to truly meet one another. Now more than ever!

With extensive experience of outdoor activities for newly arrived young people, we share lessons from creating genuine encounters between our participants and Swedish politicians in nature. We explain how to create settings and meetings where more people feel included.

Come and discover practical tips and methods for your work, whether you are a politician, active in civil society or an official at an authority or municipality.
content.subject: Democracy

content.title: Longer lives, shorter working days – an impossible pension equation?
content.description: Sweden needs more people to work longer, yet many doubt they can keep going until retirement. Young people struggle to enter the labour market, while older people who want to work struggle to find jobs. Many also want shorter working days, but knowledge of how life choices affect pensions is limited. How can the equation add up?
content.extendedDescription:
Drawing on Globeknot's first report, we discuss how Sweden can meet simultaneous challenges: longer lives, later entry into employment, AI-driven transformation and a growing need for flexibility and career change.

The starting point is creating sustainable, inclusive working lives throughout life, enabling more people to work longer and giving them knowledge to make informed choices about work, working hours and retirement. How can flexibility be combined with financial security without eroding pension levels? The seminar focuses on links between working conditions, preventive health, life choices and pensions, and the changes needed for working life to function for young people, those mid-career and older people in a changing society.
content.subject: Economy
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Member of Parliament, Committee on Social Insurance

content.title: Physical AI for industry – from pilot to production reality
content.description: Physical AI is moving from screens to machines, and Swedish industry faces a choice. How do we move from promising pilots to reliable production, and what is needed for Sweden to truly lead the industrial AI transition?
content.extendedDescription:
Circle Series is an initiative within Tech Forward, a collaboration between Techarenan and Teknikföretagen, bringing together 8–16 hand-picked decision-makers, experts and innovators to explore an urgent topic related to innovation, growth and the future in depth.

Unlike traditional panel discussions, Circle Series is an active conversation where everyone contributes. Each circle has a leader and meets 4–6 times over a year, creating continuity, trust and opportunities to move from insight to action.

The circle on physical AI for industry starts during Almedalsveckan 2026, meets again in the autumn and concludes at Techarenan's major event in February 2027.
content.subject: Digitalisation
content.accessibility: Hearing loop, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Education and skills provision for total defence – from needs to implementation
content.description: Sweden's total defence faces a profoundly changed security situation. Meeting both civilian and military needs requires not only increased investment but also a sustainable long-term model for education and skills provision.
content.extendedDescription:
There are major challenges today involving inadequate coordination, varying knowledge levels and limited access to tailored training. There is also no shared platform where authorities, municipalities, regions and businesses can regularly meet, train and practise together.

Strengthening total defence's implementation capacity requires more than stronger governance and resources: it also needs new structures, approaches and a shared physical meeting place enabling practical application, collaboration and skills development across sectors.

The seminar starts from these challenges, examining how Sweden can move from strategy to concrete implementation and the role a new total defence training centre could play.
content.subject: Security/defence
speakerTitles: Head of the Military Defence Division and Capability Director
Professor, Director, Center for Security and Resilience

content.title: What is really being said in the energy debate: plenty of talk, little customer focus?
content.description: Electricity support, high-cost protection, capacity charges, electricity taxes, congestion revenues and prices moving in every direction. The 2026 election year has brought many variables for electricity customers to navigate, yet they are rarely present when energy is discussed.
content.extendedDescription:
We offer a review of the energy debate during Almedalsveckan and what it could mean for Swedish electricity customers, the election campaign and the coming parliamentary term.

The political ambition to electrify Sweden places high demands on the electricity system. The way forward has been extensively debated in recent years, particularly here in Almedalen. Customers are often expected to play an important role by adjusting consumption and adapting to volatile, unpredictable prices. Sometimes they are compensated afterwards. What has the debate looked like during the 2026 election year and Almedalsveckan, and what could forthcoming decisions mean for customers? What do Swedish electricity customers want today, and how can the energy industry and politicians meet those needs?
content.subject: Energy
speakerTitles: Nordic Head of Energy Sector Advisory
Head of Public Affairs and Communications

content.title: A message to Sweden's next government: we are ready to win the battle for future investment
content.description: Competitiveness is determined not by ambition or strategy documents, but by where investment actually lands, where innovations scale and where industrial resilience is built.
content.extendedDescription:
Sweden is one of the world's most innovation-driven countries. We have strong private R&D, an active capital market and a world-class industrial base. Meanwhile, the global playing field is changing rapidly. Capital is more selective, states are taking an active role in industrial policy and speed has become a decisive competitive factor.

How do we ensure Sweden's research and capital strengths lead to new operations, jobs and long-term growth at home? Is our R&D model strategic enough? Do we have the capital needed for the whole journey, from startup to global industry? And what determines whether the next billion-scale investment lands in Sweden or elsewhere?

Representatives of academia, capital markets and business meet politicians to discuss turning direction into action and how Sweden can accelerate in a new global investment landscape.
content.subject: Business
speakerTitles: Member of Parliament, Committee on Industry and Trade

content.title: How can Sweden's textile industry grow?
content.description: Sweden has the potential to become a world leader in sustainable textile development, circular flows and future production. How do we accelerate progress?
content.extendedDescription: Sweden is a textile nation of global significance. The sector is among the country's most employment-intensive industries, driving jobs, regional development and economic stability. But this is only the beginning. Sweden has the potential to lead the world in sustainable textile development, circular flows and future production. Unlocking that potential requires a national effort. Textile Valley is the hub of this movement, a unique creative ecosystem connecting education, research, entrepreneurship, design, production and commerce. At its heart is Högskolan i Borås, already offering one of the world's leading textile education programmes, with research and testing environments unparalleled in the Nordic region. The next step is logical: Sweden needs a textile university to strengthen national textile expertise and research, attract international talent and educate the workforce needed for the industry to grow nationwide.
content.subject: Security/defence

content.title: Sweden should send peace doves, not bombs
content.description: As great powers rearm and conflicts deepen, the language of peace becomes more important than ever. Diplomacy is not weakness. It is the courage to choose dialogue over confrontation and cooperation over conflict.
content.extendedDescription:
In a time of growing geopolitical tensions, rearmament and armed conflict, more spaces are needed for the voice of peace. In this workshop, participants are invited to fold peace doves and formulate personal messages about peace, dialogue and international cooperation.

The collected messages will then be compiled and delivered to Sweden's Minister for Defence as a symbolic reminder of the importance of diplomacy, human security and peaceful solutions to global conflicts.

As the world faces difficult choices, we must ask: how do we create conditions for dialogue when divisions grow?

Diplomacy is not passivity. It is active work to prevent conflict and build lasting peace. Through this workshop, we want to enable participants to contribute their own perspectives and jointly highlight the importance of the language of peace in troubled times.
content.subject: Democracy

content.title: Is today's EU what we voted for in 1994?
content.description: In 1994, Sweden voted for expanded trade and to work for a better Europe together with other EU countries. Since then, membership has prompted critical debate about increased centralisation challenging both Swedish self-government and prosperity.
content.extendedDescription: According to SCB's latest survey (May 2025), around 35% of voters oppose or are uncertain about Swedish EU membership (11% oppose and 24% are uncertain). They represent around 3 million voters who are not represented by any existing parliamentary party. Meanwhile, debate about membership is virtually absent. This may help explain why turnout in the last two EU elections fell from 55 to 53 per cent. The seminar aims to raise Swedish EU membership in the ongoing election debate. Parallels will be drawn with the United Kingdom and Norway, two countries that have chosen to remain outside the EU. The panel examines aspects of membership rarely heard in public debate, as well as what Sweden should do to finally realise what its people once voted for.
content.subject: EU

content.title: 48 hours without global cloud services – what does this reveal about Sweden's digital dependencies?
content.description: Sweden and Europe are deeply dependent on a handful of global cloud services. What happens if they stop working? This dependence is no longer just a business matter but a strategic societal issue involving vulnerability, responsibility and preparedness amid growing digital threats.
content.extendedDescription:
Cloud services from a handful of global providers have become essential to everything from banking and healthcare to media and public administration. As threats to digital infrastructure grow, analyses show that many stakeholders in essential sectors are uncertain of their role in cyber defence and total defence.

Ahead of Almedalen, Telenor is conducting an internal analysis and simulation exercise to map how a prolonged global cloud outage affects networks, operations and customers. The seminar shares these insights and places them in a wider societal context. The discussion examines digital dependencies as a strategic societal issue and how different sectors are affected by an outage. What can we learn about responsibility, cooperation and preparedness, and how do we strengthen Sweden's digital resilience?
content.subject: Digitalisation

content.title: Diversity – Sweden's most underestimated engine of growth
content.description: At a time when companies are pursuing innovation, skills and competitiveness, one of the greatest drivers of growth is already right in front of us, yet repeatedly overlooked: diversity.
content.extendedDescription:
Although many organisations say they work on inclusion, efforts often get stuck at values, policies and symbolic initiatives, without a clear link to business results.

This session challenges the view of diversity as a soft issue and shows why it is one of our most practical business strategies.

* What happens in organisations where everyone thinks alike?
* How do different perspectives affect innovation, risk assessment and decision-making?
* Why do so many companies fail to turn diversity into actual growth?

Using insights from a diversity perspective and real business cases, we explore how diversity of thought – differences in perspectives, experiences and motivations – can become a decisive competitive advantage.

We go beyond representation to discuss what really makes a difference: how organisations can understand, lead and use differences to produce results.
content.subject: Integration/diversity
content.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible toilet, wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue
speakerTitles: Chair of the Labour Market Committee

content.title: Do we need more businesses, or better ones?
content.description: Why do so few choose entrepreneurship when starting a business is easier than ever? How can we create security, business survival and societal value, and change young people's views of entrepreneurship?
content.extendedDescription:
Starting a business is easier than ever, yet few take the step. Does security determine our choices? Sweden has a high-quality business sector, and there is a desire to make starting a business easier. But perhaps the question is more about survival and long-term sustainability than starting up.

The seminar discusses how more companies can survive and create real value. We ask: does a company's survival have intrinsic value if it does not contribute to society? And how does running a business differ from being employed – can the gap be bridged?

We also examine young entrepreneurs' perspectives and views on security in career choices.
The seminar offers insights and practical examples for anyone wanting to understand the motivations, challenges and opportunities in today's entrepreneurship.
content.subject: Economy

content.title: Who Will Win the Global Fusion Energy Race?
content.description: How European cutting edge-technology, EU’s strategy for fusion industrialization and game-changing public investments can close the gap to front runners US and China, as fusion energy becomes geopolitics
content.extendedDescription:
After a hundred years of research and recent technological and political breakthroughs, fusion energy is approaching industrialisation within the next decade, with the USA and China in the lead and Europe close behind. With major public investment, an explosive increase in private capital and a growing number of private pilot plants, the global fusion race is in full swing, with the Nordic region and Sweden at the forefront. A series of seminars discusses the potential and challenges for Swedish, Nordic and European fusion power. What opportunities for national, regional and global development, prosperity and innovation emerge when energy is no longer a limiting factor?

Nordic fusion energy initiative Novatron meets politics, industry, energy companies and civil society.
content.subject: Energy
speakerTitles: EU Senior Policy Advisor on Energy Technology
Director of Government and International Affairs
Expert EU energy and climat policies

content.title: 200,000 more hours of leadership – can broader collaboration create the care of the future?
content.description: Care managers face growing documentation requirements, tighter regulations and increasing needs. Meanwhile, time for hands-on leadership is more important than ever as the pace of change keeps accelerating. How can this equation work?
content.extendedDescription:
Ambea has implemented AI support at scale and now frees up almost 200,000 management hours annually. Investigation times have halved, recruitment processes shortened and administration simplified. Technology enhances people rather than replacing them.
As one of the Nordic region's largest care providers, Ambea has shown that AI can be implemented at scale. What is needed for others to make the same journey?
Can the private sector serve as a testbed and development driver for the entire care sector? How do we create more partnerships that accelerate implementation in real operations?

In this panel, municipal, private-provider and academic representatives discuss how partnerships can accelerate implementation. How do we create more partnerships where municipalities, academia and the private sector share risk, learning and results?
content.subject: Innovation

content.title: Scaling from Sweden – a compromise or a competitive advantage?
content.description: How can Sweden strengthen its ability to turn innovation into international growth, jobs and competitiveness? This matters because future prosperity depends heavily on whether new technology companies can grow from Sweden.
content.extendedDescription:
Sweden is strong at creating tech companies, and Swedish companies rank among the world's best at scaling. Talent and capital are important prerequisites, but customers are equally crucial. What role do established companies and public bodies play as the next generation of Swedish tech companies grows globally?

The discussion starts with Sweden as a base for scaling: is it a compromise, or can it become a clearer competitive advantage? For more companies to take the next step, talent and capital are needed, alongside partnerships extending beyond pilot projects and innovation programmes, giving smaller innovative companies access to early customers, strategic partners and real business.

The panel discusses building an ecosystem that optimises for upside, speed and future growth rather than reducing downside and preserving the status quo.
content.subject: Business

content.title: Inclusion in practice: what is needed to give more people a chance?
content.description: How can we create solutions to some of today's greatest societal challenges: exclusion, unemployment and a lack of inclusion?
content.extendedDescription:
MAX and a range of organisations share practical examples of how collaboration between business, civil society and public bodies can create real opportunities. Drawing on experience, they discuss integrating inclusion into core operations as part of long-term responsible employment, rather than a side project. The discussion also examines how social sustainability strengthens individuals, organisations and society, and why inclusive workplaces are crucial to future competitiveness and cohesion.

The seminar is aimed at decision-makers, employers and opinion leaders who want to understand how social responsibility can become action and make a real difference.

Arrive in good time! Before the seminar, we serve our brand-new burgers and samples of the luxury shake available exclusively during Almedalen.
content.detail: MAX Arena, the restaurant's roof terrace
content.subject: Integration/diversity

content.title: As the world shifts: why Sweden's reputation is a strategic source of power
content.description: As great powers' global influence is rapidly redistributed, a country's image – its reputation, values and international trust – becomes increasingly decisive. What does it mean when soft power becomes a strategic asset amid growing security tensions?
content.extendedDescription:
During 2025, the USA lost ground in global reputation while China strengthened its position. Sweden, however, continues to rank highly among international audiences despite its limited size, according to the Global Soft Power Index.

Join an in-depth discussion about:
• How changes in the global reputations of the USA and China affect the international balance of power
• Opportunities created when Sweden is seen as credible, stable and innovative
• How our international reputation can strengthen Swedish resilience, diplomacy and competitiveness
• How smaller states can use soft power in a turbulent world
content.subject: Security/defence
speakerTitles: Co-founder and CEO of The Decoding China Project, Affiliated Researcher at Raoul Wallenberginstitutet in Lund. Deputy Chair of EBA.

content.title: How can data and new insights strengthen civil society's role in Sweden's crisis preparedness?
content.description: Sweden's preparedness requires better coordination between the public sector and civil society. Meanwhile, technology, data and civic initiatives already exist that can strengthen society's crisis response. How can these resources be connected and used more systematically?
content.extendedDescription:
After discussing strategic conditions and civil society's role in Sweden's preparedness, this seminar turns to practical applications that already exist or can be developed quickly. New technology and data-driven analysis enable resources to be coordinated in new ways. Civilian drones, defibrillator networks and other civil society initiatives show how existing capabilities can contribute to a more robust society if connected through better data, analysis and collaboration.

In this session, we meet representatives of regions, authorities, innovation environments and civil society who work with these solutions in practice. How can data and analysis strengthen coordination between the public sector and civil society?
Which applications already exist, and what is needed to take the next step?
content.subject: Security/defence

content.title: Sweden creates world-class deep tech – so why are companies leaving?
content.description: Sweden ranks among the world's leaders in research, patents and deep tech startups per capita. Yet too many of our most promising companies scale or seek capital abroad, or are acquired by foreign giants. Why do they not stay, and what can we do about it?
content.extendedDescription:
Deep tech accounted for almost a third of all venture capital deals in Sweden during 2023–2025, despite a tough investment climate. Yet a structural gap remains: capital often comes too early or is insufficient, and the step from functioning technology to factory still lacks a financing model.

What is needed for Sweden to reap the rewards of its own innovation and strengthen its global competitiveness? Do we need longer-term capital, industrial partners willing to act early, or a clearer national determination to retain value at home?

This panel brings together investors experienced in long development cycles, founders who have moved from lab to market and politicians with the power to make changes.
content.detail: Loops arena för impact, industri och energi
content.subject: Business

content.title: When children do not tell and adults dare not ask – how do we talk about eating disorders?
content.description: Eating disorders are increasing, including at younger ages. More children and young people become trapped in self-critical thoughts, body-focused anxiety and a strong sense of inadequacy. Yet silence remains widespread. What is needed to make safe conversations about eating disorders easier?
content.extendedDescription:
This discussion explores why eating disorders remain so difficult to talk about, despite the major difference early conversations can make. Drawing on research and experience, we highlight how adults can feel more confident recognising signs, daring to ask and responding to children and young people with care.

The seminar also launches new conversation tools developed with the project's Expert Council, grounded in research, clinical expertise, lived experience and relatives' perspectives. They support adults in starting difficult conversations about concerns over eating disorders safely and compassionately.

The seminar is led by journalist Petra Nordlund McGahan and made possible by Roschier – House of Many Voices.
content.subject: Children/young people
speakerTitles: Licensed Psychologist, Licensed Psychotherapist and Associate Professor of Psychology

content.title: AI in schools: how do we prepare pupils for working life?
content.description: AI is already part of pupils' daily lives, but four in ten teachers say their school lacks a plan for digital tools. How do we equip pupils with the digital skills working life requires, and ensure their own perspectives actually shape the response?
content.extendedDescription:
Smart tools are already a natural part of many pupils' daily lives. They use them to learn and make decisions about the future, often faster than school practices can adapt. Meanwhile, four in ten teachers say their school lacks a plan for digital tools. This creates a growing gap between pupils' reality and the education meant to prepare them for working life.

The panel focuses on what this gap means for schools' responsibility, governance and equity. How do we ensure every pupil gains the digital skills employers require? What role should pupils themselves play in shaping school practices? And how do we do this without losing quality and long-term thinking? The aim is to highlight choices needed now so that change reduces inequalities rather than deepening them.
content.subject: Education

content.title: Does Sweden have the energy to become a leading AI nation – or will electricity become the next bottleneck?
content.description:
AI could become Sweden's next major competitive advantage, but it comes at a price: energy.
As AI moves from experimentation to business-critical infrastructure, demands for electricity, data centres and capacity are growing at an unprecedented pace. Meanwhile, all of society must electrify, from industry to transport.
content.extendedDescription:
AI is often treated as a software issue today. In practice, however, it is a physical reality, powered by energy, computing capacity and infrastructure. In this panel, we ask the crucial question and discuss:

How AI actually affects Sweden's energy needs
Whether data centres should be prioritised in the energy system
Whether data centres can supply energy and how to think sustainably and innovatively when developing for AI
How to balance AI growth with society's electrification
What is needed for Sweden to attract and retain AI investment

Join a focused discussion where AI is about not only technology but power, priorities and future competitiveness.
content.subject: Energy
content.organizationType: Collaboration between different types of organisation

content.title: The EU's new capacity regulation – an obstacle or opportunity for regional rail?
content.description: During the 2000s, contracted regional and commuter rail services have increased by as much as 130 per cent. Existing track capacity must be used more efficiently, but how should the new regulation be applied in practice?
content.extendedDescription:
Regional public transport authorities' investments in fast, efficient rail mean regional and commuter services now play a crucial role in expanding labour market regions and helping companies recruit appropriately skilled staff. To facilitate commuting and strengthen jobs and growth nationwide, the government and parliament should therefore invest in regional and commuter rail. New lines are necessary, but these services cannot wait for capacity expansion well into the 2030s or beyond. Will regional and commuter rail gain more track capacity under the EU's new capacity regulation, whose introduction begins this year?

The seminar offers perspectives from Öresundståg and Trafikverket, among others.
content.subject: Infrastructure/transport

content.title: Where are the limits of digitalisation?
content.description: How digitalisation and new, sometimes mandatory standards can create efficiency and societal benefits for businesses while risking obsolescence or market distortion, and where the limits lie for public steering of innovation.
content.extendedDescription:
In debates about business, freedom and deregulation are often presented as the opposite of red tape and compulsion. But digitalisation challenges this dichotomy. New standards, sometimes mandatory, can create enormous benefits for businesses and society. More efficient reporting to authorities and e-invoicing, for example, can free up time and resources.

Yet risks remain. Initiatives can quickly become outdated or drive developments that suit political priorities rather than companies. There are also distortions affecting specific industries. Where should the line be drawn? Can the public sector genuinely steer digital development constructively, and where does it go wrong?

In this breakfast seminar, we discuss the balance between rules and innovation, opportunities and pitfalls, and how digitalisation can become a tool rather than an obstacle.

Breakfast is served.
content.subject: Digitalisation

content.title: What might the future look like and how might it work? Which signals enable us to shape it?
content.description: Global challenges are substantial and societal change is accelerating. What signals do we see today, and what clues to possible futures can they provide?
content.extendedDescription:
Welcome to a Foresight Wednesday from Framtidens trädgård, featuring brief observations from different perspectives.

What signals have our guests heard, seen or experienced that offer clues to possible futures?
After listening for signals, we need to ask: “What kind of change does this signal represent? Where does it take us?” and “What trend or broader phenomenon drives us in that direction?” Signal plus driving force equals foresight.

Foresight gives us the power to help shape the future rather than simply letting it happen. It is not about predicting the future; nobody can do that! It means using today's signals and knowledge to work with future scenarios, helping us make better-informed decisions.
content.subject: Innovation
content.accessibility: The event is captioned, Wheelchair-accessible toilet, Wheelchair-accessible entrance and venue

content.title: Heavy vehicles' journey towards fossil-free competitiveness – what policies are needed now?
content.description: When will demand for electric trucks take off, and what is needed? What do we expect from technological development, and what supports rapid electrification? What will relations with China look like? What are the biggest pitfalls?
content.extendedDescription:
The government initiative Fossilfritt Sverige turns ten and invites two of Sweden's leading industrial figures, Christian Levin, CEO of Scania, and Martin Lundstedt, CEO of AB Volvo, to look back and ahead.

We begin with the past ten years: what did we believe in 2016? What surprised us? Which individual events influenced progress towards fossil-free operations, politically, globally and personally?

We then look ten years ahead and explore what Volvo and Scania need from policymakers.

Infrastructure Minister Andreas Carlson (KD) and Mikael Damberg, former Finance Minister and Socialdemokraterna's Economic Policy Spokesperson, reflect on the industrial leaders' observations and respond to their policy requests. Jessica Alenius, incoming CEO of Mobility Sweden, closes the seminar with her reflections.
content.subject: Business

content.title: The 2026 US midterm elections – what do they mean for Sweden and the global economy?
content.description: President Trump's approval ratings are at historic lows, and suddenly even Texas is in play. The 2026 US midterm elections could reshape the balance in Congress, the global economy and Swedish export industry. What would a shift in power mean?
content.extendedDescription:
Reform Society takes a deep dive into the US midterm elections together with Matt McMillan, an award-winning international political consultant and campaign strategist with experience from national elections in more than 40 countries and hundreds of congressional, senate and state-level races.

We look in particular at the senate race in Texas, where the Democrats' James Talarico – a teacher and theologian who frames progressive politics in Christian terms – faces the Trump-backed and controversial Ken Paxton. What would a shift of power in Congress mean for the US and for Sweden?

The format is an informal but well-informed on-stage conversation with plenty of room for questions, input and discussion from the audience.

content.title: Heavy transport in transition – electrification, hydrogen and Europe's competitiveness
content.description: Transport needs to transition while Europe strengthens competitiveness and resilience. How can industry and decision-makers create the right conditions amid rapid technological development and geopolitical uncertainty?
content.extendedDescription:
The transport sector must transition while European industry strengthens competitiveness amid rapid technological development and geopolitical uncertainty. Electrification is the main route for heavy transport, with hydrogen an important complement, particularly for long-distance journeys.

The issue is primarily about creating conditions for innovation, investment and large-scale deployment at the right pace, rather than choosing technologies. Infrastructure, energy systems and regulations must develop alongside industrial investment.
This discussion brings together leading industry representatives to share insights into technological shifts, investment conditions and the policies needed to build a competitive, fossil-free transport system.

content.title: Swedish entrepreneurship education supporting the future of Ukrainian women
content.description: Can Swedish higher education support Ukrainian needs, in addressing gender inequality, economic marginalisation and the hurdles refugees face when building resilient enterprises?
content.extendedDescription:
We will highlight how the entrepreneurship educational projects equip Ukrainian women with skills on how to launch and develop their business as well as psychological tools on how to stay resilient on their entrepreneurial journey. 

Drivhuset is a Nordic organization dedicated to strengthening entrepreneurial skills and supporting individuals in developing ideas into sustainable businesses. With over 30 years of experience, Drivhuset works closely with universities and partners to empower aspiring entrepreneurs through education, coaching, and practical tools.

NGO Evolve is a Ukrainian non-profit organization working on supporting female entrepreneurship and providing opportunities for internationalisation and growth to entrepreneurs and businesses in Ukraine since 2018.

Advicera is a development company from Helsinki dedicated to fostering innovation, entrepreneurship, and business growth.

content.title: How do we create circular packaging chains in practice?
content.description: Packaging is an integral part of everyday life, but the system behind it is complex and fragmented. Many companies struggle to navigate new regulations and lack resources, testing environments and support to transition to more circular solutions. How can we make the packaging system more circular together?
content.extendedDescription:
This panel brings together representatives of the packaging value chain to discuss challenges and possible solutions. The focus is on creating more resource-efficient, circular flows in practice and establishing shared dialogue and approaches that can lead to real change.

Participants:
Kai-Yee Thim, Head of Product and Product Safety Affairs,
Skogsindustrierna

Sarah Nilsson, Product Manager for Packaging, PostNord

The panel is organised within Cirkulära förpackningskedjor, an initiative seeking to accelerate the transition to circular packaging in line with new EU requirements.

The panel concludes with a joint networking reception. Welcome!

content.title: Sweden and Ukraine's shared future: what do the Swedish parties say?
content.description: Sweden has supported Ukraine financially and militarily since 2022. But what is Sweden's long-term policy, and what do the parties actually say about a shared future beyond the end of the war?
content.extendedDescription:
Sweden has provided military, humanitarian and financial support to Ukraine. But what does a long-term commitment mean, and are Swedish parties prepared to discuss it openly?
This is an open-table discussion without a stage or prepared speeches. Politicians, Ukrainians, volunteers and the public sit around the same table. Everyone is welcome regardless of political views, nationality or background. Questions come from everyone in the room, not just a moderator.

The event takes place twice: Tuesday 23 June at 13:00 and Thursday 25 June at 13:00, at the same location.

The discussion is organised as part of Samarbetsplattformen: Sverige & Ukraina (SPSU), a KlinteVolontär project giving Ukrainian civil society its own voice in Swedish democratic debate and bringing together Swedish and Ukrainian organisations to strengthen long-term cooperation between the countries.

content.title: Sweden should send peace doves, not bombs
content.description: As major powers build up their armed forces and conflicts deepen, the language of peace becomes more important than ever. Diplomacy is not weakness. It is the courage to choose dialogue over confrontation and cooperation over conflict.
content.extendedDescription:
In a time of growing geopolitical tensions, rearmament and armed conflict, we need more spaces where the voice of peace can be heard. In this workshop, participants are invited to fold peace doves and write personal messages about peace, dialogue and international cooperation. The collected messages will then be compiled and presented to Sweden's Minister for Defence as a symbolic reminder of the importance of safeguarding diplomacy, human security and peaceful solutions to global conflicts.

As the world faces difficult choices, we need to ask ourselves: How do we create conditions for dialogue as divisions grow? How do we ensure that conversation and cooperation have more space than confrontation and mistrust?

Diplomacy is not passivity. It is active work to prevent conflicts and build lasting peace. In this workshop, we fold peace doves and write messages about the future we want to see.
content.subject: Security/defence

content.title: What signals about the future has the week brought?
content.description: Global challenges are substantial and societal change is accelerating. What signals have we noticed during Almedalsveckan, and what clues might they offer about the future?
content.extendedDescription:
Join us to explore the signals together! Breakfast is served from 09.00. What signals has the week brought? What have you and others heard, seen or experienced that might offer clues about the future? How can you notice and interpret the signals about the future that Almedalsveckan has given us?

After listening for signals, we need to ask questions such as: ‘What kind of change does this signal represent? In what direction does it take us?’ and ‘What trend or broader phenomenon is driving us in that direction?’ Signal plus driving force equals foresight.

Foresight is an approach that gives us the power to help shape the future, rather than simply letting it happen. It is not about predicting the future — no one can do that! It is about using the signals we see and the knowledge we have today to work with scenarios for the future. These can help us make better-informed decisions.
content.subject: Innovation

content.title: Education based on scientific evidence — what does it mean?
content.description: It goes without saying that education should be based on research. At the same time, this raises questions about which research is relevant, how it is made accessible and how it can be used in the school system.
content.extendedDescription:
The purpose of education is complex and requires insights from several fields of research. There are no simple answers or single research approach that can meet every need. Instead, we need a broad and nuanced understanding of what knowledge is relevant to the school system. Education professionals also need a central role in determining what knowledge is needed in practice. This raises questions about research literacy and requires educational research to be made accessible and useful in practice.

The seminar is organised by ULF (Utbildning, Lärande, Forskning), a collaboration between Swedish higher education institutions offering teacher education and school authorities on practice-oriented educational research. During the seminar, people with different roles and connections to the school system come together to discuss what education based on scientific evidence means.
content.subject: Education

content.title: Set research free — it is an election year!
content.description: In recent years, the issue of academic freedom has moved beyond higher education into the public sphere. Everyone seems to agree that academic freedom needs defending — the government is even investigating how to strengthen it. But do we agree on what academic freedom means?
content.extendedDescription:
Ever since the first self-governing universities were established in the Middle Ages, teachers and students have defended the right to seek knowledge freely, without political control. In today's debate, the issue ranges from academics' freedom of expression to the very essence of research and higher education, and to a fundamental democratic principle that concerns us all.
Why must academic freedom be protected right now? And can it be combined with growing demands for publicly funded research and higher education to be relevant to society?
This discussion addresses the tension between academic freedom and demands for education and research to benefit society. The panel includes representatives from academia, politics and the media.

content.title: Digital trust and federated infrastructure — the key to secure cooperation between organisations
content.description: The public sector and businesses increasingly need to share data and use common services. How does digital trust make this easier? How do we create infrastructure that enables secure cooperation without every organisation building its own solutions?
content.extendedDescription: The ability to share data between government agencies, municipalities, regions and businesses is essential to greater efficiency and societal security. Many different solutions are used today, leading to inefficiency and increased costs. Federated solutions are presented as the route to digital trust in complex ecosystems, but trust requires shared ground rules, clear governance and enough connected organisations. A federation creates value only when many members and service providers participate. In this seminar, we discuss how national federated infrastructure can enable secure and efficient cooperation. The discussion draws on experience from Digg's work with Ena and Samordnad identitet och behörighet, as well as findings from a recent PwC report. The focus is on benefits to society across sectors in a more connected digital Sweden.
content.subject: Digitalisation

content.title: 10 years back and 10 years ahead — perspectives on the turbulent journey towards a fossil-free future
content.description: What are the most important developments of the past ten years on Sweden's journey towards a fossil-free future? What has surprised us most? And what do we think could happen over the next ten years?
content.extendedDescription:
The government initiative Fossilfritt Sverige works to accelerate industry's transition away from fossil fuels. This year marks our tenth anniversary, so we are inviting some of Sweden's leading opinion-makers and experts on the climate transition to take a broader view and widen our perspectives. Can looking back also give us inspiration and energy for the road ahead?

Come and celebrate with us! We will offer anniversary cake, a boost of inspiration, networking and music in our garden during the breaks.

14.15-14.45: Johan Kuylenstierna, Director-General, Naturvårdsverket & Annie Reuterskiöld, political reporter, Dagens Nyheter

15.00-15.30: PM Nilsson, CEO, Timbro & Maria Wetterstrand, senior adviser, Miltton

16.00-16.30: Therese Svanström, Chair, TCO & Patrik Kronqvist, political editor, Expressen

Read more about what our observers will discuss on our website: https://fossilfrittsverige.se/event/fossilfritt-sverige-i-almedalen-2026/
content.subject: Business

content.title: A pain nurse at every primary care centre
content.description: One in five people lives with persistent pain, but primary care often lacks the right expertise. A pain nurse at every primary care centre could provide early support, create equitable care and reduce sick leave, mental ill health and the need for specialist care. Patients are currently passed around the healthcare system without a clear way forward.
content.extendedDescription:
One in five people in Sweden lives with persistent pain, making it one of our greatest public health challenges. Despite this, primary care, where most patients first seek help, often lacks structured pain expertise. Many primary care centres now have diabetes and asthma nurses, but no equivalent role for patients with pain.

Since the previous Almedalen, we have advocated for a pain nurse at every primary care centre. A pain nurse can contribute early assessment, continuity, patient education and coordination of care. This can reduce the risk of long-term sick leave, mental ill health and patients being passed between different healthcare contacts without clear treatment.

Stronger expertise in primary care can make care more equitable, accessible and effective for people living with pain.
content.subject: Health and social care
