content.title: From words to action? How can collaboration between social services, schools and police develop?
content.description: Recent reports repeatedly highlight the risk of children and young people being drawn into serious crime at an early age. Different societal actors therefore need to collaborate to identify these children early. How can we achieve this in practice?
content.extendedDescription:
Preventing children and young people from becoming involved in crime or other socially destructive behaviour is an urgent task for society. 'What Works?' is an interdisciplinary research programme (2024-2029) at the Department of Social Work at Uppsala universitet. In collaboration with social services, schools, police, child health services and service users, it develops methods for preventive work with children and young people in social services and schools. The programme focuses on early intervention and collaboration with practitioners.

During the seminar, researchers and a panel of people in senior positions in government, police, social services, schools and voluntary organisations discuss how new findings can be used in prevention. How can we work together to identify concerns early and prevent children and young people from being drawn into crime or other destructive behaviour?

content.title: Make higher education possible where people actually live
content.description: Sweden cannot afford to make higher education a metropolitan privilege. If we are serious about addressing skills shortages, strengthening rural areas and giving people a fair chance, policy must open the door to higher education throughout the country, not only where universities already stand.
content.extendedDescription:
Today, postcodes largely determine people's opportunities for further study. Those living near a university or higher education institution find it much easier to enter higher education than those in smaller municipalities, even though skills needs are often greatest there. This is a democratic problem and a growing obstacle to both welfare services and business.
Employers in smaller and medium-sized municipalities far from the nearest higher education institution repeatedly report difficulties recruiting teachers, nurses, engineers, social workers and other key professionals. Meanwhile, people wanting initial or further education can neither afford nor manage to move or commute to study. The gap between willingness and opportunity is widening, and politicians are responsible for narrowing it.

The question is not whether we can afford to make higher education accessible where people live. The question is whether we can afford not to.

content.title: The sweater of the future – can it be both climate-smart and resource-efficient?
content.description:
The clothing industry is one of the world's most environmentally impactful industries. The textile value chain needs to reduce both its climate impact and resource use.

Can a circular textile economy achieve both?
Is resource efficiency the same as wise resource use in the textile value chain?
content.extendedDescription:
Around 12 kilograms of clothing per person are discarded in the EU every year. Meanwhile, textile consumption increased by 2 kilograms per person from 2017 to 2019.

Work to transform the textile value chain, including raw material production, manufacturing, consumption and waste management, is under way. In 2025, new EU requirements arrived for separate collection of textile waste and the European Commission's new legislation on extended producer responsibility for textiles.

What does the future hold for the clothes you wear today, and how do we need to handle clothing and textiles in future?

Listen to researchers and experts discussing different perspectives on questions such as:

• What can a circular textile value chain solve, and what can it not solve?
• What action is needed in different parts of the chain?
• How do we balance resource efficiency and scalability to achieve sustainability?
• How much do consumption behaviours affect the chain's climate impact and resource use?
• What is required of research and innovation to make the textile and fashion industry sustainable in the long term?
